Loading the Groundwater Toolkit demo. The Python runtime and scientific libraries (about 60 MB) are downloaded on first visit and cached by the browser afterwards.

\n \n\n"}, "groundwater/depth_spine/inline.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Render the workspace as one self-contained page.\n\nThe in-browser demo runs Streamlit under WebAssembly, where there is no server\nto serve a custom component's frontend from disk. ``st.components.v1.html`` is\ncore Streamlit, though - it puts a string in an iframe - so the same workspace\ncan be shown there by baking the payload into a single-file build.\n\nWhat the demo loses is only the return trip: the screen handles cannot hand\nintervals back for Python to re-derive. The page says so, and offers the same\nedit through ordinary Streamlit inputs instead, so the demo reaches the same\ndesigns by a different gesture.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\n#: The single-file build, carried inside the package.\n#:\n#: It lives here rather than beside the component build in ui/ because the\n#: in-browser demo mounts the package into a filesystem where ui/ does not\n#: exist. ``npm run build:inline`` writes it.\nSTATIC_BUILD = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / \"static\" / \"workspace.html\"\n\n_PLACEHOLDER = \"__SPINE_VIEW__\"\n\n\ndef static_build_available() -> bool:\n return STATIC_BUILD.is_file()\n\n\ndef render_static(\n view: dict[str, Any],\n *,\n template: str | None = None,\n interactive: bool = False,\n) -> str:\n \"\"\"Return a complete HTML document with ``view`` baked in.\n\n ``template`` is the single-file build's markup; it is read from\n :data:`STATIC_BUILD` when not supplied, which keeps this function testable\n without the frontend having been built.\n \"\"\"\n if template is None:\n if not static_build_available():\n raise RuntimeError(\n f\"Static build not found at {STATIC_BUILD}. Run \"\n \"`npm install && npm run build:inline` in ui/depth-spine/.\"\n )\n template = STATIC_BUILD.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n payload = json.dumps(\n {\"view\": view, \"interactive\": interactive},\n allow_nan=False,\n )\n # The payload is injected into a \"\n # inside any string - a laboratory name, a flag message - would end the\n # block early and break the page. JSON keeps the escape, the browser does\n # not see a closing tag.\n payload = payload.replace(\" list[SampleProject]:\n \"\"\"Sample projects that carry enough data for the workspace to draw.\"\"\"\n return [s for s in SAMPLES if s.drilling and (_EXAMPLES / s.folder).is_dir()]\n\n\ndef load(key: str, config: Config | None = None) -> SpineInputs:\n \"\"\"Parse one sample project and run the analyses it supports.\"\"\"\n sample = next((s for s in SAMPLES if s.key == key), None)\n if sample is None:\n raise KeyError(f\"unknown sample project: {key}\")\n if not sample.drilling:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"{sample.name} has no drilling log, so there is no borehole section \"\n \"to place screens on.\"\n )\n\n config = config or Config()\n folder = _EXAMPLES / sample.folder\n log = read_drilling_workbook(folder / sample.drilling)\n\n analysis = None\n if sample.pumping:\n test = read_pumping_workbook(folder / sample.pumping)\n analysis = analyse_pumping_test(test, config.pumping)\n # The safe yield rests on an assumed storativity, effective radius and\n # seasonal decline. Attaching the envelope is what lets the workspace\n # show a band instead of a bare number.\n attach_yield_envelope(analysis, config.pumping)\n\n quality = None\n if sample.quality:\n quality = read_quality_workbook(folder / sample.quality)\n\n return SpineInputs(\n name=sample.name,\n log=log,\n analysis=analysis,\n quality=quality,\n config=config,\n )\n"}, "groundwater/depth_spine/static/workspace.html": {"t": "text", "d": "\n\n \n \n \n Depth Spine \u2014 Geomentaqua Groundwater Toolkit\n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n
\n \n\n"}, "groundwater/depth_spine/view.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Build the Depth Spine view payload from the analysis objects.\n\nThe browser draws; this module decides. Every number the workspace shows is\ncomputed here by the same functions the reports use, so the section, the rail\nand the bill of quantities cannot drift from the .docx. The frontend owns only\nthe depth-to-pixel mapping and the pointer.\n\nPure and Streamlit-free, so the payload is unit-testable.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Any, Optional\n\nfrom ..config import Config\nfrom ..costing.model import (\n CostEstimate,\n estimate_borehole_cost,\n inputs_from_design,\n)\nfrom ..design.designer import BoreholeDesign, design_borehole\nfrom ..hydraulics.analysis import PumpingTestAnalysis\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, DrillingLog, WaterQualitySample\nfrom ..quality.assess import WaterQualityAssessment, assess_sample\nfrom ..quality.standards import Limit\n\n\ndef _flag(flag: DataFlag) -> dict[str, str]:\n return {\n \"level\": flag.level,\n \"code\": flag.code,\n \"message\": flag.message,\n \"context\": flag.context,\n }\n\n\ndef _round(value: Optional[float], places: int = 2) -> Optional[float]:\n return None if value is None else round(float(value), places)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SpineInputs:\n \"\"\"Everything the workspace can draw, in whatever combination exists.\n\n Only the drilling log is required. A project with no pumping test still\n gets a section and a bill of quantities; the yield card says what is\n missing rather than inventing a number.\n \"\"\"\n\n name: str\n log: DrillingLog\n analysis: Optional[PumpingTestAnalysis] = None\n #: A raw sample, assessed here.\n quality: Optional[WaterQualitySample] = None\n #: An assessment the caller already ran - preferred over ``quality``, so\n #: the workspace shows the same object the Water quality page does rather\n #: than a second run of the same computation.\n assessment: Optional[WaterQualityAssessment] = None\n config: Optional[Config] = None\n mobilisation_distance_km: float = 0.0\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Section\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _section(log: DrillingLog, design: BoreholeDesign, analysis, config: Config) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Everything indexed by depth, on one axis.\"\"\"\n total_depth = design.total_depth_m\n # A little air below the hole so the total-depth line is not on the edge.\n domain = total_depth * 1.06\n\n # one class table for every drawing: the class and colour ride with each\n # interval so the workspace shades the log the way the report draws it\n from ..design.lithology import lithology_class\n\n lithology = [\n {\n \"top\": iv.top_m,\n \"base\": iv.bottom_m,\n \"description\": iv.description,\n \"aquifer\": _looks_like_aquifer(iv.description),\n \"class\": lithology_class(iv.description).label,\n \"colour\": lithology_class(iv.description).colour,\n }\n for iv in log.intervals\n ]\n\n levels: dict[str, Any] = {}\n swl = design.static_water_level_m\n if swl is not None:\n levels[\"restLevel\"] = _round(swl)\n if analysis is not None:\n # The toolkit only calls a level \"stabilised\" when the last readings\n # agree within 5 cm. When they do not, the honest line to draw is the\n # deepest level reached, labelled as still falling \u2014 drawing it as a\n # stabilised pumping level would overstate what the test showed.\n levels[\"stabilised\"] = analysis.stabilised_level_m is not None\n levels[\"maxDrawdown\"] = _round(analysis.max_drawdown_m)\n if analysis.stabilised_level_m is not None:\n levels[\"pumpingLevel\"] = _round(analysis.stabilised_level_m)\n elif swl is not None and analysis.max_drawdown_m is not None:\n levels[\"pumpingLevel\"] = _round(swl + analysis.max_drawdown_m)\n if design.pump_intake_m is not None:\n levels[\"pumpIntake\"] = _round(design.pump_intake_m, 1)\n\n return {\n \"totalDepth\": total_depth,\n \"domain\": domain,\n \"lithology\": lithology,\n \"waterStrikes\": list(design.water_strikes_m),\n \"segments\": [\n {\"kind\": s.kind, \"top\": s.top_m, \"base\": s.bottom_m} for s in design.segments\n ],\n \"gravelPack\": list(design.gravel_pack),\n \"annularFill\": design.annular_fill,\n \"backfill\": list(design.backfill),\n \"sanitarySeal\": list(design.sanitary_seal),\n \"levels\": levels,\n \"boreDiameterIn\": design.borehole_diameter_in,\n \"casingDiameterIn\": design.casing_diameter_in,\n \"casingMaterial\": design.casing_material,\n \"slotMm\": design.screen_slot_mm,\n \"stickupM\": design.stickup_m,\n \"drillingMethod\": log.drilling_method,\n # The handles may not move a screen outside this band.\n \"screenLimits\": {\n \"top\": 0.0,\n \"base\": total_depth - config.design.sump_length_m,\n \"minLength\": 0.5,\n },\n }\n\n\n_AQUIFER_HINTS = (\"fracture\", \"water\", \"aquifer\")\n\n\ndef _looks_like_aquifer(description: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Only for shading the log \u2014 screen placement uses designer._target_zones.\"\"\"\n text = (description or \"\").lower()\n if any(neg in text for neg in (\"no water\", \"not reached\", \"without water\")):\n return False\n return any(hint in text for hint in _AQUIFER_HINTS)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Design decisions\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _design_decisions(design: BoreholeDesign, analysis, config: Config) -> dict:\n rules = config.design\n screens = design.screens\n yield_block: dict[str, Any] = {\"pending\": \"No pumping test loaded for this borehole.\"}\n\n if analysis is not None and analysis.yield_recommendation is not None:\n rec = analysis.yield_recommendation\n yield_block = {\n \"pending\": rec.pending_reason or \"\",\n \"safeYieldM3PerH\": _round(rec.safe_yield_m3_per_h),\n \"lowM3PerH\": _round(rec.safe_yield_low_m3_per_h),\n \"highM3PerH\": _round(rec.safe_yield_high_m3_per_h),\n \"rangeText\": rec.yield_range_text,\n \"longTermM3PerH\": _round(rec.long_term_yield_m3_per_h),\n \"specificCapacity\": _round(rec.specific_capacity_m3hr_per_m),\n \"availableDrawdownM\": _round(rec.available_drawdown_m),\n \"usableDrawdownM\": _round(rec.usable_drawdown_m),\n \"pumpDepthM\": _round(rec.pump_installation_depth_m, 1),\n \"safetyFactor\": rec.safety_factor,\n \"designPeriodDays\": rec.design_period_days,\n \"basis\": rec.basis,\n \"envelopeBasis\": rec.envelope_basis,\n \"transmissivity\": _round(analysis.transmissivity_m2_per_day, 2),\n \"methods\": _methods(analysis),\n }\n\n return {\n \"yield\": yield_block,\n \"screens\": [{\"top\": s.top_m, \"base\": s.bottom_m} for s in screens],\n \"totalScreenM\": _round(design.total_screen_length_m, 1),\n \"screenShare\": _round(\n design.total_screen_length_m / design.total_depth_m * 100, 1\n ),\n \"slotMm\": design.screen_slot_mm,\n \"rules\": {\n \"sumpLengthM\": rules.sump_length_m,\n \"gravelAboveTopScreenM\": rules.gravel_pack_above_top_screen_m,\n \"sanitarySealDepthM\": rules.sanitary_seal_depth_m,\n \"minScreenBelowSwlM\": rules.min_screen_below_swl_m,\n \"submergenceMinM\": config.pumping.pump_submergence_min_m,\n \"seasonalAllowanceM\": config.pumping.seasonal_allowance_m,\n },\n \"basis\": list(design.design_basis),\n \"flags\": [_flag(f) for f in design.flags]\n + ([_flag(f) for f in analysis.flags] if analysis is not None else []),\n }\n\n\ndef _methods(analysis: PumpingTestAnalysis) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Cross-method transmissivity, so agreement is visible rather than claimed.\"\"\"\n out = []\n for label, result in (\n (\"Cooper-Jacob\", analysis.cooper_jacob),\n (\"Theis\", analysis.theis),\n (\"Recovery\", analysis.recovery),\n ):\n if result is None:\n continue\n out.append(\n {\n \"label\": label,\n \"transmissivity\": _round(result.transmissivity_m2_per_day, 2),\n }\n )\n return out\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Water quality\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _binding_limit(row) -> tuple[Optional[Limit], str]:\n \"\"\"The limit a row is judged against, and what kind of limit it is.\n\n The strictest applicable maximum binds. Which one it was matters in the\n report - a national limit exceeded is a compliance failure, an\n acceptability limit exceeded is a taste complaint - so the name travels\n with the number.\n \"\"\"\n candidates = [\n (\"WHO health\", Limit.parse(row.who_health)),\n (\"WHO acceptability\", Limit.parse(row.who_aesthetic)),\n (\"national\", Limit.parse(row.sl_standard)),\n ]\n best: tuple[Optional[Limit], str] = (None, \"\")\n for name, limit in candidates:\n if limit is None:\n continue\n if limit.minimum is not None: # a range, e.g. pH\n return limit, name\n if limit.maximum is None:\n continue\n if best[0] is None or limit.maximum < best[0].maximum:\n best = (limit, name)\n return best\n\n\ndef _quality(assessment: WaterQualityAssessment) -> dict:\n rows = []\n for r in assessment.rows:\n limit, limit_name = _binding_limit(r)\n # The chart plots every determinand as a multiple of its own limit, so\n # the ratio is computed here rather than by parsing limit strings in\n # the browser.\n ratio = None\n kind = \"none\"\n if limit is not None:\n kind = \"range\" if limit.minimum is not None else \"max\"\n # The limit is written in the guideline's unit, so the value has\n # to be on that scale too. Dividing the raw reported number by it\n # plotted a compliant ug/L result a thousand times over its line.\n if r.value_in_guideline_unit is not None and limit.maximum:\n ratio = float(r.value_in_guideline_unit) / float(limit.maximum)\n rows.append(\n {\n \"parameter\": r.parameter,\n \"value\": _round(r.value, 4),\n \"unit\": r.unit,\n \"valueInGuidelineUnit\": _round(r.value_in_guideline_unit, 4),\n \"guidelineUnit\": r.guideline_unit,\n \"evaluable\": r.evaluable,\n \"reason\": r.reason,\n \"belowDetection\": r.below_detection,\n \"whoHealth\": r.who_health,\n \"whoAesthetic\": r.who_aesthetic,\n \"national\": r.sl_standard,\n \"status\": r.status,\n \"remark\": r.remark,\n \"limitKind\": kind,\n \"limitName\": limit_name,\n \"limitMax\": _round(limit.maximum, 4) if limit else None,\n \"limitMin\": _round(limit.minimum, 4) if limit else None,\n \"ratio\": _round(ratio, 4),\n }\n )\n\n ionic = None\n if assessment.ionic is not None:\n ionic = {\n \"cationsMeq\": _round(assessment.ionic.sum_cations_meq, 3),\n \"anionsMeq\": _round(assessment.ionic.sum_anions_meq, 3),\n \"errorPercent\": _round(assessment.ionic.error_percent, 2),\n \"cations\": {k: _round(v, 4) for k, v in assessment.ionic.cations_meq.items()},\n \"anions\": {k: _round(v, 4) for k, v in assessment.ionic.anions_meq.items()},\n \"usedAlkalinity\": assessment.ionic.used_alkalinity_for_bicarbonate,\n }\n\n corrosivity = None\n if assessment.corrosivity is not None:\n c = assessment.corrosivity\n corrosivity = {\n \"lsi\": _round(c.lsi),\n \"rsi\": _round(c.rsi),\n \"aggressiveIndex\": _round(c.aggressive_index),\n \"larsonSkold\": _round(c.larson_skold),\n \"classification\": c.classification,\n \"isAggressive\": c.is_aggressive,\n \"verdict\": c.verdict,\n \"materialsNote\": c.materials_note,\n \"assumptions\": list(c.assumptions),\n }\n\n piper = _piper(assessment)\n\n wqi = None\n if assessment.wqi is not None:\n wqi = {\n \"value\": _round(assessment.wqi.value, 1),\n \"rating\": assessment.wqi.rating,\n }\n\n return {\n \"sampleId\": assessment.sample.sample_id,\n \"sampleDate\": assessment.sample.sample_date,\n \"laboratory\": assessment.sample.laboratory,\n \"rows\": rows,\n \"verdict\": assessment.verdict,\n \"verdictState\": assessment.verdict_state,\n \"uncertainties\": list(assessment.uncertainties),\n \"healthExceedances\": [r.parameter for r in assessment.health_exceedances],\n \"nationalExceedances\": [r.parameter for r in assessment.national_exceedances],\n \"aestheticExceedances\": [\n r.parameter for r in assessment.aesthetic_exceedances\n ],\n \"indeterminate\": [r.parameter for r in assessment.indeterminate_rows],\n \"ionic\": ionic,\n \"piper\": piper,\n \"corrosivity\": corrosivity,\n \"wqi\": wqi,\n \"flags\": [_flag(f) for f in assessment.flags],\n }\n\n\ndef _piper(assessment: WaterQualityAssessment) -> Optional[dict]:\n \"\"\"Cation and anion percentages for the Piper and Stiff plots.\n\n Reuses the milliequivalents the ionic balance already worked out, so the\n diagrams and the balance check can never disagree.\n \"\"\"\n if assessment.ionic is None:\n return None\n cations = assessment.ionic.cations_meq\n anions = assessment.ionic.anions_meq\n total_c = sum(cations.values())\n total_a = sum(anions.values())\n if total_c <= 0 or total_a <= 0:\n return None\n\n def c(key: str) -> float:\n return cations.get(key, 0.0)\n\n def a(key: str) -> float:\n return anions.get(key, 0.0)\n\n na_k = c(\"sodium\") + c(\"potassium\")\n return {\n \"meq\": {\n \"ca\": _round(c(\"calcium\"), 4),\n \"mg\": _round(c(\"magnesium\"), 4),\n \"naK\": _round(na_k, 4),\n \"hco3\": _round(a(\"bicarbonate\"), 4),\n \"cl\": _round(a(\"chloride\"), 4),\n \"so4\": _round(a(\"sulfate\"), 4),\n },\n \"percent\": {\n \"ca\": _round(c(\"calcium\") / total_c, 4),\n \"mg\": _round(c(\"magnesium\") / total_c, 4),\n \"naK\": _round(na_k / total_c, 4),\n \"hco3\": _round(a(\"bicarbonate\") / total_a, 4),\n \"cl\": _round(a(\"chloride\") / total_a, 4),\n \"so4\": _round(a(\"sulfate\") / total_a, 4),\n },\n }\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Costing\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _costing(estimate: CostEstimate) -> dict:\n items = [\n {\n \"code\": i.code,\n \"stage\": i.stage,\n \"category\": i.category,\n \"item\": i.item,\n \"unit\": i.unit,\n \"quantity\": _round(i.quantity, 3),\n \"unitCost\": _round(i.unit_cost_usd),\n \"amount\": _round(i.amount_usd),\n \"note\": i.note,\n }\n for i in estimate.items\n ]\n\n def _group(key: str) -> list[dict]:\n totals: dict[str, float] = {}\n for i in estimate.items:\n totals[getattr(i, key)] = totals.get(getattr(i, key), 0.0) + i.amount_usd\n direct = estimate.direct_cost_usd or 1.0\n return sorted(\n (\n {\"label\": k, \"amount\": _round(v), \"share\": _round(v / direct * 100, 1)}\n for k, v in totals.items()\n ),\n key=lambda row: row[\"amount\"],\n reverse=True,\n )\n\n return {\n \"items\": items,\n \"byStage\": _group(\"stage\"),\n \"byCategory\": _group(\"category\"),\n \"directCost\": _round(estimate.direct_cost_usd),\n \"overheads\": _round(estimate.overheads_usd),\n \"totalCost\": _round(estimate.total_cost_usd),\n \"margin\": _round(estimate.margin_usd),\n \"price\": _round(estimate.price_usd),\n \"vat\": _round(estimate.vat_usd),\n \"costPerMetre\": _round(estimate.cost_per_meter_usd),\n \"overheadsPercent\": estimate.overheads_percent,\n \"marginPercent\": estimate.margin_percent,\n \"contingencyPercent\": estimate.contingency_percent,\n \"vatPercent\": estimate.vat_percent,\n \"exchangeRate\": estimate.exchange_rate_sle_per_usd,\n \"assumptions\": list(estimate.assumptions),\n \"flags\": [_flag(f) for f in estimate.flags],\n \"quantityBasis\": {\n \"totalDepthM\": estimate.inputs.total_depth_m,\n \"casingM\": _round(estimate.inputs.casing_m, 1),\n \"screenM\": _round(estimate.inputs.screen_m, 1),\n \"gravelIntervalM\": _round(estimate.inputs.gravel_interval_m, 1),\n \"overburdenM\": _round(estimate.inputs.overburden_m, 1),\n },\n }\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Entry point\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef build_view(\n inputs: SpineInputs,\n screens_m: list[tuple[float, float]] | None = None,\n) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Derive the whole workspace from the analysis objects.\n\n ``screens_m`` is the analyst's screen placement from the section. Passing\n it re-runs the design and everything downstream of it - the annulus, the\n checks and the bill of quantities - so the drawing and the BoQ are always\n the same design.\n \"\"\"\n config = inputs.config or Config()\n analysis = inputs.analysis\n swl = None\n pump_intake = None\n if analysis is not None:\n swl = analysis.test.static_water_level_m\n if analysis.yield_recommendation is not None:\n pump_intake = analysis.yield_recommendation.pump_installation_depth_m\n\n design = design_borehole(\n log=inputs.log,\n static_water_level_m=swl,\n pump_intake_m=pump_intake,\n rules=config.design,\n screens_m=screens_m,\n )\n\n estimate = estimate_borehole_cost(\n inputs_from_design(\n design, mobilisation_distance_km=inputs.mobilisation_distance_km\n )\n )\n\n site = inputs.log.site\n payload: dict[str, Any] = {\n \"project\": inputs.name,\n \"site\": {\n \"community\": site.community,\n \"district\": site.district,\n \"chiefdom\": site.chiefdom,\n \"client\": site.client,\n \"boreholeRef\": inputs.log.borehole_ref,\n \"latlon\": list(site.latlon) if site.latlon else None,\n },\n \"section\": _section(inputs.log, design, analysis, config),\n \"design\": _design_decisions(design, analysis, config),\n \"costing\": _costing(estimate),\n \"quality\": None,\n \"edited\": screens_m is not None,\n }\n\n assessment = inputs.assessment\n if assessment is None and inputs.quality is not None:\n assessment = assess_sample(inputs.quality)\n if assessment is not None:\n payload[\"quality\"] = _quality(assessment)\n\n return payload\n"}, "groundwater/design/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Borehole design: construction plan generation and schematic drawing.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .designer import (\n AS_BUILT_NOTE,\n DESIGN_NOTE,\n BoreholeDesign,\n CasingSegment,\n design_borehole,\n logged_diameter_in,\n seal_depth_for,\n)\nfrom .drawing import draw_borehole_design\nfrom .lithology import (\n LITHOLOGY_CLASSES,\n LithologyClass,\n fracture_ranges,\n is_clayey,\n lithology_bands,\n lithology_class,\n)\n\n__all__ = [\n \"AS_BUILT_NOTE\",\n \"DESIGN_NOTE\",\n \"LITHOLOGY_CLASSES\",\n \"BoreholeDesign\",\n \"CasingSegment\",\n \"LithologyClass\",\n \"design_borehole\",\n \"draw_borehole_design\",\n \"fracture_ranges\",\n \"is_clayey\",\n \"lithology_bands\",\n \"lithology_class\",\n \"logged_diameter_in\",\n \"seal_depth_for\",\n]\n"}, "groundwater/design/designer.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Generate a borehole construction design from the available data.\n\nInputs are whatever exists at design time: the drilling log (lithology\nintervals, water strikes, total depth), the VES interpretation (water\nzones, recommended depth) when the hole is still to be drilled, the\nstatic water level and the pumping test results when available.\n\nThe rules follow common Sierra Leone practice and RWSN professional\ndrilling guidance and live in :class:`~groundwater.config.DesignRules`\nso they can be adjusted per client without touching code:\n\n* plain casing from surface, screens set against the aquifer zones,\n* screens kept below static water level by a configurable margin,\n* a sump of plain casing below the lowest screen,\n* gravel pack from the bottom to a margin above the top screen,\n* backfill above the gravel pack up to the sanitary seal,\n* cement sanitary seal from surface,\n* casing stick-up above ground.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom ..config import DesignRules\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, DrillingLog\nfrom ..ves.interpret import SiteInterpretation\nfrom .lithology import fracture_ranges, is_clayey\n\n# Lithology phrases that mark an interval as a screening target, and phrases\n# that negate it. Matching is on whole words/phrases so a description like\n# \"dry, no water struck\" is not screened just because it contains \"water\".\n_AQUIFER_WORDS = {\"fracture\", \"fractured\", \"fractures\", \"aquifer\"}\n_AQUIFER_PHRASES = (\"water-bearing\", \"water bearing\", \"waterbearing\",\n \"water strike\", \"water struck\", \"water inflow\")\n_NEGATION_PHRASES = (\"no water\", \"not reached\", \"without water\", \"water table not\")\n\n#: The annular fill a design carries, decided by the annulus the hole and\n#: casing leave: a filter pack needs 70 mm a side, anything can be placed\n#: past 50 mm, and under that nothing can be poured without bridging.\nANNULUS_PACK_MIN_MM = 50.0\nANNULUS_FILTER_MIN_MM = 70.0\n\n#: How construction was arrived at, printed under every drawing.\nDESIGN_NOTE = (\n \"Construction generated from the drilling log by the design rules. The \"\n \"log records no casing string, so this is a design, not an as-built record.\"\n)\nAS_BUILT_NOTE = (\n \"As built: the screens are those recorded as installed on the drilling \"\n \"log; the rest of the string follows the design rules.\"\n)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass CasingSegment:\n top_m: float\n bottom_m: float\n kind: str # \"plain\" | \"screen\" | \"sump\"\n\n @property\n def length_m(self) -> float:\n return self.bottom_m - self.top_m\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass BoreholeDesign:\n total_depth_m: float\n borehole_diameter_in: float\n casing_diameter_in: float\n casing_material: str\n segments: list[CasingSegment]\n gravel_pack: tuple[float, float]\n backfill: tuple[float, float]\n sanitary_seal: tuple[float, float]\n stickup_m: float\n screen_slot_mm: float\n water_strikes_m: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)\n static_water_level_m: float | None = None\n pump_intake_m: float | None = None\n design_basis: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n # \"gravel pack\" (a filter pack, 70 mm or more a side), \"formation\n # stabiliser\" (placeable but too thin to filter) or \"none\" (an annulus\n # nothing can be poured into). The drawing, the summary and the bill of\n # quantities all read this; a 19 mm annulus used to carry a 2-4 mm pack\n # on every one of them.\n annular_fill: str = \"gravel pack\"\n annular_fill_material: str = \"\"\n annulus_mm: float = 0.0\n # True when the screens are the ones recorded as installed on the log\n as_built: bool = False\n construction_note: str = DESIGN_NOTE\n\n @property\n def screens(self) -> list[CasingSegment]:\n return [s for s in self.segments if s.kind == \"screen\"]\n\n @property\n def total_screen_length_m(self) -> float:\n return sum(s.length_m for s in self.screens)\n\n @property\n def annular_fill_label(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"What the annulus below the seal holds, for a drawing or a table.\"\"\"\n if self.annular_fill == \"none\":\n return (f\"no gravel pack: the {self.annulus_mm:.0f} mm annulus is too \"\n \"thin to place one\")\n if self.annular_fill == \"formation stabiliser\":\n return (f\"formation stabiliser ({self.annular_fill_material}); the \"\n f\"{self.annulus_mm:.0f} mm annulus is too thin for a filter pack\")\n return f\"gravel pack ({self.annular_fill_material})\"\n\n def summary_rows(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n # depths print as written (14.5, not 14): the table used to round\n # 14.5 m to \"14\" beside a drawing that said 14.5\n rows = [\n (\"Total depth\", f\"{self.total_depth_m:g} m\"),\n (\"Drilled diameter\", f'{self.borehole_diameter_in:g}\"'),\n (\n \"Casing\",\n (f'{self.casing_diameter_in:g}\" {self.casing_material}, stick-up '\n f\"{self.stickup_m:g} m\"),\n ),\n (\n \"Screens\" + (\" (as installed)\" if self.as_built else \"\"),\n \"; \".join(f\"{s.top_m:g}-{s.bottom_m:g} m\" for s in self.screens)\n + f\" (slot {self.screen_slot_mm:g} mm)\",\n ),\n (\n \"Annular fill\",\n (f\"{self.gravel_pack[0]:g}-{self.gravel_pack[1]:g} m: \"\n f\"{self.annular_fill_label}\"),\n ),\n (\"Backfill\", f\"{self.backfill[0]:g}-{self.backfill[1]:g} m\"),\n (\n \"Sanitary seal\",\n f\"{self.sanitary_seal[0]:g}-{self.sanitary_seal[1]:g} m cement grout\",\n ),\n ]\n if self.static_water_level_m is not None:\n rows.append((\"Static water level\", f\"{self.static_water_level_m:.2f} m\"))\n if self.water_strikes_m:\n rows.append(\n (\"Water strikes\", \", \".join(f\"{w:g} m\" for w in self.water_strikes_m))\n )\n if self.pump_intake_m is not \"\"\"The drilled diameter the log records, from its diameter column.\n\n The deepest interval with a diameter is the production diameter; a\n hole reamed wider at the top is logged that way.\n \"\"\"\n if log is None:\n return None\n with_diameter = [iv for iv in log.intervals if iv.bit_diameter_in]\n if not with_diameter:\n return None\n return float(max(with_diameter, key=lambda iv: = math.ceil(max(top, floor) * 2.0) / 2.0\n bottom = math.floor(min(bottom, total_depth - rules.sump_length_m) * 2.0) / 2.0\n if bottom - top >= 1.0:\n clipped.append((top, bottom))\n return clipped\n\n basis = []\n strike_zones: list[tuple[float, float]] = []\n litho_zones: list[tuple[float, float]] = []\n named_zones: list[tuple[float, float]] = []\n named_text: list[str] = []\n fractured_intervals: list[str] = []\n excluded: list[str] = []\n kept_strikes: list[float] = []\n if log is not None:\n for strike in log.water_strikes_m:\n host = _interval_at(log, strike)\n reasons = []\n if host is not None and is_clayey(host.description):\n reasons.append(\n f\"it is in {host.description.lower()}, a seepage horizon that \"\n \"is cased and grouted off rather than screened\"\n \".join(reasons)\n )\n continue\n zone = (max(strike - 1.0, 0.0), strike + 5.0)\n if clip([zone]):\n strike_zones.append(zone)\n kept_strikes.append(strike)\n for interval in log.intervals:\n text = {interval.top_m:g}-{interval.bottom_m:g} m interval is not \"\n f\"screened: {interval.description.lower()} is clayey ground\"\n )\n continue\n # \"fracture zone 49-52 m\" on the 45-50 m row: the zone \".join(f\"{w:g} m\" for w in kept_strikes) + \")\"\n )\n if named_zones and clip(named_zones):\n basis.append(\n \"screens positioned against the fracture zones the log names (\"\n + \", \".join(named_text)\n + f\"), with {rules.fracture_zone_margin_m:g} m of screen either side\"\n )\n if litho_zones and clip(litho_zones):\n basis.append(\n \"screens positioned against the fractured = clip([(t, b) for t, b in interpretation.water_zones])\n if clipped:\n basis.append(\n \"screens positioned against the low resistivity zones of the VES \"\n \"interpretation (\"\n + \", \".join(f\"{int(t)}-{int(b)} m\" for t, b in interpretation.water_zones)\n + \")\"\n )\n clipped.sort()\n merged: list[tuple[float, float]] = []\n for zone in clipped:\n if merged and zone[0] <= total_depth_m=total_depth_m,\n borehole_diameter_in=bore_in,\n casing_diameter_in=rules.casing_diameter_in,\n casing_material=rules.casing_material,\n segments=segments,\n gravel_pack=gravel,\n backfill=backfill,\n sanitary_seal=seal,\n stickup_m=rules.stickup_m,\n screen_slot_mm=rules.screen_slot_mm,\n water_strikes_m=list(log.water_strikes_m) if log else [],\n static_water_level_m=swl,\n pump_intake_m=pump_intake_m,\n design_basis=basis,\n flags=flags,\n annular_fill=fill,\n annular_fill_material=material,\n annulus_mm=annulus_mm,\n as_built=as_built,\n construction_note=AS_BUILT_NOTE if as_built else DESIGN_NOTE,\n )\n"}, "groundwater/design/drawing.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"To-scale borehole design schematic.\n\nDraws the lithology column beside the construction column with a\nshared depth axis, in the layout of the contractor borehole record\nsheets: header block, formation profile on the left, borehole diagram\nwith annotated construction elements on the right, water strikes and\nstatic water level marked, and a legend.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport textwrap\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nfrom matplotlib.lines import Line2D\nfrom matplotlib.patches import Patch, Rectangle\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..models import DrillingLog\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\nfrom .designer import BoreholeDesign\nfrom .lithology import lithology_bands\n\n#: The annulus below the seal, by what the design says it holds.\n_FILL_STYLES = {\n \"gravel pack\": (\"#F0E3B2\", \"..\", \"gravel pack\"),\n \"formation stabiliser\": (\"#EAD9A8\", \".\", \"formation stabiliser\"),\n \"none\": (\"#F4F1EA\", \"\", \"no gravel pack (formation)\"),\n}\n\n\ndef _stack_labels(\n entries: list[tuple[float, ...]], min_gap: float, y_min: float, y_max: float\n) -> list[tuple[float, tuple]]:\n \"\"\"Place labels without overlap and inside the axis.\n\n Labels are sorted by their anchor depth, pushed down until they no\n longer collide, then pulled back up from the bottom so nothing\n ends up outside ``y_max``. Returns ``(label_y, entry)`` pairs.\n \"\"\"\n placed: list[tuple[float, tuple]] = []\n level = y_min\n for entry in sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e[0]):\n y = max(entry[0], level)\n placed.append((y, entry))\n level = y + min_gap\n limit = y_max\n for i in range(len(placed) - 1, -1, -1):\n y, entry = placed[i]\n if y > limit:\n y = limit\n placed[i] = (y, entry)\n limit = y - min_gap\n return placed\n\n\n_HEADER_LINE_CHARS = 88\n\n\ndef _header_lines(pairs) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"Header pairs packed into lines of at most ``_HEADER_LINE_CHARS``.\n\n A pair is never split; a single pair longer than the limit gets a line\n of its own (and is the contractor's problem to shorten).\n \"\"\"\n lines: list[str] = []\n current = \"\"\n for key, value in pairs:\n piece = f\"{key}: {value}\"\n joined = f\"{current} {piece}\" if current else piece\n if current and len(joined) > _HEADER_LINE_CHARS:\n lines.append(current)\n current = piece\n else:\n current = joined\n if current:\n lines.append(current)\n return lines\n\n\ndef draw_borehole_design(\n design: BoreholeDesign,\n log: DrillingLog | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n header_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Draw the design; returns the saved path (or the figure).\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n depth = design.total_depth_m\n stick = design.stickup_m\n y_top = -stick - 1.2 # air above ground\n\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, (ax_l, ax_c) = plt.subplots(\n 1, 2, figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 9.4), sharey=True,\n width_ratios=[1.0, 1.3],\n )\n for ax in (ax_l, ax_c):\n ax.set_ylim(depth + depth * 0.04, y_top)\n ax.grid(False)\n # no frame box: the old right/bottom spines ran through the\n # depth labels; the drawing carries its own outlines\n for side in (\"top\", \"right\", \"bottom\"):\n ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)\n ax_c.spines[\"left\"].set_visible(False)\n ax_c.tick_params(left=False, labelleft=False)\n # the depth axis ends at the bottom of the hole, not below it\n ax_l.spines[\"left\"].set_bounds(y_top, depth)\n\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n # left: lithology column\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n ax_l.set_xlim(0, 1.02)\n ax_l.set_xticks([])\n ax_l.set_ylabel(\"Depth (m)\")\n ax_l.set_title(\"Formation\", fontsize=10)\n litho_classes: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}\n if log is not None and log.intervals:\n litho_entries = []\n # one class table for every drawing, and a fracture zone the\n # driller named with its depths is drawn at those depths, not\n # hatched across the five metres it was logged on\n for top, bottom, klass in lithology_bands(log.intervals):\n if klass.label not in litho_classes:\n litho_classes[klass.label] = (klass.colour, klass.hatch)\n ax_l.add_patch(\n Rectangle(\n (0.06, top), 0.32, bottom - top,\n facecolor=klass.colour, hatch=klass.hatch,\n edgecolor=\"#555555\", lw=0.6,\n )\n )\n for interval in log.intervals:\n wrapped = textwrap.fill(interval.description, 26)\n mid = (interval.top_m + interval.bottom_m) / 2\n litho_entries.append((mid, wrapped))\n gap = depth / 26.0\n for label_y, (_mid, wrapped) in _stack_labels(\n litho_entries, gap, y_top + gap, depth + depth * 0.02\n ):\n ax_l.text(0.42, label_y, wrapped, fontsize=6.5, va=\"center\",\n linespacing=1.1)\n else:\n ax_l.text(0.5, depth / 2, \"no drilling log\", ha=\"center\", fontsize=9,\n color=\"#888888\")\n ax_l.axhline(0, color=\"#333333\", lw=1.2)\n ax_l.text(0.01, -0.6, \"GL\", fontsize=7, color=\"#333333\")\n\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n # right: construction column\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n ax_c.set_xlim(0, 1.16)\n ax_c.set_xticks([])\n ax_c.set_title(\"Construction\", fontsize=10)\n x_hole, w_hole = 0.30, 0.26\n x_case = x_hole + w_hole / 2 - 0.055\n w_case = 0.11\n\n # annulus fills\n seal_top, seal_bot = design.sanitary_seal\n back_top, back_bot = design.backfill\n grav_top, grav_bot = design.gravel_pack\n fill_style = _FILL_STYLES.get(design.annular_fill, _FILL_STYLES[\"gravel pack\"])\n for (top, bot), (color, hatch, _label) in (\n ((seal_top, seal_bot), (\"#B0B0B0\", \"//\", \"cement sanitary seal\")),\n ((back_top, back_bot), (\"#E0D5C0\", \"\", \"backfill\")),\n ((grav_top, grav_bot), fill_style),\n ):\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_hole, top), w_hole, bot - top, facecolor=color,\n hatch=hatch, edgecolor=\"#777777\", lw=0.5)\n )\n # borehole wall\n ax_c.plot([x_hole, x_hole], [0, depth], color=\"#333333\", lw=1.4)\n ax_c.plot([x_hole + w_hole, x_hole + w_hole], [0, depth], color=\"#333333\", lw=1.4)\n ax_c.plot([x_hole, x_hole + w_hole], [depth, depth], color=\"#333333\", lw=1.6)\n\n # the water standing in the casing: the reason the borehole exists,\n # and the quickest check that the screens are where the water is\n if design.static_water_level_m is not None:\n swl_m = design.static_water_level_m\n if swl_m < depth:\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_case, swl_m), w_case, depth - swl_m,\n facecolor=\"#CBE3F5\", edgecolor=\"none\", zorder=3)\n )\n\n # casing string\n for segment in design.segments:\n if segment.kind == \"screen\":\n face, hatch = \"none\", \"---\"\n edge = style.accent_color\n elif segment.kind == \"sump\":\n face, hatch = \"#D8D8D8\", \"\"\n edge = \"#333333\"\n else:\n face, hatch = \"none\", \"\"\n edge = \"#333333\"\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_case, segment.top_m), w_case,\n segment.bottom_m - segment.top_m,\n facecolor=face, hatch=hatch, edgecolor=edge, lw=1.0,\n zorder=5)\n )\n # headworks: the apron slab and plinth the casing comes up through,\n # so the top of the drawing is a wellhead and not a cut pipe\n apron_h = max(stick * 0.35, depth * 0.006)\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_hole - 0.10, -apron_h), w_hole + 0.20, apron_h,\n facecolor=\"#BEBBB2\", hatch=\"//\", edgecolor=\"#5C6360\",\n lw=0.6, zorder=4)\n )\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_case - 0.035, -stick * 0.72), w_case + 0.07,\n stick * 0.72, facecolor=\"#BEBBB2\", hatch=\"//\",\n edgecolor=\"#5C6360\", lw=0.6, zorder=4)\n )\n # stick-up and cap\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_case, -stick), w_case, stick, facecolor=\"white\",\n edgecolor=\"#333333\", lw=1.0, zorder=5)\n )\n ax_c.plot([x_case - 0.02, x_case + w_case + 0.02], [-stick, -stick],\n color=\"#333333\", lw=2.0, zorder=6)\n # bottom plug\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_case, depth - 0.6), w_case, 0.6, facecolor=\"#555555\",\n edgecolor=\"#333333\", zorder=6)\n )\n # ground line\n ax_c.axhline(0, color=\"#333333\", lw=1.2)\n\n # water level marker and strikes (labels join the right-hand\n # column below so nothing is written across the annulus)\n neutral = \"#999999\"\n annos: list[tuple[float, str, str]] = [] # (anchor depth, text, colour)\n if design.static_water_level_m is not None:\n swl = design.static_water_level_m\n ax_c.plot([x_case + w_case / 2], [swl], marker=\"v\", ms=8,\n color=style.accent_color, zorder=7)\n annos.append((swl, f\"SWL {swl:.2f} m\", style.accent_color))\n for strike in design.water_strikes_m:\n ax_c.annotate(\n \"\", xy=(x_hole, strike), xytext=(x_hole - 0.09, strike),\n arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle=\"->\", color=\"#2A6EBB\", lw=1.4),\n )\n # named for what it is: a bare \"12 m\" beside an arrow read as\n # anything from a casing joint to a sample depth\n ax_c.text(x_hole - 0.10, strike, f\"water strike\\n{strike:g} m\",\n fontsize=6.5, ha=\"right\", va=\"center\", color=\"#2A6EBB\",\n linespacing=1.0)\n if design.pump_intake_m is not None:\n y = design.pump_intake_m\n # the rising main from the headworks down to the pump, so the\n # intake reads as the bottom of a pump and not as a loose block\n main_w = w_case * 0.16\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_case + w_case / 2 - main_w / 2, -stick), main_w,\n y + stick, facecolor=\"#B7BDBB\", edgecolor=\"#5C6360\",\n lw=0.5, zorder=7)\n )\n pump_h = max(depth * 0.02, 0.8)\n ax_c.add_patch(\n Rectangle((x_case + w_case * 0.22, y - pump_h / 2),\n w_case * 0.56, pump_h * 2,\n facecolor=style.secondary_color, edgecolor=\"white\",\n lw=0.8, zorder=8)\n )\n # a design's pump is where the pump should go; only an as-built\n # record can say where one is\n annos.append((y, f\"pump intake {y:g} m\"\n + (\"\" if design.as_built else \" (recommended)\"),\n style.secondary_color))\n\n # right-hand annotations with depths\n screens = design.screens\n annos += [\n (seal_bot / 2 if seal_bot else 1.5,\n f\"cement grout 0-{seal_bot:g} m\", neutral),\n ((back_top + back_bot) / 2,\n f\"backfill {back_top:g}-{back_bot:g} m\", neutral),\n ((grav_top + min(grav_bot, depth)) / 2,\n f\"{fill_style[2]} {grav_top:g}-{grav_bot:g} m\", neutral),\n ]\n for s in screens:\n annos.append(((s.top_m + s.bottom_m) / 2,\n f\"screen {s.top_m:g}-{s.bottom_m:g} m\", neutral))\n sump = [s for s in design.segments if s.kind == \"sump\"]\n if sump:\n annos.append(((sump[0].top_m + sump[0].bottom_m) / 2,\n (f\"sump (sediment trap) \"\n f\"{sump[0].top_m:g}-{sump[0].bottom_m:g} m, \"\n f\"bottom plug at {depth:g} m\"),\n neutral))\n else:\n annos.append((depth - 0.3, f\"bottom plug at {depth:g} m\", neutral))\n x_text = x_hole + w_hole + 0.06\n min_gap = depth / 28.0\n for label_y, (anchor_y, text, color) in _stack_labels(\n annos, min_gap, y_top + min_gap, depth + depth * 0.02\n ):\n text_color = \"#444444\" if color == neutral else color\n ax_c.annotate(\n text, xy=(x_hole + w_hole, min(anchor_y, depth)),\n xytext=(x_text, label_y), fontsize=7.0, va=\"center\",\n color=text_color,\n arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle=\"-\", color=color, lw=0.7,\n shrinkA=2, shrinkB=1),\n )\n\n # scale ticks every 5 m on both axes\n ticks = np.arange(0, depth + 1, 5)\n for ax in (ax_l, ax_c):\n ax.set_yticks(ticks)\n\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n # legend: what each fill means, once, rather than a word on every band\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n handles: list = [\n Patch(facecolor=fill_style[0], hatch=fill_style[1], edgecolor=\"#777777\",\n label=fill_style[2]),\n Patch(facecolor=\"#E0D5C0\", edgecolor=\"#777777\", label=\"backfill\"),\n Patch(facecolor=\"#B0B0B0\", hatch=\"//\", edgecolor=\"#777777\",\n label=\"cement sanitary seal\"),\n Patch(facecolor=\"white\", edgecolor=\"#333333\", label=\"plain casing\"),\n Patch(facecolor=\"white\", hatch=\"---\", edgecolor=style.accent_color,\n label=\"screen\"),\n ]\n if any(seg.kind == \"sump\" for seg in design.segments):\n handles.append(\n Patch(facecolor=\"#D8D8D8\", edgecolor=\"#333333\", label=\"sump\")\n )\n if design.static_water_level_m is not None:\n handles.append(\n Patch(facecolor=\"#CBE3F5\", edgecolor=\"#7FB0DA\",\n label=\"water in the casing\")\n )\n if design.pump_intake_m is not None:\n handles.append(\n Line2D([], [], color=\"#B7BDBB\", lw=4, label=\"rising main\")\n )\n handles.append(\n Patch(facecolor=style.secondary_color, edgecolor=\"white\",\n label=\"pump\")\n )\n for klass, (color, hatch) in litho_classes.items():\n handles.append(\n Patch(facecolor=color, hatch=hatch, edgecolor=\"#555555\",\n label=klass.lower())\n )\n legend_cols = 4\n legend_rows = (len(handles) + legend_cols - 1) // legend_cols\n legend_space = 0.022 * legend_rows + 0.03\n fig.legend(handles=handles, loc=\"lower center\", ncol=legend_cols,\n fontsize=7, frameon=False,\n bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.004))\n\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n # title and header block\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n fig.suptitle(\n title or (\"As-built borehole record\" if design.as_built else \"Borehole design\"),\n fontsize=12, fontweight=\"bold\", color=style.accent_color,\n )\n header_pairs = list(header_pairs or [])\n header_pairs.append((\n \"Construction\",\n (f'{design.borehole_diameter_in:g}\" hole, '\n f'{design.casing_diameter_in:g}\" {design.casing_material}'),\n ))\n # what the drawing is: the log records no casing string, so a\n # drawing built by the rules says so on its own face\n header_pairs.append((\n \"Drawing\", \"as built\" if design.as_built else \"design generated from the log\",\n ))\n # The header is laid out in rows that fit the canvas. One long line\n # does not clip: save_figure uses bbox_inches=\"tight\", which grows the\n # canvas sideways to fit it, and the completion report's drawing came\n # out a third narrower than the handover's for the same borehole.\n header_lines = _header_lines(header_pairs)\n for i, line in enumerate(header_lines):\n fig.text(0.5, 0.948 - 0.018 * i, line, ha=\"center\", fontsize=8,\n color=\"#444444\")\n header_space = 0.018 * max(len(header_lines) - 1, 0)\n fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, legend_space, 1, 0.94 - header_space))\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n"}, "groundwater/design/lithology.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"One reading of the driller's words, shared by every drawing.\n\nThe borehole drawing, the browser drawing and the Depth Spine each kept\ntheir own table of lithology keywords, so the same log was \"clay\" on one\nfigure, \"clay and saprolite\" on another and \"fresh basement\" on a third\nfor an interval the driller had called slightly weathered granite. This\nmodule is the one table. A description is matched against the classes in\norder and the first match wins, except that a fracture zone named with a\ndepth range inside a longer interval (\"Light colour granite, fracture zone\n49-52 m\") is a band of its own: the range is the fracture zone, the rest\nof the interval is the rock it is in, and the drawing used to hatch the\nwhole five metres.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom ..models import LithologyInterval\n\n_RANGE = r\"(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*(?:-|\u2013|to)\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*m\\b\"\n\n#: \"fracture zone 49-52 m\", \"fractured 60-62 m\", \"fractures at 30-31 m\":\n#: a depth range named against a fracture phrase.\nFRACTURE_RANGE_RE = re.compile(\n r\"fracture[ds]?\\s*(?:zones?)?\\s*(?:at|from|between)?\\s*\" + _RANGE,\n re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n#: Any depth range written into a description.\nANY_RANGE_RE = re.compile(_RANGE, re.IGNORECASE)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass LithologyClass:\n key: str\n label: str\n colour: str\n hatch: str\n\n\n#: In matching order. The regexes are applied to the lowercased description.\nLITHOLOGY_CLASSES: tuple[tuple[LithologyClass, re.Pattern], ...] = tuple(\n (LithologyClass(key, label, colour, hatch), re.compile(pattern))\n for key, label, colour, hatch, pattern in (\n (\"fracture\", \"Fracture zone\", \"#9FB6CD\", \"xx\", r\"fracture|fissure\"),\n (\"topsoil\", \"Topsoil\", \"#8B5A2B\", \"\", r\"topsoil|top soil\"),\n (\"laterite\", \"Laterite\", \"#C4703E\", \"\", r\"laterit|duricrust\"),\n (\"saprolite\", \"Saprolite\", \"#D2B48C\", \"..\", r\"saprolit|regolith\"),\n (\"clay\", \"Clay\", \"#B8860B\", \"--\", r\"\\bclay\"),\n (\"sand\", \"Sand and gravel\", \"#E8D8A0\", \"..\", r\"\\bsand|gravel\"),\n (\"weathered\", \"Weathered rock\", \"#A98F63\", \"//\", r\"weather\"),\n (\"basement\", \"Basement rock\", \"#A9A9A9\", \"++\",\n r\"granite|gneiss|schist|basement|bedrock|\\brock\\b|fresh\"),\n )\n)\n\nOTHER = LithologyClass(\"other\", \"Other material\", \"#CCCCCC\", \"\")\n\n#: Words that make an interval clayey ground: a seepage in it is cased and\n#: grouted off, not screened, whatever the strike column says.\nCLAYEY_RE = re.compile(r\"\\bclay|laterit|topsoil|top soil\")\n\n\ndef lithology_class(description: str) -> LithologyClass:\n \"\"\"The class of a description as a whole.\"\"\"\n text = (description or \"\").lower()\n for klass, pattern in LITHOLOGY_CLASSES:\n if pattern.search(text):\n return klass\n return OTHER\n\n\ndef is_clayey(description: str) -> bool:\n return bool(CLAYEY_RE.search((description or \"\").lower()))\n\n\ndef fracture_ranges(description: str) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:\n \"\"\"Depth ranges a description names as fractured, in metres.\"\"\"\n out = []\n for match in FRACTURE_RANGE_RE.finditer(description or \"\"):\n top, bottom = float(match.group(1)), float(match.group(2))\n if bottom < top:\n top, bottom = bottom, top\n if bottom > top:\n out.append((top, bottom))\n return out\n\n\ndef host_description(description: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"The description with its named fracture ranges taken out.\n\n \"Light colour granite, fracture zone 49-52 m\" -> \"Light colour granite\",\n so the rock around a named zone is classed as what it is.\n \"\"\"\n text = FRACTURE_RANGE_RE.sub(\"\", description or \"\")\n return re.sub(r\"[\\s,;]+$\", \"\", text).strip(\" ,;\")\n\n\ndef lithology_bands(\n intervals: list[LithologyInterval] | LithologyInterval,\n) -> list[tuple[float, float, LithologyClass]]:\n \"\"\"The log split into bands, each with its class.\n\n A fracture zone named with its depths is a band of its own wherever\n those depths fall, which is not always the row it was written on: the\n driller logs \"fracture zone 60-62 m\" against the 55-60 m interval he was\n drilling when he saw it. The rest of every interval is the rock the\n description names once the zone is taken out of it. Pass one interval\n to band it alone (the named zones of the others are then unknown).\n \"\"\"\n if isinstance(intervals, LithologyInterval):\n intervals = [intervals]\n named = sorted(\n zone for interval in intervals for zone in fracture_ranges(interval.description)\n )\n fracture = lithology_class(\"fracture\")\n bands: list[tuple[float, float, LithologyClass]] = []\n for interval in sorted(intervals, key=lambda iv: iv.top_m):\n top, bottom = float(interval.top_m), float(interval.bottom_m)\n # the host rock: the description without the zone it names, so\n # \"Light colour granite, fracture zone 49-52 m\" is granite here\n host = lithology_class(\n host_description(interval.description)\n if fracture_ranges(interval.description) else interval.description\n )\n cursor = top\n for t, b in named:\n t, b = max(t, top), min(b, bottom)\n if b <= max(t, cursor):\n continue\n if t > cursor:\n bands.append((cursor, t, host))\n bands.append((max(t, cursor), b, fracture))\n cursor = b\n if cursor < bottom:\n bands.append((cursor, bottom, host))\n return bands\n"}, "groundwater/extraction/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Scanned field sheet extraction workflow.\n\nTurns scanned field sheets and PDFs into the standard data templates\nwith low-confidence values flagged for manual review.\n\nTwo extraction paths share one output structure\n(:class:`~groundwater.extraction.models.ExtractedDocument`):\n\n* :func:`extract_pdf_text` - rule based, for PDFs with a text layer\n (no API key needed).\n* :class:`ClaudeExtractor` - AI assisted, for photos and scans\n (requires ``pip install groundwater-toolkit[ai]`` and an Anthropic\n API key).\n\nBoth feed :func:`write_review_workbook`, which produces an Excel\nreview file with uncertain cells highlighted, and (for recognised\ndocument kinds) a filled standard template ready for the parsers.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom .models import ExtractedDocument, ExtractedField, ExtractedTable, UncertainCell\nfrom .pdf_text import extract_pdf_text\nfrom .review import write_review_workbook, fill_ves_template\n\n__all__ = [\n \"ExtractedDocument\",\n \"ExtractedField\",\n \"ExtractedTable\",\n \"UncertainCell\",\n \"extract_pdf_text\",\n \"write_review_workbook\",\n \"fill_ves_template\",\n \"ClaudeExtractor\",\n]\n\n\ndef __getattr__(name):\n if name == \"ClaudeExtractor\":\n from .claude import ClaudeExtractor\n\n return ClaudeExtractor\n raise AttributeError(name)\n"}, "groundwater/extraction/claude.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"AI assisted extraction of scanned field sheets with Claude.\n\nSends the scan (image or PDF) to the Claude API and gets back the\nheader fields and data tables as structured JSON with a confidence per\nvalue, which feeds the same review workflow as the rule based path.\n\nRequires the optional dependency (``pip install\ngroundwater-toolkit[ai]``) and an Anthropic API key (the SDK reads\n``ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`` from the environment).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport base64\nimport json\nimport mimetypes\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .models import (\n ExtractedDocument,\n ExtractedField,\n ExtractedTable,\n UncertainCell,\n)\n\n_MODEL = \"claude-opus-5\"\n\n_SCHEMA = {\n \"type\": \"object\",\n \"properties\": {\n \"document_kind\": {\n \"type\": \"string\",\n \"enum\": [\"ves\", \"pumping_test\", \"drilling_log\", \"water_quality\", \"unknown\"],\n },\n \"header\": {\n \"type\": \"array\",\n \"items\": {\n \"type\": \"object\",\n \"properties\": {\n \"name\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n \"value\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n \"confidence\": {\n \"type\": \"number\",\n \"description\": \"0 to 1; below 0.85 means needs manual review\",\n },\n },\n \"required\": [\"name\", \"value\", \"confidence\"],\n \"additionalProperties\": False,\n },\n },\n \"tables\": {\n \"type\": \"array\",\n \"items\": {\n \"type\": \"object\",\n \"properties\": {\n \"title\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n \"columns\": {\"type\": \"array\", \"items\": {\"type\": \"string\"}},\n \"rows\": {\n \"type\": \"array\",\n \"items\": {\"type\": \"array\", \"items\": {\"type\": \"string\"}},\n },\n },\n \"required\": [\"title\", \"columns\", \"rows\"],\n \"additionalProperties\": False,\n },\n },\n \"uncertain_cells\": {\n \"type\": \"array\",\n \"items\": {\n \"type\": \"object\",\n \"properties\": {\n \"table_index\": {\"type\": \"integer\"},\n \"row\": {\"type\": \"integer\"},\n \"column\": {\"type\": \"integer\"},\n \"reason\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n },\n \"required\": [\"table_index\", \"row\", \"column\", \"reason\"],\n \"additionalProperties\": False,\n },\n },\n \"notes\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n },\n \"required\": [\"document_kind\", \"header\", \"tables\", \"uncertain_cells\", \"notes\"],\n \"additionalProperties\": False,\n}\n\n_PROMPT = \"\"\"You are transcribing a groundwater field data sheet from Sierra Leone\n(vertical electrical sounding, pumping test, drilling log or water quality\nlaboratory sheet).\n\nExtract:\n1. document_kind: which sheet type this is.\n2. header: every label/value pair from the header block (community, client,\n district, date, borehole reference, static water level, GPS coordinates,\n elevation, supervisor and so on). Use the label wording from the sheet.\n3. tables: every data table, with its column headings and every row, in\n order. Transcribe numbers exactly as written, including leading zeros\n (for example 078.7). Do not invent values for illegible cells; write an\n empty string and flag the cell.\n4. uncertain_cells: every table cell you are not fully certain about\n (handwriting hard to read, smudges, ambiguous digits), with a short\n reason. Indices are zero based; row counts data rows only.\n5. Give each header field a confidence between 0 and 1. Use values below\n 0.85 whenever a reasonable person could read the handwriting differently.\n\nAccuracy matters more than completeness: flag anything doubtful rather than\nguessing silently.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass ClaudeExtractor:\n \"\"\"Extract field sheet content from scans using the Claude API.\"\"\"\n\n def __init__(self, model: str = _MODEL, api_key: str | None = None):\n try:\n import anthropic\n except ImportError as exc:\n raise ImportError(\n \"AI extraction needs the anthropic SDK; install with \"\n \"'pip install groundwater-toolkit[ai]'\"\n ) from exc\n self._anthropic = anthropic\n self.model = model\n self.client = (\n anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=api_key) if api_key else anthropic.Anthropic()\n )\n\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n def extract(self, path: str | Path) -> ExtractedDocument:\n \"\"\"Extract a scanned sheet (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or PDF).\"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n media_type = mimetypes.guess_type(path.name)[0] or \"application/pdf\"\n data = base64.standard_b64encode(path.read_bytes()).decode(\"utf-8\")\n\n if media_type == \"application/pdf\":\n source_block = {\n \"type\": \"document\",\n \"source\": {\n \"type\": \"base64\",\n \"media_type\": \"application/pdf\",\n \"data\": data,\n },\n }\n elif media_type.startswith(\"image/\"):\n source_block = {\n \"type\": \"image\",\n \"source\": {\"type\": \"base64\", \"media_type\": media_type, \"data\": data},\n }\n else:\n raise ValueError(f\"Unsupported file type for extraction: {media_type}\")\n\n response = self.client.messages.create(\n model=self.model,\n max_tokens=16000,\n thinking={\"type\": \"adaptive\"},\n output_config={\"format\": {\"type\": \"json_schema\", \"schema\": _SCHEMA}},\n messages=[\n {\n \"role\": \"user\",\n \"content\": [source_block, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": _PROMPT}],\n }\n ],\n )\n if response.stop_reason == \"refusal\":\n raise RuntimeError(\n \"The extraction request was declined by the model; check the \"\n \"document content.\"\n )\n # A refusal leaves content empty, and hitting the output cap can leave\n # only thinking blocks; either way there is no transcription to parse,\n # and a bare StopIteration would say nothing about why.\n text = next((b.text for b in response.content if b.type == \"text\"), None)\n if text is None:\n raise RuntimeError(\n \"The model returned no transcription \"\n f\"(stop reason: {response.stop_reason}). Try a clearer scan.\"\n )\n payload = json.loads(text)\n return self._to_document(payload, str(path))\n\n # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n @staticmethod\n def _to_document(payload: dict, source: str) -> ExtractedDocument:\n header = [\n ExtractedField(\n name=f.get(\"name\", \"\"),\n value=f.get(\"value\", \"\"),\n confidence=float(f.get(\"confidence\", 0.5)),\n )\n for f in payload.get(\"header\", [])\n ]\n tables = [\n ExtractedTable(\n title=t.get(\"title\", f\"Table {i + 1}\"),\n columns=[str(c) for c in t.get(\"columns\", [])],\n rows=[[str(c) for c in row] for row in t.get(\"rows\", [])],\n )\n for i, t in enumerate(payload.get(\"tables\", []))\n ]\n uncertain = [\n UncertainCell(\n table_index=int(c.get(\"table_index\", 0)),\n row=int(c.get(\"row\", 0)),\n column=int(c.get(\"column\", 0)),\n reason=c.get(\"reason\", \"\"),\n )\n for c in payload.get(\"uncertain_cells\", [])\n ]\n return ExtractedDocument(\n source=source,\n document_kind=payload.get(\"document_kind\", \"unknown\"),\n header=header,\n tables=tables,\n uncertain_cells=uncertain,\n notes=payload.get(\"notes\", \"\"),\n extractor=\"claude\",\n )\n"}, "groundwater/extraction/models.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Common structure for extracted field sheet content.\n\nWhatever the source (text PDF, photographed sheet, AI extraction),\nthe result is header fields plus data tables, each value carrying a\nconfidence in [0, 1]. Values below the review threshold are flagged\nand highlighted in the review workbook rather than silently accepted.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nREVIEW_THRESHOLD = 0.85\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ExtractedField:\n name: str\n value: str\n confidence: float = 1.0\n\n @property\n def needs_review(self) -> bool:\n return self.confidence < REVIEW_THRESHOLD\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass UncertainCell:\n table_index: int\n row: int # 0-based data row\n column: int # 0-based column\n reason: str = \"\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ExtractedTable:\n title: str\n columns: list[str]\n rows: list[list[str]]\n row_confidence: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n def confidence_for_row(self, index: int) -> float:\n if index < len(self.row_confidence):\n return self.row_confidence[index]\n return 1.0\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ExtractedDocument:\n source: str\n document_kind: str = \"unknown\" # ves | pumping_test | drilling_log | water_quality | unknown\n header: list[ExtractedField] = field(default_factory=list)\n tables: list[ExtractedTable] = field(default_factory=list)\n uncertain_cells: list[UncertainCell] = field(default_factory=list)\n notes: str = \"\"\n extractor: str = \"\" # \"pdf-text\" | \"claude\"\n\n def get(self, name: str) -> str:\n key = name.strip().lower()\n for f in self.header:\n if f.name.strip().lower() == key:\n return f.value\n return \"\"\n\n @property\n def review_items(self) -> list[str]:\n items = [\n f\"header field '{f.name}' = '{f.value}' (confidence {f.confidence:.2f})\"\n for f in self.header\n if f.needs_review\n ]\n for cell in self.uncertain_cells:\n if cell.table_index < len(self.tables):\n table = self.tables[cell.table_index]\n value = \"\"\n if cell.row < len(table.rows) and cell.column < len(table.rows[cell.row]):\n value = table.rows[cell.row][cell.column]\n items.append(\n f\"table '{table.title}' row {cell.row + 1}, column \"\n f\"'{table.columns[cell.column] if cell.column < len(table.columns) else cell.column + 1}'\"\n f\" = '{value}'\" + (f\" ({cell.reason})\" if cell.reason else \"\")\n )\n return items\n"}, "groundwater/extraction/pdf_text.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Rule based extraction from PDFs that carry a text layer.\n\nUses pdfplumber (``pip install groundwater-toolkit[extract]``) to pull\nwords and tables, then matches header labels with the same canonical\npatterns the template parsers use. Clean numeric parses get full\nconfidence; anything ambiguous is flagged for review. Image-only scans\nyield no text here and should go through the AI extractor instead.\n\nTwo things a field sheet does that a naive reader gets wrong, and which\nthis module handles from word positions rather than from the page's\nline art:\n\n* **Header pairs run together.** ``extract_text()`` collapses the wide\n gap between two columns to a single space, so ``Community: Rokel``\n beside ``Client: Living Water International`` reads as one label with\n the other's text glued onto its value. Lines are rebuilt here from\n word coordinates, and a gap wide enough to be a column break is\n written as one, so the two are read as two fields.\n\n* **Tables without ruling lines are invisible.** ``extract_tables()``\n finds a table by the rules drawn around it. A typed sheet very often\n has none - the columns are held by whitespace alone. Where that\n happens the table is found from the layout instead: a run of\n consecutive lines sharing a column structure. Ruled tables still go\n through pdfplumber, which is better at them.\n\nThe browser reader in ``docs/js/gwt-core.js`` does the same job with the\nsame algorithm, so a sheet read in either place gives the same tables.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Iterable, Optional\n\nfrom ..ingestion.common import match_label, split_inline_value\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\nfrom .models import (\n ExtractedDocument,\n ExtractedField,\n ExtractedTable,\n UncertainCell,\n)\n\n_KIND_MARKERS = {\n \"ves\": (\"ves\", \"schlumberger\", \"apparent resistivity\", \"sounding\"),\n \"pumping_test\": (\"pumping test\", \"step test\", \"constant discharge\", \"drawdown\"),\n \"drilling_log\": (\"drilling\", \"borehole log\", \"penetration\"),\n \"water_quality\": (\"water quality\", \"laboratory\", \"parameter\", \"guideline\"),\n}\n\n#: Horizontal gap, in points, that reads as a column break rather than a\n#: word space. About three characters at 10 pt.\n_COLUMN_GAP_PT = 14.0\n\n#: How far apart two word starts can be and still be the same column.\n_COLUMN_TOLERANCE_PT = 8.0\n\n\ndef _guess_kind(text: str) -> str:\n text = text.lower()\n scores = {\n kind: sum(1 for marker in markers if marker in text)\n for kind, markers in _KIND_MARKERS.items()\n }\n best = max(scores, key=scores.get)\n return best if scores[best] > 0 else \"unknown\"\n\n\ndef extract_pdf_text(path: str | Path) -> ExtractedDocument:\n \"\"\"Extract header fields and tables from a text-layer PDF.\"\"\"\n try:\n import pdfplumber\n except ImportError as exc:\n raise ImportError(\n \"PDF extraction needs pdfplumber; install with \"\n \"'pip install groundwater-toolkit[extract]'\"\n ) from exc\n\n path = Path(path)\n header: list[ExtractedField] = []\n tables: list[ExtractedTable] = []\n uncertain: list[UncertainCell] = []\n all_text: list[str] = []\n seen_fields: set[str] = set()\n\n with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:\n for page in pdf.pages:\n lines = _page_lines(page)\n all_text.append(\"\\n\".join(_line_text(line) for line in lines))\n\n # header labels from text lines (\"Community: Rokel Date: ...\")\n header_lines: list[int] = []\n for position, line in enumerate(lines):\n matched = False\n for part in _split_line(_line_text(line)):\n label, value = split_inline_value(part)\n key = match_label(label)\n if not key or not value:\n continue\n matched = True\n if key in seen_fields:\n continue\n seen_fields.add(key)\n header.append(ExtractedField(key, clean_text(value), 0.95))\n if matched:\n header_lines.append(position)\n\n # Ruled tables are pdfplumber's job; it is better at them than a\n # column-clustering pass, which cannot see a merged cell.\n found = [_clean_table(raw) for raw in page.extract_tables() or []]\n candidates = [t for t in found if t is not None]\n if not candidates:\n candidates = _tables_from_lines(lines, set(header_lines))\n\n for columns, rows in candidates:\n index = len(tables)\n confidences = []\n for r, row in enumerate(rows):\n row_conf = 1.0\n for c, cell in enumerate(row):\n conf, reason = _cell_confidence(\n cell, columns[c] if c < len(columns) else \"\"\n )\n if conf < 1.0:\n uncertain.append(UncertainCell(index, r, c, reason))\n row_conf = min(row_conf, conf)\n confidences.append(row_conf)\n tables.append(\n ExtractedTable(\n title=f\"Table {index + 1}\",\n columns=columns,\n rows=rows,\n row_confidence=confidences,\n )\n )\n\n text_blob = \"\\n\".join(all_text)\n return ExtractedDocument(\n source=str(path),\n document_kind=_guess_kind(text_blob),\n header=header,\n tables=tables,\n uncertain_cells=uncertain,\n extractor=\"pdf-text\",\n notes=\"Rule based extraction from the PDF text layer.\",\n )\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------- page layout\n\n#: A word as this module needs it: the text and where it starts and ends.\n_Word = dict[str, Any]\n_Line = list[_Word]\n\n\ndef _page_lines(page) -> list[_Line]:\n \"\"\"Words grouped into lines, in reading order.\n\n ``extract_words`` returns words with coordinates but no line\n structure. Words are grouped by their vertical position, with a\n tolerance drawn from the word's own height so a large heading and\n small body text are each grouped at their own scale.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n words = page.extract_words(use_text_flow=False, keep_blank_chars=False)\n except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 # pragma: no cover\n # Not a page with no text layer - that one raises nothing and\n # simply yields no words. What reaches here is a content stream\n # pdfplumber could not parse, and returning [] leaves it looking\n # blank. One unreadable page must not cost the other nine, so it\n # stays a skip until the reader has a flag channel to say so.\n return []\n\n lines: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n for word in words:\n text = clean_text(word.get(\"text\", \"\"))\n if not text:\n continue\n top = float(word.get(\"top\", 0.0))\n height = max(float(word.get(\"bottom\", top)) - top, 1.0)\n tolerance = max(height * 0.5, 2.0)\n for line in lines:\n if abs(line[\"top\"] - top) <= tolerance:\n line[\"words\"].append(\n {\"text\": text, \"x0\": float(word.get(\"x0\", 0.0)),\n \"x1\": float(word.get(\"x1\", 0.0))}\n )\n break\n else:\n lines.append({\n \"top\": top,\n \"words\": [{\"text\": text, \"x0\": float(word.get(\"x0\", 0.0)),\n \"x1\": float(word.get(\"x1\", 0.0))}],\n })\n\n lines.sort(key=lambda line: line[\"top\"])\n out: list[_Line] = []\n for line in lines:\n line[\"words\"].sort(key=lambda w: w[\"x0\"])\n out.append(line[\"words\"])\n return out\n\n\ndef _line_text(line: _Line) -> str:\n \"\"\"A line as text, with column breaks written as three spaces.\n\n That is the shape ``_split_line`` reads, and it is the piece\n ``extract_text()`` throws away.\n \"\"\"\n parts: list[str] = []\n for i, word in enumerate(line):\n if i == 0:\n parts.append(word[\"text\"])\n continue\n gap = word[\"x0\"] - line[i - 1][\"x1\"]\n parts.append((\" \" if gap > _COLUMN_GAP_PT else \" \") + word[\"text\"])\n return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _tables_from_lines(\n lines: list[_Line], header_lines: set[int]\n) -> list[tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]]:\n \"\"\"Tables from the layout, for sheets with no ruling lines.\n\n A run of consecutive multi-word lines that share a column structure\n is a table. The first line of the run is its header row.\n \"\"\"\n tables: list[tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]] = []\n run: list[_Line] = []\n\n def flush() -> None:\n nonlocal run\n if len(run) >= 3:\n columns = _column_positions(run)\n if len(columns) >= 2:\n grid = [_to_cells(line, columns) for line in run]\n header, rows = grid[0], grid[1:]\n if rows:\n tables.append((header, rows))\n run = []\n\n for position, line in enumerate(lines):\n # The header block is a two-column layout too, but its lines are\n # label/value pairs already read as header fields; folding them into\n # the reading table would put \"Community: Rokel\" where an AB/2\n # spacing belongs.\n if len(line) >= 2 and position not in header_lines:\n run.append(line)\n else:\n flush()\n flush()\n return tables\n\n\ndef _column_positions(lines: list[_Line]) -> list[float]:\n \"\"\"Column edges: word start positions that recur down the block.\"\"\"\n starts = sorted(word[\"x0\"] for line in lines for word in line)\n clusters: list[dict[str, float]] = []\n for x in starts:\n if clusters and x - clusters[-1][\"at\"] <= _COLUMN_TOLERANCE_PT:\n clusters[-1][\"n\"] += 1\n clusters[-1][\"at\"] = (clusters[-1][\"at\"] + x) / 2\n continue\n clusters.append({\"at\": x, \"n\": 1})\n threshold = max(2, len(lines) // 2)\n return [c[\"at\"] for c in clusters if c[\"n\"] >= threshold]\n\n\ndef _to_cells(line: _Line, columns: list[float]) -> list[str]:\n cells = [\"\"] * len(columns)\n for word in line:\n index = 0\n for i, edge in enumerate(columns):\n if word[\"x0\"] >= edge - _COLUMN_TOLERANCE_PT:\n index = i\n cells[index] = f'{cells[index]} {word[\"text\"]}' if cells[index] else word[\"text\"]\n return cells\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ grading\n\n\ndef _split_line(line: str) -> list[str]:\n return [p for p in re.split(r\"\\t+|\\s{3,}\", line) if p.strip()]\n\n\ndef _clean_table(raw: Iterable[Iterable]) -> Optional[tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]]:\n rows = [[clean_text(c) for c in row] for row in raw if any(clean_text(c) for c in row)]\n if len(rows) < 2:\n return None\n return rows[0], rows[1:]\n\n\ndef _cell_confidence(cell: str, column: str) -> tuple[float, str]:\n \"\"\"Numeric columns should parse as numbers; empty cells in numeric\n columns and non-numeric junk are review items.\"\"\"\n numeric_column = any(\n marker in column.lower()\n for marker in (\"(m)\", \"m)\", \"ohm\", \"rate\", \"level\", \"depth\", \"time\", \"value\", \"ab/2\", \"mn\")\n )\n if not numeric_column:\n return 1.0, \"\"\n if cell == \"\":\n return 0.6, \"empty cell in a numeric column\"\n if parse_number(cell) is None:\n return 0.4, \"does not parse as a number\"\n return 1.0, \"\"\n"}, "groundwater/extraction/review.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Review workbook generation for extracted documents.\n\nEvery extraction produces a review workbook: the header fields and\nevery table, with uncertain values highlighted amber and a Review\nsheet listing everything that needs checking. For recognised VES\nsheets the standard template can also be filled directly so the normal\nparsers pick the data up after review.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom openpyxl import Workbook, load_workbook\nfrom openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill\n\nfrom ..ingestion.common import match_label\nfrom .models import REVIEW_THRESHOLD, ExtractedDocument\n\n_AMBER = PatternFill(\"solid\", fgColor=\"FFE08A\")\n_HEADER_FONT = Font(bold=True)\n\n\ndef write_review_workbook(document: ExtractedDocument, path: str | Path) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Write the extraction to an Excel review workbook.\n\n Sheet 1 (Header): field, value, confidence; low confidence rows\n highlighted. One sheet per table with uncertain cells highlighted.\n Final Review sheet lists every flagged item with its reason.\n \"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n wb = Workbook()\n\n ws = wb.active\n ws.title = \"Header\"\n ws.append([\"Field\", \"Value\", \"Confidence\"])\n for cell in ws[1]:\n cell.font = _HEADER_FONT\n for field in document.header:\n ws.append([field.name, field.value, round(field.confidence, 2)])\n if field.needs_review:\n for cell in ws[ws.max_row]:\n cell.fill = _AMBER\n ws.column_dimensions[\"A\"].width = 28\n ws.column_dimensions[\"B\"].width = 32\n\n flagged = {(c.table_index, c.row, c.column): c.reason for c in document.uncertain_cells}\n for index, table in enumerate(document.tables):\n sheet = wb.create_sheet(f\"Table {index + 1}\"[:31])\n sheet.append([table.title])\n sheet[\"A1\"].font = _HEADER_FONT\n sheet.append(table.columns)\n for cell in sheet[2]:\n cell.font = _HEADER_FONT\n for r, row in enumerate(table.rows):\n sheet.append(row)\n for c in range(len(row)):\n if (index, r, c) in flagged:\n sheet.cell(row=sheet.max_row, column=c + 1).fill = _AMBER\n if table.confidence_for_row(r) < REVIEW_THRESHOLD:\n for c in range(len(row)):\n sheet.cell(row=sheet.max_row, column=c + 1).fill = _AMBER\n\n review = wb.create_sheet(\"Review\")\n review.append([\"Items needing manual review\"])\n review[\"A1\"].font = _HEADER_FONT\n items = document.review_items\n if items:\n for item in items:\n review.append([item])\n else:\n review.append([\"None: all values extracted with high confidence.\"])\n review.append([])\n review.append([f\"Source: {document.source}\"])\n review.append([f\"Extractor: {document.extractor}\"])\n review.append([f\"Document kind: {document.document_kind}\"])\n if document.notes:\n review.append([f\"Notes: {document.notes}\"])\n review.column_dimensions[\"A\"].width = 100\n\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n wb.save(path)\n return path\n\n\ndef fill_ves_template(document: ExtractedDocument, path: str | Path) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Fill the standard VES template from an extracted VES sheet.\n\n Header fields are mapped through the same label patterns the\n parsers use; the first table supplies the readings. Values that\n need review keep their amber highlight in the filled template.\n \"\"\"\n from ..ingestion.templates import write_ves_template\n\n if document.document_kind != \"ves\":\n raise ValueError(\"fill_ves_template needs a document of kind 'ves'\")\n if not document.tables:\n raise ValueError(\"No data table was extracted\")\n\n table = document.tables[0]\n path = Path(path)\n write_ves_template(path, n_soundings=1, n_rows=max(len(table.rows), 18))\n wb = load_workbook(path)\n ws = wb.active\n\n # header mapping: canonical key -> template value cell\n cell_map = {\n \"client\": \"B2\", \"community\": \"D2\",\n \"project\": \"B3\", \"sounding_id\": \"D3\",\n \"district\": \"B4\", \"easting\": \"D4\",\n \"date\": \"B5\", \"northing\": \"D5\",\n \"supervisor\": \"B6\", \"elevation_m\": \"D6\",\n \"chiefdom\": \"B7\", \"utm_zone\": \"D7\",\n \"array_type\": \"B8\", \"instrument\": \"D8\",\n }\n for field in document.header:\n # The AI extractor names a field the way the sheet does (\"Sounding\n # Number\"), which the label patterns resolve. The text-layer extractor\n # has already resolved it, so its name is the canonical key itself -\n # and a canonical key does not match its own pattern (\"sounding_id\" is\n # not \"sounding number\"). Accept either, or the field silently fails\n # to land in the template.\n key = field.name if field.name in cell_map else match_label(field.name)\n target = cell_map.get(key or \"\")\n if target:\n ws[target] = field.value\n if field.needs_review:\n ws[target].fill = _AMBER\n\n flagged = {\n (c.row, c.column): c.reason\n for c in document.uncertain_cells\n if c.table_index == 0\n }\n # locate the AB/2, MN and resistivity columns in the extracted table\n def find_column(*needles):\n for i, name in enumerate(table.columns):\n low = name.lower()\n if any(n in low for n in needles):\n return i\n return None\n\n col_ab2 = find_column(\"ab/2\", \"ab2\")\n col_mn = find_column(\"mn\")\n col_rho = find_column(\"resist\", \"ohm\", \"rho\")\n for r, row in enumerate(table.rows):\n target_row = 11 + r\n ws.cell(row=target_row, column=1, value=r + 1)\n for source_col, target_col in ((col_ab2, 2), (col_mn, 3), (col_rho, 4)):\n if source_col is None or source_col >= len(row):\n continue\n cell = ws.cell(row=target_row, column=target_col, value=row[source_col])\n if (r, source_col) in flagged:\n cell.fill = _AMBER\n wb.save(path)\n return path\n"}, "groundwater/geo.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Coordinate handling: WGS84 geographic and UTM zones 28N / 29N.\n\nImplements the transverse Mercator projection with the Krueger series\n(Karney 2011 formulation, terms to n**4), which is accurate to well\nunder a millimetre across a UTM zone. This keeps the toolkit free of\nheavy GIS dependencies; if pyproj is installed the same API is used\ntransparently for validation.\n\nSierra Leone spans two UTM zones. West of 12 degrees W (Freetown\npeninsula, Port Loko, Kambia, most of the coast) is zone 28N with\ncentral meridian 15 degrees W. East of 12 degrees W is zone 29N with\ncentral meridian 9 degrees W.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\n# WGS84 ellipsoid\n_A = 6378137.0\n_F = 1 / 298.257223563\n_E2 = _F * (2 - _F)\n_E = math.sqrt(_E2)\n_N = _F / (2 - _F) # third flattening\n\n_K0 = 0.9996\n_FALSE_EASTING = 500000.0\n\n# Rectifying radius\n_A1 = _A / (1 + _N) * (1 + _N**2 / 4 + _N**4 / 64)\n\n# Krueger series coefficients (Karney 2011, order n^4)\n_ALPHA = (\n _N / 2 - 2 * _N**2 / 3 + 5 * _N**3 / 16 + 41 * _N**4 / 180,\n 13 * _N**2 / 48 - 3 * _N**3 / 5 + 557 * _N**4 / 1440,\n 61 * _N**3 / 240 - 103 * _N**4 / 140,\n 49561 * _N**4 / 161280,\n)\n_BETA = (\n _N / 2 - 2 * _N**2 / 3 + 37 * _N**3 / 96 - _N**4 / 360,\n _N**2 / 48 + _N**3 / 15 - 437 * _N**4 / 1440,\n 17 * _N**3 / 480 - 37 * _N**4 / 840,\n 4397 * _N**4 / 161280,\n)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass UTMCoordinate:\n easting: float\n northing: float\n zone: int\n hemisphere: str = \"N\"\n\n def __str__(self) -> str:\n return (\n f\"{self.easting:.0f} mE, {self.northing:.0f} mN \"\n f\"(UTM {self.zone}{self.hemisphere})\"\n )\n\n\ndef utm_zone_from_lon(lon: float) -> int:\n \"\"\"UTM zone number for a longitude in degrees.\"\"\"\n return int((lon + 180) // 6) + 1\n\n\ndef _central_meridian(zone: int) -> float:\n return -183.0 + 6.0 * zone\n\n\ndef geographic_to_utm(lat: float, lon: float, zone: int | None = None) -> UTMCoordinate:\n \"\"\"Convert WGS84 latitude/longitude (degrees) to UTM.\n\n If ``zone`` is omitted the natural zone for the longitude is used.\n Passing a zone allows forcing the survey's working zone near the\n 28N/29N boundary at 12 degrees W.\n \"\"\"\n if zone is None:\n zone = utm_zone_from_lon(lon)\n lam0 = math.radians(_central_meridian(zone))\n phi = math.radians(lat)\n lam = math.radians(lon) -
