with the fitted straight line.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n t = np.asarray(time_min, dtype=float)\n s = np.asarray(drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = t > 0\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.85, 3.2))\n ax.semilogx(t[keep], s[keep], \"o\", ms=4, mfc=\"white\",\n mec=style.accent_color, mew=1.2, label=\"drawdown\")\n if result is not None:\n t_line = np.geomspace(max(result.intercept_t0_min, t[keep].min() / 3), t[keep].max() * 1.3, 50)\n s_line = result.slope_m_per_log_cycle * np.log10(t_line / result.intercept_t0_min)\n ax.semilogx(t_line, s_line, \"-\", color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8,\n label=(\n f\"fit: {result.slope_m_per_log_cycle:.2f} m/log cycle, \"\n f\"T = {result.transmissivity_m2_per_day:.1f} m2/day\"\n ))\n ax.axvspan(*result.fit_window_min, color=style.accent_color, alpha=0.08,\n label=\"fitted window\")\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Time (min)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Drawdown (m)\")\n ax.invert_yaxis()\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_theis(\n time_min: np.ndarray,\n drawdown_m: np.ndarray,\n result: TheisResult | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Theis curve fit\",\n):\n \"\"\"Log-log drawdown against time with the fitted Theis curve.\"\"\"\n from scipy.special import exp1\n\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n t = np.asarray(time_min, dtype=float)\n s = np.asarray(drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = (t > 0) & (s > 0)\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.85, 3.2))\n ax.loglog(t[keep], s[keep], \"o\", ms=4, mfc=\"white\",\n mec=style.accent_color, mew=1.2, label=\"drawdown\")\n if result is not None:\n t_line = np.geomspace(t[keep].min(), t[keep].max(), 80)\n t_day = t_line / 1440.0\n q_day = result.discharge_m3_per_h * 24.0\n u = result.radius_m**2 * result.storativity / (\n 4.0 * result.transmissivity_m2_per_day * t_day\n )\n s_line = q_day / (4.0 * np.pi * result.transmissivity_m2_per_day) * exp1(u)\n label = (\n f\"Theis fit: T = {result.transmissivity_m2_per_day:.1f} m2/day, \"\n f\"S = {result.storativity:.1e}\"\n )\n if not result.storativity_reliable:\n label += \" (S indicative)\"\n ax.loglog(t_line, s_line, \"-\", color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8, label=label)\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Time (min)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Drawdown (m)\")\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_recovery(\n recovery_time_min: np.ndarray,\n residual_drawdown_m: np.ndarray,\n pumping_duration_min: float,\n result: RecoveryResult | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Theis recovery analysis\",\n):\n \"\"\"Residual drawdown against t/t' on a semi-log axis.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n tp = np.asarray(recovery_time_min, dtype=float)\n sp = np.asarray(residual_drawdown_m, dtype=float)\n keep = tp > 0\n ratio = (pumping_duration_min + tp[keep]) / tp[keep]\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.85, 3.2))\n ax.semilogx(ratio, sp[keep], \"o\", ms=4, mfc=\"white\",\n mec=style.accent_color, mew=1.2, label=\"residual drawdown\")\n if result is not None:\n r_line = np.geomspace(1.001, ratio.max() * 1.2, 50)\n # the line that was actually fitted, intercept included: forcing\n # it through the origin drew a line beside the data it claims to fit\n s_line = (\n result.slope_m_per_log_cycle * np.log10(r_line)\n + result.intercept_m\n )\n ax.semilogx(r_line, s_line, \"-\", color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8,\n label=(\n f\"fit: {result.slope_m_per_log_cycle:.2f} m/log cycle, \"\n f\"T = {result.transmissivity_m2_per_day:.1f} m2/day\"\n ))\n # where theory says the line meets t/t' = 1, and where this one does\n ax.axvline(1.0, color=\"#999999\", lw=0.8, ls=\":\")\n ax.plot([1.0], [result.intercept_m], \"x\", color=style.secondary_color,\n ms=7, mew=1.6,\n label=f\"intercept {result.intercept_m:.1f} m (theory: 0)\")\n if result.equivalent_time:\n ax.text(0.02, 0.04,\n f\"t = equivalent pumping time {pumping_duration_min:.0f} min\",\n transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.5, color=\"#555555\")\n ax.set_xlabel(\"t / t'\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Residual drawdown (m)\")\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_step_test(\n test: PumpingTest,\n result: StepTestResult | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Step test figure: drawdown per step, plus the Hantush-Bierschenk\n sw/Q against Q fit when discharges are available.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n swl = test.static_water_level_m\n with figure_context(style):\n if result is not None:\n fig, (ax, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 3.6))\n else:\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.85, 3.6))\n ax2 = None\n for k, step in enumerate(test.steps):\n s = step.water_level_m - swl if swl is not None else step.water_level_m\n q_note = (\n f\", Q = {step.discharge_m3_per_h:.1f} m3/h\"\n if step.discharge_m3_per_h is not None\n else \", Q pending\"\n )\n ax.plot(step.time_min, s, \"-o\", ms=3, lw=1.2,\n color=STEP_COLOURS[k % len(STEP_COLOURS)],\n label=f\"{step.label}{q_note}\")\n # the intake and the hole bottom, as drawdown: a step that runs past\n # either is a datum error, and the figure used to give no way to see it\n _depth_references(ax, test, swl, as_drawdown=swl is not None)\n ax.invert_yaxis()\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Time since test start (min)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Drawdown below static (m)\" if swl is not None else \"Water level (m)\")\n ax.set_title(_figure_title(\"Step drawdown test\", test), fontsize=9)\n # the early steps run along the top of an inverted drawdown axis and\n # the last one ends at the bottom right, so the lower left is the\n # one corner nothing is drawn in\n ax.legend(loc=\"lower left\", fontsize=7)\n\n if ax2 is not None and result is not None:\n q = np.array([s[\"discharge_m3_per_h\"] for s in result.steps]) * 24.0\n sq = np.array([s[\"sw_over_q_day_per_m2\"] for s in result.steps])\n ax2.plot(q, sq, \"o\", ms=5, mfc=\"white\", mec=style.accent_color, mew=1.4,\n label=\"observed\")\n q_line = np.linspace(0, q.max() * 1.15, 40)\n ax2.plot(q_line, result.aquifer_loss_B + result.well_loss_C * q_line, \"-\",\n color=style.secondary_color, lw=1.8,\n label=(\n f\"B = {result.aquifer_loss_B:.2e} day/m2\\n\"\n f\"C = {result.well_loss_C:.2e} day2/m5\"\n ))\n ax2.set_xlabel(\"Discharge Q (m3/day)\")\n ax2.set_ylabel(\"s_w / Q (day/m2)\")\n ax2.set_title(\n \"Hantush-Bierschenk\" + (\" (two points)\" if result.two_point else \"\"),\n fontsize=9,\n )\n ax2.legend(loc=\"best\", fontsize=8)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Data ingestion: standard templates, parsers and consistency checks.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .templates import write_all_templates\nfrom .ves import read_ves_workbook, read_ves_csv\nfrom .pumping import read_pumping_workbook, read_pumping_docx\nfrom .drilling import read_drilling_workbook\nfrom .waterquality import read_quality_workbook\nfrom .checks import check_site_consistency, check_all\n\n__all__ = [\n \"write_all_templates\",\n \"read_ves_workbook\",\n \"read_ves_csv\",\n \"read_pumping_workbook\",\n \"read_pumping_docx\",\n \"read_drilling_workbook\",\n \"read_quality_workbook\",\n \"check_site_consistency\",\n \"check_all\",\n]\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/checks.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Metadata consistency checks.\n\nField sheets are often filled by copying the previous sheet, so wrong\ndistricts, communities and coordinates slip through (the Rokel survey\nreport states \"Port Loko\" for a sounding whose coordinates fall in the\nWestern Area). These checks flag such conflicts before they reach a\nreport.\n\nThe district a point is in is read from the bundled geoBoundaries\npolygons, through the mapping package's own lookups - the same answer\nthe maps, the coverage ranking and the browser build give. The package\nalso bundles a table of district bounding boxes\n(``data/sl_districts.csv``) and this check used to be judged against\nit; boxes drawn around districts overlap over half the country, so one\npoint came back as \"Western Area Rural, Moyamba\", and they miss ground\nthe districts actually cover. The table is still bundled for the\nname-and-province list the apps offer, but nothing here consults it.\n\nThe polygon layer is geoBoundaries as released, which predates the 2017\ncreation of Karene and Falaba; the bundled chiefdom crosswalk supplies\nthose two, and where even that cannot place a point the check says so\nrather than choosing a district for it.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport functools\nfrom typing import Iterable\n\nfrom ..geo import infer_zone_for_sierra_leone, utm_distance_m, utm_to_geographic\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, SiteMetadata\n\n# Sierra Leone in geographic coordinates, generous margin\n_SL_BOUNDS = (-13.6, -10.0, 6.7, 10.2) # lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max\n\n# \"Western Area\" is a region, not one of the sixteen districts: it is the\n# peninsula's two districts together. Field sheets write it constantly, so\n# it is read as both of them - a site anywhere in either satisfies it -\n# rather than as Western Area Urban, which is what taking the first\n# substring hit did, flagging every correctly labelled site on the\n# southern peninsula.\n_REGIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n \"western area\": (\"Western Area Urban\", \"Western Area Rural\"),\n}\n\n# The two districts created in 2017 and the pre-2017 district each was\n# split out of. The bundled district polygons predate the split, so where\n# the chiefdom layer cannot place a point and those polygons answer\n# instead, \"Bombali\" is an answer that cannot tell Bombali from Karene.\n_SPLIT_FROM = {\"Karene\": \"Bombali\", \"Falaba\": \"Koinadugu\"}\n\n\ndef _fmt_latlon(lat: float, lon: float) -> str:\n \"\"\"Human-readable coordinates with correct hemisphere letters.\n\n Sierra Leone is in the western hemisphere, so longitudes are negative and\n must read 'W', not 'E'.\n \"\"\"\n ns = \"N\" if lat >= 0 else \"S\"\n ew = \"E\" if lon >= 0 else \"W\"\n return f\"{abs(lat):.4f} {ns}, {abs(lon):.4f} {ew}\"\n\n\n@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)\ndef district_names() -> tuple[str, ...]:\n \"\"\"The sixteen districts, spelled as the boundary lookups spell them.\n\n Taken from the chiefdom -> current-district crosswalk rather than from\n a list written out here, so the names this check accepts are exactly\n the names the point lookup can return. Imported inside the function\n because the ingestion package is imported to read a spreadsheet and\n should not drag the boundary data in with it.\n \"\"\"\n from ..coverage import load_chiefdom_district\n\n return tuple(sorted(set(load_chiefdom_district().values())))\n\n\ndef _key(name: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"A stated name reduced to what can be compared: case, spacing, and a\n trailing \"district\" the sheet added (\"Port Loko District\").\"\"\"\n words = str(name or \"\").replace(\".\", \" \").split()\n if len(words) > 1 and words[-1].lower().rstrip(\",\") in (\"district\", \"districts\"):\n words = words[:-1]\n return \" \".join(words).lower()\n\n\n@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)\ndef _named_areas() -> dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]:\n \"\"\"Every administrative name read here -> the districts it covers.\"\"\"\n areas = {_key(name): (name,) for name in district_names()}\n areas.update(_REGIONS)\n return areas\n\n\ndef _prefix_hit(key: str, candidate: str) -> bool:\n return candidate.startswith(key)\n\n\ndef _words_hit(key: str, candidate: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"True when every word of the stated name begins a word of the\n candidate, in order: \"Western Urban\" for Western Area Urban.\"\"\"\n words = iter(candidate.split())\n return all(\n any(word.startswith(part) for word in words) for part in key.split()\n )\n\n\ndef match_district(name: str) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]]:\n \"\"\"Read a district name off a sheet: ``(resolved, candidates)``.\n\n ``resolved`` is the districts the name can only mean - one district,\n or the two of the Western Area for a name that means the region. It is\n empty when the name matches nothing, and empty when it matches more\n than one district, in which case ``candidates`` lists what it could\n have meant. An exact name wins; then a name that prefixes exactly one\n (\"Bomb\" for Bombali); then one whose words begin the words of exactly\n one (\"Western Urban\"). Matching on the first substring hit, which is\n what this did, read \"Ko\" as Port Loko and \"Western Area\" as Western\n Area Urban; a name that could be two districts is worth refusing, and\n saying which two, rather than silently picking one of them.\n \"\"\"\n key = _key(name)\n if not key:\n return (), ()\n areas = _named_areas()\n if key in areas:\n return areas[key], areas[key]\n for hit in (_prefix_hit, _words_hit):\n names = [known for known in areas if hit(key, known)]\n if not names:\n continue\n covered = {d for known in names for d in areas[known]}\n for known in names:\n # \"Western\" matches both halves of the Western Area and the\n # region over them, and the region is a single answer; \"Ko\"\n # matches Koinadugu and Kono, and there is no such answer.\n if set(areas[known]) == covered:\n return areas[known], areas[known]\n return (), tuple(sorted(covered))\n return (), ()\n\n\ndef districts_named(name: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n \"\"\"The districts a district name written on a sheet can only mean.\"\"\"\n return match_district(name)[0]\n\n\ndef district_at(lat: float, lon: float) -> tuple[str, str, bool]:\n \"\"\"Where the bundled boundaries put a point.\n\n Returns ``(chiefdom, district, current)``. ``current`` is True when the\n district is the one the point is in today, which is what the chiefdom\n layer plus the crosswalk give; it is False when only the district\n polygons could answer, because those predate the 2017 split and so\n cannot tell Bombali from Karene or Koinadugu from Falaba. Both are\n empty when no polygon holds the point.\n\n The mapping package owns the point-in-polygon lookups and is imported\n here rather than at module scope because it pulls in matplotlib, and\n reading a field sheet must not depend on a plotting stack.\n \"\"\"\n from ..mapping.regional import chiefdom_of, district_of\n\n chiefdom, district = chiefdom_of(lat, lon)\n if district:\n return chiefdom, district, True\n # No chiefdom holds the point, and none is within the seam tolerance of\n # it either. district_of is asked next, and with the bundled layer it\n # now resolves through the same chiefdom polygons, so in practice it\n # answers nothing here: a caller that supplies its own district layer is\n # the only way this returns a name, and that name may be pre-2017.\n return \"\", district_of(lat, lon), False\n\n\ndef _or_list(names: Iterable[str]) -> str:\n \"\"\"A list an operator reads as a sentence: \"Koinadugu or Kono\".\"\"\"\n names = list(names)\n if len(names) < 2:\n return \"\".join(names)\n return f\"{', '.join(names[:-1])} or {names[-1]}\"\n\n\ndef check_site_consistency(site: SiteMetadata, context: str = \"\") -> list[DataFlag]:\n \"\"\"Check one site record: coordinates against country, zone and district.\"\"\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n ctx = context or site.community or \"\"\n\n if site.easting is None or site.northing is None:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\"info\", \"missing_coordinates\", \"No GPS coordinates recorded.\", ctx)\n )\n return flags\n\n zone = site.utm_zone\n if zone is None:\n zone = infer_zone_for_sierra_leone(site.easting)\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"utm_zone_assumed\",\n f\"UTM zone not recorded; assumed {zone}N from the easting.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n lat, lon = utm_to_geographic(site.easting, site.northing, zone)\n\n lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max = _SL_BOUNDS\n if not (lon_min <= lon <= lon_max and lat_min <= lat <= lat_max):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"coordinates_outside_country\",\n f\"Coordinates convert to {_fmt_latlon(lat, lon)} which is outside \"\n \"Sierra Leone; check easting/northing and the UTM zone.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n return flags\n\n resolved, candidates = match_district(site.district)\n if site.district and not resolved:\n if len(candidates) > 1:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"ambiguous_district\",\n f\"District '{site.district}' could be \"\n f\"{_or_list(candidates)}; it is not read as any of them. \"\n \"Write the district out in full.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n else:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"unknown_district\",\n f\"District '{site.district}' is not a recognised Sierra \"\n \"Leone district name, so the coordinates were not checked \"\n \"against it.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n elif resolved:\n chiefdom, found, current = district_at(lat, lon)\n if not found:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"coordinates_outside_districts\",\n f\"The boundary polygons place the coordinates \"\n f\"({_fmt_latlon(lat, lon)}) in no district, so district \"\n f\"'{site.district}' could not be checked against them; \"\n \"the point may be offshore, over the border, or in a gap \"\n \"between the boundaries.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n elif found not in resolved:\n # A point no chiefdom polygon holds is placed by the district\n # polygons, and those predate the 2017 split: for a site stated\n # to be in Karene or Falaba they can only name the district it\n # was split from, which neither confirms nor contradicts it.\n split = next(\n (d for d in resolved if not current and _SPLIT_FROM.get(d) == found),\n \"\",\n )\n if split:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"district_predates_boundaries\",\n f\"District '{site.district}' could not be checked \"\n f\"against the coordinates ({_fmt_latlon(lat, lon)}): \"\n \"no chiefdom polygon holds them, and the district \"\n f\"polygons predate the 2017 creation of {split}, so \"\n f\"the {found} they give is the district {split} was \"\n \"split from.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n elif current:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"district_coordinate_conflict\",\n f\"Stated district '{site.district}' does not contain \"\n f\"the coordinates ({_fmt_latlon(lat, lon)}), which \"\n f\"fall in {chiefdom} chiefdom, {found} district. \"\n \"Verify against the field notes.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n else:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"district_coordinate_conflict\",\n f\"Stated district '{site.district}' does not contain \"\n f\"the coordinates ({_fmt_latlon(lat, lon)}). No \"\n \"chiefdom polygon holds them; the district polygons, \"\n \"which predate the 2017 creation of Karene and \"\n f\"Falaba, place them in {found}. Verify against the \"\n \"field notes.\",\n ctx,\n )\n )\n return flags\n\n\ndef check_group_consistency(\n sites: Iterable[tuple[str, SiteMetadata]], max_separation_km: float = 5.0\n) -> list[DataFlag]:\n \"\"\"Cross-record checks for one survey or project.\n\n Flags differing client/community/district values between sheets of\n the same project and points unexpectedly far apart.\n \"\"\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n records = list(sites)\n if len(records) < 2:\n return flags\n\n for field in (\"client\", \"community\", \"district\"):\n values = {}\n for label, site in records:\n value = getattr(site, field).strip()\n if not value:\n continue\n # Two sheets of one project can spell the same ground two ways -\n # \"Western Area\" on one and \"Western Area Rural\" on the other -\n # and each passes its own single-sheet check. Compared as plain\n # strings they were then reported together as an inconsistency,\n # so the two checks contradicted each other. Districts are\n # grouped by what the name can mean, not by how it is typed.\n key = value.lower()\n if field == \"district\":\n resolved = match_district(value)[0]\n if resolved:\n # \"Western Area\" can mean either half of the region and\n # \"Western Area Rural\" only one of them; the two overlap,\n # so they are one value here. Only names that can share\n # no district at all are a disagreement.\n key = next(\n (\n existing\n for existing in values\n if isinstance(existing, frozenset)\n and existing & set(resolved)\n ),\n frozenset(resolved),\n )\n values.setdefault(key, (value, []))[1].append(label)\n if len(values) > 1:\n detail = \"; \".join(\n f\"'{v}' on {', '.join(labels)}\" for v, labels in values.values()\n )\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n f\"inconsistent_{field}\",\n f\"Different {field} values within one project: {detail}. \"\n \"This usually comes from copying the previous sheet.\",\n )\n )\n\n # Pairwise separation, measured on the ground rather than by subtracting\n # raw eastings. Sierra Leone straddles UTM zones 28N and 29N, and each\n # zone restarts its easting at its own central meridian: two sites 2 km\n # apart either side of the 12 degrees W boundary differ by about 659 km\n # on paper. Every point is converted through its own zone first.\n points = []\n for label, site in records:\n utm = site.utm # resolves the zone, inferring it when unrecorded\n if utm is not None:\n points.append((label, utm))\n for i in range(len(points)):\n for j in range(i + 1, len(points)):\n li, ui = points[i]\n lj, uj = points[j]\n try:\n dist_km = utm_distance_m(ui, uj) / 1000.0\n except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError, OverflowError):\n # An unconvertible coordinate is already reported per site by\n # check_site_consistency; it must not sink the whole check.\n continue\n if dist_km > max_separation_km:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"points_far_apart\",\n f\"{li} and {lj} are {dist_km:.1f} km apart, which is \"\n \"unusually far for one site; check the coordinates.\",\n )\n )\n return flags\n\n\ndef check_all(records: Iterable[tuple[str, SiteMetadata]]) -> list[DataFlag]:\n \"\"\"Per-site and cross-site checks for a set of (label, site) records.\"\"\"\n records = list(records)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n for label, site in records:\n flags.extend(check_site_consistency(site, context=label))\n flags.extend(check_group_consistency(records))\n return flags\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/common.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Shared helpers for reading field sheet layouts.\n\nField sheets use a header block of ``Label: value`` pairs followed by\none or more data tables. Labels vary between sheets (\"Field\nSupervisor\", \"Test conducted by\", \"Operator\"), values sometimes live\nin the same cell after a colon and sometimes several columns to the\nright, and numbers may be stored as text with leading zeros. The\nhelpers here deal with all of that in one place.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport datetime\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom openpyxl import load_workbook\n\nfrom ..geo import parse_utm_zone\nfrom ..models import SiteMetadata\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\n\n# Canonical header keys and the label patterns that map to them.\nLABEL_PATTERNS: dict[str, list[str]] = {\n \"client\": [r\"^client\\b\"],\n \"project\": [r\"^project(?!\\s*ref)\"],\n \"project_ref\": [r\"^project\\s*ref\", r\"^geophysics\\s*ref\"],\n \"community\": [r\"^community\\b\", r\"^village\\b\", r\"^location\\b\"],\n \"chiefdom\": [r\"^chiefdom\\b\"],\n \"district\": [r\"^district\\b\"],\n \"sounding_id\": [r\"^sounding\\s*(number|no)\", r\"^ves\\s*(point|number|no)\"],\n \"date\": [r\"^date\\b\"],\n \"supervisor\": [\n r\"^field\\s*supervisor\",\n r\"^test\\s*conducted\\s*by\",\n r\"^operator\\b\",\n r\"^supervisor\\b\",\n ],\n \"contractor\": [r\"^(drilling\\s*)?contractor\\b\"],\n \"easting\": [r\"^gps\\s*coordinate\\s*east\", r\"^east(ing)?\\b\", r\"^utm\\s*east\"],\n \"northing\": [r\"^gps\\s*coordinate\\s*north\", r\"^north(ing)?\\b\", r\"^utm\\s*north\"],\n \"utm_zone\": [r\"^utm\\s*zone\", r\"^zone\\b\"],\n \"elevation_m\": [r\"^elevation\", r\"^altitude\"],\n \"array_type\": [r\"^array\\b\", r\"^electrode\\s*(array|configuration)\"],\n \"instrument\": [r\"^instrument\\b\", r\"^equipment\\b\"],\n \"borehole_ref\": [r\"^borehole\\s*/?\\s*ref\", r\"^bh\\s*ref\", r\"^borehole\\s*(number|no)\"],\n \"borehole_depth_m\": [r\"^depth\\s*of\\s*borehole\", r\"^borehole\\s*depth\", r\"^total\\s*depth\", r\"^depth\\b\"],\n \"static_water_level_m\": [r\"^static\\s*water\\s*level\", r\"^swl\\b\"],\n \"pump_setting_m\": [r\"^pump\\s*setting\", r\"^pump\\s*installation\\s*depth\"],\n \"step_length_min\": [r\"^length\\s*of\\s*each\\s*step\", r\"^step\\s*length\"],\n \"test_type\": [r\"^test\\s*type\"],\n \"start_time\": [r\"^time\\b\", r\"^start\\s*time\"],\n \"duration\": [r\"^duration\"],\n \"drilling_method\": [r\"^(drilling\\s*)?method\\b\"],\n \"start_date\": [r\"^(drilling\\s*)?start\\s*date\"],\n \"completion_date\": [r\"^compl(etion)?\\.?\\s*date\"],\n \"status\": [r\"^(bh\\s*)?status\"],\n \"sample_id\": [r\"^sample\\s*(id|number|no|ref)\"],\n \"laboratory\": [r\"^lab(oratory)?\\b\"],\n \"sample_date\": [r\"^sample\\s*date\", r\"^date\\s*sampled\"],\n \"grouting_depth_m\": [r\"^grout(ing)?\\b\"],\n \"drill_rig\": [r\"^drill\\s*rig\"],\n \"installed_screens\": [r\"^screens?\\s*installed\", r\"^installed\\s*screens?\",\n r\"^screens?\\s*(set|as\\s*built)\"],\n}\n\n_COMPILED = {\n key: [re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE) for p in pats]\n for key, pats in LABEL_PATTERNS.items()\n}\n\nNUMERIC_HEADER_KEYS = {\n \"easting\",\n \"northing\",\n \"elevation_m\",\n \"borehole_depth_m\",\n \"static_water_level_m\",\n \"pump_setting_m\",\n \"step_length_min\",\n \"grouting_depth_m\",\n}\n\n\ndef load_grid(path: str | Path, sheet: str | None = None) -> tuple[list[list], str]:\n \"\"\"Load a worksheet as a rectangular grid of raw cell values.\"\"\"\n wb = load_workbook(path, data_only=True, read_only=True)\n ws = wb[sheet] if sheet else wb.worksheets[0]\n grid = [list(row) for row in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]\n title = ws.title\n wb.close()\n return grid, title\n\n\ndef sheet_names(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:\n wb = load_workbook(path, read_only=True)\n names = list(wb.sheetnames)\n wb.close()\n return names\n\n\n# Every dash a sheet can carry: the hyphen variants, the figure, en, em and\n# horizontal dashes, the true minus sign and the full-width hyphen.\n_DASH_RE = re.compile(\"[\\u2010-\\u2015\\u2212\\ufe58\\ufe63\\uff0d]\")\n\n\ndef normalise_dashes(value):\n \"\"\"Replace every dash a text cell can carry with the plain hyphen.\n\n Word turns \"5-10\" into \"5\\u201310\" as the crew types it and the en dash\n survives the copy into Excel, so a depth interval or a screen range\n written on a laptop reaches the range patterns as a character they do\n not list. The row was then dropped in silence and the only trace was an\n \"interval_gap\" flag blaming the log for a gap the crew never left\n (ROADMAP data-ingestion-8). A value that is not text is handed back\n untouched, so a date or a number still reaches its own parser as itself.\n\n >>> normalise_dashes(\"5\\u201310\")\n '5-10'\n \"\"\"\n if not isinstance(value, str):\n return value\n return _DASH_RE.sub(\"-\", value)\n\n\ndef match_label(text: str) -> str | None:\n \"\"\"Return the canonical key for a label cell, if any.\"\"\"\n matched = match_label_priority(text)\n return matched[0] if matched else None\n\n\ndef match_label_priority(text: str) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n \"\"\"Return ``(key, priority)`` for a label cell.\n\n Priority is the pattern index within the key's list: 0 is the most\n specific wording (\"Depth of Borehole\"), higher numbers are generic\n fallbacks (\"Depth\"). A more specific match later in the sheet may\n overwrite a generic one.\n \"\"\"\n label = clean_text(text).rstrip(\":\").strip()\n if not label:\n return None\n best: tuple[str, int] | None = None\n for key, patterns in _COMPILED.items():\n for priority, pattern in enumerate(patterns):\n if pattern.search(label):\n if best is None or priority < best[1]:\n if priority == 0:\n return key, 0\n best = (key, priority)\n break\n return best\n\n\ndef split_inline_value(cell_text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:\n \"\"\"Split ``\"Community: Kuntoloh\"`` into label and inline value.\"\"\"\n text = clean_text(cell_text)\n if \":\" in text:\n label, _, value = text.partition(\":\")\n value = value.strip()\n return label, value if value else None\n return text, None\n\n\ndef extract_header_fields(grid: list[list], max_rows: int = 30) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Scan the top of a sheet for ``Label -> value`` pairs.\n\n A value is taken from the same cell after a colon when present,\n otherwise from the next non-empty cell to the right. The first\n occurrence of a key wins, except that a more specific label wording\n later in the sheet (\"Depth of Borehole\") overrides a generic one\n seen earlier (\"Depth\").\n \"\"\"\n fields: dict = {}\n priorities: dict[str, int] = {}\n for _r, row in enumerate(grid[:max_rows]):\n for c, cell in enumerate(row):\n if cell is None or isinstance(cell, (int, float)):\n continue\n label_text, inline_value = split_inline_value(str(cell))\n matched = match_label_priority(label_text)\n if matched is None:\n continue\n key, priority = matched\n if key in fields and priorities.get(key, 99) <= priority:\n continue\n value = inline_value\n if value is None:\n for cc in range(c + 1, min(c + 8, len(row))):\n nxt = row[cc]\n if nxt is not None and clean_text(nxt) != \"\":\n # Stop if the neighbouring cell is itself a label\n # (with or without its own inline value).\n if not isinstance(nxt, (int, float)):\n nxt_label, _ = split_inline_value(str(nxt))\n if match_label(nxt_label):\n break\n value = nxt\n break\n if value is None:\n # A columnar header block - labels across one row, values in\n # the row beneath - used to parse to nothing at all. The cell\n # below is taken only when it is not itself a label, so the\n # stacked template layout (label over label) is unaffected.\n value = _value_below(grid, _r, c)\n if value is None:\n continue\n if key in NUMERIC_HEADER_KEYS:\n number = parse_number(value)\n if number is not None:\n fields[key] = number\n priorities[key] = priority\n else:\n fields[key] = clean_text(_date_text(value))\n priorities[key] = priority\n return fields\n\n\ndef _value_below(grid: list[list], r: int, c: int):\n if r + 1 >= len(grid) or c >= len(grid[r + 1]):\n return None\n below = grid[r + 1][c]\n if below is None or clean_text(below) == \"\":\n return None\n if not isinstance(below, (int, float)):\n below_label, _ = split_inline_value(str(below))\n if match_label(below_label):\n return None\n return below\n\n\ndef _date_text(value):\n \"\"\"A date cell as text: ``2015-12-08``, not ``2015-12-08 00:00:00``.\n\n openpyxl hands a cell typed as a date back as a datetime, and str() of\n that carried a midnight time onto the report cover. ISO is what the\n browser app already prints for the same cell, so the two apps agree.\n \"\"\"\n if isinstance(value, datetime.datetime):\n if value.hour or value.minute or value.second:\n return value.isoformat(sep=\" \", timespec=\"minutes\")\n return value.date().isoformat()\n if isinstance(value, datetime.date):\n return value.isoformat()\n return value\n\n\ndef site_from_fields(fields: dict, source: str = \"\") -> SiteMetadata:\n \"\"\"Build SiteMetadata from extracted header fields.\n\n The zone cell is read with :func:`groundwater.geo.parse_utm_zone`, which\n takes the number that follows a label and refuses anything that names no\n single zone. It used to be read with ``parse_number``, which takes the\n first number in the cell whatever that number is. On a sheet whose zone\n pair sits directly above the GPS pair, the value cell \"Zone 28\" matches\n the ``^zone`` label pattern, so ``extract_header_fields`` treats it as a\n label of its own and hunts for a value below it - and what is below it is\n the easting. The site was then carried as \"zone 708958\" and projected\n tens of degrees out of the country (ROADMAP data-ingestion-14). A zone\n that cannot be read is left unrecorded, which ``SiteMetadata.utm`` infers\n from the easting and ``check_site_consistency`` reports as\n ``utm_zone_assumed``; naming no zone and saying so is safe where guessing\n one is not, because the same easting in the next zone is a site 660 km\n away.\n \"\"\"\n return SiteMetadata(\n client=fields.get(\"client\", \"\"),\n project=fields.get(\"project\", \"\"),\n community=fields.get(\"community\", \"\"),\n chiefdom=fields.get(\"chiefdom\", \"\"),\n district=fields.get(\"district\", \"\"),\n project_ref=fields.get(\"project_ref\", \"\"),\n easting=fields.get(\"easting\"),\n northing=fields.get(\"northing\"),\n utm_zone=parse_utm_zone(fields.get(\"utm_zone\")),\n elevation_m=fields.get(\"elevation_m\"),\n date=str(fields.get(\"date\", \"\")),\n supervisor=fields.get(\"supervisor\", \"\"),\n contractor=fields.get(\"contractor\", \"\"),\n source=source,\n )\n\n\ndef find_row(grid: list[list], predicate, start: int = 0) -> int | None:\n \"\"\"Index of the first row for which ``predicate(row)`` is true.\"\"\"\n for r in range(start, len(grid)):\n if predicate(grid[r]):\n return r\n return None\n\n\ndef row_text(row: list) -> list[str]:\n return [clean_text(c).lower() for c in row]\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/drilling.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Parser for drilling log sheets (Excel template and WiNGiN style tables).\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport re\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, DrillingLog, LithologyInterval\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_depth_interval, parse_number, plural\nfrom . import common\n\n_SCREEN_RANGE_RE = re.compile(r\"(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*(?:-|\u2013|to)\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\")\n\n# A clock time carries a colon or an \"h\" between the hour and the minutes\n# (\"14:30\", \"14h30\"). A decimal point is deliberately not a clock separator\n# here: \"8.50\" in a strike note is a depth far more often than it is ten to\n# nine, and reading it as a time would lose the strike.\n#\n# A driller also writes the hour with no separator at all and the word after\n# it instead (\"1430 hrs\"), and that form reached the depth reader untouched:\n# a 30 m borehole was handed over recording a water strike at 1430 m\n# (ROADMAP data-ingestion-9, the same clock read as a depth as \"14:30\" was).\n# Three or four digits carrying \"hrs\" or \"hours\" are a time of day and never\n# a depth in metres, so they are removed with the other clock forms; a bare\n# \"2 hrs\" is an elapsed time and too short to be a clock, so it is left\n# alone, and no number that carries a metre unit is touched either way.\n_CLOCK_TIME_RE = re.compile(\n r\"\\b\\d{1,2}\\s*[:h]\\s*\\d{2}\\b(?:\\s*(?:am|pm|hrs?))?\"\n r\"|\\b\\d{3,4}\\s*(?:hrs?|hours?)\\b\",\n re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n# One depth, or a list of them sharing the unit written after the last\n# (\"12, 18 and 30 m\"), in metres. The lookahead keeps the \"m\" of a rate\n# (\"0.5 m/min\") from reading as a depth in metres.\n_DEPTH_LIST_RE = re.compile(\n # A slash is not a list separator here. \"1/2 m\" is half a metre and\n # \"12/30\" is as likely a date as a pair, and both used to come out as\n # two strikes - which is the invention this parser exists to stop.\n r\"(?:\\d+(?:[.,]\\d+)?\\s*(?:,|&|\\+|and\\b)\\s*)*\"\n r\"\\d+(?:[.,]\\d+)?\\s*(?:met(?:re|er)s?|m)\\b(?!\\s*/)\",\n re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n_NUMBER_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r\"\\d+(?:[.,]\\d+)?\")\n\n# The unit a diameter cell carries, if it carries one at all. Bit sizes are\n# quoted in halves and eighths of an inch, so the number may be a whole and a\n# fraction (\"6 1/2 in\"); the lookbehind keeps the denominator of that fraction\n# from being read as the diameter on its own.\n_DIAMETER_UNIT_RE = re.compile(\n r\"(?\\d+(?:[.,]\\d+)?)\"\n r\"(?:\\s*(?P\\d+)\\s*/\\s*(?P\\d+))?\\s*\"\n # The abbreviations take a plural on a field sheet as readily as the\n # spelled-out words do. \"165 mms\" fell past an \"mm\" that could not end in\n # an s, and a metric bit was recorded as a 165 inch hole exactly as\n # \"165 mm\" was before this parser existed (ROADMAP data-ingestion-15) -\n # and that diameter is what sizes the casing and the gravel pack.\n r\"(?Pmillimet(?:re|er)s?|mms?|centimet(?:re|er)s?|cms?\"\n r\"|inch(?:es)?|in|''|\\\"|\u201d|\u2033)(?![a-z])\",\n re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n# The unit a penetration rate cell carries: metres per minute or hour, or the\n# time per metre a driller times with a stopwatch and writes the other way up.\n# The metre is written out as often as it is abbreviated, and the hour takes\n# a plural: \"30 metres/hour\" and \"30 m/hrs\" carry their unit as plainly as\n# \"30 m/hr\" does, but neither was matched, so both fell through to the bare\n# number and were recorded as thirty metres a minute - sixty times too fast,\n# which is the defect this parser was written to close (ROADMAP\n# data-ingestion-15). The longer spelling is listed before the shorter one in\n# each pair so \"metres\" is not read as an \"m\" followed by rubbish.\n_METRE = r\"(?:met(?:re|er)s?|m)\"\n_RATE_UNIT_RE = re.compile(\n r\"(?\\d+(?:[.,]\\d+)?)\\s*(?P\"\n + _METRE + r\"\\s*(?:/|per)\\s*min(?:ute)?s?\"\n r\"|\" + _METRE + r\"\\s*(?:/|per)\\s*(?:hrs?|hours?|h)\"\n r\"|min(?:ute)?s?\\s*(?:/|per)\\s*\" + _METRE +\n r\"|sec(?:ond)?s?\\s*(?:/|per)\\s*\" + _METRE +\n r\"|s\\s*(?:/|per)\\s*\" + _METRE +\n r\")(?![a-z])\",\n re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n\n#: Two numbers with a slash between them: a fraction, a date, or a run\n#: number, none of which is a depth.\n_FRACTION_RE = re.compile(r\"\\d\\s*/\\s*\\d\")\n\n\ndef parse_water_strike_depths(value) -> tuple[list[float], str]:\n \"\"\"Read the strike depths a cell names, in metres.\n\n Returns ``(depths, reason)``: the depths the cell can be read to name,\n or an empty list and the reason it cannot be read confidently, which the\n caller raises as a flag. Recording nothing and saying so is the right\n answer here, because a strike depth places the screens.\n\n A strike cell used to be read as the last number after the last colon,\n so \"Water strike: 8 m at 14:30\" recorded a 30 m strike - the minutes of\n the clock time - \"at 12 m and 30 m\" recorded only 12 m, and a 0 typed in\n the strike column to mean \"no water on this row\" recorded a strike at the\n surface, which then seeded a 0-5 m screen against the topsoil (ROADMAP\n data-ingestion-9). Clock times are removed before any number is read, a\n number that carries a metre unit is a depth, and a zero is an empty cell.\n\n >>> parse_water_strike_depths(\"Water strike: 8 m at 14:30\")\n ([8.0], '')\n >>> parse_water_strike_depths(\"Water strikes at 12 m and 30 m\")\n ([12.0, 30.0], '')\n >>> parse_water_strike_depths(0)\n ([], '')\n \"\"\"\n if value is None:\n return [], \"\"\n if isinstance(value, (datetime.date, datetime.datetime)):\n # Excel hands a cell typed as a time back as a datetime, and reading\n # it as a number recorded the year as a strike depth.\n return [], \"the cell holds a date or a time rather than a depth\"\n if isinstance(value, bool):\n return [], \"\"\n if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n return ([float(value)] if value > 0 else []), \"\"\n\n text = _CLOCK_TIME_RE.sub(\" \", clean_text(value))\n # A fraction between two digits is half a metre, or a date, or a run\n # number; it is not two depths and it is not its own denominator.\n # \"Water strike 1/2 m\" read as a strike at 2 m, which would place a\n # screen. Refusing it and saying so is the only honest answer.\n if _FRACTION_RE.search(text):\n return [], \"it writes a fraction or a date, which names no single depth\"\n depths: list[float] = []\n for match in _DEPTH_LIST_RE.finditer(text):\n for token in _NUMBER_TOKEN_RE.findall(match.group(0)):\n depth = parse_number(token)\n if depth is not None and depth > 0:\n depths.append(depth)\n if depths:\n return depths, \"\"\n\n # No number carries a unit. A single number is the depth the note is\n # about (\"First water strike: 12\"); several are a sentence this parser\n # cannot take apart, and guessing one of them is worse than refusing.\n numbers = _NUMBER_TOKEN_RE.findall(text)\n if not numbers:\n return [], \"\"\n if len(numbers) > 1:\n return [], \"it names several numbers and none of them carries a unit\"\n depth = parse_number(numbers[0])\n if depth is None or depth <= 0:\n return [], \"\"\n return [depth], \"\"\n\n\ndef _unreadable_strike_flag(text: str, reason: str) -> DataFlag:\n \"\"\"The flag raised for a strike cell that cannot be read as a depth.\n\n Refusing the cell costs the log a strike, so the flag names the cell it\n refused, why it refused it, and the wording that would have read.\n \"\"\"\n return DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"water_strike_unreadable\",\n f'Water strike cell \"{text}\" was not read as a depth: {reason}. '\n \"No strike was recorded from it; write each depth with its unit, as \"\n '\"water strike at 12 m and 30 m\".',\n )\n\n\ndef parse_bit_diameter_in(value) -> float | None:\n \"\"\"The drilled diameter in inches, converting the unit the cell carries.\n\n Crews quote a bit in millimetres as often as in inches, and the column\n was read as a bare number, so \"165 mm\" was recorded as a 165 inch hole\n (ROADMAP data-ingestion-15) - a metre and a half of annulus in the bill\n of quantities and in the completion drawing. A cell with no unit at all\n is read as inches, which is the unit the template column asks for\n (\"Drilling diameter (in)\") and the unit the design rules are written in.\n\n A converted diameter is kept to two decimals: 165 mm is the metric name\n of a 6.5 in bit, and 6.5 in is what the completion log should print.\n\n >>> parse_bit_diameter_in(\"165 mm\")\n 6.5\n >>> parse_bit_diameter_in('6 1/2\"')\n 6.5\n >>> parse_bit_diameter_in(6.5)\n 6.5\n \"\"\"\n if value is None:\n return None\n if isinstance(value, bool):\n return None\n if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n return float(value)\n text = clean_text(value)\n match = _DIAMETER_UNIT_RE.search(text)\n if match is None:\n return parse_number(text)\n number = parse_number(match.group(\"number\"))\n if number is None:\n return None\n if match.group(\"numerator\") and float(match.group(\"denominator\")) != 0:\n # \"6 1/2 in\" is six and a half inches, which is how a bit is quoted.\n number += float(match.group(\"numerator\")) / float(match.group(\"denominator\"))\n unit = match.group(\"unit\").lower()\n if unit.startswith((\"mm\", \"millim\")):\n return round(number / 25.4, 2)\n if unit.startswith((\"cm\", \"centim\")):\n return round(number / 2.54, 2)\n return number\n\n\ndef parse_penetration_rate_m_per_min(value) -> float | None:\n \"\"\"The penetration rate in metres per minute, whichever way up it is written.\n\n A driller times a rod with a stopwatch and writes what the watch says, so\n the cell carries \"5 min/m\" as readily as \"0.2 m/min\" and a rig sheet\n quotes metres per hour. The column was read as a bare number, so a hole\n advancing at five minutes to the metre was recorded as five metres a\n minute (ROADMAP data-ingestion-15), twenty-five times too fast. A cell\n with no unit is read as metres per minute, which is the unit the template\n column asks for (\"Penetration rate (m/min)\").\n\n >>> parse_penetration_rate_m_per_min(\"5 min/m\")\n 0.2\n >>> parse_penetration_rate_m_per_min(0.33)\n 0.33\n \"\"\"\n if value is None:\n return None\n if isinstance(value, bool):\n return None\n if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n return float(value)\n text = clean_text(value)\n match = _RATE_UNIT_RE.search(text)\n if match is None:\n return parse_number(text)\n number = parse_number(match.group(\"number\"))\n if number is None:\n return None\n unit = re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \"\", match.group(\"unit\")).lower().replace(\"per\", \"/\")\n if unit.startswith(\"min\"):\n # minutes per metre: the reciprocal, and a zero is not a rate at all\n return 1.0 / number if number > 0 else None\n if unit.startswith(\"s\"):\n # seconds per metre\n return 60.0 / number if number > 0 else None\n if \"/h\" in unit:\n return number / 60.0\n return number\n\n\ndef parse_installed_screens(value) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:\n \"\"\"``\"25-35; 48-53 m\"`` -> ``[(25.0, 35.0), (48.0, 53.0)]``.\n\n The as-built screens a crew writes on the sheet, as ranges separated by\n anything. A cell with no range in it records no screens. The dashes are\n normalised first so a range typed with an en or em dash is read as the\n range it is rather than dropped (ROADMAP data-ingestion-8).\n \"\"\"\n text = common.normalise_dashes(clean_text(value))\n out = []\n for match in _SCREEN_RANGE_RE.finditer(text):\n top, bottom = float(match.group(1)), float(match.group(2))\n if bottom < top:\n top, bottom = bottom, top\n if bottom > top:\n out.append((top, bottom))\n return sorted(out)\n\n\ndef _find_log_header(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:\n \"\"\"Locate the drilling table header row and map its columns.\"\"\"\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = common.row_text(row)\n cols: dict[str, int] = {}\n for c, t in enumerate(texts):\n if not t:\n continue\n if (\"depth\" in t and \"interval\" in t) or t.startswith(\"depth /\"):\n cols[\"interval\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"depth\") and \"interval\" not in cols:\n cols.setdefault(\"interval\", c)\n elif t.startswith(\"from\"):\n cols.setdefault(\"from_time\", c)\n elif t.startswith(\"to\"):\n cols.setdefault(\"to_time\", c)\n elif \"penetration\" in t:\n cols[\"rate\"] = c\n elif \"sample\" in t or \"litholog\" in t or \"description\" in t:\n cols.setdefault(\"description\", c)\n elif \"diameter\" in t or \"bit\" in t:\n cols.setdefault(\"diameter\", c)\n elif \"strike\" in t:\n cols[\"strike\"] = c\n if \"interval\" in cols:\n return r, cols\n return None\n\n\ndef read_drilling_workbook(path: str | Path) -> DrillingLog:\n grid, _ = common.load_grid(path)\n return drilling_from_grid(grid, source=str(path))\n\n\ndef drilling_from_grid(grid: list[list], source: str = \"\") -> DrillingLog:\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid, max_rows=len(grid))\n site = common.site_from_fields(fields, source=source)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n\n located = _find_log_header(grid)\n intervals: list[LithologyInterval] = []\n strikes: list[float] = []\n zero_strike_rows = 0\n if located is not None:\n header_row, cols = located\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n def cell(key):\n c = cols.get(key)\n return row[c] if c is not None and c < len(row) else None\n\n raw_interval = cell(\"interval\")\n if clean_text(raw_interval).lower().startswith(\"note\"):\n continue\n if isinstance(raw_interval, (datetime.date, datetime.datetime)):\n # Excel turns \"5-10\" typed into a General cell into 10 May.\n # Losing the row is better than a 5 to 2026 m interval, but\n # the crew has to know a row went missing.\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"interval_read_as_date\",\n f\"Depth interval cell holds the date \"\n f\"{raw_interval:%d %b %Y} - Excel converts entries like \"\n '\"5-10\" into dates. Format the depth column as Text '\n \"and retype the interval; this row was skipped.\",\n )\n )\n continue\n # Word turns \"5-10\" into \"5\u201310\" as the crew types the sheet and\n # the en dash survives the copy into Excel, but the interval\n # pattern lists only the plain hyphen, so the row was dropped\n # without a word and the gap it left was reported as a gap in the\n # crew's log (ROADMAP data-ingestion-8). Normalising the dashes\n # reads the interval as it was written, whichever dash was typed.\n interval = parse_depth_interval(common.normalise_dashes(raw_interval))\n if interval is None:\n continue\n top, bottom = interval\n description = clean_text(cell(\"description\"))\n intervals.append(\n LithologyInterval(\n top_m=top,\n bottom_m=bottom,\n description=description,\n from_time=clean_text(cell(\"from_time\")),\n to_time=clean_text(cell(\"to_time\")),\n penetration_rate_m_per_min=parse_penetration_rate_m_per_min(\n cell(\"rate\")\n ),\n bit_diameter_in=parse_bit_diameter_in(cell(\"diameter\")),\n )\n )\n raw_strike = cell(\"strike\")\n depths, reason = parse_water_strike_depths(raw_strike)\n strikes.extend(depths)\n if reason:\n flags.append(\n _unreadable_strike_flag(clean_text(raw_strike), reason)\n )\n elif not depths and parse_number(raw_strike) == 0:\n # A crew fills the strike column with 0 to mean \"no water on\n # this row\". Read as a number it was a strike at 0 m, which\n # seeded a screen against the topsoil (ROADMAP\n # data-ingestion-9); it is counted here so the refusal is\n # visible rather than silent.\n zero_strike_rows += 1\n\n if zero_strike_rows:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"water_strike_zero_ignored\",\n f\"The water strike column holds 0 on {zero_strike_rows} \"\n \"row(s); a zero there is read as no strike on that row, \"\n \"not as a strike at 0 m.\",\n )\n )\n\n # Water strikes noted as text lines (\"First water strike: 12m\"). The note\n # used to be read as the last number after the last colon, so\n # \"Water strike: 8 m at 14:30\" recorded a 30 m strike and a note naming\n # two strikes recorded only the first (ROADMAP data-ingestion-9).\n for row in grid:\n for c in row:\n raw = clean_text(c)\n text = raw.lower()\n if \"water strike\" in text and not text.startswith(\"note\"):\n depths, reason = parse_water_strike_depths(raw)\n for value in depths:\n if value not in strikes:\n strikes.append(value)\n if reason:\n # A cell in the strike column that is also a note has\n # already been refused once by the loop above, and one\n # refusal of one cell is one flag.\n flag = _unreadable_strike_flag(raw, reason)\n if all(f.message != flag.message for f in flags):\n flags.append(flag)\n\n total = fields.get(\"borehole_depth_m\")\n if total is None and intervals:\n total = max(iv.bottom_m for iv in intervals)\n\n # A strike below the bottom of the hole is a number the drilling never\n # reached. It survives only as a figure printed to the client - the\n # handover report lists the strikes - because the screen designer clips\n # it out, so nothing else in the toolkit ever contradicts it.\n if total is not None:\n too_deep = [v for v in strikes if v > float(total)]\n if too_deep:\n strikes = [v for v in strikes if v <= float(total)]\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"water_strike_below_total_depth\",\n \"Water \"\n + plural(len(too_deep), \"strike\")\n + \" at \"\n + \", \".join(f\"{v:g} m\" for v in sorted(too_deep))\n + f\" below the recorded total depth of {float(total):g} m, \"\n \"so it was not recorded; check the cell it came from.\",\n )\n )\n\n log = DrillingLog(\n site=site,\n borehole_ref=str(fields.get(\"borehole_ref\", \"\") or \"\"),\n total_depth_m=total,\n drilling_method=fields.get(\"drilling_method\", \"\"),\n intervals=sorted(intervals, key=lambda iv: iv.top_m),\n water_strikes_m=sorted(strikes),\n grouting_depth_m=fields.get(\"grouting_depth_m\"),\n installed_screens_m=parse_installed_screens(fields.get(\"installed_screens\", \"\")),\n start_date=str(fields.get(\"start_date\", \"\")),\n completion_date=str(fields.get(\"completion_date\", \"\")),\n status=fields.get(\"status\", \"\"),\n source=str(source),\n )\n\n # consistency of the interval column\n # intervals[1:] is one shorter by design: n intervals give n-1 boundaries.\n for a, b in zip(log.intervals, log.intervals[1:], strict=False):\n if b.top_m < a.bottom_m - 1e-9:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"interval_overlap\",\n f\"Depth intervals overlap at {b.top_m} m.\",\n )\n )\n elif b.top_m > a.bottom_m + 1e-9:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"interval_gap\",\n f\"Gap in the drilling log between {a.bottom_m} m and {b.top_m} m.\",\n )\n )\n if total and log.intervals and abs(log.intervals[-1].bottom_m - total) > 1e-6:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"depth_mismatch\",\n f\"Stated total depth {total} m differs from the deepest logged \"\n f\"interval {log.intervals[-1].bottom_m} m.\",\n )\n )\n if not log.intervals:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\"error\", \"no_intervals\", \"No depth intervals found in the log.\")\n )\n missing_desc = sum(1 for iv in log.intervals if not iv.description)\n if log.intervals and missing_desc:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"missing_lithology\",\n f\"{missing_desc} interval(s) have no lithology description.\",\n )\n )\n log.flags = flags\n return log\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/pumping.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Parsers for pumping test field sheets (Excel template and Word sheets).\n\nThe paper layout (WiNGiN step test sheet) records readings in side by\nside hourly column groups, each with Time (min), Water Level (m) and\nDrawdown (m), followed by a Recovery block. Two rules from the sheets\ndrive the parsing:\n\n* The recorded drawdown column is the increment between successive\n readings, not drawdown below static. Only time and water level are\n read; true drawdown is always recomputed as water level minus static\n water level.\n* Discharge is often missing. The test still parses and produces water\n level and drawdown series, but a ``missing_discharge`` flag marks all\n transmissivity and yield results as pending.\n* Units are read, not assumed. The sheet's own headings say what the\n numbers mean - \"Time (min)\", \"Discharge per step (m3/h)\" - and a crew\n that heads the column L/s or records the times in hours means exactly\n that. Both are converted to the canonical m3/h and minutes. A unit the\n toolkit cannot read is refused rather than guessed at: a discharge in an\n unreadable unit leaves the step pending, and a time column in one is\n dropped, because there is no pending state for time and every consumer\n would otherwise fit a curve to the wrong axis.\n\nTimes within each group are irregular (1, 2, 3 and 5 minute spacing);\nnothing assumes uniform sampling.\n\nTwo recovery layouts occur on real sheets and both are handled:\n\n* A dedicated recovery block with its own Time and Water Level columns,\n followed by a Recovery column and sometimes by a Drawdown column as\n well (Time / Level / Drawdown / Recovery, Kuntolo sheet). The water\n level column is read; the Drawdown and Recovery columns are increments\n between readings and are ignored, exactly as on a pumping block.\n* A single shared time column with a Recovery column that says it holds\n water levels (\"Recovery water level\"). That column is read against the\n shared times, interpreted as minutes since the pump stopped.\n\nA recovery column the sheet never explains - one sitting apart from the\nblock's own columns and headed only \"Recovery\" - is refused with a flag\nrather than read as a curve: read as levels, an increment column makes a\nrecovery that climbs a few centimetres out of a borehole tens of metres\ndeep.\n\nA constant discharge test is written in hourly blocks side by side and\neach block's elapsed time is often counted within its own hour, restarting\nat 1. The blocks are joined into one series that runs forwards, each\nblock's start taken from its own heading (\"Constant discharge 61-120 min\")\nor, failing that, from the last reading of the block before it. Read as\none column those restarts interleave into a sawtooth.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, PumpingStep, PumpingTest\nfrom ..units import Quantity, convert, read_quantity, unit_from_label\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\nfrom . import common\n\n# Free-text discharge notes: \"Constant Discharge of 2.93m3/h\", \"Q = 0.81 L/s\".\n# The unit is captured rather than assumed - the old pattern only matched an\n# m3/h tail, so a rate written in L/s was silently dropped instead of read.\n_DISCHARGE_TEXT_RE = re.compile(\n r\"discharge\\s*(?:of|0f)?\\s*[:=]?\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*\"\n r\"([a-z\u00b5\u03bc]{1,3}\\s*3?\\s*/\\s*[a-z]{1,4}|lps|lpm|lph)\",\n re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Locating the column groups\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# The heading a sheet prints over a column group - \"Constant discharge\n# 61-120 min\", \"Recovery\" - is the sheet's own statement of what the block\n# holds and which minutes of the test it covers, so both readings below take\n# the block's place in the test from it rather than from an assumption.\n_BLOCK_SPAN_RE = re.compile(\n r\"(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*(?:-|to)\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*([a-z]{1,8})?\",\n re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n\ndef _column_role(text: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"What a column's own header says the column holds.\n\n \"Recovery\" is tested before \"water level\" so a column headed \"Recovery\n water level\" is read as the recovery column it says it is, and \"drawdown\"\n before \"level\" so an increment column is never taken for a level.\n \"\"\"\n if not text:\n return \"\"\n if \"reco\" in text:\n return \"recovery\"\n if \"drawdown\" in text or \"draw down\" in text:\n return \"drawdown\"\n if \"water\" in text or text.startswith(\"level\"):\n return \"level\"\n return \"\"\n\n\ndef _block_span_min(heading: str) -> tuple[float, float] | None:\n \"\"\"The minutes a block heading says the block covers, e.g. ``(61.0, 120.0)``.\n\n ``None`` when the heading names no span, or names one in a unit that\n cannot be read: an offset applied to every reading in a block has to come\n from the sheet, never from a guess at what \"1-2\" might mean.\n \"\"\"\n match = _BLOCK_SPAN_RE.search(common.normalise_dashes(heading or \"\"))\n if match is None:\n return None\n first: float | None = float(match.group(1))\n last: float | None = float(match.group(2))\n written = (match.group(3) or \"\").strip()\n if written:\n first = convert(first, written, \"min\", dimension=\"time\")\n last = convert(last, written, \"min\", dimension=\"time\")\n if first is None or last is None or last <= first:\n return None\n return first, last\n\n\ndef _block_heading(grid: list[list], header_row: int, start: int, end: int) -> str:\n \"\"\"The heading the sheet prints above a column group (\"\" when there is none).\n\n Only the two rows immediately above the column headers are read - on the\n template the block headings sit directly over the group's own first column -\n and only a heading the reader can act on is returned: one naming the\n recovery block, or the minutes the block covers. Anything else standing\n above the table belongs to the sheet's header block (\"Discharge per step\n (m3/h)\" sits there on the template), and carrying that into a flag as if\n the crew had written it over the readings would say more than the sheet\n does.\n \"\"\"\n for r in range(header_row - 1, max(header_row - 3, -1), -1):\n row = grid[r] if r < len(grid) else []\n for cc in range(start, min(end, len(row))):\n text = clean_text(row[cc])\n if not text:\n continue\n if \"recover\" in text.lower() or _block_span_min(text) is not None:\n return text\n return \"\"\n\n\ndef _group(base: dict, level: int, kind: str, **extra) -> dict:\n \"\"\"One column group: the base fields the whole block shares, plus its own.\"\"\"\n return {**base, \"level\": level, \"kind\": kind, **extra}\n\n\ndef _find_groups(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, list[dict]] | None:\n \"\"\"Find the header row of Time / Water Level / ... column groups.\n\n Returns ``(row_index, groups)``. Each group carries its column indices, the\n header its time column declares, the heading printed above the block, and a\n ``kind``:\n\n ``\"pumping\"``\n time and water level while the pump ran.\n ``\"recovery\"``\n time and water level after it stopped. A recovery block's Drawdown and\n Recovery columns are increments between readings, so the water level\n column is the one read: a block laid out Time / Level / Drawdown /\n Recovery used to have its fourth column read as the levels, which made\n the recovery curve the increment rather than the water level (ROADMAP\n data-ingestion-10).\n ``\"recovery_unreadable\"``\n a recovery column the sheet never explains. ``_assemble`` flags it and\n reads no curve from it.\n\n A block is a recovery block when its heading or its time column says\n \"recovery\", or when its columns run Time, Water Level[, Drawdown], Recovery\n with nothing else between them. A recovery column that says it holds water\n levels (\"Recovery water level\") is instead read as a second series against\n the shared time column, which is the other layout the sheets use.\n \"\"\"\n best: tuple[int, list[dict]] | None = None\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = common.row_text(row)\n time_cols = [c for c, t in enumerate(texts) if t.startswith(\"time\")]\n if not time_cols:\n continue\n groups: list[dict] = []\n for gi, c in enumerate(time_cols):\n end = time_cols[gi + 1] if gi + 1 < len(time_cols) else len(texts)\n roles: dict[str, int] = {}\n for cc in range(c + 1, end):\n role = _column_role(texts[cc])\n if role and role not in roles:\n roles[role] = cc\n level_col = roles.get(\"level\")\n draw_col = roles.get(\"drawdown\")\n reco_col = roles.get(\"recovery\")\n if level_col is None and reco_col is None:\n continue\n # The header text travels with the group so the time unit it\n # declares - \"Time (min)\", \"Time (h)\" - is read rather than assumed,\n # and the block heading travels with it so a constant test's hourly\n # blocks can be put back in the order the sheet gives them.\n header = texts[c]\n heading = _block_heading(grid, r, c, end)\n base = {\"time\": c, \"time_header\": header, \"block_heading\": heading}\n says_recovery = \"recover\" in heading.lower() or \"recover\" in header\n reco_says_level = reco_col is not None and (\n \"level\" in texts[reco_col] or \"water\" in texts[reco_col]\n )\n\n if reco_col is None:\n groups.append(_group(base, level_col,\n \"recovery\" if says_recovery else \"pumping\"))\n elif says_recovery:\n # The sheet names the block, so its level column is the level\n # and its recovery column is an increment, as the drawdown\n # column is on a pumping block.\n groups.append(_group(\n base, level_col if level_col is not None else reco_col,\n \"recovery\"))\n elif level_col is None:\n # Nothing else in the block can be a water level, so the\n # recovery column is read as one.\n groups.append(_group(base, reco_col, \"recovery\"))\n elif reco_says_level and (\n len(time_cols) == 1 or max(level_col, reco_col) - c > 2\n ):\n # A shared time column with a recovery column that says it\n # holds levels: two series read against the same times. A\n # block with its own time column and the recovery column\n # beside it is a recovery block, not a pumping block with a\n # second series; read the other way, its water levels were\n # joined onto the drawdown curve as the next hour.\n groups.append(_group(base, level_col, \"pumping\"))\n groups.append(_group(base, reco_col, \"recovery\"))\n elif max(level_col, reco_col) - c <= 2:\n # Time, Water Level, Recovery: the recovery block the bundled\n # template prints.\n groups.append(_group(base, level_col, \"recovery\"))\n elif (level_col == c + 1 and draw_col == c + 2 and reco_col == c + 3\n and len(time_cols) > 1):\n # Time, Level, Drawdown, Recovery: a recovery block written\n # with both increment columns. Reading its fourth column as the\n # levels made the recovery curve the rise between readings\n # rather than the water level (ROADMAP data-ingestion-10). It\n # is read this way only when another group holds the pumping\n # readings; alone on a sheet the same four columns could be a\n # whole test against one time column, which is refused below.\n groups.append(_group(base, level_col, \"recovery\"))\n else:\n # A recovery column standing apart from the block's own\n # columns: it may hold levels or increments and the sheet does\n # not say which, so the pumping pair is read and the recovery\n # column is refused by name.\n groups.append(_group(base, level_col, \"pumping\"))\n groups.append(_group(base, reco_col, \"recovery_unreadable\",\n recovery_header=clean_text(row[reco_col])))\n if groups and (best is None or len(groups) > len(best[1])):\n best = (r, groups)\n return best\n\n\ndef _read_series(\n grid: list[list], header_row: int, group: dict\n) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, str, list[str]]:\n \"\"\"Read one Time / Water Level pair, with the times put into minutes.\n\n Returns ``(times_min, levels, time_unit, skipped)``. ``time_unit`` is the\n unit the column declared; it is empty when nothing was declared (minutes\n assumed) and ``\"?\"`` when the *header* declared one that could not\n be read - in which case the caller must drop the group rather than treat\n unknown units as minutes. Unlike discharge, there is no \"pending\" state\n for time: every consumer would silently produce wrong transmissivities.\n\n ``skipped`` lists individual cells whose own text could not be read; they\n cost one reading each rather than the column, and the caller reports\n them.\n \"\"\"\n header = group.get(\"time_header\", \"\")\n # A unit the header declares applies to the whole column, so an\n # unreadable one there costs the group. A unit written into one cell\n # applies to that cell, so an unreadable one there costs one reading -\n # otherwise a single annotated entry (\"5 (approx)\") threw away the test.\n declared, header_unit = unit_from_label(header, dimension=\"time\")\n if declared and header_unit is None:\n return (np.array([], dtype=float), np.array([], dtype=float),\n f\"?{declared}\", [])\n\n times, levels, skipped = [], [], []\n unit_text = declared\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n cell = row[group[\"time\"]] if group[\"time\"] < len(row) else None\n wl = parse_number(row[group[\"level\"]]) if group[\"level\"] < len(row) else None\n quantity = read_quantity(cell, header, dimension=\"time\")\n if quantity.status == \"absent\" or wl is None:\n continue\n if quantity.status == \"unknown\":\n # one unreadable reading, not a broken column - but never silent\n skipped.append(str(cell))\n continue\n if quantity.unit_text:\n unit_text = quantity.unit_text\n times.append(quantity.value)\n levels.append(wl)\n return (np.array(times, dtype=float), np.array(levels, dtype=float),\n unit_text, skipped)\n\n\n_STEP_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*step\\s*\\d*\\s*q\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\n\n\ndef _row_unit_hint(row: list) -> str:\n \"\"\"The row's own leading label, e.g. 'Discharge per step (m3/h)'.\"\"\"\n for cell in row:\n text = clean_text(cell)\n if text and \"discharge\" in text.lower():\n return text\n return \"\"\n\n\ndef _find_step_discharges(grid: list[list]) -> dict[int, \"Quantity\"]:\n \"\"\"Read per step discharge from 'Step n Q' labelled cells.\n\n Two hazards on a real sheet, both handled here:\n\n * The rate is written in whatever unit the crew used. The unit is taken\n from the value cell, then the label, then the row's discharge caption,\n and the value is converted to m3/h. A unit that cannot be read is\n refused, which routes the step into the existing \"discharge missing,\n results pending\" path rather than producing a wrong transmissivity.\n * The neighbouring cell may be the *next* step's label rather than a\n value. Scanning it blindly read \"Step 2 Q (m3/h)\" as a discharge of\n 2 m3/h whenever the first step's box was left empty, and fitted a\n transmissivity to it. Label-shaped cells are skipped.\n \"\"\"\n discharges: dict[int, Quantity] = {}\n for row in grid:\n row_hint = _row_unit_hint(row)\n for c, cell in enumerate(row):\n label = clean_text(cell)\n if not _STEP_LABEL_RE.match(label):\n continue\n num = parse_number(label.lower().split(\"q\")[0])\n if num is None:\n continue\n for cc in range(c + 1, min(c + 3, len(row))):\n neighbour = row[cc]\n if _STEP_LABEL_RE.match(clean_text(neighbour)):\n break # the next step's label, not this step's value\n quantity = read_quantity(\n neighbour, label, row_hint, dimension=\"flow\"\n )\n if quantity.status == \"absent\":\n continue\n discharges[int(num)] = quantity\n break\n return discharges\n\n\ndef _discharge_candidates_from_text(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[list[float], list[str]]:\n \"\"\"Discharge values mentioned in free text such as\n 'Constant Discharge of 2.93m3/h'.\n\n Returns ``(values_in_m3_per_h, unreadable_unit_texts)``. A note whose\n unit cannot be read is reported rather than converted, so it can be\n raised as a flag instead of quietly becoming a number in m3/h.\n \"\"\"\n found: list[float] = []\n unreadable: list[str] = []\n for row in grid:\n for cell in row:\n if cell is None or isinstance(cell, (int, float)):\n continue\n for m in _DISCHARGE_TEXT_RE.finditer(str(cell)):\n written = m.group(2).strip()\n value = convert(float(m.group(1)), written, \"m3/h\", dimension=\"flow\")\n if value is None:\n if written not in unreadable:\n unreadable.append(written)\n continue\n if value not in found:\n found.append(value)\n return found, unreadable\n\n\n# Pre-printed text that names a test kind without recording which test was\n# run: the template's own title mentions both, and its constant-discharge\n# column labels (\"Constant discharge 61-120 min\") sit on every sheet whatever\n# was pumped. Reading either as an answer turned step tests into constant ones.\n_CONSTANT_COLUMN_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"constant\\s+discharge\\s*\\d\")\n\n\ndef _sheet_test_type(grid: list[list]) -> str:\n \"\"\"Look for 'STEP TEST' or 'CONSTANT DISCHARGE' banners in the sheet.\n\n Only decisive text counts. A cell naming both kinds is a form title\n (\"PUMPING TEST FIELD SHEET (STEP / CONSTANT DISCHARGE)\"), and a\n constant-discharge column label is a heading for one of the hourly\n groups - neither says which test the crew actually ran.\n \"\"\"\n for row in grid:\n for cell in row:\n text = clean_text(cell).lower()\n if not text:\n continue\n step_words = \"step test\" in text or \"step drawdown\" in text\n constant_words = (\n \"constant discharge\" in text or \"constant rate\" in text\n )\n # \"(STEP / CONSTANT DISCHARGE)\" offers both; any mention of a step\n # alongside constant wording makes the cell a title, not an answer\n if constant_words and \"step\" in text:\n continue\n if step_words:\n return \"step\"\n if constant_words and not _CONSTANT_COLUMN_LABEL_RE.search(text):\n return \"constant\"\n return \"\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Assembling the PumpingTest\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _join_constant_blocks(\n blocks: list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, dict]],\n) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list[str], list[str]]:\n \"\"\"Join the hourly blocks of a constant discharge test into one series.\n\n A constant discharge sheet is written in hourly column groups side by side\n and each group's elapsed time is often counted within its own hour: 1, 2, 3\n in the first block and 1, 2, 3 again in the second. Concatenating the\n groups and sorting the result interleaved them into a sawtooth - minute 1\n of every hour, then minute 2 of every hour - and every drawdown curve and\n every transmissivity fitted to it was wrong (ROADMAP data-ingestion-10).\n\n Each block's place in the test is read off the sheet: the minutes its own\n heading names (\"Constant discharge 61-120 min\"), or, when the heading names\n none, the last reading of the block before it, which is what a block whose\n times go backwards continues from. A block that is neither - one starting\n inside the readings already taken and running past them - is left out and\n named, because a block placed at a minute nobody can check produces a curve\n nobody can trust.\n\n Returns ``(times_min, levels, joined, dropped)``. ``joined`` and ``dropped``\n are sentences naming what was done, for the caller to raise as flags.\n \"\"\"\n times: list[np.ndarray] = []\n levels: list[np.ndarray] = []\n joined: list[str] = []\n dropped: list[str] = []\n end: float | None = None\n for number, (t, wl, group) in enumerate(blocks, start=1):\n heading = str(group.get(\"block_heading\", \"\") or \"\")\n span = _block_span_min(heading)\n first = float(t[0])\n offset = 0.0\n # The sentence describing the shift is held back until the block has\n # actually been kept. Appended where the offset is worked out, a block\n # that the backwards check below then drops was named in both flags at\n # once, and the report said in one sentence that the block had been\n # joined with so many minutes added and in the next that it had been\n # left out (ROADMAP data-ingestion-10).\n note = \"\"\n if span is not None and first < span[0]:\n offset = span[0] - first\n note = (\n f\"block {number} counts its time within its own hour from \"\n f\"{first:g} min and its heading '{heading}' covers {span[0]:g} \"\n f\"to {span[1]:g} min, so {offset:g} min were added to it\"\n )\n elif span is not None or end is None or first > end:\n offset = 0.0\n elif float(t.max()) <= end:\n offset = end\n note = (\n f\"block {number} restarts its time at {first:g} min, inside the \"\n f\"{end:g} min already read, and its heading names no minutes, so \"\n f\"it was read as continuing from the last reading before it and \"\n f\"{offset:g} min were added to it\"\n )\n else:\n dropped.append(\n f\"Block {number} of the constant discharge readings starts at \"\n f\"{first:g} min, inside the {end:g} min already read, and runs \"\n f\"past them to {float(t.max()):g} min, so the sheet does not say \"\n \"whether its times count from the start of the test or from the \"\n \"start of the block.\"\n )\n continue\n shifted = t + offset\n if end is not None and float(shifted[0]) < end:\n dropped.append(\n f\"Block {number} of the constant discharge readings still starts \"\n f\"at {float(shifted[0]):g} min once placed, before the {end:g} \"\n \"min already read, so its readings would run backwards into the \"\n \"block before it.\"\n )\n continue\n if note:\n joined.append(note)\n times.append(shifted)\n levels.append(wl)\n end = float(shifted.max())\n if not times:\n empty = np.array([], dtype=float)\n return empty, empty, joined, dropped\n all_t = np.concatenate(times)\n all_wl = np.concatenate(levels)\n order = np.argsort(all_t, kind=\"stable\")\n return all_t[order], all_wl[order], joined, dropped\n\n\ndef _assemble(grid: list[list], source: str) -> PumpingTest:\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid, max_rows=len(grid))\n site = common.site_from_fields(fields, source=source)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n\n located = _find_groups(grid)\n if located is None:\n raise ValueError(f\"No Time/Water Level column groups found in {source}\")\n header_row, groups = located\n\n for group in groups:\n if group[\"kind\"] != \"recovery_unreadable\":\n continue\n # The sheet carries a recovery column but never says what is in it, and\n # a recovery curve drawn from increments is wrong by the whole depth to\n # water. Refusing it and naming it is the only honest answer (ROADMAP\n # data-ingestion-10).\n where = (f\" in the '{group['block_heading']}' block\"\n if group[\"block_heading\"] else \"\")\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"recovery_layout_unreadable\",\n f\"A column headed '{group.get('recovery_header', '')}' stands \"\n f\"apart from the water level column{where}, and nothing on the \"\n \"sheet says whether it holds water levels or the rise between \"\n \"readings, so no recovery curve was read from it. Head the \"\n \"recovery block 'Recovery', or the column 'Recovery water \"\n \"level (m)'.\",\n )\n )\n\n def _series(kind: str) -> list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, dict]]:\n \"\"\"Read every column group of one kind, dropping unreadable-unit ones.\n\n A time column whose unit cannot be read is dropped rather than taken\n as minutes: reading hours as minutes would rescale every drawdown\n curve and every transmissivity fitted to it, silently.\n\n Each block is handed back with the group it came from, because a\n constant test's blocks are placed by the heading the sheet prints over\n them before they are joined into one series.\n \"\"\"\n out = []\n for group in groups:\n if group[\"kind\"] != kind:\n continue\n t, wl, unit_text, skipped = _read_series(grid, header_row, group)\n if unit_text.startswith(\"?\"):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"time_unit_unknown\",\n f\"The {kind} time column is headed \"\n f\"'{group.get('time_header', '')}' and its unit \"\n f\"'{unit_text[1:]}' could not be read, so the readings \"\n \"were not used. Name a fracture \"\n \"zone with its depths in the description (fracture zone 49-52 m) and, \"\n \"once the casing is set, the screens installed as ranges (25-35; 48-53).\"\n )).font = Font(italic=True, size=9)\n for col, width in zip(\"ABCDEFG\", (18, 10, 10, 20, 42, 18, 20), strict=True):\n ws.column_dimensions[col].width = width\n wb.save(path)\n return Path(path)\n\n\ndef write_daily_log_template(path: str | Path, n_rows: int = 14) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Driller's daily report template.\n\n The daily record the supervision guidance expects: per interval\n times, depths, formation, water strikes and airlift yield, plus\n the day totals, standing time and the double signature (rig\n operator and supervisor) that makes the log auditable against\n invoiced metres.\n \"\"\"\n wb = Workbook()\n ws = wb.active\n ws.title = \"Daily Log\"\n _title(ws, \"A1\", \"DRILLER'S DAILY REPORT\", \"A1:G1\")\n pairs = [\n (\"A2\", \"Community\", \"B2\"), (\"D2\", \"Borehole Ref. No.\", \"E2\"),\n (\"A3\", \"Date\", \"B3\"), (\"D3\", \"Drill rig\", \"E3\"),\n (\"A4\", \"Contractor\", \"B4\"), (\"D4\", \"Supervisor\", \"E4\"),\n (\"A5\", \"Weather / site conditions\", \"B5\"), (\"D5\", \"Record taker\", \"E5\"),\n ]\n for lab_cell, lab, val_cell in pairs:\n _label(ws, lab_cell, lab)\n _value(ws, val_cell)\n _table_header(\n ws,\n 7,\n [\n \"Time from\",\n \"Time to\",\n \"Depth from (m)\",\n \"Depth to (m)\",\n \"Formation / activity\",\n \"Water strike (m)\",\n \"Airlift yield (L/s)\",\n ],\n )\n for r in range(8, 8 + n_rows):\n for c in range(1, 8):\n ws.cell(row=r, column=c).border = BORDER\n totals_row = 9 + n_rows\n for cell, label in (\n (f\"A{totals_row}\", \"Metres drilled today\"),\n (f\"C{totals_row}\", \"Cumulative metres\"),\n (f\"E{totals_row}\", \"Casing installed today (m)\"),\n (f\"A{totals_row + 1}\", \"Standing / breakdown hours\"),\n (f\"C{totals_row + 1}\", \"Reason\"),\n ):\n _label(ws, cell, label)\n for cell in (f\"B{totals_row}\", f\"D{totals_row}\", f\"F{totals_row}\",\n f\"B{totals_row + 1}\", f\"D{totals_row + 1}\"):\n _value(ws, cell)\n sign_row = totals_row + 3\n for cell, label in (\n (f\"A{sign_row}\", \"Rig operator signature\"),\n (f\"D{sign_row}\", \"Supervisor signature\"),\n ):\n _label(ws, cell, label)\n _value(ws, cell.replace(\"A\", \"B\").replace(\"D\", \"E\"))\n ws.cell(row=sign_row + 2, column=1, value=(\n \"Notes: one row per drilled interval or activity (moving, standing, \"\n \"casing).
