Both signatures are required every day; the office checks \"\n \"invoiced metres against these logs.\"\n )).font = Font(italic=True, size=9)\n for col, width in zip(\"ABCDEFG\", (12, 12, 14, 14, 40, 16, 16), strict=True):\n ws.column_dimensions[col].width = width\n wb.save(path)\n return Path(path)\n\n\nSTANDARD_PARAMETERS = [\n (\"pH\", \"pH units\"), (\"Electrical conductivity\", \"uS/cm\"), (\"TDS\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Turbidity\", \"NTU\"), (\"Temperature\", \"deg C\"), (\"Total hardness\", \"mg/L as CaCO3\"),\n (\"Alkalinity\", \"mg/L as CaCO3\"), (\"Calcium\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Magnesium\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Sodium\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Potassium\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Bicarbonate\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Chloride\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Sulfate\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Nitrate (as NO3)\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Nitrite (as NO2)\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Ammonia (as N)\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Fluoride\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Iron\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Manganese\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Arsenic\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Lead\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Copper\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Zinc\", \"mg/L\"), (\"Chromium (total)\", \"mg/L\"),\n (\"Cadmium\", \"mg/L\"), (\"E. coli\", \"CFU/100 mL\"), (\"Total coliforms\", \"CFU/100 mL\"),\n]\n\n\ndef write_quality_template(path: str | Path) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Water quality laboratory results template.\"\"\"\n wb = Workbook()\n ws = wb.active\n ws.title = \"Water Quality\"\n _title(ws, \"A1\", \"WATER QUALITY LABORATORY RESULTS\", \"A1:E1\")\n pairs = [\n (\"A2\", \"Community\", \"B2\"), (\"D2\", \"Client\", \"E2\"),\n (\"A3\", \"Sample ID\", \"B3\"), (\"D3\", \"Borehole Ref. No.\", \"E3\"),\n (\"A4\", \"Sample date\", \"B4\"), (\"D4\", \"Laboratory\", \"E4\"),\n (\"A5\", \"District\", \"B5\"), (\"D5\", \"Project\", \"E5\"),\n ]\n for lab_cell, lab, val_cell in pairs:\n _label(ws, lab_cell, lab)\n _value(ws, val_cell)\n _table_header(\n ws, 7, [\"Parameter\", \"Unit\", \"Value\", \"Detection limit\", \"Method\"]\n )\n for i, (param, unit) in enumerate(STANDARD_PARAMETERS):\n r = 8 + i\n ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value=param).border = BORDER\n ws.cell(row=r, column=2, value=unit).border = BORDER\n for c in (3, 4, 5):\n ws.cell(row=r, column=c).border = BORDER\n ws.cell(row=9 + len(STANDARD_PARAMETERS), column=1, value=(\n \"Notes: for results below detection write
list[Path]:\n \"\"\"Write every field template into ``folder`` and return the paths.\"\"\"\n folder = Path(folder)\n folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n return [\n write_ves_template(folder / \"template_ves.xlsx\"),\n write_pumping_template(folder / \"template_pumping_test.xlsx\"),\n write_drilling_template(folder / \"template_drilling_log.xlsx\"),\n write_quality_template(folder / \"template_water_quality.xlsx\"),\n write_daily_log_template(folder / \"template_daily_drilling_report.xlsx\"),\n ]\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/ves.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Parser for VES field data sheets (Excel and CSV).\n\nReads the Rokel style layout: a header block (client, community,\ndistrict, sounding number, GPS east/north, elevation, date, field\nsupervisor) followed by a table with columns No., AB/2 (m), MN (m) and\napparent resistivity (ohm-m). Values stored as text with leading\nzeros (for example ``078.7`` or GPS ``0708958``) parse cleanly.\n\nDuplicate AB/2 values with different MN mark Schlumberger segment\nchanges; both readings are kept.\n\nBoth of the arrays the toolkit models are read. Which one a sheet was\nrun with is worked out from the sheet itself - the array field in the\nheader block, the wording above the table, a spacing column headed\n\"a\", and whether there is an MN column at all - and a Wenner sounding\nis stored the way ``array_type == \"wenner\"`` means everywhere else:\n``ab2`` holds the Wenner spacing a. Where the sheet settles none of\nthat the Schlumberger default stands and a flag says it was assumed.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..ves.arrays import geometric_factor\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, VESSounding\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\nfrom . import common\n\n# \"MN/2\", \"MN / 2\", \"MN /2 (m)\" - a typed header keeps its spaces\n_MN_HALF_RE = re.compile(r\"mn\\s*/\\s*2\")\n# \"Resistance (ohm)\", \"R (ohm)\", \"V/I\", \"dV/I\", \"\u0394V/I\": a measured resistance\n_RESISTANCE_RE = re.compile(r\"resistance|^r\\s*\\(|v\\s*/\\s*i\")\n\n# The array a sheet names, wherever on the sheet it names it: the title of a\n# template (\"SCHLUMBERGER ARRAY VES FIELD DATA\"), the array field itself, or\n# a note. \"Wenner alpha\" and \"half-Schlumberger\" are the same two arrays.\n_WENNER_RE = re.compile(r\"wenner\")\n_SCHLUMBERGER_RE = re.compile(r\"schlum\")\n\n# \"a\" is the whole name of the Wenner spacing, so the column header is short\n# and the reader has to accept the few ways a crew writes it out.\n_WENNER_A_HEADERS = frozenset({\n \"a\", \"a (m)\", \"a(m)\", \"a m\", \"a, m\", \"a (metres)\", \"a (meters)\",\n \"a-spacing\", \"a-spacing (m)\", \"a spacing\", \"a spacing (m)\",\n \"spacing a\", \"spacing a (m)\", \"wenner a\", \"wenner a (m)\", \"a (wenner)\",\n})\n\n# A Wenner array is A M N B at equal spacing a, so AB = 3a and a Wenner sheet\n# that tabulates AB/2 has written 1.5 a in that column.\n_WENNER_AB2_PER_A = 1.5\n\n\ndef _array_named_in(text: str) -> str | None:\n \"\"\"The array a piece of sheet text names, or ``None``.\n\n ``None`` covers both the text that names no array and the text that\n names two: an unfilled \"Schlumberger / Wenner\" template choice settles\n nothing, and reading it as either would be a guess.\n \"\"\"\n lowered = text.lower()\n wenner = bool(_WENNER_RE.search(lowered))\n schlumberger = bool(_SCHLUMBERGER_RE.search(lowered))\n if wenner == schlumberger:\n return None\n return \"wenner\" if wenner else \"schlumberger\"\n\n\ndef _array_named_above_table(grid: list[list], header_row: int) -> str | None:\n \"\"\"The array the wording above the data table names, if only one is named.\"\"\"\n found: set[str] = set()\n for row in grid[:header_row]:\n for text in common.row_text(row):\n if _WENNER_RE.search(text):\n found.add(\"wenner\")\n if _SCHLUMBERGER_RE.search(text):\n found.add(\"schlumberger\")\n return next(iter(found)) if len(found) == 1 else None\n\n\ndef _detect_array(\n grid: list[list], header_row: int, cols: dict, fields: dict\n) -> tuple[str, list[DataFlag]]:\n \"\"\"The array a sheet was run with, and the flags reading it raised.\n\n The forward model, the inversion, the splice and the curve plot all\n branch on ``array_type``, but the reader never looked at the sheet for\n it beyond copying out the array field: a Wenner sounding had no\n ingestion path, and a Wenner sheet headed AB/2 was inverted with AB/2\n for the spacing a (ROADMAP data-ingestion-11). That is wrong by tens of\n percent and nothing downstream can notice.\n\n The sheet is asked in the order its answers are worth trusting: the\n array field of the header block, then any other wording above the table\n (a template title is boilerplate, so it only speaks when the field is\n silent), then the table's own columns - a spacing column headed \"a\" is\n the Wenner spacing, and an MN column is the Schlumberger one. Where the\n sheet settles nothing, or contradicts itself, the Schlumberger default\n stands and a flag says what was assumed and why, because an assumption\n made in silence is how the wrong array reaches a client report.\n \"\"\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n declared_text = clean_text(fields.get(\"array_type\", \"\"))\n declared = _array_named_in(declared_text)\n named = declared if declared is not None else _array_named_above_table(grid, header_row)\n from_columns = (\n \"wenner\" if \"a\" in cols\n else \"schlumberger\" if (\"mn\" in cols or \"mn_half\" in cols)\n else None\n )\n\n conflicted = named == \"schlumberger\" and from_columns == \"wenner\"\n array_type = \"schlumberger\" if conflicted else (named or from_columns or \"schlumberger\")\n\n if conflicted:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\n \"warning\", \"array_type_conflict\",\n \"The sheet names the Schlumberger array but heads its spacing \"\n \"column \\\"a\\\", which is the Wenner spacing; the two readings of \"\n \"the same column differ by half again. The sounding was read as \"\n \"Schlumberger, with that column taken as AB/2. Confirm the array \"\n \"with the field crew before the model is used.\",\n ))\n elif declared_text and declared is None:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\n \"warning\", \"array_type_unrecognised\",\n f\"The sheet's array field reads \\\"{declared_text}\\\", which does \"\n \"not name one of the two arrays this toolkit models \"\n \"(Schlumberger and Wenner); the sounding was read as \"\n f\"{array_type.capitalize()}. Confirm the array with the field \"\n \"crew: the wrong forward model is wrong by tens of percent.\",\n ))\n elif named is None and from_columns is None:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\n \"warning\", \"array_type_assumed\",\n \"The sheet does not say which electrode array was used, and its \"\n \"columns do not settle it either: there is no MN column, which a \"\n \"Schlumberger sheet carries, and no \\\"a\\\" column, which a Wenner \"\n \"sheet carries. Schlumberger was assumed, as the toolkit's \"\n \"default. Confirm the array with the field crew: a Wenner \"\n \"sounding inverted as Schlumberger is wrong by tens of percent \"\n \"and nothing further down the chain can notice.\",\n ))\n elif named is None and from_columns == \"wenner\":\n flags.append(DataFlag(\n \"info\", \"array_type_inferred\",\n \"No array is named on the sheet; its spacing column is headed \"\n \"\\\"a\\\", which is the Wenner spacing, so the sounding was read as \"\n \"Wenner.\",\n ))\n return array_type, flags\n\n\ndef _find_data_header(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:\n \"\"\"Locate the data table header row and map columns.\n\n Returns (row_index, {\"no\": c, \"ab2\": c, \"a\": c, \"mn\": c, \"rho\": c}).\n \"\"\"\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = common.row_text(row)\n cols: dict[str, int] = {}\n for c, t in enumerate(texts):\n if not t:\n continue\n if \"ab/2\" in t or t == \"ab2\" or \"ab / 2\" in t:\n cols[\"ab2\"] = c\n # The Wenner spacing column, headed \"a\" or \"a (m)\", meant nothing\n # to the reader at all, so a Wenner sheet was dropped whole as\n # having no data table (ROADMAP data-ingestion-11)\n elif t in _WENNER_A_HEADERS:\n cols[\"a\"] = c\n # half-MN first, and tolerant of the spaces a typed header carries:\n # \"MN / 2 (m)\" does not contain the literal \"/2\", so it used to fall\n # through to the full-MN branch and halve every potential spacing\n elif t.startswith(\"mn\") and _MN_HALF_RE.search(t):\n cols[\"mn_half\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"mn\"):\n cols[\"mn\"] = c\n # a sheet that records V/I (a resistance, in ohms) is not a\n # resistivity sheet: \"R (ohm)\" used to match the \"ohm\" test below\n # and every reading came through as a resistivity of 0.9\n elif _RESISTANCE_RE.search(t):\n cols[\"resistance\"] = c\n elif (\n \"resistivity\" in t or t.startswith(\"rho\") or \"ohm\" in t\n or \"apparent\" in t or \"\u03c1\" in t or \"\u03c9\" in t\n ):\n cols[\"rho\"] = c\n elif t in (\"k\", \"k (m)\", \"k(m)\", \"geometric factor\"):\n cols[\"k\"] = c\n elif t in (\"no.\", \"no\", \"reading\", \"n\"):\n cols[\"no\"] = c\n if (\"ab2\" in cols or \"a\" in cols) and (\"rho\" in cols or \"resistance\" in cols):\n return r, cols\n return None\n\n\ndef _sounding_from_grid(\n grid: list[list], source: str, sheet_name: str = \"\"\n) -> VESSounding | None:\n sounding, _ = _sounding_or_reason(grid, source, sheet_name)\n return sounding\n\n\ndef _sounding_or_reason(\n grid: list[list], source: str, sheet_name: str = \"\"\n) -> tuple[VESSounding | None, str]:\n \"\"\"The sounding on a sheet, or the reason there is none.\n\n A sheet the reader could not use was dropped without a word, so a\n three-sheet workbook with one mislabelled sheet came back as two\n soundings and nothing said so.\n \"\"\"\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid)\n site = common.site_from_fields(fields, source=source)\n located = _find_data_header(grid)\n if located is None:\n return None, (\n \"no data table found: a header row needs an AB/2 column (or the \"\n \"Wenner spacing column \\\"a\\\") and an apparent-resistivity column \"\n \"(Resistivity, Rho, ohm.m, \u03c1 or \u03a9)\"\n )\n header_row, cols = located\n\n array_type, flags = _detect_array(grid, header_row, cols, fields)\n is_wenner = array_type.startswith(\"wenner\")\n\n ab2, mn, rho = [], [], []\n mn_is_half = \"mn\" not in cols and \"mn_half\" in cols\n mn_col = cols.get(\"mn\", cols.get(\"mn_half\"))\n from_resistance = \"rho\" not in cols\n value_col = cols[\"rho\"] if not from_resistance else cols[\"resistance\"]\n k_col = cols.get(\"k\")\n # The spacing column. A Wenner sheet with its own \"a\" column is read from\n # it as it stands; anything else is read from AB/2, which on a Wenner\n # sheet is 1.5 a and has to be converted below.\n if is_wenner and \"a\" in cols:\n spacing_col, wenner_from_ab2 = cols[\"a\"], False\n elif \"ab2\" in cols:\n spacing_col, wenner_from_ab2 = cols[\"ab2\"], is_wenner\n else:\n spacing_col, wenner_from_ab2 = cols[\"a\"], False\n blank_run = 0\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n a = parse_number(row[spacing_col]) if spacing_col < len(row) else None\n r = parse_number(row[value_col]) if value_col < len(row) else None\n m = (\n parse_number(row[mn_col])\n if mn_col is not None and mn_col < len(row)\n else None\n )\n if a is not None and wenner_from_ab2:\n # The sheet is Wenner but tabulates AB/2, and AB = 3a, so the\n # column holds 1.5 a. Taken for the spacing a, as it used to be\n # (ROADMAP data-ingestion-11), every reading sits at half again\n # its true spacing and the whole curve shifts along the depth\n # axis. Convert once, here, so ab2 means what the forward model,\n # the inversion and the plots take it to mean for a Wenner\n # sounding: the spacing a.\n a = a / _WENNER_AB2_PER_A\n if from_resistance and a is not None and r is not None:\n # rho_a = K * (dV/I): use the sheet's own K column when it has\n # one, otherwise the geometric factor of the array the sheet was\n # run with. The Wenner factor is 2 pi a and needs no MN, which is\n # as well: a Wenner sheet does not carry an MN column, so the\n # Schlumberger factor left K unknown and the row was dropped.\n k = parse_number(row[k_col]) if k_col is not None and k_col < len(row) else None\n if k is None and is_wenner:\n k = float(geometric_factor(\"wenner\", a=a))\n elif k is None:\n spacing = 2.0 * m if (m is not None and mn_is_half) else m\n if spacing:\n k = float(geometric_factor(\"schlumberger\", ab2=a, mn=spacing))\n r = k * r if k else None\n if a is None and r is None:\n fully_blank = all(v is None or clean_text(v) == \"\" for v in row)\n if ab2 and fully_blank:\n # Tolerate an isolated blank spacer row inside the table -\n # field sheets routinely leave one at a Schlumberger MN segment\n # change. Only two consecutive fully-blank rows mark the true\n # end of the table, so the deep branch after a spacer is kept.\n blank_run += 1\n if blank_run >= 2:\n break\n continue\n if a is None or r is None:\n continue\n blank_run = 0\n if m is not None and mn_is_half:\n m = 2.0 * m\n ab2.append(a)\n mn.append(m if m is not None else np.nan)\n rho.append(r)\n\n if not ab2:\n return None, (\n \"the data table has a header but no numeric rows; if the cells \"\n \"hold formulas, open the workbook in Excel and save it so the \"\n \"values are stored\"\n )\n if wenner_from_ab2:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\n \"info\", \"wenner_spacing_from_ab2\",\n \"The sheet is a Wenner sounding tabulated as AB/2. The Wenner \"\n \"array has AB = 3a, so each spacing was read as a = two thirds of \"\n \"the tabulated AB/2, which is the spacing the Wenner geometric \"\n \"factor and forward model take.\",\n ))\n if from_resistance:\n flags.append(DataFlag(\n \"info\", \"rho_computed_from_resistance\",\n \"The sheet records a resistance (V/I), not a resistivity; apparent \"\n \"resistivity was computed as K x R from the electrode spacings\"\n + (\"\" if k_col is None else \" and the sheet's K column\") + \".\",\n ))\n\n sounding_id = str(fields.get(\"sounding_id\", \"\") or sheet_name or \"VES 1\")\n sounding = VESSounding(\n site=site,\n sounding_id=sounding_id if sounding_id else \"VES 1\",\n ab2=np.array(ab2),\n mn=np.array(mn),\n rho_app=np.array(rho),\n array_type=array_type,\n instrument=fields.get(\"instrument\", \"\"),\n source=str(source),\n )\n\n # Data quality checks\n if np.any(sounding.rho_app <= 0):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"nonpositive_resistivity\",\n \"Apparent resistivity values must be positive.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n if np.any(np.diff(sounding.ab2) < 0):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"ab2_not_sorted\",\n \"AB/2 values are not in increasing order; check the sheet.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n finite_mn = sounding.mn[np.isfinite(sounding.mn)]\n if len(finite_mn) and np.any(sounding.ab2[np.isfinite(sounding.mn)] <= finite_mn / 2):\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"mn_exceeds_ab\",\n \"MN/2 is not smaller than AB/2 for some readings.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n dup = _duplicate_ab2_count(sounding.ab2)\n if dup:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"segment_overlap\",\n f\"{dup} AB/2 value(s) repeated with different MN (segment changes); \"\n \"both readings kept.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n discrepant = _overlap_discrepancies(sounding.ab2, sounding.rho_app)\n if discrepant:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"segment_overlap_discrepancy\",\n \"At an MN change the two readings at one AB/2 should agree \"\n \"within a few percent; these differ by more than \"\n f\"{(OVERLAP_DISCREPANCY_RATIO - 1) * 100:.0f} percent: \"\n + \"; \".join(discrepant)\n + \". That is a field problem (potential-electrode contact, \"\n \"lateral inhomogeneity at the new MN) or a transcription \"\n \"slip, and the inversion merges the pair by geometric \"\n \"mean, so part of the model misfit is made by the splice. \"\n \"Check the sheet before relying on the deep branch.\",\n sounding.sounding_id,\n )\n )\n sounding.flags = flags\n return sounding, \"\"\n\n\n# Readings at one AB/2 taken with two MN spacings should agree closely; a\n# ratio beyond this is not the segment shift the splice is built for.\nOVERLAP_DISCREPANCY_RATIO = 1.2\n\n\ndef _overlap_discrepancies(ab2: np.ndarray, rho: np.ndarray) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"Overlap pairs whose readings disagree by more than the ratio, as\n \"AB/2 40 m: 156.1 and 78.7 ohm-m (ratio 1.98)\".\"\"\"\n out: list[str] = []\n for value in np.unique(ab2):\n readings = rho[(ab2 == value) & np.isfinite(rho) & (rho > 0)]\n if len(readings) < 2:\n continue\n ratio = float(np.max(readings) / np.min(readings))\n if ratio > OVERLAP_DISCREPANCY_RATIO:\n pair = \" and \".join(f\"{r:g}\" for r in readings[:2])\n out.append(f\"AB/2 {value:g} m: {pair} ohm-m (ratio {ratio:.2f})\")\n return out\n\n\ndef _duplicate_ab2_count(ab2: np.ndarray) -> int:\n unique, counts = np.unique(ab2, return_counts=True)\n return int(np.sum(counts > 1))\n\n\ndef read_ves_workbook(\n path: str | Path, skipped: list[DataFlag] | None = None\n) -> list[VESSounding]:\n \"\"\"Read every sounding in a VES workbook (one worksheet per sounding).\n\n A sheet that yields no sounding is skipped; pass ``skipped`` to be told\n which sheets and why (one warning flag per sheet), so a mislabelled\n sheet in a three-sheet workbook does not vanish silently.\n \"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n soundings = []\n for name in common.sheet_names(path):\n grid, title = common.load_grid(path, sheet=name)\n sounding, reason = _sounding_or_reason(grid, source=str(path), sheet_name=title)\n if sounding is not None:\n soundings.append(sounding)\n elif skipped is not None:\n skipped.append(DataFlag(\n \"warning\", \"sheet_skipped\",\n f\"Sheet '{title}' was skipped: {reason}.\",\n ))\n return soundings\n\n\ndef read_ves_csv(path: str | Path) -> VESSounding:\n \"\"\"Read a single sounding from CSV (same layout as one worksheet).\"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8-sig\") as fh:\n grid = [row for row in csv.reader(fh)]\n grid = [[cell if cell != \"\" else None for cell in row] for row in grid]\n sounding = _sounding_from_grid(grid, source=str(path), sheet_name=path.stem)\n if sounding is None:\n raise ValueError(f\"No VES data table found in {path}\")\n return sounding\n"}, "groundwater/ingestion/waterquality.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Parser for water quality laboratory result sheets.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualityResult, WaterQualitySample\nfrom ..utils import clean_text, parse_number\nfrom . import common\n\n\ndef _find_results_header(grid: list[list]) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:\n for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n texts = common.row_text(row)\n cols: dict[str, int] = {}\n for c, t in enumerate(texts):\n if not t:\n continue\n if t.startswith(\"parameter\") or t.startswith(\"determinand\"):\n cols[\"parameter\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"unit\"):\n cols[\"unit\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"value\") or t.startswith(\"result\"):\n cols[\"value\"] = c\n elif \"detection\" in t or t == \"dl\":\n cols[\"dl\"] = c\n elif t.startswith(\"method\"):\n cols[\"method\"] = c\n if \"parameter\" in cols and \"value\" in cols:\n return r, cols\n return None\n\n\n#: What a laboratory writes for \"nothing found\": read as a below-detection\n#: result with no stated limit, which the assessment then judges by the\n#: parameter (a microbiological count with nothing in 100 mL meets its\n#: guideline; a chemical determinand still needs the method's limit).\nABSENCE_TOKENS = frozenset({\n \"absent\", \"nd\", \"n.d\", \"n/d\", \"nil\", \"none\", \"not detected\", \"none detected\",\n \"bdl\", \"below detection\", \"below detection limit\", \"[a-z][a-z.\\s/]*?)\\s*[(\\[]?\\s*\\d+(?:[.,]\\d+)?)\\s*[)\\]]?\\.?$\"\n)\n\n#: What a laboratory writes when it saw the determinand and put no number to\n#: it. For a determinand whose limit is zero that is the whole finding: a\n#: sample with E. coli 0 and total coliforms TNTC was graded \"Safe\" because\n#: the count read as \"not measured\".\nPRESENCE_TOKENS = frozenset({\n \"tntc\", \"t.n.t.c\", \"too numerous to count\", \"confluent\", \"confluent growth\",\n \"present\", \"positive\", \"pos\", \"+ve\", \"detected\",\n})\n\n#: \"greater than\" results: at least this much, not exactly this much.\n_GREATER_THAN = re.compile(r\"^(?:>|>=|\\u2265|more than|greater than)\\s*\"\n r\"(?P\\d+(?:[.,]\\d+)?)\\s*\\+?$\")\n\n\ndef _absence_limit(text: str) -> float | None:\n \"\"\"The detection limit an absence phrase carries, if it carries one.\"\"\"\n match = _ABSENCE_WITH_LIMIT.match(text.lower().strip())\n if not match:\n return None\n word = re.sub(r\"[\\s.]+$\", \"\", match.group(\"word\")).strip()\n if word not in ABSENCE_TOKENS:\n return None\n return parse_number(match.group(\"limit\"))\n\n\ndef read_quality_workbook(path: str | Path) -> WaterQualitySample:\n grid, _ = common.load_grid(path)\n fields = common.extract_header_fields(grid)\n site = common.site_from_fields(fields, source=str(path))\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n\n located = _find_results_header(grid)\n if located is None:\n raise ValueError(f\"No results table (Parameter/Value) found in {path}\")\n header_row, cols = located\n\n results: list[WaterQualityResult] = []\n for row in grid[header_row + 1 :]:\n def cell(key):\n c = cols.get(key)\n return row[c] if c is not None and c < len(row) else None\n\n parameter = clean_text(cell(\"parameter\"))\n if not parameter or parameter.lower().startswith(\"note\"):\n continue\n raw_value = cell(\"value\")\n text_value = clean_text(raw_value)\n plain = text_value.lower().rstrip(\".\")\n # \"<1\", the words a certificate uses for the same thing, and those\n # same words with the limit written after them (\"ND (<0.05)\")\n worded_limit = _absence_limit(text_value)\n below_detection = (\n text_value.startswith(\"<\")\n or plain in ABSENCE_TOKENS\n or worded_limit is not None\n )\n # A count the laboratory saw and did not quantify, and a \">50\" that\n # used to be read as exactly 50.\n greater_than = None\n if not below_detection:\n if plain in PRESENCE_TOKENS:\n greater_than = 0.0\n else:\n match = _GREATER_THAN.match(plain)\n if match:\n greater_than = parse_number(match.group(\"value\"))\n value = (\n None\n if plain in ABSENCE_TOKENS or worded_limit is not None\n or greater_than is not None\n else parse_number(raw_value)\n )\n dl = parse_number(cell(\"dl\"))\n if worded_limit is not None and dl is None:\n dl = worded_limit\n if below_detection:\n # A \" float:\n \"\"\"sRGB relative luminance, 0 (black) to 1 (white): what a photocopy keeps.\"\"\"\n rgb = [int(colour.lstrip(\"#\")[i:i + 2], 16) / 255.0 for i in (0, 2, 4)]\n lin = [c / 12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4 for c in rgb]\n return 0.2126 * lin[0] + 0.7152 * lin[1] + 0.0722 * lin[2]\n\n\ndef geology_colour(code: str, source_colour: str, prefer_source: bool = False) -> str:\n \"\"\"The fill for one geological unit.\"\"\"\n if prefer_source:\n return source_colour\n return GEOLOGY_COLOURS.get(code, source_colour)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass LineStyle:\n color: str\n width: float\n zorder: float\n\n\n#: One place to change how heavy each class of boundary is drawn.\nLINES = {\n \"coast\": LineStyle(COAST, 1.5, 6.0),\n \"district\": LineStyle(DISTRICT, 0.9, 5.0),\n \"chiefdom\": LineStyle(CHIEFDOM, 0.5, 4.0),\n \"contact\": LineStyle(\"#8A8A8A\", 0.35, 3.0),\n}\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Type\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef halo(size: float = 2.2, color: str = \"#FFFFFF\"):\n \"\"\"A cut-out behind a label so it reads over any fill.\n\n Every place name on these maps sits on top of something - a\n geological unit, a hypsometric tint, a choropleth class. Without a\n halo the name takes the colour of whatever it landed on and a third\n of the labels become unreadable, which is the single thing that most\n made these figures look homemade.\n \"\"\"\n return [path_effects.withStroke(linewidth=size, foreground=color)]\n\n\ndef place_label(ax, lon, lat, text, *, size=7.0, color=INK_MUTED,\n weight=\"normal\", style=\"normal\", zorder=8.0, ha=\"center\",\n va=\"center\", halo_color=\"#FFFFFF\", halo_size=2.2):\n \"\"\"Draw a place name with a halo, in the house type scale.\"\"\"\n return ax.annotate(\n text, xy=(lon, lat), ha=ha, va=va, fontsize=size, color=color,\n fontweight=weight, fontstyle=style, zorder=zorder,\n path_effects=halo(halo_size, halo_color),\n )\n\n\ndef declutter(\n candidates: list[tuple[float, float, str]],\n extent: tuple[float, float, float, float],\n min_sep_frac: float = 0.052,\n priority: list[float] | None = None,\n reserved: list[tuple[float, float, float, float]] | None = None,\n) -> list[tuple[float, float, str]]:\n \"\"\"Keep the labels that fit, drop the ones that would overlap.\n\n Matplotlib will happily draw two names through each other. On a\n window crossing the Western Area the chiefdoms are small enough that\n four names landed in the same centimetre, and a name nobody can read\n is worse than no name: the reader cannot tell which polygon the\n legible one belongs to either.\n\n Greedy, largest-first, over estimated text boxes rather than points.\n ``priority`` (bigger is more important, the polygon's area is the\n obvious choice) decides who wins a collision, so the chiefdom filling\n the frame keeps its name and the sliver clipped by the corner loses\n it. A label whose text would run off the frame is dropped too: a name\n half outside the neatline points at nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if not candidates:\n return []\n order = (\n np.argsort(priority)[::-1] if priority is not None\n else np.arange(len(candidates))\n )\n width = extent[2] - extent[0]\n height = extent[3] - extent[1]\n # A label is a box, not a dot. Testing centre-to-centre distance kept\n # \"Western Area Urban\" and \"Western Area Rural\" because their centroids\n # are far enough apart - while the words themselves, fifteen characters\n # wide, ran straight through each other. Character width is estimated\n # rather than measured because the renderer has not laid the text out\n # yet, and an estimate that is roughly right for DejaVu Sans at these\n # sizes is enough to separate the cases that actually collide.\n char_w = width * min_sep_frac * 0.30\n line_h = height * min_sep_frac * 0.62\n kept: list[tuple[float, float, str]] = []\n # boxes nothing may be written over: the site marker, the inset, a\n # legend. The site star used to be drawn through the district's name.\n boxes: list[tuple[float, float, float, float]] = list(reserved or [])\n for i in order:\n lon, lat, text = candidates[int(i)]\n half_w = len(text) * char_w / 2.0\n half_h = line_h / 2.0\n box = (lon - half_w, lat - half_h, lon + half_w, lat + half_h)\n # a name whose word runs off the frame, sideways or vertically,\n # points at nothing\n if not (extent[0] < lon < extent[2] and extent[1] < lat < extent[3]):\n continue\n if box[0] < extent[0] or box[2] > extent[2]:\n continue\n if box[1] < extent[1] or box[3] > extent[3]:\n continue\n if any(\n box[0] < b[2] and box[2] > b[0] and box[1] < b[3] and box[3] > b[1]\n for b in boxes\n ):\n continue\n kept.append((lon, lat, text))\n boxes.append(box)\n return kept\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Graticule\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _nice_interval(span_deg: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"A round graticule interval giving three to six lines across.\n\n Five was the target and the steps are coarse, so a 1.2 degree window\n fell to a 0.1 degree step and thirteen labels ran into each other\n along the bottom edge. A degree-and-minute label is about a tenth of\n the frame wide at this size; six across is the most that stay apart.\n \"\"\"\n target = span_deg / 3.5\n for step in (5.0, 2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.025, 0.02,\n 0.01, 0.005, 0.002, 0.001):\n if step <= target:\n return step\n return 0.001\n\n\ndef _dms(value: float, axis: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"A coordinate as degrees and minutes, the way a map writes them.\n\n ``-13.5`` is how a spreadsheet writes a longitude. A map writes\n 13 degrees 30 minutes West, and a hydrogeologist reading a GPS in\n the field is reading degrees and minutes.\n \"\"\"\n hemi = (\"N\" if value >= 0 else \"S\") if axis == \"lat\" else (\"E\" if value >= 0 else \"W\")\n value = abs(value)\n deg = int(value)\n minutes = (value - deg) * 60.0\n # 12.99999 is sixty minutes past twelve, which is thirteen degrees, not\n # \"12 deg 60'\". Floating point put a tick just short of 13 W and the\n # graticule on every map of the Western Area was labelled 12 deg 60' W.\n if minutes >= 59.95:\n deg += 1\n minutes = 0.0\n if minutes < 0.05:\n return f\"{deg}\u00b0{hemi}\"\n if abs(minutes - round(minutes)) < 0.05:\n return f\"{deg}\u00b0{round(minutes):02d}\u2032{hemi}\"\n return f\"{deg}\u00b0{minutes:04.1f}\u2032{hemi}\"\n\n\ndef graticule(ax, *, interval: float | None = None, label_size: float = 7.0):\n \"\"\"A hairline graticule with degree-and-minute labels.\n\n Replaces the full grey grid, which was the heaviest thing on most of\n these maps and drew the eye before the data did.\n \"\"\"\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n step = interval or _nice_interval(max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0))\n # only ticks inside the frame: a tick placed past the limit made\n # matplotlib grow the axes to include it, which put a white strip on\n # the national maps and moved every local window off its site\n eps = step * 1e-6\n xs = np.array([x for x in np.arange(math.ceil(x0 / step) * step, x1 + step / 2, step)\n if x0 - eps <= x <= x1 + eps])\n ys = np.array([y for y in np.arange(math.ceil(y0 / step) * step, y1 + step / 2, step)\n if y0 - eps <= y <= y1 + eps])\n for x in xs:\n ax.axvline(x, color=GRATICULE, lw=0.5, zorder=2.5)\n for y in ys:\n ax.axhline(y, color=GRATICULE, lw=0.5, zorder=2.5)\n ax.set_xticks(xs)\n ax.set_yticks(ys)\n ax.set_xticklabels([_dms(x, \"lon\") for x in xs], fontsize=label_size,\n color=INK_MUTED)\n ax.set_yticklabels([_dms(y, \"lat\") for y in ys], fontsize=label_size,\n color=INK_MUTED)\n ax.tick_params(length=3, width=0.6, color=INK_FAINT, pad=2)\n ax.set_xlim(x0, x1)\n ax.set_ylim(y0, y1)\n ax.grid(False)\n for spine in ax.spines.values():\n spine.set_edgecolor(COAST)\n spine.set_linewidth(0.9)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Scale bar\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _nice_scale_length(span_km: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"A round bar length at roughly a quarter of the frame.\"\"\"\n target = span_km / 4.0\n if target <= 0:\n return 1.0\n power = 10 ** math.floor(math.log10(target))\n for mult in (5, 4, 2, 1):\n if power * mult <= target:\n return power * mult\n return power\n\n\ndef scale_bar(ax, mean_lat: float, *, segments: int = 4, frac_x: float = 0.055,\n frac_y: float = 0.055, height_frac: float = 0.011):\n \"\"\"An alternating-segment scale bar with ticked divisions.\n\n The old bar was a black line with a white half drawn over it and one\n label at the middle, which tells a reader the total and nothing else.\n This is the bar on a published sheet: a zero at the left, divisions\n that can actually be counted off against a distance on the map, and\n the unit stated once at the right.\n \"\"\"\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n km_per_deg = 111.32 * math.cos(math.radians(mean_lat))\n total_km = _nice_scale_length((x1 - x0) * km_per_deg)\n bar_deg = total_km / km_per_deg\n seg_deg = bar_deg / segments\n\n bx = x0 + (x1 - x0) * frac_x\n by = y0 + (y1 - y0) * frac_y\n bh = (y1 - y0) * height_frac\n\n for i in range(segments):\n ax.add_patch(\n MplPolygon(\n [(bx + i * seg_deg, by), (bx + (i + 1) * seg_deg, by),\n (bx + (i + 1) * seg_deg, by + bh), (bx + i * seg_deg, by + bh)],\n closed=True, facecolor=INK if i % 2 == 0 else \"#FFFFFF\",\n edgecolor=INK, lw=0.6, zorder=10.0,\n )\n )\n # a zero, the midpoint and the total with its unit: enough to measure\n # against. The unit used to be a separate \"km\" beside the bar, which\n # the total overprinted whenever it had two digits.\n ticks = {0: \"0\", segments // 2: f\"{total_km / 2:g}\", segments: f\"{total_km:g} km\"}\n for i, text in ticks.items():\n ax.annotate(\n text, xy=(bx + i * seg_deg, by + bh * 1.25),\n ha=\"center\" if i < segments else \"left\",\n xytext=(0, 0) if i < segments else (-4, 0), textcoords=\"offset points\",\n va=\"bottom\", fontsize=6.5, color=INK, zorder=10.0,\n path_effects=halo(2.0),\n )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# North arrow\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef north_arrow(ax, *, frac_x: float = 0.945, frac_y: float = 0.9,\n size_frac: float = 0.055):\n \"\"\"A filled compass needle rather than a line with a letter over it.\n\n Two triangles about a common axis: the east half solid, the west half\n open. It reads as a needle at a centimetre high, which an annotate\n arrow does not.\n \"\"\"\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n cx = x0 + (x1 - x0) * frac_x\n cy = y0 + (y1 - y0) * frac_y\n h = (y1 - y0) * size_frac\n w = h * 0.32 * ((x1 - x0) / (y1 - y0)) * 0.55\n\n ax.add_patch(MplPolygon([(cx, cy + h), (cx + w, cy - h * 0.45), (cx, cy - h * 0.12)],\n closed=True, facecolor=INK, edgecolor=INK,\n lw=0.5, zorder=10.0))\n ax.add_patch(MplPolygon([(cx, cy + h), (cx - w, cy - h * 0.45), (cx, cy - h * 0.12)],\n closed=True, facecolor=\"#FFFFFF\", edgecolor=INK,\n lw=0.5, zorder=10.0))\n ax.annotate(\"N\", xy=(cx, cy + h * 1.18), ha=\"center\", va=\"bottom\",\n fontsize=8.0, fontweight=\"bold\", color=INK, zorder=10.0,\n path_effects=halo(2.2))\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Sea, and the land across the border\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef sea_and_neighbours(ax, outline_rings: list[np.ndarray], background: str,\n foreign_rings: list[np.ndarray] | None = None):\n \"\"\"Fill the frame as sea, then lay the country on top of it.\n\n Sierra Leone has 400 km of coast and this toolkit's busiest site is\n on the Freetown peninsula, where half of every window is Atlantic.\n Drawn as white it read as blank paper, so the coastline looked like\n the edge of the data rather than the edge of the land - the single\n thing that most made these look unfinished.\n\n Everything outside the national outline is filled: across the land\n border that is Guinea or Liberia, not ocean, so it is drawn in a\n neutral paper tone and the sea proper is only claimed where the\n caller knows it is sea. The two are told apart by the caller, not\n guessed here.\n \"\"\"\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n ax.add_patch(\n MplPolygon([(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)], closed=True,\n facecolor=SEA, edgecolor=\"none\", zorder=0.4)\n )\n # Guinea and Liberia, in the paper tone, laid over the sea and under\n # the country. They were painted the same blue as the Atlantic on every\n # map, so a site near the border looked like a site on the coast. The\n # caller passes what it knows is land across the border; without it,\n # everything outside the outline stays sea.\n for ring in foreign_rings or []:\n ax.add_patch(\n MplPolygon(ring, closed=True, facecolor=FOREIGN_LAND,\n edgecolor=\"none\", zorder=0.5)\n )\n for ring in outline_rings:\n ax.add_patch(\n MplPolygon(ring, closed=True, facecolor=background,\n edgecolor=\"none\", zorder=0.6)\n )\n\n\ndef neatline(ax):\n \"\"\"The frame. A map has an edge; a chart has axes.\"\"\"\n for spine in ax.spines.values():\n spine.set_visible(True)\n spine.set_edgecolor(COAST)\n spine.set_linewidth(0.9)\n spine.set_zorder(11.0)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Attribution\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef attribution(ax, text: str, *, width: int = 104, size: float = 5.8) -> float:\n \"\"\"The sources, set small, at the foot, on a plate that keeps it legible.\n\n It is small because it is not the map; it is present because a\n figure without its sources cannot be checked. Returns the axes-fraction\n y a caller should put the next block of small print at, because a\n three-source credit wraps to three lines and anything written at a\n fixed offset below it lands on top of it.\n \"\"\"\n import textwrap\n\n # Under the frame, not inside it. Inside, a three-source credit wrapped\n # to three lines across the bottom-left corner and buried the scale bar,\n # which is the one piece of furniture a reader actually measures with.\n wrapped = textwrap.fill(text, width)\n ax.text(\n 1.0, -0.055, wrapped, transform=ax.transAxes,\n ha=\"right\", va=\"top\", fontsize=size, color=INK_FAINT,\n style=\"italic\", linespacing=1.4,\n )\n # how far down the next block has to start to clear this one\n return -0.055 - (wrapped.count(\"\\n\") + 1) * 0.026\n\n\ndef title_block(ax, title: str, subtitle: str = \"\"):\n \"\"\"Title above the frame, subtitle under it in the muted weight.\"\"\"\n ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11.5, fontweight=\"600\", color=INK, pad=9)\n if subtitle:\n ax.text(0.0, 1.012, subtitle, transform=ax.transAxes, ha=\"left\",\n va=\"bottom\", fontsize=7.5, color=INK_MUTED)\n"}, "groundwater/mapping/export.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"GIS layer export: GeoJSON always, GeoPackage when geopandas is\ninstalled (``pip install groundwater-toolkit[gis]``).\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom ..geo import utm_to_geographic\nfrom .maps import MapPoint\n\n\ndef export_geojson(\n points: list[MapPoint],\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path,\n extra_properties: dict[str, dict] | None = None,\n) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Write survey points as a WGS84 GeoJSON FeatureCollection.\n\n ``extra_properties`` maps point label to additional attribute\n dictionaries (for example layer tables or water zones).\n \"\"\"\n features = []\n for p in points:\n lat, lon = utm_to_geographic(p.easting, p.northing, zone)\n props = {\n \"label\": p.label,\n \"kind\": p.kind,\n \"easting_utm\": p.easting,\n \"northing_utm\": p.northing,\n \"utm_zone\": f\"{zone}N\",\n }\n if p.value is not None:\n props[\"value\"] = p.value\n if extra_properties and p.label in extra_properties:\n props.update(extra_properties[p.label])\n features.append(\n {\n \"type\": \"Feature\",\n \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [round(lon, 6), round(lat, 6)]},\n \"properties\": props,\n }\n )\n collection = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}\n path = Path(path)\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n json.dump(collection, fh, indent=2)\n return path\n\n\ndef export_gpkg(\n points: list[MapPoint],\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path,\n layer: str = \"survey_points\",\n) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Write survey points to a GeoPackage (requires geopandas).\"\"\"\n try:\n import geopandas as gpd\n from shapely.geometry import Point\n except ImportError as exc:\n raise ImportError(\n \"GeoPackage export needs geopandas; install with \"\n \"'pip install groundwater-toolkit[gis]' or use export_geojson()\"\n ) from exc\n\n records = []\n geometry = []\n for p in points:\n records.append(\n {\n \"label\": p.label,\n \"kind\": p.kind,\n \"value\": p.value,\n \"easting_utm\": p.easting,\n \"northing_utm\": p.northing,\n }\n )\n geometry.append(Point(p.easting, p.northing))\n epsg = 32600 + zone # WGS84 / UTM north\n gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(records, geometry=geometry, crs=f\"EPSG:{epsg}\")\n path = Path(path)\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n gdf.to_file(path, layer=layer, driver=\"GPKG\")\n return path\n"}, "groundwater/mapping/geolibre.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"GeoLibre project files: the survey as a map somebody can open.\n\nEvery map this toolkit draws is a picture. A picture is the right thing\nto put in a report and the wrong thing to hand to somebody who wants to\nknow what is under the next hill: it cannot be panned, the VES station\ncannot be clicked, and there is nothing underneath it but graph paper.\n\n`GeoLibre `_ is a free, MIT-licensed GIS that runs\nin a browser, on a desktop, on a phone and inside a notebook, and reads\na documented plain-JSON project file. So the cheapest way to give this\ntoolkit an interactive map is not to write one. It is to write that\nfile.\n\nDesign\n------\n**Nothing new is imported.** The format is JSON, the geometry is the\nGeoJSON we already emit, and the projection is the one in\n:mod:`groundwater.geo`. This module needs the standard library and\nnothing else - not even numpy or matplotlib, so it stays importable\nwhere those are not. Ring coordinates arrive as numpy arrays from\n:mod:`groundwater.mapping.regional` and are read row by row as plain\nfloats rather than by importing numpy to do it.\n\n**Deterministic.** Re-running on the same data produces a byte-identical\nfile, which is the rule everywhere else in this toolkit and is the\nreason layer identifiers are slugs of their names rather than the random\nUUIDs the format's own examples use. A file that differs on every run\ncannot be checked into a project folder or diffed against last month's.\n\n**Per-feature colour, not a renderer.** Colours ride on the features\nthemselves as simplestyle properties (``fill``, ``stroke``,\n``marker-color``), with a plain single-symbol style beside them as the\nfallback. A categorised renderer would say the same thing in a schema\nthat is at version 0.1.0 and will move; simplestyle is older than this\nformat and will outlive this version of it.\n\n**Attribution travels with the layer.** The bundled datasets are not all\nalike - geoBoundaries is CC BY 4.0, the BGS aquifer layer is CC BY-SA\n4.0, WPDx is CC BY 4.0 - so every layer carries its own credit in its\nmetadata and the project carries the full list. A layer whose licence\nrequires attribution must not be able to leave here without it.\n\nNote on ShareAlike\n------------------\n:func:`site_project` inlines the geometry it is given, and inlining a\nCC BY-SA layer carries ShareAlike into the resulting file. That is fine\nfor a project file shared under the same terms and is the reason the\ncredit is written next to the geometry rather than in a note somewhere\nelse. Where the layer can be referenced by URL instead, prefer that.\n\nUsage\n-----\n>>> from groundwater.mapping import geolibre\n>>> project = geolibre.site_project(site=site, survey_points=points, zone=28)\n>>> geolibre.write_project(project, \"rokel.geolibre.json\")\n\nThe written file opens unchanged in the GeoLibre web app, the desktop\napp, the Android and iOS apps, and the Jupyter widget.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport math\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Iterable, Sequence\n\nfrom ..geo import utm_to_geographic\nfrom ..site_status import STATUS_COLORS, STATUS_LABELS, coerce_status\n\n__all__ = [\n \"GEOLIBRE_WEB_APP\",\n \"PROJECT_FORMAT_VERSION\",\n \"area_features\",\n \"build_project\",\n \"data_link\",\n \"features_within\",\n \"geojson_layer\",\n \"points_within_window\",\n \"portfolio_features\",\n \"portfolio_project\",\n \"project_link\",\n \"site_project\",\n \"suitability_features\",\n \"survey_point_features\",\n \"unit_features\",\n \"water_point_features\",\n \"window_around\",\n \"write_project\",\n]\n\n#: The hosted web build. A self-hosted deployment passes its own base URL.\nGEOLIBRE_WEB_APP = \"https://web.geolibre.app/\"\n\n#: The project schema version this module writes. GeoLibre is young and\n#: the format is explicitly pre-1.0, so the version is stated rather than\n#: assumed, and everything that knows about the format lives in this file.\nPROJECT_FORMAT_VERSION = \"0.1.0\"\n\n#: A blank background rather than a basemap. Deliberate: the toolkit's\n#: own maps are drawn on a plain grid, and a project that silently\n#: reached for OpenStreetMap tiles would be the app's first unannounced\n#: network call. The user switches a basemap on; the file does not.\nBLANK_BASEMAP = \"\"\n\n#: Coordinates are written to six decimal places, matching\n#: :func:`groundwater.mapping.export.export_geojson`. Six places is about\n#: 0.1 m at this latitude - far finer than a handheld GPS fix and finer\n#: than the survey it describes.\n_COORD_DP = 6\n\n# Suitability grades, coloured red-to-green to match ``suitability_map``.\n_GRADE_COLORS = {\n \"Very good\": \"#1A9850\",\n \"Good\": \"#A6D96A\",\n \"Moderate\": \"#FDAE61\",\n \"Poor\": \"#D73027\",\n}\n\n# A water point that nobody has reported on is grey, not green. The same\n# rule the asset registry keeps: absence of bad news is not good news.\n_FUNCTIONAL_COLORS = {True: \"#2E7D5B\", False: \"#B23A2E\", None: \"#6B7785\"}\n_FUNCTIONAL_LABELS = {True: \"Functional\", False: \"Non-functional\", None: \"Unknown\"}\n\n# Metadata keys that would be a credential leaving the machine. The rule\n# elsewhere in this toolkit is that the API key never enters a saved\n# project file, so sharing a project never shares the key; a GeoLibre\n# project is a saved project file and the rule holds there too.\n_SECRET_HINTS = (\"key\", \"token\", \"secret\", \"password\", \"credential\", \"auth\")\n\n_SLUG_STRIP = re.compile(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\")\n\n\ndef _slug(text: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"A stable identifier from a layer name.\n\n The format's examples use random UUIDs. This toolkit promises that\n re-running on the same raw data produces byte-identical output, and a\n random identifier breaks that promise on the first rerun, so the name\n is slugged instead. Two layers with the same name would collide;\n :func:`build_project` numbers duplicates rather than letting one\n quietly overwrite the other.\n \"\"\"\n slug = _SLUG_STRIP.sub(\"-\", str(text or \"\").strip().lower()).strip(\"-\")\n return slug or \"layer\"\n\n\ndef _round(value: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"Round a coordinate, and hand back a float rather than a numpy scalar.\"\"\"\n return round(float(value), _COORD_DP)\n\n\ndef _ring(points) -> list[list[float]]:\n \"\"\"A GeoJSON linear ring from a sequence of (lon, lat) pairs.\n\n Accepts numpy arrays without importing numpy: each row is unpacked and\n coerced. GeoJSON requires a closed ring, and the bundled boundary data\n does not always close, so it is closed here rather than trusted to be.\n \"\"\"\n ring = [[_round(lon), _round(lat)] for lon, lat in points]\n if len(ring) >= 2 and ring[0] != ring[-1]:\n ring.append(list(ring[0]))\n return ring\n\n\ndef _feature(geometry: dict, properties: dict) -> dict:\n return {\"type\": \"Feature\", \"geometry\": geometry, \"properties\": properties}\n\n\ndef _point(lon: float, lat: float, properties: dict) -> dict:\n return _feature(\n {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [_round(lon), _round(lat)]}, properties\n )\n\n\ndef _clean(properties: dict) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Drop empty values so a feature's popup is not a wall of blanks.\"\"\"\n return {k: v for k, v in properties.items() if v not in (None, \"\")}\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Features from the objects this toolkit already has\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef survey_point_features(points: Iterable, zone: int) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"GeoJSON point features from :class:`~groundwater.mapping.maps.MapPoint`.\n\n ``MapPoint`` carries projected UTM metres because the printed maps are\n drawn in metres; a project file is WGS84, so each point is unprojected\n through the same transform the GeoJSON export uses.\n\n Duck-typed on ``label``/``easting``/``northing``/``value``/``kind``\n rather than imported, which keeps this module free of matplotlib.\n \"\"\"\n features = []\n for point in points:\n lat, lon = utm_to_geographic(point.easting, point.northing, zone)\n properties = _clean(\n {\n \"label\": point.label,\n \"kind\": point.kind,\n \"value\": point.value,\n \"easting_utm\": round(float(point.easting), 1),\n \"northing_utm\": round(float(point.northing), 1),\n \"utm_zone\": f\"{zone}N\",\n \"marker-color\": \"#17527E\",\n \"fill\": \"#17527E\",\n \"stroke\": \"#FFFFFF\",\n }\n )\n features.append(_point(lon, lat, properties))\n return features\n\n\ndef suitability_features(scores: Iterable, zone: int) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Point features from :class:`~groundwater.siting.suitability.SitingSuitability`.\n\n Each point is coloured by its grade, so the drill-target ranking reads\n off the map the way it reads off the table. Scores without a position\n are skipped: a suitability with nowhere to put it is a table row, not\n a map feature.\n \"\"\"\n features = []\n for score in scores:\n if score.easting is None or score.northing is None:\n continue\n lat, lon = utm_to_geographic(score.easting, score.northing, zone)\n colour = _GRADE_COLORS.get(score.grade, \"#6B7785\")\n properties = _clean(\n {\n \"sounding\": score.sounding_id,\n \"suitability\": round(float(score.suitability), 1),\n \"grade\": score.grade,\n \"rank\": score.rank,\n \"rationale\": score.rationale,\n \"marker-color\": colour,\n \"fill\": colour,\n \"stroke\": \"#222222\",\n }\n )\n features.append(_point(lon, lat, properties))\n return features\n\n\ndef water_point_features(points: Iterable) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Point features from :class:`~groundwater.waterpoints.WaterPoint`.\n\n Coloured by functionality, with unknown grey rather than green. The\n survey year rides along, because a point reported functional in 2016\n is evidence about 2016.\n \"\"\"\n features = []\n for point in points:\n colour = _FUNCTIONAL_COLORS[point.functional]\n properties = _clean(\n {\n \"status\": _FUNCTIONAL_LABELS[point.functional],\n \"status_raw\": point.status,\n \"source\": point.source,\n \"technology\": point.technology,\n \"improved\": point.improved,\n \"installed\": point.install_year,\n \"surveyed\": point.report_year,\n \"months_per_year\": point.months_per_year,\n \"distance_m\": (\n round(point.distance_m) if point.distance_m is not None else None\n ),\n \"marker-color\": colour,\n \"fill\": colour,\n \"stroke\": \"#FFFFFF\",\n }\n )\n features.append(_point(point.lon, point.lat, properties))\n return features\n\n\ndef portfolio_features(points: Iterable[dict]) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Point features from :func:`groundwater.portfolio.portfolio_points`.\n\n Those are already ``{label, lat, lon, status}`` dicts in WGS84, so\n this only attaches the status colour and its readable label.\n \"\"\"\n features = []\n for point in points:\n status = coerce_status(point.get(\"status\")).value\n colour = STATUS_COLORS[status]\n properties = _clean(\n {\n \"label\": point.get(\"label\"),\n \"status\": STATUS_LABELS[status],\n \"marker-color\": colour,\n \"fill\": colour,\n \"stroke\": \"#FFFFFF\",\n }\n )\n features.append(_point(point[\"lon\"], point[\"lat\"], properties))\n return features\n\n\ndef area_features(areas: Iterable) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Polygon features from :class:`~groundwater.mapping.regional.AdminArea`.\n\n Interior rings are kept. Nongowa encloses Kenema Town, and a chiefdom\n drawn without its hole swallows the town it surrounds.\n \"\"\"\n features = []\n for area in areas:\n holes = list(getattr(area, \"holes\", []) or [])\n polygons = []\n for index, ring in enumerate(area.rings):\n inner = holes[index] if index < len(holes) else []\n polygons.append([_ring(ring)] + [_ring(hole) for hole in inner])\n if not polygons:\n continue\n geometry = (\n {\"type\": \"Polygon\", \"coordinates\": polygons[0]}\n if len(polygons) == 1\n else {\"type\": \"MultiPolygon\", \"coordinates\": polygons}\n )\n properties = _clean(\n {\n \"name\": area.name,\n \"level\": area.level,\n \"district\": getattr(area, \"district\", \"\"),\n \"fill\": \"#FFFFFF\",\n \"fill-opacity\": 0.0,\n \"stroke\": \"#6B7785\",\n \"stroke-width\": 1,\n }\n )\n features.append(_feature(geometry, properties))\n return features\n\n\ndef unit_features(units: Iterable) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Polygon features from :class:`~groundwater.mapping.regional.GeologyUnit`.\n\n Serves both the geology and the aquifer layers: the loaders return the\n same shape, with ``glg`` carrying the USGS unit code in one and the BGS\n combined code in the other. Each polygon keeps the colour its own\n dataset assigns, so the map matches the printed one.\n \"\"\"\n features = []\n for unit in units:\n properties = _clean(\n {\n \"code\": unit.glg,\n \"unit\": unit.unit,\n \"class\": unit.era,\n \"fill\": unit.color,\n \"fill-opacity\": 0.7,\n \"stroke\": \"#FFFFFF\",\n \"stroke-width\": 0.5,\n }\n )\n features.append(\n _feature(\n {\"type\": \"Polygon\", \"coordinates\": [_ring(unit.ring)]}, properties\n )\n )\n return features\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Layers, framing and the project itself\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef geojson_layer(\n name: str,\n features: Sequence[dict],\n *,\n kind: str = \"point\",\n color: str = \"#17527E\",\n stroke: str = \"#FFFFFF\",\n radius: float = 7.0,\n fill_opacity: float = 0.7,\n stroke_width: float = 1.0,\n visible: bool = True,\n opacity: float = 1.0,\n attribution: str = \"\",\n) -> dict:\n \"\"\"One inline GeoJSON layer.\n\n ``kind`` picks the fallback single-symbol style, which is what a\n viewer that ignores the per-feature simplestyle properties will draw.\n Both are written: the features carry their own colours, and the layer\n still looks deliberate without them.\n \"\"\"\n style = {\n \"simpleStyleEnabled\": True,\n \"fillColor\": color,\n \"strokeColor\": stroke,\n \"strokeWidth\": stroke_width,\n \"fillOpacity\": 1.0 if kind == \"point\" else fill_opacity,\n }\n if kind == \"point\":\n style[\"circleRadius\"] = radius\n layer = {\n \"id\": _slug(name),\n \"name\": name,\n \"type\": \"geojson\",\n \"source\": {\"type\": \"geojson\"},\n \"visible\": visible,\n \"opacity\": opacity,\n \"style\": style,\n \"geojson\": {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": list(features)},\n \"metadata\": {},\n }\n if attribution:\n layer[\"metadata\"][\"attribution\"] = attribution\n return layer\n\n\ndef _geometry_bbox(geometry: dict) -> tuple[float, float, float, float] | None:\n \"\"\"West, south, east, north of one geometry, at any nesting depth.\"\"\"\n west = south = math.inf\n east = north = -math.inf\n\n def walk(coordinates) -> None:\n nonlocal west, south, east, north\n if (\n len(coordinates) == 2\n and isinstance(coordinates[0], (int, float))\n and isinstance(coordinates[1], (int, float))\n ):\n lon, lat = coordinates\n west, east = min(west, lon), max(east, lon)\n south, north = min(south, lat), max(north, lat)\n return\n for part in coordinates:\n walk(part)\n\n if not (geometry or {}).get(\"coordinates\"):\n return None\n walk(geometry[\"coordinates\"])\n return None if west is math.inf else (west, south, east, north)\n\n\ndef _layer_bbox(layer: dict) -> tuple[float, float, float, float] | None:\n \"\"\"West, south, east, north over every feature in a layer.\"\"\"\n return _union(\n _geometry_bbox(feature.get(\"geometry\") or {})\n for feature in layer.get(\"geojson\", {}).get(\"features\", [])\n )\n\n\ndef window_around(lat: float, lon: float, radius_km: float):\n \"\"\"A square window of ``radius_km`` about a position, in degrees.\n\n The same window the printed local geology and aquifer maps are drawn\n in, expressed as a bounding box so features can be selected against\n it. A degree of latitude is a fixed distance; a degree of longitude\n shrinks towards the poles, so it is scaled by the cosine.\n \"\"\"\n dlat = radius_km / 111.32\n dlon = radius_km / max(111.32 * math.cos(math.radians(lat)), 1e-6)\n return lon - dlon, lat - dlat, lon + dlon, lat + dlat\n\n\ndef points_within_window(points: Iterable, window) -> list:\n \"\"\"Water points whose position falls inside ``window``.\n\n Applied to the records rather than to features built from them, because\n the inventory this filters can be national. The web app's coverage page\n fetches up to 200,000 points into the same place the site page reads\n them from, and building a quarter of a million features in order to\n throw almost all of them away is work nobody asked for.\n \"\"\"\n if window is None:\n return list(points)\n west, south, east, north = window\n return [\n point for point in points\n if west <= point.lon <= east and south <= point.lat <= north\n ]\n\n\ndef features_within(features: Iterable[dict], window) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Features whose extent reaches into ``window``.\n\n A bounding-box test, not a clip. A polygon that overlaps the window is\n kept whole, so the unit the site sits in arrives with its real shape\n rather than a truncated one, and nothing is invented at the edge. It\n is there to keep a national layer from being inlined in full when only\n the ground around the site is being asked about.\n \"\"\"\n if window is None:\n return list(features)\n kept = []\n for feature in features:\n bbox = _geometry_bbox(feature.get(\"geometry\") or {})\n if bbox is not None and _overlaps(bbox, window):\n kept.append(feature)\n return kept\n\n\ndef _union(boxes: Iterable[tuple[float, float, float, float]]):\n \"\"\"The bounding box covering every box given, or ``None`` for none.\"\"\"\n boxes = [box for box in boxes if box]\n if not boxes:\n return None\n return (\n min(b[0] for b in boxes),\n min(b[1] for b in boxes),\n max(b[2] for b in boxes),\n max(b[3] for b in boxes),\n )\n\n\ndef _at_least(bbox, span: float):\n \"\"\"Grow a bounding box about its centre until it spans at least ``span``.\"\"\"\n west, south, east, north = bbox\n if east - west < span:\n mid = (west + east) / 2\n west, east = mid - span / 2, mid + span / 2\n if north - south < span:\n mid = (south + north) / 2\n south, north = mid - span / 2, mid + span / 2\n return west, south, east, north\n\n\ndef _ring_bbox(points):\n \"\"\"West, south, east, north of a ring, without importing numpy.\"\"\"\n lons = []\n lats = []\n for lon, lat in points:\n lons.append(float(lon))\n lats.append(float(lat))\n if not lons:\n return None\n return min(lons), min(lats), max(lons), max(lats)\n\n\ndef _overlaps(a, b) -> bool:\n return not (a[2] < b[0] or a[0] > b[2] or a[3] < b[1] or a[1] > b[3])\n\n\ndef _merc_y(lat: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"Web Mercator y for a latitude, clamped short of the poles.\"\"\"\n lat = max(min(lat, 85.05112878), -85.05112878)\n return math.log(math.tan(math.pi / 4 + math.radians(lat) / 2))\n\n\n#: The smallest extent a project is framed on, in degrees - about 550 m\n#: at this latitude. A project holding one borehole has no extent at all,\n#: and framing it literally opens at maximum zoom on a blank background\n#: with the wellhead filling the screen. A survey is looked at over a few\n#: hundred metres, so that is the floor.\n_MIN_SPAN_DEG = 0.005\n\n\ndef _frame(\n bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float],\n *,\n width_px: float = 1024.0,\n height_px: float = 768.0,\n pad: float = 0.12,\n) -> tuple[list[float], float]:\n \"\"\"Centre and zoom that fit a bounding box, with a margin.\n\n The format stores a centre and a zoom rather than a bounding box, so\n the fit is computed here. It is an approximation - the viewport is\n assumed rather than known - and it is allowed to be: half a zoom\n level either way is the difference between a comfortable margin and a\n generous one, not between the right place and the wrong one.\n \"\"\"\n west, south, east, north = _at_least(bbox, _MIN_SPAN_DEG)\n centre = [_round((west + east) / 2), _round((south + north) / 2)]\n lon_span = max(east - west, 1e-6)\n y_span = max(_merc_y(north) - _merc_y(south), 1e-9)\n zoom_lon = math.log2(width_px * 360.0 / (256.0 * lon_span))\n zoom_lat = math.log2(height_px * 2 * math.pi / (256.0 * y_span))\n zoom = min(zoom_lon, zoom_lat) - math.log2(1 + 2 * pad)\n return centre, round(max(0.0, min(zoom, 20.0)), 2)\n\n\ndef _assert_no_secrets(metadata, _where: str = \"metadata\") -> None:\n \"\"\"Refuse metadata that looks like a credential, at any depth.\n\n A GeoLibre project is a file made to be handed to somebody else. The\n rule the rest of this toolkit keeps - the API key stays out of saved\n project files, so sharing a project never shares the key - is only\n kept if something checks, so this checks.\n\n It recurses, because a guard that reads only the top level is a guard\n that says ``{\"service\": {\"api_key\": ...}}`` is fine, and the file it\n waves through carries the key anyway. Only the metadata regions are\n scanned - the project's and each layer's - and not feature properties:\n a credential does not arrive as an attribute of a mapped water point,\n and walking a national inventory to look for one would cost more than\n it could ever find.\n \"\"\"\n if isinstance(metadata, dict):\n for key, value in metadata.items():\n lowered = str(key).lower()\n if any(hint in lowered for hint in _SECRET_HINTS):\n raise ValueError(\n f\"refusing to write {key!r} into a GeoLibre project \"\n f\"({_where}): it reads as a credential, and a project \"\n \"file is made to be shared\"\n )\n _assert_no_secrets(value, f\"{_where}.{key}\")\n elif isinstance(metadata, (list, tuple)):\n for item in metadata:\n _assert_no_secrets(item, _where)\n\n\ndef build_project(\n name: str,\n layers: Sequence[dict],\n *,\n center: Sequence[float] | None = None,\n zoom: float | None = None,\n metadata: dict | None = None,\n legend_title: str = \"Legend\",\n basemap: str = BLANK_BASEMAP,\n credits: Sequence[str] = (),\n frame_on: Sequence[str] = (),\n) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Assemble a ``.geolibre.json`` project from prepared layers.\n\n Empty layers are dropped rather than written: a legend entry for a\n layer with nothing in it says there is nothing there, which is not\n the same as saying nothing was looked for.\n\n ``frame_on`` names the layers the camera should open on. Without it a\n site project frames every layer it holds, and since the geology layer\n covers Sierra Leone that means opening on Sierra Leone - the country,\n with the survey somewhere in it as three pixels. The context layers\n are there to be zoomed out to, not to be opened at. Named layers with\n nothing in them are ignored, so a project written before the survey\n arrived still frames on whatever it does have.\n \"\"\"\n kept = [\n layer\n for layer in layers\n if layer and layer.get(\"geojson\", {}).get(\"features\")\n ]\n\n seen: dict[str, int] = {}\n for layer in kept:\n base = layer[\"id\"]\n count = seen.get(base, 0)\n seen[base] = count + 1\n if count:\n layer[\"id\"] = f\"{base}-{count + 1}\"\n\n wanted = {_slug(name) for name in frame_on}\n focal = [layer for layer in kept if layer[\"id\"] in wanted]\n bbox = _union(_layer_bbox(layer) for layer in (focal or kept))\n\n if bbox is None:\n # Nothing to frame: the centre of Sierra Leone, whole country.\n center = center if center is not None else [-11.78, 8.46]\n zoom = zoom if zoom is not None else 7.0\n else:\n framed_center, framed_zoom = _frame(bbox)\n center = center if center is not None else framed_center\n zoom = zoom if zoom is not None else framed_zoom\n\n map_view = {\n \"center\": [_round(center[0]), _round(center[1])],\n \"zoom\": round(float(zoom), 2),\n \"bearing\": 0,\n \"pitch\": 0,\n }\n if bbox is not None:\n map_view[\"bbox\"] = [_round(v) for v in _at_least(bbox, _MIN_SPAN_DEG)]\n\n project_metadata = dict(metadata or {})\n _assert_no_secrets(project_metadata, \"project metadata\")\n for layer in kept:\n _assert_no_secrets(layer.get(\"metadata\"), f\"layer {layer['name']!r}\")\n project_metadata.setdefault(\"generator\", \"Groundwater Investigation Toolkit\")\n layer_credits = [\n layer[\"metadata\"][\"attribution\"]\n for layer in kept\n if layer.get(\"metadata\", {}).get(\"attribution\")\n ]\n attribution = list(dict.fromkeys(list(credits) + layer_credits))\n if attribution:\n project_metadata[\"attribution\"] = attribution\n\n return {\n \"version\": PROJECT_FORMAT_VERSION,\n \"name\": name,\n \"mapView\": map_view,\n \"basemapStyleUrl\": basemap,\n \"basemapVisible\": bool(basemap),\n \"basemapOpacity\": 1,\n \"layers\": kept,\n \"styles\": {layer[\"id\"]: layer[\"style\"] for layer in kept},\n \"legend\": {\"title\": legend_title, \"groupByLayer\": True},\n \"metadata\": project_metadata,\n }\n\n\ndef write_project(project: dict, path: str | Path) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Write a project to ``path``, creating parent directories.\n\n Two spaces of indentation and a trailing newline, so the file is\n readable in a diff and well-formed to every tool that reads the last\n line. ``ensure_ascii=False`` keeps a community name spelled the way\n it is spelled.\n \"\"\"\n # Checked again here, not only in build_project: this is the point at\n # which the project stops being a dict in memory and becomes a file\n # somebody can send, and a project assembled by hand never passed\n # through the other check at all.\n _assert_no_secrets(project.get(\"metadata\"), \"project metadata\")\n for layer in project.get(\"layers\", []):\n _assert_no_secrets(layer.get(\"metadata\"), f\"layer {layer.get('name')!r}\")\n\n path = Path(path)\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n json.dump(project, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)\n fh.write(\"\\n\")\n return path\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Deep links\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\n#: Characters left alone inside a deep link's parameter value. A published\n#: project URL is itself a URL, and the separators that matter - ``&``, ``=``,\n#: ``?``, ``#`` - have to be encoded or the outer query swallows the inner\n#: one: a signed link ending ``?sig=a&expires=1`` would otherwise hand\n#: GeoLibre an ``expires`` parameter of its own and truncate the address it\n#: was supposed to open. The scheme and path separators stay readable, and\n#: the set matches JavaScript's ``encodeURIComponent`` exactly so the two\n#: apps build the same link.\n_LINK_SAFE = \":/!*'()\"\n\n\ndef _link(app: str, params: dict) -> str:\n from urllib.parse import quote\n\n parts = []\n for key, value in params.items():\n # A valueless parameter is written bare, as the GeoLibre\n # documentation writes ``&maponly``, rather than as ``maponly=``.\n parts.append(key if value == \"\" else\n f\"{key}={quote(str(value), safe=_LINK_SAFE)}\")\n query = \"&\".join(parts)\n separator = \"\" if app.endswith((\"?\", \"&\")) else \"?\"\n return f\"{app.rstrip('?&')}{separator}{query}\" if query else app\n\n\ndef project_link(\n url: str,\n *,\n app: str = GEOLIBRE_WEB_APP,\n maponly: bool = False,\n viewer: bool = False,\n theme: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n \"\"\"A link that opens a *published* project file in GeoLibre.\n\n ``url`` must be reachable by the browser that follows the link. A file\n that has only been downloaded to the machine has no URL, and no query\n parameter can conjure one - that file is opened from inside GeoLibre\n instead. This is for the hosted case: a project on the Pages site, a\n programme's own server, a shared bucket.\n \"\"\"\n params = {\"url\": url}\n if viewer:\n params[\"layout\"] = \"viewer\"\n if theme:\n params[\"theme\"] = theme\n if maponly:\n params[\"maponly\"] = \"\"\n return _link(app, params)\n\n\ndef data_link(\n url: str, *, app: str = GEOLIBRE_WEB_APP, style_url: str | None = None\n) -> str:\n \"\"\"A link that opens one published data file - the GeoJSON we export.\n\n Lighter than a project: no styling, no legend, no framing, just the\n layer on a map. Useful for the bundled national layers, which do have\n a public URL.\n \"\"\"\n params = {\"data\": url}\n if style_url:\n params[\"style\"] = style_url\n return _link(app, params)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The two projects worth writing\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef site_project(\n *,\n name: str = \"\",\n site=None,\n zone: int | None = None,\n survey_points: Iterable | None = None,\n suitability: Iterable | None = None,\n water_points: Iterable | None = None,\n chiefdoms: Iterable | None = None,\n geology: Iterable | None = None,\n hydrogeology: Iterable | None = None,\n window_km: float | None = None,\n area=None,\n metadata: dict | None = None,\n) -> dict:\n \"\"\"One site, with whatever context the caller has to hand.\n\n Every argument is optional, because the toolkit's pages fill up in\n the order the fieldwork happens: a project written after the survey\n has soundings and no borehole, one written after handover has both.\n Layers are ordered back to front - geology and aquifers underneath,\n boundaries over them, then the survey, then the point that matters.\n\n ``zone`` is the UTM zone the projected inputs are in. It is taken\n from ``site`` when not given, and is only needed when there are\n projected inputs to unproject.\n\n ``window_km`` trims the national context layers to the ground around\n the site, the same way the printed local geology and aquifer maps are\n windowed. Without it the whole country is inlined, which is correct\n and about 400 kB.\n\n A site with no GPS fix still gets a project.\n :func:`~groundwater.mapping.regional.area_window` resolves it to the\n chiefdom it is in, or failing that the district, and the map opens\n there. What it does *not* do is plant a marker: a dot at a chiefdom\n centroid is indistinguishable on screen from a surveyed wellhead, and\n a reader who cannot tell the difference will measure from it. So the\n area is framed and named, the ground around it is drawn, and the\n position stays absent because it is absent. Pass ``area`` to override\n the resolution, or nothing to have it done here.\n \"\"\"\n from ..waterpoints import WPDX_CREDIT\n from .regional import ADMIN_CREDIT, GEOLOGY_CREDIT, HYDRO_CREDIT\n\n if zone is None and site is not None and site.utm is not None:\n zone = site.utm.zone\n\n window = None\n center = None\n zoom = None\n has_fix = site is not None and site.latlon is not None\n if has_fix:\n if window_km:\n lat, lon = site.latlon\n window = window_around(lat, lon, window_km)\n else:\n # An area given outright is honoured whether or not a site came with\n # it. Requiring one meant a caller could hand over an area, have it\n # silently ignored, and get a file whose metadata said it was centred\n # on that area while the camera sat on the country - the map and the\n # words about it disagreeing, which is the one thing a project file\n # must never do.\n if area is None and site is not None:\n from .regional import area_window as _resolve_area\n\n area = _resolve_area(site, window_km)\n if area is not None:\n window = window_around(area.lat, area.lon, area.radius_km)\n # Framed explicitly: without a fix there is no focal layer for\n # the camera to find, and the context layers alone would open\n # on the country.\n center, zoom = _frame(window)\n\n layers: list[dict] = []\n if hydrogeology:\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\n \"Aquifer productivity\",\n features_within(unit_features(hydrogeology), window),\n kind=\"polygon\",\n attribution=HYDRO_CREDIT,\n )\n )\n if geology:\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\n \"Geology\",\n features_within(unit_features(geology), window),\n kind=\"polygon\",\n visible=False,\n attribution=GEOLOGY_CREDIT,\n )\n )\n if chiefdoms:\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\n \"Chiefdoms\",\n features_within(area_features(chiefdoms), window),\n kind=\"polygon\",\n color=\"#FFFFFF\",\n stroke=\"#6B7785\",\n fill_opacity=0.0,\n attribution=ADMIN_CREDIT,\n )\n )\n if water_points:\n # Windowed like the context layers, and for a sharper reason: the\n # water points are one of the layers the camera frames on, so a\n # national inventory arriving here would not merely make the file\n # large, it would open the project on Sierra Leone with the survey\n # lost inside it.\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\n \"Existing water points\",\n water_point_features(points_within_window(water_points, window)),\n radius=6.0,\n attribution=WPDX_CREDIT,\n )\n )\n if survey_points:\n if zone is None:\n raise ValueError(\n \"survey_points are in projected UTM metres, so a zone is \"\n \"needed to unproject them; pass zone= or a site with a position\"\n )\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\"Survey points\", survey_point_features(survey_points, zone))\n )\n if suitability:\n if zone is None:\n raise ValueError(\n \"suitability scores are in projected UTM metres, so a zone is \"\n \"needed to unproject them; pass zone= or a site with a position\"\n )\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\n \"Drill-target suitability\",\n suitability_features(suitability, zone),\n radius=9.0,\n stroke=\"#222222\",\n )\n )\n\n site_metadata = dict(metadata or {})\n if site is not None:\n site_metadata.update(\n _clean(\n {\n \"community\": site.community,\n \"chiefdom\": site.chiefdom,\n \"district\": site.district,\n \"client\": site.client,\n \"project\": site.project,\n \"project_ref\": site.project_ref,\n }\n )\n )\n latlon = site.latlon\n if latlon is not None:\n lat, lon = latlon\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\n \"Site\",\n [\n _point(\n lon,\n lat,\n _clean(\n {\n \"label\": site.community or \"Site\",\n \"district\": site.district,\n \"chiefdom\": site.chiefdom,\n \"marker-color\": \"#B23A2E\",\n \"fill\": \"#B23A2E\",\n \"stroke\": \"#FFFFFF\",\n }\n ),\n )\n ],\n radius=10.0,\n color=\"#B23A2E\",\n )\n )\n\n if area is not None and not area.exact:\n # Said in the file, not only in the framing: a reader opening this\n # somewhere else has no other way to know the centre is a centroid.\n site_metadata[\"area\"] = area.label\n site_metadata[\"position\"] = (\n f\"centred on {area.label} - an area centroid, not a surveyed \"\n \"position; this site has no GPS fix\"\n )\n\n if not name:\n name = (\n (site.community if site is not None and site.community else \"\")\n or (area.label if area is not None else \"\")\n or \"Site\"\n )\n\n return build_project(\n name,\n layers,\n center=center,\n zoom=zoom,\n metadata=site_metadata,\n # The survey and the site are what the project is about; the\n # geology underneath it covers Sierra Leone and is context to zoom\n # out to, never the thing to open on.\n frame_on=(\n \"Site\",\n \"Drill-target suitability\",\n \"Survey points\",\n \"Existing water points\",\n ),\n )\n\n\ndef portfolio_project(\n points: Iterable[dict],\n *,\n name: str = \"Borehole portfolio\",\n districts: Iterable | None = None,\n metadata: dict | None = None,\n) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Every site in the portfolio, coloured by status, over the districts.\"\"\"\n from .regional import ADMIN_CREDIT\n\n layers = []\n if districts:\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\n \"Districts\",\n area_features(districts),\n kind=\"polygon\",\n color=\"#FFFFFF\",\n stroke=\"#6B7785\",\n fill_opacity=0.0,\n attribution=ADMIN_CREDIT,\n )\n )\n layers.append(\n geojson_layer(\"Boreholes\", portfolio_features(points), radius=8.0)\n )\n return build_project(\n name, layers, metadata=dict(metadata or {}), frame_on=(\"Boreholes\",)\n )\n"}, "groundwater/mapping/lithology.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"What the geology polygons are made of, rather than how old they are.\n\nThe bundled geological layer is the USGS Geologic Map of Africa at\n1:5,000,000, and it carries seven classes for the whole country. They are\nages: \"Paleozoic Igneous\", \"Precambrian\", \"Holocene\". A driller cannot\nuse an age. What decides whether a borehole yields is the lithology -\nwhether the rock weathers to a regolith that stores water, whether it\nfractures, whether it is porous in itself - and the USGS classes say\nnothing about any of that.\n\nThey are also, in one case, wrong. The single polygon the USGS layer\ncalls \"Paleozoic Igneous\" is the Freetown peninsula, and the rock there\nis the Freetown Layered Complex: a Jurassic layered gabbro, about 193\nmillion years old, which is Mesozoic. A reader told \"Paleozoic Igneous\"\nhas been given a wrong age and no rock.\n\nSo this module annotates. It does not reclassify: the polygon and its\nboundary still come from the 1:5M layer and are no more accurate for\nbeing better named. What it adds is the formation name and lithology\nfrom the Geology of Sierra Leone map (MoWR/SALWACO 2017, 1:600,000),\nwhich this repository commits and the geophysical report already cites\nin its prose, and a note on what that lithology means for drilling.\n\nWhere the two sources disagree on age, both are shown. Quietly rewriting\nsomebody else's dataset leaves a reader unable to tell what they are\nlooking at, which is a worse failure than the wrong age.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport functools\nimport io\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom importlib import resources\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n#: Which districts count as which region in the crosswalk.
