None of the three is recorded for this \"\n \"site, so there is no study area to draw.\"\n )\n outline, districts = load_admin(admin_path)\n chiefdoms = load_chiefdoms(chiefdom_path)\n dlat = window.radius_km / 111.32\n dlon = window.radius_km / (111.32 * math.cos(math.radians(window.lat)))\n box = (window.lon - dlon, window.lat - dlat,\n window.lon + dlon, window.lat + dlat)\n\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.8))\n ax.set_xlim(box[0], box[2])\n ax.set_ylim(box[1], box[3])\n carto.sea_and_neighbours(ax, outline.rings, carto.LAND,\n foreign_rings=foreign_land_rings(box))\n\n credit = ADMIN_CREDIT\n if show_geology:\n for unit in load_geology(geology_path):\n if not _ring_in_box(unit.ring, box):\n continue\n ax.add_patch(\n plt.Polygon(unit.ring, closed=True, facecolor=unit.color,\n edgecolor=\"none\", alpha=0.45, zorder=1)\n )\n credit = f\"{GEOLOGY_CREDIT}. {credit}\"\n\n # chiefdoms first: they are the boundaries a community is found by\n candidates: list[tuple[float, float, str]] = []\n weights: list[float] = []\n for area in chiefdoms:\n drawn = [r for r in area.rings if _ring_in_box(r, box)]\n for ring in drawn:\n ax.add_patch(\n plt.Polygon(ring, closed=True, facecolor=\"none\",\n edgecolor=carto.CHIEFDOM,\n lw=carto.LINES[\"chiefdom\"].width, zorder=3)\n )\n # one label per chiefdom, on the part of it that is in view.\n # Labelling every ring wrote \"Kaffu Bullom\" five times across the\n # top of the first map this drew: the chiefdom reaches the window\n # as five islands, and each one asked for its own name.\n spot = _label_spot(drawn, box)\n if spot is not None:\n candidates.append((*spot, area.label))\n weights.append(sum(abs(_ring_area(r)) for r in drawn))\n # Where the inset goes is settled before the names are placed, and\n # from the DATA only. Counting chiefdom names as occupancy put the\n # inset on top of a survey point, because three droppable labels in\n # one corner outvoted the one thing on the map that cannot move.\n drawn_at = [\n (pt.get(\"lon\"), pt.get(\"lat\")) for pt in (points or [])\n if pt.get(\"lon\") is not None and pt.get(\"lat\") is not None\n ]\n if site is not None and window.exact and site.latlon is not None and mark_site:\n drawn_at.append((site.latlon[1], site.latlon[0]))\n occupancy = _corner_occupancy(ax, drawn_at)\n free = sorted((\"lower right\", \"upper left\"), key=lambda c: occupancy[c])\n # both furniture corners are kept clear of names: the inset takes\n # one and the legend the other, and a chiefdom name under the\n # legend read as part of it (\"East I ecommended point\")\n reserved_boxes = [_corner_box(ax, free[0])]\n if points:\n reserved_boxes.append(_corner_box(ax, free[1]))\n visible = [\n (c, w) for c, w in zip(candidates, weights, strict=True)\n if not any(_inside(c[0], c[1], box) for box in reserved_boxes)\n ]\n for lon, lat, name in carto.declutter(\n [c for c, _ in visible], box, min_sep_frac=0.05,\n priority=[w for _, w in visible],\n ):\n carto.place_label(ax, lon, lat, name, size=6.6,\n color=carto.INK_MUTED, style=\"italic\")\n for district in districts:\n for ring in district.rings:\n if _ring_in_box(ring, box):\n ax.plot(ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1], color=carto.DISTRICT,\n lw=carto.LINES[\"district\"].width, zorder=5)\n for ring in outline.rings:\n if _ring_in_box(ring, box):\n ax.plot(ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1], color=carto.COAST,\n lw=carto.LINES[\"coast\"].width, zorder=6)\n\n handles = _plot_area_points(ax, points or [], style)\n if site is not None and window.exact and mark_site:\n _mark_site(ax, site, carto.SITE)\n\n below = _geo_axes_finish(ax, window.lat, credit)\n # the scale bar owns the lower left and the north arrow the upper\n # right; the inset and the legend share what is left, and which\n # corner each gets was settled above, before the names were placed\n _locator_inset(ax, outline, window, districts, style, corner=free[0])\n if handles:\n # lifted clear of the attribution line, which sits on the axes\n # floor and which the legend box otherwise lands on top of\n lift = 0.035 if free[1].startswith(\"lower\") else 0.0\n ax.legend(\n handles.values(), handles.keys(), loc=free[1],\n bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, lift, 1.0, 1.0 - lift),\n fontsize=7, framealpha=0.95,\n )\n if title is None:\n title = f\"Study area - {window.label}\"\n if not window.exact:\n title += \" (no site position recorded)\"\n ax.set_title(title)\n if show_geology:\n note = _scale_caveat(window.radius_km, _USGS_SOURCE_SCALE)\n if note:\n # wrapped by hand: an unwrapped line under the axes is one\n # long line, and the tight bounding box at save time grows\n # the canvas sideways to hold it, leaving the map off-centre\n # in its own figure\n ax.text(0.5, below - 0.012, textwrap.fill(note, 96),\n transform=ax.transAxes, ha=\"center\", va=\"top\",\n fontsize=6.5, color=\"#8A5A00\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\n#: Marker and colour per point kind on the study-area map.\n_AREA_MARKERS = {\n \"VES point\": (\"^\", \"#1F5C8B\"),\n #: the sounding the survey recommends drilling at: the one marker on a\n #: siting map that has to be unmistakable\n \"recommended point\": (\"*\", \"#B00020\"),\n \"borehole\": (\"o\", \"#0F7B3F\"),\n \"water point\": (\"s\", \"#7B5AA6\"),\n \"settlement\": (\".\", \"#555555\"),\n}\n\n\ndef _plot_area_points(ax, points: list[dict], style: HouseStyle) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Draw the study-area overlays, one legend entry per kind.\"\"\"\n handles: dict[str, object] = {}\n for point in points:\n lon, lat = point.get(\"lon\"), point.get(\"lat\")\n if lon is None or lat is None:\n continue\n kind = str(point.get(\"kind\") or \"point\")\n marker, colour = _AREA_MARKERS.get(kind, (\"D\", style.secondary_color))\n size = {\"*\": 15, \".\": 10}.get(marker, 8)\n handle, = ax.plot(\n lon, lat, marker, ms=size, mfc=colour,\n mec=\"white\", mew=0.9, zorder=8 if marker == \"*\" else 7,\n )\n handles.setdefault(kind, handle)\n label = point.get(\"label\")\n if label:\n # below the marker, because the site star labels itself above\n # its own point and the two collided wherever a sounding sat on\n # the wellhead - which is most surveys\n ax.annotate(str(label), xy=(lon, lat), xytext=(7, -11),\n textcoords=\"offset points\", fontsize=7.5,\n color=\"#222222\", zorder=8)\n return handles\n\n\ndef _clear_of(\n spot: tuple[float, float],\n placed: list[tuple[float, float]],\n box: tuple[float, float, float, float],\n min_sep_frac: float = 0.055,\n) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Is there room to write another name here?\n\n Matplotlib will happily draw two labels through each other, and on a\n window crossing the Western Area the chiefdoms are small enough that\n three or four names landed in the same centimetre. A name that cannot\n be read is worse than no name: the reader cannot tell which polygon\n the legible one belongs to either.\n \"\"\"\n gap = max(box[2] - box[0], box[3] - box[1]) * min_sep_frac\n return all(\n math.hypot(spot[0] - other[0], spot[1] - other[1]) > gap\n for other in placed\n )\n\n\ndef _corner_box(ax, corner: str) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:\n \"\"\"The data-coordinate rectangle an inset will cover.\"\"\"\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n fx, fy, fw, fh = _INSET_BOXES.get(corner, _INSET_BOXES[\"lower right\"])\n return (\n x0 + (x1 - x0) * fx, y0 + (y1 - y0) * fy,\n x0 + (x1 - x0) * (fx + fw), y0 + (y1 - y0) * (fy + fh),\n )\n\n\ndef _inside(lon: float, lat: float, box: tuple[float, float, float, float]) -> bool:\n return box[0] <= lon <= box[2] and box[1] <= lat <= box[3]\n\n\ndef _label_spot(\n rings: list[np.ndarray], box: tuple[float, float, float, float]\n) -> tuple[float, float] | None:\n \"\"\"Where to write an area's name, given only the parts of it in view.\n\n The centroid of the largest ring is the right answer for a whole\n country and the wrong one for a chiefdom clipped by the window: it\n lands outside the frame, and the name is either not drawn or drawn\n on the edge pointing at nothing. The mean of the vertices that are\n actually inside the window is inside the window by construction.\n \"\"\"\n inside = [\n v for ring in rings for v in ring\n if box[0] < v[0] < box[2] and box[1] < v[1] < box[3]\n ]\n if len(inside) < 3:\n return None\n pts = np.asarray(inside, dtype=float)\n return float(pts[:, 0].mean()), float(pts[:, 1].mean())\n\n\ndef _ring_in_box(ring: np.ndarray, box: tuple[float, float, float, float]) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Does a ring actually reach into the window?\n\n The extents are tested first because they reject almost everything\n almost free - drawing all 166 chiefdoms and the whole geological map\n into a 25 km window and letting matplotlib discard them costs a\n second a figure, and the reports draw several.\n\n What follows the extent test is the part that matters for the legend.\n Two rectangles can overlap while the shapes inside them do not touch,\n and a legend built on the cheap test alone named a consolidated\n sedimentary aquifer on a map of the Freetown peninsula because that\n unit's bounding box reaches across the country the polygon does not.\n So: a vertex inside the window, a window corner inside the ring, or\n an edge of one crossing an edge of the other. Those three are the\n whole of it.\n \"\"\"\n lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max = box\n if not (\n ring[:, 0].max() >= lon_min and ring[:, 0].min() <= lon_max\n and ring[:, 1].max() >= lat_min and ring[:, 1].min() <= lat_max\n ):\n return False\n inside = (\n (ring[:, 0] >= lon_min) & (ring[:, 0] <= lon_max)\n & (ring[:, 1] >= lat_min) & (ring[:, 1] <= lat_max)\n )\n if inside.any():\n return True\n corners = (\n (lon_min, lat_min), (lon_max, lat_min),\n (lon_max, lat_max), (lon_min, lat_max),\n )\n if any(_point_in_ring(lon, lat, ring) for lon, lat in corners):\n return True\n return _ring_crosses_box_edge(ring, box)\n\n\ndef _ring_crosses_box_edge(\n ring: np.ndarray, box: tuple[float, float, float, float]\n) -> bool:\n \"\"\"A ring that slices the window without a vertex landing in it.\n\n The remaining case: a long thin polygon - a dyke, a river, a coastal\n strip - passing clean through the frame. Its segments are tested\n against the four sides of the window, vectorised, because a national\n geology layer holds tens of thousands of segments and this runs once\n per unit per figure.\n \"\"\"\n lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max = box\n p1 = ring[:-1]\n p2 = ring[1:]\n sides = (\n ((lon_min, lat_min), (lon_max, lat_min)),\n ((lon_max, lat_min), (lon_max, lat_max)),\n ((lon_max, lat_max), (lon_min, lat_max)),\n ((lon_min, lat_max), (lon_min, lat_min)),\n )\n for (ax_, ay), (bx, by) in sides:\n q1 = np.array([ax_, ay])\n q2 = np.array([bx, by])\n d1 = _cross_sign(q1, q2, p1)\n d2 = _cross_sign(q1, q2, p2)\n d3 = _cross_sign(p1, p2, q1)\n d4 = _cross_sign(p1, p2, q2)\n if np.any((d1 * d2 < 0) & (d3 * d4 < 0)):\n return True\n return False\n\n\ndef _cross_sign(a, b, c) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Which side of the line a-b each point c falls on.\"\"\"\n a = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(a, dtype=float))\n b = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(b, dtype=float))\n c = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(c, dtype=float))\n return ((b[:, 0] - a[:, 0]) * (c[:, 1] - a[:, 1])\n - (b[:, 1] - a[:, 1]) * (c[:, 0] - a[:, 0]))\n"}, "groundwater/mapping/subsurface.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Subsurface maps and sections from the survey's own measurements.\n\nEverything here is drawn from what the soundings measured and the\ninversion interpreted, so unlike the geology and aquifer layers - which\nare national datasets read at a site - these are maps of this site, at\nthe scale the site was surveyed at.\n\nFive things the survey already knows and did not previously draw:\n\n* **depth to bedrock**, the overburden the driller passes through,\n* **aquifer thickness**, the saturated weathered and fractured section\n that decides whether the borehole is worth completing,\n* **bedrock elevation**, the same surface as a landform rather than a\n depth - which is what shows a buried valley, where basement groundwater\n collects,\n* **protective capacity**, the longitudinal conductance of the cover, so\n a productive but unprotected aquifer is not sited beside a latrine,\n* **the apparent-resistivity pseudo-section**, the measurements\n themselves laid out along the traverse before any inversion has been\n believed.\n\nEvery interpolated surface is masked to the hull of the soundings, the\nsame rule the iso-resistivity and overburden maps already follow: a\ncontour 400 m from the nearest sounding is the interpolator continuing a\ntrend, and somebody will drill on it.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nfrom matplotlib.colors import BoundaryNorm, ListedColormap, LogNorm\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\nfrom .maps import MapPoint, _interpolated_map\n\n#: The crystalline-basement protective-capacity classes, as\n#: ``groundwater.ves.interpret`` rates them. The breaks are the standard\n#: longitudinal-conductance classification and the colours run from\n#: exposed (red) to protected (blue); the map and its key read from this\n#: one table, so the two can never disagree.\nPROTECTIVE_CLASSES: tuple[tuple[float, float, str, str], ...] = (\n (0.0, 0.1, \"poor\", \"#B2182B\"),\n (0.1, 0.2, \"weak\", \"#EF8A62\"),\n (0.2, 0.7, \"moderate\", \"#FDDBC7\"),\n (0.7, 5.0, \"good\", \"#92C5DE\"),\n (5.0, math.inf, \"very good\", \"#2166AC\"),\n)\n\nSUBSURFACE_CREDIT = (\n \"Subsurface interpretation from this survey's vertical electrical \"\n \"soundings; no external dataset\"\n)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Turning interpretations into mappable points\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _positioned(interpretations: list) -> list:\n return [\n interp for interp in interpretations\n if getattr(interp, \"site_easting\", None) is not None\n and getattr(interp, \"site_northing\", None) is not None\n ]\n\n\ndef subsurface_map_points(\n interpretations: list,\n attribute: str,\n) -> list[MapPoint]:\n \"\"\"Build :class:`~groundwater.mapping.maps.MapPoint` list for one quantity.\n\n ``attribute`` names a field of\n :class:`~groundwater.ves.interpret.SiteInterpretation`, for example\n ``depth_to_basement_m`` or ``aquifer_thickness_m``. Soundings without\n a position are dropped - they cannot be put on a map - and so are\n those whose value the interpretation left unset, because a sounding\n whose curve never reached basement has no depth to basement and\n plotting a zero there would draw basement at the surface.\n \"\"\"\n points: list[MapPoint] = []\n for interp in _positioned(interpretations):\n value = getattr(interp, attribute, None)\n if value is None or not math.isfinite(float(value)):\n continue\n points.append(\n MapPoint(\n label=interp.sounding_id or \"VES\",\n easting=float(interp.site_easting),\n northing=float(interp.site_northing),\n value=float(value),\n kind=\"VES point\",\n )\n )\n return points\n\n\ndef bedrock_elevation_points(interpretations: list) -> list[MapPoint]:\n \"\"\"Bedrock surface elevation: ground level less the depth to basement.\n\n Needs both numbers at the same sounding. A survey that recorded no\n elevations gives an empty list rather than a bedrock surface at\n sea level, which is what subtracting a depth from nothing amounts to.\n \"\"\"\n points: list[MapPoint] = []\n for interp in _positioned(interpretations):\n ground = getattr(interp, \"site_elevation_m\", None)\n depth = getattr(interp, \"depth_to_basement_m\", None)\n if ground is None or depth is None:\n continue\n points.append(\n MapPoint(\n label=interp.sounding_id or \"VES\",\n easting=float(interp.site_easting),\n northing=float(interp.site_northing),\n value=float(ground) - float(depth),\n kind=\"VES point\",\n )\n )\n return points\n\n\ndef common_ab2_spacings(soundings: list) -> list[float]:\n \"\"\"The AB/2 spacings every sounding in the survey actually measured.\n\n An iso-resistivity map compares one spacing across the site, so the\n spacings worth offering are the ones present in every curve. Offering\n a spacing two of five soundings skipped produces a map interpolated\n from three points and labelled as though it came from five.\n \"\"\"\n if not soundings:\n return []\n shared: set[float] | None = None\n for sounding in soundings:\n present = {round(float(v), 4) for v in sounding.ab2 if math.isfinite(v)}\n shared = present if shared is None else (shared & present)\n return sorted(shared or set())\n\n\ndef iso_resistivity_points(\n soundings: list,\n ab2: float,\n tolerance: float = 1e-6,\n) -> list[MapPoint]:\n \"\"\"Measured apparent resistivity at one spacing, at each sounding.\n\n The reading is taken, not interpolated: a curve without that spacing\n contributes nothing rather than a value read off between its points.\n Where a Schlumberger segment change recorded the same AB/2 twice with\n different MN, the readings are averaged geometrically, which is how\n the two overlapping segments are spliced everywhere else in the\n toolkit.\n \"\"\"\n points: list[MapPoint] = []\n for sounding in soundings:\n site = getattr(sounding, \"site\", None)\n if site is None or site.easting is None or site.northing is None:\n continue\n hits = [\n float(rho)\n for spacing, rho in zip(sounding.ab2, sounding.rho_app, strict=True)\n if abs(float(spacing) - ab2) <= max(tolerance, abs(ab2) * 1e-6)\n and math.isfinite(rho) and rho > 0\n ]\n if not hits:\n continue\n value = math.exp(sum(math.log(h) for h in hits) / len(hits))\n points.append(\n MapPoint(\n label=sounding.sounding_id or \"VES\",\n easting=float(site.easting),\n northing=float(site.northing),\n value=value,\n kind=\"VES point\",\n )\n )\n return points\n\n\ndef _require_points(points: list[MapPoint], what: str, need: int = 3) -> None:\n if len(points) < need:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"{'an' if what[:1] in 'aeiou' else 'a'} {what} needs at least \"\n f\"{need} soundings that carry both a \"\n f\"position and the value; {len(points)} do. Record the GPS \"\n \"position of every sounding on the field sheet.\"\n )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The interpolated subsurface maps\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef depth_to_bedrock_map(\n interpretations: list,\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Depth to bedrock\",\n):\n \"\"\"Overburden the driller passes through before fresh basement.\n\n The same surface as the overburden thickness map, built from the\n interpretations rather than from a hand-assembled point list, so the\n Maps page can draw it without the caller re-deriving anything.\n \"\"\"\n points = subsurface_map_points(interpretations, \"depth_to_basement_m\")\n _require_points(points, \"depth to bedrock map\")\n return _interpolated_map(\n points, zone, title=title, cbar_label=\"Depth to bedrock (m)\",\n path=path, style=style, log_scale=False, cmap=\"YlOrBr\",\n )\n\n\ndef aquifer_thickness_map(\n interpretations: list,\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Interpreted aquifer thickness\",\n):\n \"\"\"Saturated weathered and fractured thickness, the yield's raw material.\"\"\"\n points = subsurface_map_points(interpretations, \"aquifer_thickness_m\")\n _require_points(points, \"aquifer thickness map\")\n return _interpolated_map(\n points, zone, title=title,\n cbar_label=\"Interpreted aquifer thickness (m)\",\n path=path, style=style, log_scale=False, cmap=\"GnBu\",\n )\n\n\ndef bedrock_elevation_map(\n interpretations: list,\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Bedrock surface elevation\",\n):\n \"\"\"The basement surface as a landform.\n\n A depth map and an elevation map of the same contact are different\n pictures on sloping ground: the deepest overburden is not\n necessarily the lowest bedrock, and it is the low bedrock - the\n buried valley - that basement groundwater drains towards.\n \"\"\"\n points = bedrock_elevation_points(interpretations)\n _require_points(points, \"bedrock elevation map\")\n return _interpolated_map(\n points, zone, title=title,\n cbar_label=\"Bedrock surface elevation (m)\",\n path=path, style=style, log_scale=False, cmap=\"terrain\",\n )\n\n\ndef transverse_resistance_map(\n interpretations: list,\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Transverse resistance (Dar-Zarrouk T)\",\n):\n \"\"\"Transverse resistance, which tracks transmissivity in basement terrain.\n\n T = Sum(h x rho) over the overburden. It is not transmissivity and is\n not labelled as though it were: the two correlate where the\n resistivity of the water is roughly constant across a small area,\n which is the assumption, not a result.\n \"\"\"\n points = subsurface_map_points(interpretations, \"transverse_resistance_t\")\n _require_points(points, \"transverse resistance map\")\n return _interpolated_map(\n points, zone, title=title,\n cbar_label=\"Transverse resistance (ohm m2)\",\n path=path, style=style, log_scale=True, cmap=\"magma\",\n )\n\n\ndef protective_capacity_map(\n interpretations: list,\n zone: int,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Aquifer protective capacity\",\n):\n \"\"\"Longitudinal conductance of the cover, in its standard classes.\n\n Drawn in classes rather than on a continuous ramp, because the\n decision this map informs is categorical - is this aquifer protected\n enough to site a borehole near a latrine or a cattle crossing - and a\n smooth ramp invites reading a difference between 0.68 and 0.71\n siemens that the method does not support.\n\n Class colours and breaks come from :data:`PROTECTIVE_CLASSES`, the\n same table ``groundwater.ves.interpret`` rates a sounding against, so\n a point's colour and the word in its report cannot disagree.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n points = subsurface_map_points(interpretations, \"protective_conductance_s\")\n _require_points(points, \"protective capacity map\", need=1)\n\n bounds = [c[0] for c in PROTECTIVE_CLASSES]\n # the top class is unbounded; contouring needs a finite ceiling, so use\n # the largest value on this map or the class floor, whichever is bigger\n bounds.append(max(max(p.value for p in points if p.value is not None), 5.0) * 1.05)\n cmap = ListedColormap([c[3] for c in PROTECTIVE_CLASSES])\n norm = BoundaryNorm(bounds, cmap.N)\n\n from matplotlib.patches import Patch\n\n from .maps import (\n _clip_to_surveyed_ground,\n _extent,\n _figsize,\n _format_grid,\n _no_surface_note,\n _north_arrow,\n _pad_limits,\n _scale_bar,\n _surface,\n )\n\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=_figsize(style, *_extent(points)))\n _pad_limits(ax, points)\n if len(points) >= 3:\n e = np.array([p.easting for p in points])\n n = np.array([p.northing for p in points])\n v = np.array([p.value for p in points], dtype=float)\n x0, x1 = ax.get_xlim()\n y0, y1 = ax.get_ylim()\n gx, gy = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(x0, x1, 200), np.linspace(y0, y1, 200))\n grid = _surface(e, n, v, gx, gy)\n if grid is not None:\n grid, _clipped = _clip_to_surveyed_ground(ax, grid, e, n, gx, gy)\n ax.contourf(gx, gy, grid, levels=bounds, cmap=cmap, norm=norm,\n alpha=0.8)\n else:\n _no_surface_note(ax, len(points))\n for p in points:\n colour = _protective_colour(p.value)\n ax.plot(p.easting, p.northing, \"o\", ms=11, mfc=colour,\n mec=\"#222222\", mew=1.3, zorder=6)\n ax.annotate(\n f\"{p.label}\\n{p.value:.2f} S\", xy=(p.easting, p.northing),\n xytext=(9, 6), textcoords=\"offset points\", fontsize=8,\n fontweight=\"bold\", color=\"#222222\", zorder=7,\n )\n _format_grid(ax, zone)\n _scale_bar(ax, style)\n _north_arrow(ax)\n ax.legend(\n handles=[\n Patch(facecolor=colour, edgecolor=\"#222222\",\n label=f\"{name} ({lo:g}\"\n + (f\"-{hi:g} S)\" if math.isfinite(hi) else \"+ S)\"))\n for lo, hi, name, colour in PROTECTIVE_CLASSES\n ],\n loc=\"lower right\", fontsize=7, framealpha=0.95,\n title=\"Longitudinal conductance of the cover\",\n title_fontsize=7.5,\n )\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef _protective_colour(conductance: float | None) -> str:\n if conductance is None:\n return \"#BBBBBB\"\n for lo, hi, _name, colour in PROTECTIVE_CLASSES:\n if lo <= conductance < hi:\n return colour\n return PROTECTIVE_CLASSES[-1][3]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The traverse: putting the soundings on a line\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass TraverseProfile:\n \"\"\"Soundings projected onto the best-fit line through them.\n\n ``chainage_m`` is the distance along that line from its first\n station, which is what a cross-section's horizontal axis wants.\n ``offset_m`` is how far each sounding sits off the line, and it is\n the number that decides whether a section through these points means\n anything: soundings scattered 300 m either side of a line are not a\n section, they are a map drawn edge-on, and ``straightness`` says so\n rather than leaving the figure to imply otherwise.\n \"\"\"\n\n labels: list[str]\n chainage_m: np.ndarray\n offset_m: np.ndarray\n #: the largest perpendicular offset, in metres\n max_offset_m: float\n #: max offset as a fraction of the traverse length\n straightness: float\n #: bearing of the profile line, degrees clockwise from north\n bearing_deg: float\n eastings: np.ndarray\n northings: np.ndarray\n\n @property\n def is_collinear(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"True when the soundings sit close enough to a line to section.\n\n A tenth of the traverse length is the working rule: on a 400 m\n line that is 40 m, which is inside the positional error of a\n handheld GPS under canopy and well inside the lateral resolution\n of a Schlumberger sounding.\n \"\"\"\n return self.straightness <= 0.10\n\n @property\n def length_m(self) -> float:\n return float(self.chainage_m.max() - self.chainage_m.min())\n\n\ndef traverse_profile(interpretations: list) -> TraverseProfile:\n \"\"\"Project positioned soundings onto the best-fit line through them.\n\n The line is the principal axis of the positions (total least\n squares), not the line joining the first and last sounding: a\n traverse with a dog-leg in the middle has no reason to be summarised\n by its endpoints, and the endpoints are exactly the two stations most\n likely to have been added last and placed loosely.\n\n Soundings are returned in order along the line, which is the order a\n section draws them in. That is not always field order, and where it\n differs, field order was drawing the section back on itself.\n \"\"\"\n positioned = _positioned(interpretations)\n if len(positioned) < 2:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"{len(positioned)} of {len(interpretations)} soundings carry a \"\n \"position. A traverse needs at least two: record the GPS \"\n \"position of every sounding on the field sheet.\"\n )\n e = np.array([float(i.site_easting) for i in positioned])\n n = np.array([float(i.site_northing) for i in positioned])\n labels = [i.sounding_id or f\"VES {k + 1}\" for k, i in enumerate(positioned)]\n\n centre = np.array([e.mean(), n.mean()])\n coords = np.column_stack([e, n]) - centre\n # the principal axis is the first right singular vector\n _u, _s, vt = np.linalg.svd(coords, full_matrices=False)\n direction = vt[0]\n # The sign of a singular vector is arbitrary, so the same five soundings\n # handed over in a different order came back as a section drawn the other\n # way round - the same ground, mirrored, with the chainages reversed. The\n # line is made to run eastwards, or northwards where it is within a degree\n # of north-south, so a survey has one section rather than two.\n if direction[0] < 0 or (direction[0] == 0 and direction[1] < 0):\n direction = -direction\n normal = np.array([-direction[1], direction[0]])\n along = coords @ direction\n across = coords @ normal\n\n order = np.argsort(along)\n along, across = along[order], across[order]\n chainage = along - along.min()\n length = float(chainage.max()) or 1.0\n max_offset = float(np.abs(across).max())\n bearing = (math.degrees(math.atan2(direction[0], direction[1]))) % 180.0\n return TraverseProfile(\n labels=[labels[k] for k in order],\n chainage_m=chainage,\n offset_m=across,\n max_offset_m=max_offset,\n straightness=max_offset / length,\n bearing_deg=bearing,\n eastings=e[order],\n northings=n[order],\n )\n\n\ndef geoelectric_section_along_traverse(\n interpretations: list,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n depth_max: float | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"The interpreted section, drawn at the soundings' real spacing.\n\n :func:`groundwater.ves.plots.plot_geoelectric_section` already draws\n this picture, but it has to be told where the soundings are and its\n default is to space them 100 m apart in the order they were handed\n over. A survey that walked 40 m between two pegs and 300 m to the\n next came out evenly spaced, which reads as a uniformly thickening\n weathered zone when what the ground did was thicken over 40 m and\n hold for 300.\n\n This projects the soundings onto the best-fit line through their\n recorded positions and hands the real chainages over, so the\n horizontal axis is ground distance. Where the soundings are too\n scattered for a line to mean anything the title says so, rather than\n the figure implying a section nobody could walk.\n \"\"\"\n from ..ves.plots import plot_geoelectric_section\n\n profile = traverse_profile(interpretations)\n by_id = {\n (interp.sounding_id or f\"VES {k + 1}\"): interp\n for k, interp in enumerate(interpretations)\n }\n ordered = [by_id[label] for label in profile.labels if label in by_id]\n if len(ordered) < 2:\n raise ValueError(\n \"the traverse and the interpretations share fewer than two \"\n \"sounding identifiers, so the section cannot be placed\"\n )\n if title is None:\n title = (\n f\"Interpreted geoelectric section, {profile.length_m:.0f} m along \"\n f\"bearing {profile.bearing_deg:.0f} degrees\"\n )\n if not profile.is_collinear:\n title += (\n f\" (soundings up to {profile.max_offset_m:.0f} m off the line)\"\n )\n # A column stands for the ground the sounding sampled, which is about\n # its largest electrode half-spacing either side of the peg - not for\n # an equal share of the profile. Two Rokel soundings 20 km apart came\n # out as two columns 8 km wide, which claims each sounding measured\n # 8 km of ground.\n reach = max(\n (float(getattr(i, \"investigation_depth_m\", 0.0)) for i in ordered),\n default=0.0,\n )\n if depth_max is None and reach > 0:\n # the section is drawn to the depth the soundings resolve, the same\n # rule as every other figure, and never so shallow that a fitted\n # interface falls off the bottom of it\n deepest_interface = max(\n (float(i.model.depths_top[-1]) for i in ordered if i.model.n_layers > 1),\n default=0.0,\n )\n depth_max = max(reach, deepest_interface * 1.2 + 2.0)\n # A boundary is correlated between two stations only when they are\n # within the correlation rule of each other. Two Rokel soundings 20.7 km\n # apart used to come out as a 60 m section with a dashed horizon joining\n # them: a line between two points in different chiefdoms, called a\n # section. Where no pair of neighbours is within reach there is no\n # section to draw and the caller is told why; where some are, the\n # boundaries are correlated across those gaps only.\n gaps = np.diff(np.asarray(profile.chainage_m, float))\n wide = _wide_gaps(profile, reach)\n if wide and all(wide):\n widest = float(gaps.max())\n raise ValueError(\n f\"the soundings are {widest:,.0f} m apart, about {widest / reach:.0f} \"\n f\"times the {reach:,.0f} m they resolve; a section between them would \"\n \"join two measurements with no measurement between, so none is drawn. \"\n \"A section needs stations within a few times the depth of \"\n \"investigation of each other.\"\n )\n return plot_geoelectric_section(\n [interp.model for interp in ordered],\n positions=[float(x) for x in profile.chainage_m],\n labels=[interp.sounding_id or \"VES\" for interp in ordered],\n path=path, style=style, depth_max=depth_max, title=title,\n half_width_m=reach or None,\n correlate=[not w for w in wide] or None,\n note=_correlation_note(profile, reach, wide),\n )\n\n\n#: Stations further apart than this many times the depth of investigation\n#: have nothing measured between them: no boundary is correlated across\n#: such a gap, and a survey with no closer pair gets no section at all.\nCORRELATION_REACH_MULTIPLE = 10.0\n\n\ndef _wide_gaps(profile: \"TraverseProfile\", reach_m: float) -> list[bool]:\n \"\"\"Which gaps between neighbouring stations are too wide to correlate.\"\"\"\n if reach_m <= 0 or len(profile.chainage_m) < 2:\n return []\n gaps = np.diff(np.asarray(profile.chainage_m, float))\n return [bool(gap > reach_m * CORRELATION_REACH_MULTIPLE) for gap in gaps]\n\n\ndef _correlation_note(profile: \"TraverseProfile\", reach_m: float,\n wide: list[bool] | None = None) -> str:\n \"\"\"What is not correlated on the section, and why.\n\n A sounding sees the ground under it, to a lateral reach of roughly\n its largest electrode half-spacing. Joining a layer boundary across\n a gap many times that is drawing a line between two points and\n calling it a horizon. The classic rule of thumb is that correlation\n needs stations no more than a few times the depth of investigation\n apart; beyond about ten times there is nothing between them at all,\n and the section leaves such a gap uncorrelated and says so.\n \"\"\"\n if wide is None:\n wide = _wide_gaps(profile, reach_m)\n if reach_m <= 0 or len(profile.chainage_m) < 2 or not any(wide):\n return \"\"\n gaps = np.diff(np.asarray(profile.chainage_m, float))\n parts = [\n f\"{profile.labels[k]} to {profile.labels[k + 1]} ({gaps[k]:,.0f} m, about \"\n f\"{gaps[k] / reach_m:.0f} times the {reach_m:,.0f} m the soundings reached)\"\n for k, is_wide in enumerate(wide) if is_wide\n ]\n return (\n \"No boundary is correlated across the gap \"\n + \"; \".join(parts)\n + \": there is no measurement between those stations, and a dashed \"\n \"line across them would be a proposal drawn as a horizon.\"\n )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The pseudo-section\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef apparent_resistivity_pseudosection(\n soundings: list,\n profile: TraverseProfile | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Apparent resistivity pseudo-section along the traverse\",\n):\n \"\"\"The measurements themselves, laid out along the traverse.\n\n Every other subsurface figure in this module is drawn from the\n inverted layer models, which are one interpretation of the curves\n among several that fit them. This one is not: each cell is a reading\n off the instrument, plotted at the station it was taken at and the\n electrode spacing it was taken with. If the inversion is wrong, this\n figure is still right.\n\n The vertical axis is AB/2 - the electrode half-spacing - and is\n labelled as such rather than converted to a depth. Current spreads\n further as the electrodes spread, so a larger AB/2 does see deeper,\n but the pseudo-depth conversions are rules of thumb that vary with\n the very layering the section is being drawn to reveal. Calling a\n measurement geometry a depth is how a pseudo-section starts being\n read as a cross-section.\n\n ``profile`` places the stations; without one the soundings are laid\n out in the order given, evenly spaced, and the figure says so.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n if len(soundings) < 2:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"a pseudo-section needs at least two soundings; got {len(soundings)}\"\n )\n by_id = {s.sounding_id or f\"VES {k + 1}\": s for k, s in enumerate(soundings)}\n if profile is not None:\n ordered = [by_id[label] for label in profile.labels if label in by_id]\n stations = [\n float(x) for label, x in zip(profile.labels, profile.chainage_m, strict=True)\n if label in by_id\n ]\n x_label = \"Distance along traverse (m)\"\n spaced_evenly = False\n else:\n ordered = list(soundings)\n stations = [float(k) * 100.0 for k in range(len(ordered))]\n x_label = \"Station (evenly spaced; no positions recorded)\"\n spaced_evenly = True\n if len(ordered) < 2:\n raise ValueError(\n \"the traverse profile and the soundings share fewer than two \"\n \"sounding identifiers, so the stations cannot be placed\"\n )\n\n xs: list[float] = []\n ys: list[float] = []\n vs: list[float] = []\n for station, sounding in zip(stations, ordered, strict=True):\n for ab2, rho in zip(sounding.ab2, sounding.rho_app, strict=True):\n if not (math.isfinite(ab2) and math.isfinite(rho)) or rho <= 0:\n continue\n xs.append(station)\n ys.append(float(ab2))\n vs.append(float(rho))\n if len(vs) < 4:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"{len(vs)} usable readings across {len(ordered)} soundings; a \"\n \"pseudo-section needs a curve at each station.\"\n )\n\n x = np.array(xs)\n y = np.array(ys)\n v = np.array(vs)\n # Colour is interpolated between two stations only when they are within\n # the correlation rule of each other; between a pair further apart\n # there is no measurement, and a continuous banded fill across 20 km\n # read as a 20 km resistivity cross-section.\n max_gap = float(np.max(y)) * 0.5 * CORRELATION_REACH_MULTIPLE\n uncorrelated: list[tuple[str, str, float]] = []\n for k in range(len(stations) - 1):\n gap = stations[k + 1] - stations[k]\n if gap > max_gap:\n uncorrelated.append((ordered[k].sounding_id or \"VES\",\n ordered[k + 1].sounding_id or \"VES\", gap))\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 3.4))\n vmin = max(float(v.min()), 1.0)\n vmax = max(float(v.max()), vmin * 1.05)\n norm = LogNorm(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)\n # Levels spaced the way the colours are. Asking for a plain level\n # count under a log norm gets evenly spaced levels in ohm-m, which\n # a log ramp then squeezes into two bands: a section spanning 60 to\n # 900 ohm-m came out one flat colour with a stripe through it, and\n # the fill disagreed with the very readings drawn on top of it.\n levels = np.logspace(math.log10(vmin), math.log10(vmax), 14)\n # a triangulated fill between the readings, then the readings\n # themselves on top: the colour between two stations is\n # interpolation and the dots are where the instrument actually was\n if len(np.unique(x)) >= 2 and len(np.unique(y)) >= 2:\n from matplotlib.tri import Triangulation\n\n tri = Triangulation(x, np.log10(y))\n span = x[tri.triangles].max(axis=1) - x[tri.triangles].min(axis=1)\n tri.set_mask(span > max_gap)\n if not tri.mask.all():\n ax.tricontourf(tri, v, levels=levels, cmap=\"viridis\",\n norm=norm, alpha=0.85, extend=\"both\")\n sc = ax.scatter(x, np.log10(y), c=v, cmap=\"viridis\", norm=norm,\n s=22, edgecolors=\"white\", linewidths=0.6, zorder=5)\n cbar = fig.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, pad=0.02)\n cbar.set_label(\"Apparent resistivity (ohm-m)\")\n # decade ticks, but only the ones the readings reach: an 80 m spread\n # does not get a 100 m tick\n ticks = [t for t in np.unique(np.round(np.log10(y)))\n if y.min() / 1.5 <= 10 ** t <= y.max() * 1.5]\n ax.set_yticks(ticks)\n ax.set_yticklabels([f\"{10 ** t:g}\" for t in ticks])\n ax.invert_yaxis()\n ax.set_ylabel(\"AB/2 (m)\")\n ax.set_xlabel(x_label)\n # station names above the frame, clear of the shallowest readings;\n # the end stations lean inwards so they stay on the page\n for k, (station, sounding) in enumerate(zip(stations, ordered, strict=True)):\n ha = \"center\"\n if len(stations) > 1 and k == 0:\n ha = \"left\"\n elif len(stations) > 1 and k == len(stations) - 1:\n ha = \"right\"\n ax.annotate(\n sounding.sounding_id or \"VES\", xy=(station, np.log10(y.min())),\n xytext=(0, 4), textcoords=\"offset points\", ha=ha,\n va=\"bottom\", fontsize=7.5, fontweight=\"bold\",\n color=style.accent_color, annotation_clip=False,\n )\n notes = [\n (\"AB/2 is the electrode half-spacing, not a depth: a deeper \"\n \"reading is a wider spread, not a measured horizon.\"),\n ]\n if uncorrelated:\n notes.append(\n \"No colour is interpolated across \"\n + \"; \".join(f\"{a} to {b} ({gap:,.0f} m)\" for a, b, gap in uncorrelated)\n + \": nothing was measured between those stations.\"\n )\n if spaced_evenly:\n notes.append(\n \"Stations are drawn evenly spaced because no sounding \"\n \"positions were recorded; the horizontal scale is not ground \"\n \"distance.\"\n )\n elif profile is not None and not profile.is_collinear:\n notes.append(\n f\"The soundings sit up to {profile.max_offset_m:.0f} m off the \"\n f\"profile line ({profile.straightness * 100:.0f}% of its \"\n f\"{profile.length_m:.0f} m length), so this section cuts \"\n \"across the survey rather than along it.\"\n )\n ax.text(\n 0.5, -0.30, \" \".join(notes), transform=ax.transAxes, ha=\"center\",\n va=\"top\", fontsize=6.8, color=\"#555555\", wrap=True,\n )\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.grid(True, color=\"#DDDDDD\", lw=0.4)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n"}, "groundwater/mapping/terrain.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Topography: elevation grids read from the field, and the maps drawn from them.\n\nThis module draws the land surface. It does not carry one. No digital\nelevation model is bundled with the toolkit and none is downloaded, so\nevery topographic map here is drawn from a file the operator supplied,\nand the figure names that file's source on its own face.\n\nThat is deliberate. A topographic map is read as measurement - a\nhydrogeologist looking at a contour will site a borehole in the valley it\ndraws - and an elevation surface interpolated from the handful of spot\nheights a survey happens to record is not a measurement of the landscape.\nIt is a guess about the ground between the pegs. So the survey's own\nelevations are drawn as spot heights and as a ground profile along the\ntraverse, where they are exactly what they claim to be, and the contoured\nmap waits for a real elevation model.\n\nThree formats are read, all with numpy alone, because a drilling\nsupervisor with a laptop in Makeni can obtain any of them and cannot\ninstall GDAL:\n\n``.hgt``\n An SRTM tile as NASA publishes it: raw big-endian int16, 1201x1201\n (3 arc-second) or 3601x3601 (1 arc-second), no header at all. The\n filename carries the south-west corner (``N08W013.hgt``).\n``.asc`` / ``.grd``\n An ESRI ASCII grid: six header lines then the rows, north to south.\n Every GIS exports it.\n``.xyz`` / ``.csv``\n Three columns of longitude, latitude, elevation on a regular grid,\n in any row order. What a phone GPS logger and most online elevation\n services hand back.\n\nA void in any of them (SRTM's -32768, the grid's own NODATA value) is\ncarried through as NaN rather than as a number, so a hole in the data is\ndrawn as a hole rather than as a hollow in the ground.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..models import SiteMetadata\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\nfrom .regional import (\n ADMIN_CREDIT,\n AreaWindow,\n _geo_axes_finish,\n _mark_site,\n area_window,\n load_admin,\n)\n\n#: SRTM marks a void with this value; it is not an elevation.\n_SRTM_VOID = -32768\n\n\ndef _land_cmap():\n \"\"\"Matplotlib's ``terrain`` ramp with its bathymetry cut off.\n\n The lower quarter of ``terrain`` is blue, because the ramp is built\n for maps that carry the sea bed as well as the land. Used on a land\n elevation map it draws everything under about 25 m as water - which\n over the Sierra Leone coastal plain is most of the ground a borehole\n gets drilled into, and reads as a lagoon that is not there.\n \"\"\"\n from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap\n\n base = plt.get_cmap(\"terrain\")\n return LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(\n \"terrain_land\", base(np.linspace(0.25, 1.0, 256))\n )\n\n#: What ``.hgt`` side lengths mean, by the number of int16 samples in the file.\n_HGT_SIDES = {1201: \"3 arc-second (about 90 m)\", 3601: \"1 arc-second (about 30 m)\"}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ElevationGrid:\n \"\"\"A regular grid of ground elevations in geographic coordinates.\n\n ``lons`` and ``lats`` are the cell-centre coordinates of the columns\n and rows; ``z`` is ``(len(lats), len(lons))`` metres above the datum\n the source used, with NaN where the source had no value. ``lats``\n ascends, so row 0 is the southern edge - matplotlib's convention, not\n the raster convention, and the readers flip northern-first files to\n match rather than leaving each caller to remember which way up its\n data came.\n\n ``source`` is what the figure credits. It is not decoration: a\n contour map with no stated source is a contour map nobody can check.\n \"\"\"\n\n lons: np.ndarray\n lats: np.ndarray\n z: np.ndarray\n source: str = \"user-supplied elevation model\"\n #: metres per sample, for the resolution note on the figure\n resolution_note: str = \"\"\n\n def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n self.lons = np.asarray(self.lons, dtype=float)\n self.lats = np.asarray(self.lats, dtype=float)\n self.z = np.asarray(self.z, dtype=float)\n if self.z.shape != (len(self.lats), len(self.lons)):\n raise ValueError(\n f\"elevation grid is {self.z.shape}, but {len(self.lats)} \"\n f\"latitudes and {len(self.lons)} longitudes were given\"\n )\n\n @property\n def bounds(self) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:\n \"\"\"``(lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max)`` of the cell centres.\"\"\"\n return (\n float(self.lons.min()), float(self.lats.min()),\n float(self.lons.max()), float(self.lats.max()),\n )\n\n def covers(self, lon: float, lat: float) -> bool:\n lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max = self.bounds\n return lon_min <= lon <= lon_max and lat_min <= lat <= lat_max\n\n def elevation_at(self, lon: float, lat: float) -> float | None:\n \"\"\"Bilinear elevation at a point, or ``None`` outside or in a void.\"\"\"\n if not self.covers(lon, lat):\n return None\n ix = float(np.interp(lon, self.lons, np.arange(len(self.lons))))\n iy = float(np.interp(lat, self.lats, np.arange(len(self.lats))))\n x0, y0 = int(math.floor(ix)), int(math.floor(iy))\n x1 = min(x0 + 1, len(self.lons) - 1)\n y1 = min(y0 + 1, len(self.lats) - 1)\n fx, fy = ix - x0, iy - y0\n corners = np.array([\n [self.z[y0, x0], self.z[y0, x1]],\n [self.z[y1, x0], self.z[y1, x1]],\n ], dtype=float)\n if not np.all(np.isfinite(corners)):\n return None # a void is not an elevation, and averaging one is worse\n top = corners[0, 0] * (1 - fx) + corners[0, 1] * fx\n bottom = corners[1, 0] * (1 - fx) + corners[1, 1] * fx\n return float(top * (1 - fy) + bottom * fy)\n\n def window(self, lon: float, lat: float, radius_km: float) -> \"ElevationGrid\":\n \"\"\"The part of the grid inside a square window, for a local map.\n\n A whole SRTM tile is 1201x1201 samples and a 5 km site map wants\n about 120 of them across. Contouring the whole tile to show a\n tenth of a degree of it is slow and, worse, flattens the colour\n ramp onto the range of a mountain range the site is nowhere near.\n\n The window keeps one row and column beyond each edge where the\n grid has them, so a contour crossing the frame is drawn to the\n frame rather than stopping short of it.\n \"\"\"\n dlat = radius_km / 111.32\n dlon = radius_km / (111.32 * max(math.cos(math.radians(lat)), 1e-6))\n ix = np.where((self.lons >= lon - dlon) & (self.lons <= lon + dlon))[0]\n iy = np.where((self.lats >= lat - dlat) & (self.lats <= lat + dlat))[0]\n if len(ix) < 2 or len(iy) < 2:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"the elevation model covers {_bounds_text(self.bounds)}, which \"\n f\"holds fewer than two samples of the {radius_km:g} km window \"\n f\"around {abs(lat):.4f} {'N' if lat >= 0 else 'S'}, \"\n f\"{abs(lon):.4f} {'E' if lon >= 0 else 'W'}. Supply a model \"\n \"covering the site, or widen the window.\"\n )\n x0, x1 = max(ix[0] - 1, 0), min(ix[-1] + 2, len(self.lons))\n y0, y1 = max(iy[0] - 1, 0), min(iy[-1] + 2, len(self.lats))\n return ElevationGrid(\n self.lons[x0:x1], self.lats[y0:y1], self.z[y0:y1, x0:x1],\n source=self.source, resolution_note=self.resolution_note,\n )\n\n\ndef _bounds_text(bounds: tuple[float, float, float, float]) -> str:\n lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max = bounds\n return (\n f\"{abs(lat_min):.3f}-{abs(lat_max):.3f} \"\n f\"{'N' if lat_min >= 0 else 'S'}, \"\n f\"{abs(lon_max):.3f}-{abs(lon_min):.3f} \"\n f\"{'E' if lon_min >= 0 else 'W'}\"\n )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Readers\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef read_srtm_hgt(path: str | Path) -> ElevationGrid:\n \"\"\"Read one SRTM ``.hgt`` tile.\n\n The file is nothing but samples - big-endian int16, northern row\n first - so the corner comes from the name (``N08W013.hgt`` is the\n tile whose south-west corner is 8 N, 13 W) and the resolution from\n the file's own length. A name that does not carry a corner is an\n error rather than a guess: placing a tile in the wrong degree square\n puts the contours 100 km from the site with nothing on the figure to\n say so.\n \"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n match = re.match(\n r\"^([NS])(\\d{2})([EW])(\\d{3})\", path.stem.upper()\n )\n if match is None:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' does not name its corner. An SRTM tile is named \"\n \"for its south-west corner, as in N08W013.hgt; the file itself \"\n \"carries no header saying where on Earth it is.\"\n )\n ns, lat_deg, ew, lon_deg = match.groups()\n lat0 = float(lat_deg) * (1 if ns == \"N\" else -1)\n lon0 = float(lon_deg) * (1 if ew == \"E\" else -1)\n\n raw = np.fromfile(str(path), dtype=\">i2\")\n side = int(round(math.sqrt(raw.size)))\n if side * side != raw.size or side not in _HGT_SIDES:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' holds {raw.size} samples, which is not a square \"\n f\"SRTM tile ({' or '.join(f'{s}x{s}' for s in _HGT_SIDES)}).\"\n )\n grid = raw.reshape(side, side).astype(float)\n grid[grid == _SRTM_VOID] = np.nan\n # the file runs north to south; ElevationGrid runs south to north\n grid = grid[::-1, :]\n step = 1.0 / (side - 1)\n lons = lon0 + np.arange(side) * step\n lats = lat0 + np.arange(side) * step\n return ElevationGrid(\n lons, lats, grid,\n source=f\"SRTM tile {path.stem.upper()} (NASA/USGS, public domain)\",\n resolution_note=_HGT_SIDES[side],\n )\n\n\ndef read_esri_ascii(path: str | Path) -> ElevationGrid:\n \"\"\"Read an ESRI ASCII grid (``.asc``).\n\n Six header lines then the rows, north first. ``xllcorner`` gives the\n outer edge of the first cell and ``xllcenter`` its centre; both are\n accepted, and the difference between them is half a cell - which at\n 3 arc-seconds is 45 m, enough to move a contour off a valley.\n \"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n header: dict[str, float] = {}\n rows: list[list[float]] = []\n with open(path, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n for line in fh:\n parts = line.split()\n if not parts:\n continue\n key = parts[0].lower()\n if key in {\n \"ncols\", \"nrows\", \"xllcorner\", \"yllcorner\", \"xllcenter\",\n \"yllcenter\", \"cellsize\", \"nodata_value\",\n }:\n header[key] = float(parts[1])\n continue\n rows.append([float(v) for v in parts])\n\n for required in (\"ncols\", \"nrows\", \"cellsize\"):\n if required not in header:\n raise ValueError(f\"'{path.name}' has no {required} in its header\")\n ncols, nrows = int(header[\"ncols\"]), int(header[\"nrows\"])\n cell = header[\"cellsize\"]\n if \"xllcenter\" in header:\n x0, y0 = header[\"xllcenter\"], header[\"yllcenter\"]\n else:\n x0 = header[\"xllcorner\"] + cell / 2.0\n y0 = header[\"yllcorner\"] + cell / 2.0\n\n flat = np.array([v for row in rows for v in row], dtype=float)\n if flat.size != ncols * nrows:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' declares {nrows}x{ncols} cells but holds \"\n f\"{flat.size} values\"\n )\n grid = flat.reshape(nrows, ncols)\n nodata = header.get(\"nodata_value\")\n if nodata is not None:\n grid = np.where(grid == nodata, np.nan, grid)\n grid = grid[::-1, :] # the file runs north to south\n return ElevationGrid(\n x0 + np.arange(ncols) * cell,\n y0 + np.arange(nrows) * cell,\n grid,\n source=f\"elevation grid {path.name}\",\n resolution_note=f\"{cell * 111320:.0f} m cell\",\n )\n\n\ndef read_xyz(path: str | Path) -> ElevationGrid:\n \"\"\"Read longitude, latitude, elevation columns onto a regular grid.\n\n Row order does not matter; the distinct longitudes and latitudes are\n recovered and each triple placed in its cell. Any cell no row filled\n stays NaN, so a partial export is a map with a hole in it rather than\n a map with a fabricated hollow.\n\n A file whose points do not sit on a regular grid is refused. Gridding\n scattered heights is interpolation, and interpolating a landscape\n from scattered points is the thing this module will not do quietly.\n \"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n values: list[tuple[float, float, float]] = []\n with open(path, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n for line in fh:\n line = line.strip()\n if not line or line[0] in \"#;\":\n continue\n parts = re.split(r\"[,\\s;]+\", line)\n if len(parts) < 3:\n continue\n try:\n values.append((float(parts[0]), float(parts[1]), float(parts[2])))\n except ValueError:\n continue # a header row, named or not\n if len(values) < 4:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' holds {len(values)} usable rows; an elevation \"\n \"grid needs at least a 2x2 block of longitude, latitude, elevation.\"\n )\n arr = np.array(values, dtype=float)\n lons = np.unique(np.round(arr[:, 0], 9))\n lats = np.unique(np.round(arr[:, 1], 9))\n if len(lons) < 2 or len(lats) < 2:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' spans {len(lons)} longitudes and {len(lats)} \"\n \"latitudes; a grid needs at least two of each.\"\n )\n if len(lons) * len(lats) < len(arr):\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' holds {len(arr)} rows over a \"\n f\"{len(lats)}x{len(lons)} grid, so some cells are given twice. \"\n \"This reader places points on a grid; it does not interpolate.\"\n )\n # A regular grid has evenly spaced columns and rows. Without this, any\n # scatter of points is a \"grid\" whose axes are the distinct coordinates\n # that happen to appear, and searchsorted drops each reading into a cell\n # chosen by rounding - a landscape assembled out of nothing.\n for axis, values in ((\"longitudes\", lons), (\"latitudes\", lats)):\n steps = np.diff(values)\n if len(steps) > 1 and steps.std() > steps.mean() * 0.01:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' has unevenly spaced {axis}, so its points do \"\n \"not lie on a regular grid. This reader places points on a \"\n \"grid; it does not interpolate a surface from scattered \"\n \"heights.\"\n )\n filled = int(np.isfinite(grid_fill_probe(arr, lons, lats)).sum())\n cells = len(lons) * len(lats)\n if filled * 2 < cells:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' fills {filled} of {cells} cells in the \"\n f\"{len(lats)}x{len(lons)} grid its coordinates imply. That is a \"\n \"scatter of points rather than a grid with gaps in it, and this \"\n \"reader does not interpolate a surface from scattered heights.\"\n )\n grid = np.full((len(lats), len(lons)), np.nan)\n ix = np.searchsorted(lons, np.round(arr[:, 0], 9))\n iy = np.searchsorted(lats, np.round(arr[:, 1], 9))\n grid[iy, ix] = arr[:, 2]\n step = float(np.median(np.diff(lons))) if len(lons) > 1 else 0.0\n return ElevationGrid(\n lons, lats, grid,\n source=f\"elevation grid {path.name}\",\n resolution_note=f\"{step * 111320:.0f} m cell\" if step else \"\",\n )\n\n\ndef grid_fill_probe(\n arr: np.ndarray, lons: np.ndarray, lats: np.ndarray\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"The grid an XYZ file would produce, for counting how full it is.\"\"\"\n grid = np.full((len(lats), len(lons)), np.nan)\n grid[np.searchsorted(lats, np.round(arr[:, 1], 9)),\n np.searchsorted(lons, np.round(arr[:, 0], 9))] = arr[:, 2]\n return grid\n\n\n_READERS = {\n \".hgt\": read_srtm_hgt,\n \".asc\": read_esri_ascii,\n \".grd\": read_esri_ascii,\n \".xyz\": read_xyz,\n \".csv\": read_xyz,\n \".txt\": read_xyz,\n}\n\n\ndef load_elevation(path: str | Path) -> ElevationGrid:\n \"\"\"Read an elevation model, choosing the reader by file extension.\"\"\"\n path = Path(path)\n reader = _READERS.get(path.suffix.lower())\n if reader is None:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"'{path.name}' is not an elevation format this toolkit reads. \"\n f\"It reads {', '.join(sorted(_READERS))}: an SRTM .hgt tile, an \"\n \"ESRI ASCII grid, or longitude/latitude/elevation columns. A \"\n \"GeoTIFF can be converted with `gdal_translate -of AAIGrid`.\"\n )\n return reader(path)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Derived surfaces\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef hillshade(\n grid: ElevationGrid,\n azimuth_deg: float = 315.0,\n altitude_deg: float = 45.0,\n vertical_exaggeration: float = 1.0,\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Shaded relief from the grid, 0 (shadow) to 1 (lit).\n\n The standard north-west sun, because relief lit from any other\n quarter reads as inverted to most people - valleys become ridges.\n\n The cell size is computed in metres at the grid's own latitude, so\n the slopes are real slopes and not a function of how far north the\n tile happens to be.\n \"\"\"\n mean_lat = float(np.mean(grid.lats))\n dx = float(np.mean(np.diff(grid.lons))) * 111320.0 * math.cos(math.radians(mean_lat))\n dy = float(np.mean(np.diff(grid.lats))) * 110574.0\n z = np.where(np.isfinite(grid.z), grid.z, np.nanmean(grid.z))\n if not np.any(np.isfinite(z)):\n return np.full(grid.z.shape, 0.5)\n gy, gx = np.gradient(z * vertical_exaggeration, dy, dx)\n slope = np.arctan(np.hypot(gx, gy))\n aspect = np.arctan2(-gx, gy)\n az = math.radians(360.0 - azimuth_deg + 90.0)\n alt = math.radians(altitude_deg)\n shaded = (\n math.sin(alt) * np.cos(slope)\n + math.cos(alt) * np.sin(slope) * np.cos(az - aspect)\n )\n return np.clip((shaded + 1.0) / 2.0, 0.0, 1.0)\n\n\ndef slope_percent(grid: ElevationGrid) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Ground slope as a percentage, for siting and access notes.\"\"\"\n mean_lat = float(np.mean(grid.lats))\n dx = float(np.mean(np.diff(grid.lons))) * 111320.0 * math.cos(math.radians(mean_lat))\n dy = float(np.mean(np.diff(grid.lats))) * 110574.0\n gy, gx = np.gradient(grid.z, dy, dx)\n return np.hypot(gx, gy) * 100.0\n\n\ndef _contour_interval(z: np.ndarray) -> float:\n \"\"\"A round contour interval giving roughly a dozen lines.\n\n Sierra Leone's basement plains and the Freetown peninsula differ by\n two orders of magnitude in relief, so a fixed interval draws either\n two contours or four hundred.\n \"\"\"\n finite = z[np.isfinite(z)]\n if finite.size == 0:\n return 10.0\n relief = float(finite.max() - finite.min())\n if relief <= 0:\n return 10.0\n target = relief / 12.0\n nice = 10 ** math.floor(math.log10(target))\n for mult in (10, 5, 2, 1):\n if nice * mult <= target * 2:\n return max(nice * mult, 1.0)\n return max(nice, 1.0)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The map\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef plot_topographic_map(\n grid: ElevationGrid,\n site: SiteMetadata | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n radius_km: float | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n contour_interval_m: float | None = None,\n spot_heights: list[tuple[float, float, str]] | None = None,\n show_hillshade: bool = True,\n admin_path: str | Path | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Topographic map of the study area: relief, contours and spot heights.\n\n ``grid`` is the elevation model; ``radius_km`` cuts a local window\n around the site out of it. The figure carries the model's own source\n and sample spacing, because a contour drawn from 90 m SRTM through a\n 5 km window is a 90 m contour however finely it is plotted, and a\n reader deciding where to put a borehole is entitled to know that.\n\n ``spot_heights`` are ``(lon, lat, label)`` triples - the survey's own\n levelled points. They are drawn as measured values on top of the\n modelled surface, not blended into it: where the two disagree the\n reader can see both and the survey is the one that was on the ground.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n if radius_km is not None:\n window = area_window(site, radius_km, admin_path) if site is not None else None\n if window is not None:\n grid = grid.window(window.lon, window.lat, radius_km)\n else:\n centre_lon = float(np.mean(grid.lons))\n centre_lat = float(np.mean(grid.lats))\n grid = grid.window(centre_lon, centre_lat, radius_km)\n else:\n window = area_window(site, None, admin_path) if site is not None else None\n\n finite = grid.z[np.isfinite(grid.z)]\n if finite.size == 0:\n raise ValueError(\n \"the elevation model holds no values over this window - every \"\n \"sample is a void. A map of voids is not a map of the ground.\"\n )\n interval = contour_interval_m or _contour_interval(grid.z)\n lo = math.floor(float(finite.min()) / interval) * interval\n hi = math.ceil(float(finite.max()) / interval) * interval\n levels = np.arange(lo, hi + interval, interval)\n\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 5.6))\n extent = (\n float(grid.lons.min()), float(grid.lons.max()),\n float(grid.lats.min()), float(grid.lats.max()),\n )\n land = _land_cmap()\n ax.imshow(\n grid.z, extent=extent, origin=\"lower\", cmap=land,\n vmin=float(finite.min()), vmax=float(finite.max()),\n interpolation=\"bilinear\", zorder=1, aspect=\"auto\",\n )\n if show_hillshade:\n ax.imshow(\n hillshade(grid), extent=extent, origin=\"lower\", cmap=\"gray\",\n alpha=0.35, interpolation=\"bilinear\", zorder=2, aspect=\"auto\",\n )\n mesh_lon, mesh_lat = np.meshgrid(grid.lons, grid.lats)\n if len(levels) > 1:\n cs = ax.contour(\n mesh_lon, mesh_lat, grid.z, levels=levels,\n colors=\"#5A3A1E\", linewidths=0.6, zorder=3,\n )\n ax.clabel(cs, cs.levels[::2], fmt=\"%g\", fontsize=6.5, inline=True)\n sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(\n cmap=land,\n norm=plt.Normalize(vmin=float(finite.min()), vmax=float(finite.max())),\n )\n cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, pad=0.02, shrink=0.85)\n cbar.set_label(\"Ground elevation (m)\")\n\n # the survey's own levelled points, over the modelled surface\n for lon, lat, label in spot_heights or []:\n ax.plot(lon, lat, \"o\", ms=5, mfc=\"white\", mec=\"#222222\", mew=1.1,\n zorder=7)\n ax.annotate(label, xy=(lon, lat), xytext=(5, 4),\n textcoords=\"offset points\", fontsize=7.5,\n fontweight=\"bold\", color=\"#222222\", zorder=7)\n\n outline, _ = load_admin(admin_path)\n for ring in outline.rings:\n ax.plot(ring[:, 0], ring[:, 1], color=\"#333333\", lw=1.0, zorder=5)\n if site is not None:\n _mark_site(ax, site, \"#C1272D\")\n ax.set_xlim(extent[0], extent[1])\n ax.set_ylim(extent[2], extent[3])\n credit = grid.source\n if grid.resolution_note:\n credit += f\", {grid.resolution_note} sampling\"\n _geo_axes_finish(ax, float(np.mean(ax.get_ylim())),\n f\"Elevation: {credit}. {ADMIN_CREDIT}\")\n ax.text(\n 0.01, 0.985,\n f\"Contour interval {interval:g} m\",\n transform=ax.transAxes, ha=\"left\", va=\"top\", fontsize=7,\n color=\"#333333\", zorder=9,\n bbox=dict(boxstyle=\"round,pad=0.25\", fc=\"white\", ec=\"#CCCCCC\",\n alpha=0.9),\n )\n if title is None:\n where = _where_label(site, window)\n title = f\"Topographic map - {where}\" if where else \"Topographic map\"\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef _where_label(site: SiteMetadata | None, window: AreaWindow | None) -> str:\n if window is not None:\n return window.label\n if site is not None and (site.community or \"\"):\n return site.community\n return \"\"\n\n\ndef plot_ground_profile(\n chainage_m: list[float] | np.ndarray,\n elevation_m: list[float] | np.ndarray,\n labels: list[str] | None = None,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Ground surface along the survey traverse\",\n grid: ElevationGrid | None = None,\n lonlats: list[tuple[float, float]] | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"The land surface along the traverse, from the survey's own levels.\n\n This is the honest topographic figure a survey can always draw: the\n elevations are measured at the pegs, and between them the line is\n drawn straight and says so. Where an elevation model is also\n supplied, its surface is drawn behind as a second line, so the two\n can be compared rather than silently averaged - a metre of\n disagreement over 200 m of traverse changes which end of the line\n the water runs to.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n chainage = np.asarray(chainage_m, dtype=float)\n elevation = np.asarray(elevation_m, dtype=float)\n if chainage.size != elevation.size:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"{chainage.size} chainages and {elevation.size} elevations: a \"\n \"ground profile needs one elevation per station.\"\n )\n known = np.isfinite(elevation)\n if known.sum() < 2:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"{int(known.sum())} of {elevation.size} stations carry an \"\n \"elevation. A ground profile needs at least two levelled \"\n \"points; record them on the field sheet.\"\n )\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in, 2.6))\n if grid is not None and lonlats is not None:\n modelled = np.array([\n grid.elevation_at(lon, lat) if grid.covers(lon, lat) else np.nan\n for lon, lat in lonlats\n ], dtype=float)\n if np.isfinite(modelled).sum() >= 2:\n ax.plot(chainage, modelled, \"-\", color=\"#888888\", lw=1.2,\n label=f\"Elevation model ({grid.source})\", zorder=2)\n ax.plot(chainage[known], elevation[known], \"-o\", color=style.accent_color,\n lw=1.8, ms=5, mfc=\"white\", mew=1.4, label=\"Levelled at the station\",\n zorder=3)\n ax.fill_between(chainage[known], elevation[known],\n float(np.nanmin(elevation)) - 2.0,\n color=style.accent_color, alpha=0.08, zorder=1)\n for x, y, label in zip(\n chainage, elevation, labels or [\"\"] * chainage.size, strict=True\n ):\n if not math.isfinite(y) or not label:\n continue\n ax.annotate(label, xy=(x, y), xytext=(0, 7),\n textcoords=\"offset points\", ha=\"center\", fontsize=7.5,\n fontweight=\"bold\", color=\"#222222\")\n if known.sum() < elevation.size:\n ax.text(\n 0.5, 0.02,\n f\"{int(elevation.size - known.sum())} of {elevation.size} \"\n \"stations recorded no elevation and are not drawn.\",\n transform=ax.transAxes, ha=\"center\", va=\"bottom\", fontsize=7,\n color=\"#B00020\",\n )\n ax.set_xlabel(\"Distance along traverse (m)\")\n ax.set_ylabel(\"Elevation (m)\")\n ax.set_title(title)\n ax.legend(loc=\"best\", fontsize=7.5)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n"}, "groundwater/models.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Core data structures shared across the toolkit.\n\nEvery parser returns one of these objects and every analysis module\nconsumes them, so the raw-data-to-report chain stays traceable: each\nobject keeps a ``source`` path and parsers attach ``flags`` describing\nanything that needs analyst attention (missing discharge, inconsistent\nmetadata, negative drawdown and so on).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom .geo import UTMCoordinate, infer_zone_for_sierra_leone, utm_to_geographic\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Flags raised during parsing and checking\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass DataFlag:\n \"\"\"A data quality or consistency issue that needs analyst review.\"\"\"\n\n level: str # \"info\" | \"warning\" | \"error\"\n code: str # short machine readable code, e.g. \"missing_discharge\"\n message: str # human readable explanation\n context: str = \"\" # e.g. \"VES 2\", \"step 3\"\n\n def __str__(self) -> str:\n prefix = f\"[{self.level.upper()}] {self.code}\"\n ctx = f\" ({self.context})\" if self.context else \"\"\n return f\"{prefix}{ctx}: {self.message}\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Site metadata\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass SiteMetadata:\n \"\"\"Header block information shared by all field sheets.\"\"\"\n\n client: str = \"\"\n project: str = \"\"\n community: str = \"\"\n chiefdom: str = \"\"\n district: str = \"\"\n country: str = \"Sierra Leone\"\n project_ref: str = \"\"\n easting: Optional[float] = None\n northing: Optional[float] = None\n utm_zone: Optional[int] = None\n elevation_m: Optional[float] = None\n date: str = \"\"\n supervisor: str = \"\"\n contractor: str = \"\"\n source: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def utm(self) -> Optional[UTMCoordinate]:\n if self.easting is None or self.northing is None:\n return None\n # A fixed fallback puts half the country in the Atlantic: the two\n # zones are 6 degrees (about 660 km) apart. The easting alone\n # identifies the zone in Sierra Leone, so infer it rather than guess.\n zone = self.utm_zone or infer_zone_for_sierra_leone(self.easting)\n return UTMCoordinate(self.easting, self.northing, zone)\n\n @property\n def latlon(self) -> Optional[tuple[float, float]]:\n utm = self.utm\n if utm is None:\n return None\n return utm_to_geographic(utm.easting, utm.northing, utm.zone)\n\n def merged_with(self, other: \"SiteMetadata\") -> \"SiteMetadata\":\n \"\"\"Fill blank fields from another metadata record.\n\n A field is \"blank\" only when it is None or an empty string. A genuine\n numeric zero - a sea-level elevation, or a zero UTM ordinate - counts\n as present and is never overwritten, so merging two records does not\n lose a real 0.0 datum.\n \"\"\"\n merged = SiteMetadata(**self.__dict__)\n for key, value in other.__dict__.items():\n current = getattr(merged, key)\n if (current is None or current == \"\") and value not in (None, \"\"):\n setattr(merged, key, value)\n return merged\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# VES\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass VESSounding:\n \"\"\"A single vertical electrical sounding.\n\n ``mn`` stores the full potential electrode spacing MN (not MN/2),\n matching the field sheets. Duplicate ``ab2`` values with different\n ``mn`` mark Schlumberger segment changes and are preserved.\n \"\"\"\n\n site: SiteMetadata\n sounding_id: str\n ab2: np.ndarray # AB/2 in metres\n mn: np.ndarray # full MN spacing in metres\n rho_app: np.ndarray # apparent resistivity, ohm-m\n array_type: str = \"schlumberger\"\n instrument: str = \"\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n source: str = \"\"\n\n def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n self.ab2 = np.asarray(self.ab2, dtype=float)\n self.mn = np.asarray(self.mn, dtype=float)\n self.rho_app = np.asarray(self.rho_app, dtype=float)\n # The array type decides which forward model is used, and the\n # inversion and forward code match it with a bare startswith().\n # \"Wenner\" from a hand-built sounding or a scanned sheet would\n # otherwise be inverted as Schlumberger - silently wrong by tens\n # of percent - so normalise it once, here.\n self.array_type = str(self.array_type or \"schlumberger\").strip().lower()\n\n @property\n def n_readings(self) -> int:\n return len(self.ab2)\n\n @property\n def label(self) -> str:\n return self.sounding_id or \"VES\"\n\n def segments(self) -> list[np.ndarray]:\n \"\"\"Indices of readings grouped by MN spacing, in field order.\n\n A new segment starts at each change of MN spacing. A blank/NaN MN is\n treated as a continuation of the current segment (its spacing is\n unknown, carried forward from the last real value) rather than\n starting a new one, so a single missing MN cell does not inject a\n spurious one-point segment and an absent MN column does not split\n every reading into its own segment.\n \"\"\"\n out: list[list[int]] = []\n last_mn: float | None = None\n for idx, mn in enumerate(self.mn):\n is_nan = mn != mn # NaN is the only value not equal to itself\n new_segment = not out or (\n not is_nan and last_mn is not None and mn != last_mn\n )\n if new_segment:\n out.append([])\n out[-1].append(idx)\n if not is_nan:\n last_mn = mn\n return [np.array(g, dtype=int) for g in out]\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass LayeredModel:\n \"\"\"A 1D layered earth model (the IPI2Win style result).\n\n ``thicknesses`` has one entry fewer than ``resistivities``; the\n last layer is the half-space (its thickness is infinite).\n \"\"\"\n\n resistivities: np.ndarray # ohm-m, length n\n thicknesses: np.ndarray # m, length n-1\n fit_error_percent: Optional[float] = None # RMS misfit, like IPI2Win ERR\n method: str = \"\" # \"ipi2win-import\" | \"damped-lsq\" | ...\n sounding_id: str = \"\"\n\n def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n self.resistivities = np.asarray(self.resistivities, dtype=float)\n self.thicknesses = np.asarray(self.thicknesses, dtype=float)\n if len(self.thicknesses) != len(self.resistivities) - 1:\n raise ValueError(\n \"thicknesses must have exactly one entry fewer than resistivities\"\n )\n\n @property\n def n_layers(self) -> int:\n return len(self.resistivities)\n\n @property\n def depths_top(self) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Depth to the top of each layer (first entry 0).\"\"\"\n return np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(self.thicknesses)])\n\n @property\n def depths_bottom(self) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Depth to the bottom of each layer (last entry inf).\"\"\"\n return np.concatenate([np.cumsum(self.thicknesses), [np.inf]])\n\n def as_table(self) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"Rows in the IPI2Win layout: N, rho, h, z (depth to top).\"\"\"\n rows = []\n tops = self.depths_top\n for i in range(self.n_layers):\n h = self.thicknesses[i] if i < len(self.thicknesses) else None\n z = \"0/0\" if i == 0 else tops[i]\n rows.append(\n {\n \"N\": i + 1,\n \"rho_ohm_m\": float(self.resistivities[i]),\n \"h_m\": None if h is None else float(h),\n \"z_m\": z,\n }\n )\n return rows\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Pumping test\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass PumpingStep:\n \"\"\"One step of a step-drawdown or constant discharge test.\"\"\"\n\n step_number: int\n time_min: np.ndarray # minutes since the start of the whole test\n water_level_m: np.ndarray # depth to water below datum\n discharge_m3_per_h: Optional[float] = None # None when missing on sheet\n label: str = \"\"\n\n def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n self.time_min = np.asarray(self.time_min, dtype=float)\n self.water_level_m = np.asarray(self.water_level_m, dtype=float)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass PumpingTest:\n \"\"\"A pumping test record built from the field sheet.\n\n The field sheets record an incremental \"drawdown\" column (change\n between successive readings). Parsers keep only time and water\n level; true drawdown below static is always recomputed here.\n \"\"\"\n\n site: SiteMetadata\n borehole_ref: str = \"\"\n test_type: str = \"step\" # \"step\" | \"constant\" | \"constant+recovery\"\n static_water_level_m: Optional[float] = None\n borehole_depth_m: Optional[float] = None\n pump_setting_m: Optional[float] = None\n step_length_min: Optional[float] = None\n steps: list[PumpingStep] = field(default_factory=list)\n recovery_time_min: Optional[np.ndarray] = None # minutes since pump stop\n recovery_level_m: Optional[np.ndarray] = None\n pumping_duration_min: Optional[float] = None # total pumping before recovery\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n source: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def has_discharge(self) -> bool:\n return any(s.discharge_m3_per_h is not None for s in self.steps)\n\n def drawdown(self, step: PumpingStep) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"True drawdown below static water level, metres.\"\"\"\n if self.static_water_level_m is None:\n raise ValueError(\"static water level is required to compute drawdown\")\n return step.water_level_m - self.static_water_level_m\n\n def all_times_levels(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n \"\"\"Concatenated pumping phase time series.\"\"\"\n t = np.concatenate([s.time_min for s in self.steps]) if self.steps else np.array([])\n wl = (\n np.concatenate([s.water_level_m for s in self.steps])\n if self.steps\n else np.array([])\n )\n order = np.argsort(t, kind=\"stable\")\n return t[order], wl[order]\n\n def residual_drawdown(self) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:\n if self.recovery_level_m is None or self.static_water_level_m is None:\n return None\n return self.recovery_level_m - self.static_water_level_m\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Drilling log\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass LithologyInterval:\n top_m: float\n bottom_m: float\n description: str = \"\"\n from_time: str = \"\"\n to_time: str = \"\"\n penetration_rate_m_per_min: Optional[float] = None\n bit_diameter_in: Optional[float] = None\n\n @property\n def thickness_m(self) -> float:\n return self.bottom_m - self.top_m\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass DrillingLog:\n site: SiteMetadata\n borehole_ref: str = \"\"\n total_depth_m: Optional[float] = None\n drilling_method: str = \"\"\n intervals: list[LithologyInterval] = field(default_factory=list)\n water_strikes_m: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)\n grouting_depth_m: Optional[float] = None\n # The screens the crew actually set, when the sheet records them. With\n # these the drawing is an as-built record; without them it is a design\n # generated by the rules, and says so.\n installed_screens_m: list[tuple[float, float]] = field(default_factory=list)\n start_date: str = \"\"\n completion_date: str = \"\"\n status: str = \"\" # e.g. \"Successful\"\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n source: str = \"\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Water quality\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass WaterQualityResult:\n parameter: str\n value: Optional[float]\n unit: str = \"\"\n detection_limit: Optional[float] = None\n below_detection: bool = False\n method: str = \"\"\n #: A lower bound on a result the laboratory did not quantify. \">50\" is\n #: at least 50, and \"TNTC\", \"Present\" and \"Positive\" are more than\n #: nothing, which for a determinand whose limit is zero is the whole\n #: finding.
