The two halves are not symmetric, which is why this\n # is written out rather than looped.\n for i in range(6):\n modules[i][8] = bit(i)\n modules[7][8] = bit(6)\n modules[8][8] = bit(7)\n modules[8][7] = bit(8)\n for i in range(9, 15):\n modules[8][14 - i] = bit(i)\n\n # Second copy, split between the other two finders, so a symbol with one\n # damaged corner still declares its own mask and level.\n for i in range(8):\n modules[8][size - 1 - i] = bit(i)\n for i in range(8, 15):\n modules[size - 15 + i][8] = bit(i)\n modules[size - 8][8] = True # the dark module, always\n\n\n#: Penalty weights from the standard: long runs, solid blocks, false finder\n#: patterns, and an overall bias away from 50% dark.\n_PENALTY_RUN, _PENALTY_BLOCK, _PENALTY_FINDER, _PENALTY_BALANCE = 3, 3, 40, 10\n\n\ndef _finder_like(history: list[int]) -> int:\n \"\"\"How many false finder patterns end at this point in a line.\n\n The standard describes the shape as a *ratio*, 1:1:3:1:1 with a light\n margin four units wide, so a run of 2:2:6:2:2 counts too - which is why\n this reads run lengths rather than matching a fixed seven-module window.\n \"\"\"\n unit = history[1]\n core = (unit > 0 and history[2] == unit and history[3] == unit * 3\n and history[4] == unit and history[5] == unit)\n return ((1 if core and history[0] >= unit * 4 and history[6] >= unit else 0)\n + (1 if core and history[6] >= unit * 4 and history[0] >= unit else 0))\n\n\ndef _penalty(modules) -> int:\n \"\"\"How badly a masked symbol scans. Lower is better.\n\n The standard's four rules exist because a symbol full of long runs,\n solid blocks or things that look like finder patterns is one a phone\n gives up on. Which mask wins is not a correctness question - every mask\n produces a symbol that decodes, and two conforming encoders often pick\n differently - so this is chosen for scannability, not for agreement with\n anyone else's encoder.\n \"\"\"\n size = len(modules)\n score = 0\n\n columns = [[modules[r][c] for r in range(size)] for c in range(size)]\n for line in [row[:] for row in modules] + columns:\n colour, run, history = False, 0, [0] * 7\n\n def remember(length: int) -> None:\n # The quiet zone outside the symbol is light, so a false finder\n # hard against the edge still has its margin and still counts.\n if history[0] == 0:\n length += size\n history[1:] = history[:-1]\n history[0] = length\n\n for cell in line:\n if cell == colour:\n run += 1\n if run == 5:\n score += _PENALTY_RUN\n elif run > 5:\n score += 1\n else:\n remember(run)\n if not colour:\n score += _finder_like(history) * _PENALTY_FINDER\n colour, run = cell, 1\n if colour:\n remember(run)\n run = 0\n remember(run + size)\n score += _finder_like(history) * _PENALTY_FINDER\n\n for i in range(size - 1):\n for j in range(size - 1):\n block = (modules[i][j], modules[i][j + 1],\n modules[i + 1][j], modules[i + 1][j + 1])\n if all(block) or not any(block):\n score += _PENALTY_BLOCK\n\n dark = sum(1 for row in modules for cell in row if cell)\n total = size * size\n # the smallest k with the dark share inside (50 +/- 5(k+1))%, in integers\n k = -(-abs(dark * 20 - total * 10) // total) - 1\n return score + max(k, 0) * _PENALTY_BALANCE\n\n\ndef encode(data: str | bytes, *, ecc: str = \"H\", min_version: int = 1,\n mask: int | None = None) -> QRCode:\n \"\"\"Encode ``data`` as a QR symbol.\n\n ``ecc`` is one of ``L``, ``M``, ``Q``, ``H``; ``H`` by default because\n the symbols this toolkit produces are printed and hung outdoors.\n ``min_version`` forces a larger, coarser symbol than the payload needs -\n useful when a batch of placards should all look alike. ``mask`` forces\n one of the eight mask patterns instead of scoring all eight; it exists\n for the tests, which compare against an independent encoder mask by mask.\n \"\"\"\n if ecc not in ECC_LEVELS:\n raise ValueError(f\"unknown error-correction level {ecc!r}\")\n if mask is not None and not 0 <= mask <= 7:\n raise ValueError(f\"mask must be 0 to 7, not {mask!r}\")\n payload = data.encode(\"utf-8\") if isinstance(data, str) else bytes(data)\n version = _choose_version(len(payload), ecc, min_version)\n\n bits = _interleave(_bitstream(payload, version, ecc), version, ecc)\n size = 17 + 4 * version\n modules, reserved = _blank(size)\n _place_function_patterns(modules, reserved, version)\n _place_data(modules, reserved, bits)\n\n best, best_mask, best_score = None, 0, None\n for candidate_mask in range(8) if mask is None else (mask,):\n candidate = _apply_mask(modules, reserved, candidate_mask)\n _place_format(candidate, ecc, candidate_mask)\n score = _penalty(candidate)\n if best_score is None or score < best_score:\n best, best_mask, best_score = candidate, candidate_mask, score\n return QRCode(version=version, ecc=ecc, mask=best_mask, modules=best)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Rendering\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef to_svg(code: QRCode, *, scale: int = 4, border: int = 4) -> str:\n \"\"\"The symbol as an SVG document, drawn as one path.\n\n The quiet zone is not decoration: a symbol printed hard against a frame\n or a photograph is much harder for a phone to find.\n \"\"\"\n size = code.size + 2 * border\n parts = []\n for row in range(code.size):\n for col in range(code.size):\n if code.modules[row][col]:\n parts.append(f\"M{col + border} {row + border}h1v1h-1z\")\n return (\n f''\n )\n\n\ndef _png_chunk(kind: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:\n body = kind + payload\n return (struct.pack(\">I\", len(payload)) + body\n + struct.pack(\">I\", zlib.crc32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF))\n\n\ndef to_png(code: QRCode, *, scale: int = 8, border: int = 4) -> bytes:\n \"\"\"The symbol as a greyscale PNG.\n\n Written here rather than through matplotlib so the bytes are identical\n on every machine: a report that changes because a plotting backend\n changed is a report nobody can diff.\n \"\"\"\n size = (code.size + 2 * border) * scale\n raw = bytearray()\n for y in range(size):\n raw.append(0) # no per-row filtering\n row = y // scale - border\n for x in range(size):\n col = x // scale - border\n dark = (0 <= row < code.size and 0 <= col < code.size\n and code.modules[row][col])\n raw.append(0 if dark else 255)\n return (\n b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\"\n + _png_chunk(b\"IHDR\", struct.pack(\">IIBBBBB\", size, size, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0))\n + _png_chunk(b\"IDAT\", zlib.compress(bytes(raw), 9))\n + _png_chunk(b\"IEND\", b\"\")\n )\n"}, "groundwater/quality/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Water quality assessment against WHO and Sierra Leone standards.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .standards import (\n PROVISIONAL_NATIONAL_NOTE,\n StandardEntry,\n load_standards,\n provisional_national_parameters,\n)\nfrom .assess import (\n ESSENTIAL_HEALTH_PARAMETERS,\n STATUS_LABELS,\n SUITABILITY_PHRASE,\n SUITABILITY_SENTENCE,\n VERDICT_LONG,\n VERDICT_ORDER,\n VERDICT_SHORT,\n ParameterAssessment,\n WaterQualityAssessment,\n assess_sample,\n)\nfrom .ionic import ionic_balance, IonicBalanceResult\nfrom .corrosivity import assess_corrosivity, CorrosivityAssessment\nfrom .indices import (\n compute_wqi,\n assess_health_risk,\n WaterQualityIndex,\n HealthRiskAssessment,\n)\nfrom .diagrams import plot_piper, plot_stiff\n\n__all__ = [\n \"ESSENTIAL_HEALTH_PARAMETERS\",\n \"STATUS_LABELS\",\n \"SUITABILITY_PHRASE\",\n \"SUITABILITY_SENTENCE\",\n \"VERDICT_LONG\",\n \"VERDICT_ORDER\",\n \"VERDICT_SHORT\",\n \"load_standards\",\n \"provisional_national_parameters\",\n \"PROVISIONAL_NATIONAL_NOTE\",\n \"StandardEntry\",\n \"assess_sample\",\n \"WaterQualityAssessment\",\n \"ParameterAssessment\",\n \"ionic_balance\",\n \"IonicBalanceResult\",\n \"assess_corrosivity\",\n \"CorrosivityAssessment\",\n \"compute_wqi\",\n \"assess_health_risk\",\n \"WaterQualityIndex\",\n \"HealthRiskAssessment\",\n \"plot_piper\",\n \"plot_stiff\",\n]\n"}, "groundwater/quality/assess.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Compare laboratory results against WHO and national standards.\n\nThe assessment is deliberately fail-closed. A drinking water verdict is a\nstatement someone acts on - a village drinks the water, a certificate is\nissued - so this module says \"suitable\" only when it can show the work, and\nsays so plainly when it cannot:\n\n* Values are converted onto the unit each guideline is written in before\n they are compared. An arsenic result of 5 ug/L is a fifth of the WHO\n guideline; compared as though it were 5 mg/L it is five hundred times\n over it, and the same arithmetic in the other direction certifies unsafe\n water as safe. A unit that cannot be read, or that measures something\n else, makes the row indeterminate rather than pass.\n* A \"below detection\" result only proves compliance when the detection\n limit is at or under the limit it is being checked against. A laboratory\n reporting \"< 0.05 mg/L\" for arsenic has not shown the water meets the\n 0.01 mg/L guideline; it has shown its method cannot see the guideline.\n* A parameter the standards table does not know is an unresolved question,\n not an absence of one, and it keeps the sample out of \"suitable\".\n* A sample with nothing evaluable in it - no results, or none that could be\n graded - is indeterminate. Silence is not a pass.\n* Naming water suitable for drinking also needs the health panel to have\n been run at all: E. coli, arsenic, fluoride and nitrate\n (:data:`ESSENTIAL_HEALTH_PARAMETERS`). Without them the sample cannot\n speak to the risks that matter most in a rural Sierra Leone borehole.\n\nOne deliberate exception: a result carrying no unit at all is read in the\nguideline's own unit, because that is the only reading under which the\nnumber means anything, and an info flag records the assumption. A result\ncarrying the *wrong* unit is the dangerous case, and that one is caught.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualitySample\nfrom .corrosivity import CorrosivityAssessment, assess_corrosivity\nfrom .indices import (\n HealthRiskAssessment,\n WaterQualityIndex,\n assess_health_risk,\n compute_wqi,\n)\nfrom .ionic import IonicBalanceResult, ionic_balance, ionic_balance_gap\nfrom ..utils import plural_noun\nfrom .standards import (\n StandardEntry,\n load_standards,\n normalise_parameter,\n to_standard_unit,\n)\n\n# status codes, ordered by severity for the summary\nSTATUS_ORDER = [\n \"exceeds_health\",\n \"exceeds_national\",\n \"exceeds_aesthetic\",\n \"indeterminate\",\n \"within_limits\",\n \"below_detection\",\n \"no_guideline\",\n \"not_measured\",\n]\n\n#: How each row status reads in a table. Kept here rather than in the report\n#: writer so the app, the browser engine and the DOCX all print one wording -\n#: a row the toolkit could not grade must never surface as a raw machine code\n#: in a client-facing document.\nSTATUS_LABELS = {\n \"within_limits\": \"Complies\",\n \"exceeds_health\": \"EXCEEDS HEALTH GUIDELINE\",\n \"exceeds_national\": \"Exceeds national/adopted limit\",\n \"exceeds_aesthetic\": \"Exceeds acceptability value\",\n \"indeterminate\": \"NOT EVALUABLE\",\n \"below_detection\": \"Below detection\",\n \"no_guideline\": \"No guideline value\",\n \"not_measured\": \"Not measured\",\n}\n\n#: Verdict states, worst first. ``indeterminate`` sits above ``aesthetic``\n#: because \"usable for drinking\" is a claim, and an open question defeats a\n#: claim; it sits below the two failures because a demonstrated exceedance\n#: is a finding, and uncertainty elsewhere does not soften it.\nVERDICT_ORDER = [\"health_fail\", \"national_fail\", \"indeterminate\", \"aesthetic\", \"pass\"]\n\n#: Short and long labels for each verdict state, shared by the app, the\n#: portfolio table and the reports so one wording is used everywhere.\nVERDICT_SHORT = {\n \"health_fail\": \"Treat before use\",\n \"national_fail\": \"Fails national limit\",\n \"indeterminate\": \"Not proven safe\",\n \"aesthetic\": \"Aesthetic only\",\n \"pass\": \"Safe\",\n}\nVERDICT_LONG = {\n \"health_fail\": \"Treat before use\",\n \"national_fail\": \"Fails the national standard\",\n \"indeterminate\": \"Not proven safe - incomplete or unevaluable results\",\n \"aesthetic\": \"Aesthetic issues only\",\n \"pass\": \"Safe to drink\",\n}\n\n#: One sentence per state, for report prose. Reports used to choose between\n#: \"requires treatment\" and \"suitable for drinking\" on the health exceedances\n#: alone, so a national breach or an unevaluable panel read as suitable.\nSUITABILITY_SENTENCE = {\n \"health_fail\": \"The water requires treatment before drinking.\",\n \"national_fail\": (\n \"The water meets the WHO health based guideline values but does not \"\n \"comply with the national standard; treatment is required before the \"\n \"supply is accepted.\"\n ),\n \"indeterminate\": (\n \"The water has not been shown to be suitable for drinking: the results \"\n \"are incomplete or could not be evaluated.\"\n ),\n \"aesthetic\": (\n \"The water is suitable for drinking on the parameters tested, with \"\n \"acceptability (taste, odour or staining) reservations.\"\n ),\n \"pass\": \"The water is suitable for drinking on the parameters tested.\",\n}\n\n#: The same, phrased to follow \"Water safety: \".\nSUITABILITY_PHRASE = {\n \"health_fail\": \"treatment required before drinking.\",\n \"national_fail\": \"does not comply with the national standard; treatment required.\",\n \"indeterminate\": \"not established - results incomplete or unevaluable.\",\n \"aesthetic\": \"suitable on the parameters tested; acceptability reservations.\",\n \"pass\": \"suitable for drinking on the parameters tested.\",\n}\n\n#: The health panel a verdict of \"suitable for drinking\" requires. E. coli is\n#: the direct indicator of faecal contamination; arsenic and fluoride are the\n#: geogenic risks that make otherwise clear, pleasant groundwater unsafe over\n#: years; nitrate is the latrine and agricultural one. A sample missing any of\n#: them cannot support the claim, however clean everything else looks.\nESSENTIAL_HEALTH_PARAMETERS = (\n \"e. coli\",\n \"arsenic\",\n \"fluoride\",\n \"nitrate (as no3)\",\n)\n\n#: Other table keys that answer the same health question: a laboratory that\n#: reports nitrate as nitrogen has measured the nitrate.\nESSENTIAL_EQUIVALENTS = {\n \"nitrate (as no3)\": (\"nitrate (as n)\",),\n}\n\n#: Machine codes explaining why a row could not be graded.\nINDETERMINATE_REASONS = {\n \"unit_unreadable\": \"the reported unit could not be read\",\n \"unit_mismatch\": \"the reported unit measures something other than the guideline\",\n \"detection_limit_above_guideline\": (\n \"the detection limit is above the limit being checked\"\n ),\n \"detection_limit_unknown\": \"the detection limit was not reported\",\n \"unknown_parameter\": \"the parameter is not in the standards table\",\n \"unit_basis_conflict\": (\n \"the unit names a different chemical basis from the parameter\"\n ),\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ParameterAssessment:\n parameter: str\n value: Optional[float]\n unit: str\n below_detection: bool\n who_health: str\n who_aesthetic: str\n sl_standard: str\n status: str\n remark: str\n #: The unit the guideline values are written in.\n guideline_unit: str = \"\"\n #: The value actually compared, in ``guideline_unit``. ``None`` when the\n #: row could not be converted, which is never the same as zero.\n value_in_guideline_unit: Optional[float] = None\n #: As reported by the laboratory, in the reported unit.\n detection_limit: Optional[float] = None\n #: Whether the row could be graded against the limits that apply to it.\n evaluable: bool = True\n #: A code from :data:`INDETERMINATE_REASONS`, ``\"unit_assumed\"``, or \"\".\n reason: str = \"\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass WaterQualityAssessment:\n sample: WaterQualitySample\n rows: list[ParameterAssessment]\n ionic: Optional[IonicBalanceResult]\n corrosivity: Optional[CorrosivityAssessment] = None\n wqi: Optional[WaterQualityIndex] = None\n health_risk: Optional[HealthRiskAssessment] = None\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n #: Parameters from :data:`ESSENTIAL_HEALTH_PARAMETERS` that the sample\n #: does not carry an evaluable result for.\n missing_essential: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n @property\n def health_exceedances(self) -> list[ParameterAssessment]:\n return [r for r in self.rows if r.status == \"exceeds_health\"]\n\n @property\n def aesthetic_exceedances(self) -> list[ParameterAssessment]:\n \"\"\"Parameters over an acceptability limit only.\n\n National exceedances are deliberately *not* included. A national\n limit is law; folding it in here reported a compliance failure as a\n matter of taste and let a breached supply show a 100% pass rate.\n Use :attr:`all_exceedances` when every exceedance is wanted.\n \"\"\"\n return [r for r in self.rows if r.status == \"exceeds_aesthetic\"]\n\n @property\n def national_exceedances(self) -> list[ParameterAssessment]:\n \"\"\"Parameters over the national standard but inside the WHO health GV.\"\"\"\n return [r for r in self.rows if r.status == \"exceeds_national\"]\n\n @property\n def all_exceedances(self) -> list[ParameterAssessment]:\n \"\"\"Every exceedance, worst first: health, then national, then aesthetic.\"\"\"\n return (\n self.health_exceedances\n + self.national_exceedances\n + self.aesthetic_exceedances\n )\n\n @property\n def indeterminate_rows(self) -> list[ParameterAssessment]:\n \"\"\"Rows that were measured but could not be graded.\"\"\"\n return [r for r in self.rows if r.status == \"indeterminate\"]\n\n @property\n def unknown_parameters(self) -> list[ParameterAssessment]:\n \"\"\"Determinands the standards table does not recognise.\"\"\"\n return [r for r in self.rows if r.reason == \"unknown_parameter\"]\n\n @property\n def evaluated_rows(self) -> list[ParameterAssessment]:\n \"\"\"Rows that were actually graded against a limit.\"\"\"\n return [\n r\n for r in self.rows\n if r.evaluable\n and r.status\n in (\n \"exceeds_health\",\n \"exceeds_national\",\n \"exceeds_aesthetic\",\n \"within_limits\",\n \"below_detection\",\n )\n ]\n\n @property\n def uncertainties(self) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"Every reason this sample cannot support a \"suitable\" verdict.\n\n Empty means nothing is unresolved; the verdict then rests only on\n what the limits say.\n \"\"\"\n reasons: list[str] = []\n if not self.rows:\n reasons.append(\"the sample carries no laboratory results\")\n elif not self.evaluated_rows:\n reasons.append(\n \"no result in the sample could be graded against a guideline value\"\n )\n for row in self.indeterminate_rows:\n why = INDETERMINATE_REASONS.get(row.reason, \"it could not be evaluated\")\n reasons.append(f\"{row.parameter} could not be assessed: {why}\")\n for row in self.unknown_parameters:\n reasons.append(\n f\"{row.parameter} has no entry in the standards table, so it \"\n \"was not checked against any limit\"\n )\n if self.missing_essential:\n reasons.append(\n \"the health panel is incomplete: no evaluable result for \"\n + \", \".join(self.missing_essential)\n )\n return reasons\n\n @property\n def verdict_state(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"One of :data:`VERDICT_ORDER`, worst applicable first.\"\"\"\n if self.health_exceedances:\n return \"health_fail\"\n if self.national_exceedances:\n return \"national_fail\"\n if self.uncertainties:\n return \"indeterminate\"\n if self.aesthetic_exceedances:\n return \"aesthetic\"\n return \"pass\"\n\n @property\n def is_potable(self) -> Optional[bool]:\n \"\"\"``True`` safe, ``False`` not safe, ``None`` not established.\n\n ``None`` is the honest answer for an incomplete or unevaluable\n sample and must never be collapsed into ``True``.\n \"\"\"\n state = self.verdict_state\n if state in (\"health_fail\", \"national_fail\"):\n return False\n if state == \"indeterminate\":\n return None\n return True\n\n @property\n def verdict(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"One line suitability statement for reports.\"\"\"\n state = self.verdict_state\n health = self.health_exceedances\n national = self.national_exceedances\n acceptability = self.aesthetic_exceedances\n\n if state == \"health_fail\":\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in health)\n return (\n \"The water does not meet the health based guideline \"\n f\"{plural_noun(len(health), 'value')} \"\n f\"for: {names}. Treatment or an alternative source is required \"\n \"before the water is used for drinking.\"\n )\n if state == \"national_fail\":\n # A national limit can be stricter than, or exist without, a WHO\n # health value - it is a legal compliance failure, not a matter of\n # taste, so it must not be reported as merely aesthetic.\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in national)\n extra = (\n \" Acceptability limits are also exceeded for: \"\n + \", \".join(r.parameter for r in acceptability)\n + \".\"\n if acceptability\n else \"\"\n )\n return (\n \"The water meets the WHO health based guideline values, but \"\n f\"does not comply with the national standard \"\n f\"{plural_noun(len(national), 'limit')} for: \"\n f\"{names}.{extra} Treatment is required before the supply can \"\n \"be accepted against the national standard; check whether the \"\n \"limit exceeded is a health or an acceptability limit.\"\n )\n if state == \"indeterminate\":\n reasons = \"; \".join(self.uncertainties)\n extra = (\n \" Acceptability limits are exceeded for: \"\n + \", \".join(r.parameter for r in acceptability)\n + \".\"\n if acceptability\n else \"\"\n )\n return (\n \"The water cannot be declared suitable for drinking on these \"\n f\"results: {reasons}.{extra} Resolve the outstanding \"\n \"parameters - re-sample, or ask the laboratory for the units \"\n \"and detection limits used - before the supply is signed off.\"\n )\n if state == \"aesthetic\":\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in acceptability)\n return (\n \"The water meets all health based guideline values. \"\n f\"Acceptability (aesthetic) limits are exceeded for: {names}. \"\n \"The water is usable for drinking, although taste, odour or \"\n \"staining complaints may arise; simple treatment is advisable.\"\n )\n return (\n \"All measured parameters comply with the WHO guideline values and \"\n \"the national standard limits applied. The water is suitable for \"\n \"drinking on the basis of the parameters tested.\"\n )\n\n\ndef _limit_maximums(entry: StandardEntry) -> list[float]:\n \"\"\"Every upper limit that applies to a parameter, in the guideline unit.\"\"\"\n out = []\n for limit in (entry.who_health, entry.sl_standard, entry.who_aesthetic):\n if limit is not None and limit.maximum is not None:\n out.append(limit.maximum)\n return out\n\n\n#: Shared with the aggregate indices, so one conversion rule serves the row\n#: comparison, the WQI, the hazard index, the ionic balance and corrosivity.\n_convert_to_guideline_unit = to_standard_unit\n\n\ndef _assess_result(result, entry: Optional[StandardEntry]) -> ParameterAssessment:\n \"\"\"Grade one laboratory result against its guideline entry.\"\"\"\n who_h = str(entry.who_health) if entry and entry.who_health else \"\"\n who_a = str(entry.who_aesthetic) if entry and entry.who_aesthetic else \"\"\n sl = str(entry.sl_standard) if entry and entry.sl_standard else \"\"\n guideline_unit = entry.unit if entry else \"\"\n\n row = ParameterAssessment(\n parameter=result.parameter,\n value=result.value,\n unit=result.unit or guideline_unit,\n below_detection=result.below_detection,\n who_health=who_h,\n who_aesthetic=who_a,\n sl_standard=sl,\n status=\"not_measured\",\n remark=\"no value reported\",\n guideline_unit=guideline_unit,\n detection_limit=result.detection_limit,\n )\n\n if result.value is None and not result.below_detection:\n if result.greater_than is not None and entry is not None:\n return _assess_unquantified(row, result, entry)\n return row\n\n if entry is None:\n # An unrecognised determinand is an open question, not a clean bill.\n row.status = \"no_guideline\"\n row.reason = \"unknown_parameter\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.remark = (\n \"parameter not in the standards table, so it was not checked \"\n \"against any limit\"\n )\n return row\n\n limits = _limit_maximums(entry)\n\n if result.below_detection and result.value is None:\n return _assess_below_detection(row, result, entry, limits)\n\n converted, reason = _convert_to_guideline_unit(\n float(result.value), result.unit, entry\n )\n if converted is None:\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.reason = reason\n row.remark = (\n f\"reported in '{result.unit}' but the guideline is in \"\n f\"'{guideline_unit}': {INDETERMINATE_REASONS[reason]}. The value \"\n \"was not compared against any limit.\"\n )\n return row\n\n row.value_in_guideline_unit = converted\n row.reason = reason\n if reason == \"unit_assumed\":\n unit_note = f\" (read as {guideline_unit}; the reported unit was '{result.unit}')\" \\\n if result.unit else f\" (read as {guideline_unit}; no unit was reported)\"\n elif converted != result.value:\n unit_note = (\n f\" ({result.value:g} {result.unit} = {converted:g} {guideline_unit})\"\n )\n else:\n unit_note = \"\"\n _grade(row, entry, converted, unit_note)\n return row\n\n\ndef _assess_unquantified(\n row: ParameterAssessment, result, entry: StandardEntry\n) -> ParameterAssessment:\n \"\"\"A result the laboratory saw and did not put a number to.\n\n \"TNTC\", \"Present\" and \"Positive\" are a count above zero; \">50\" is at\n least 50. All of them used to read as \"not measured\", so a sample with\n E. coli 0 and total coliforms TNTC was graded Safe, and a \">50\" count\n was graded as exactly 50 - inside the limit whenever the limit is 50.\n \"\"\"\n bound = float(result.greater_than)\n row.evaluable = True\n row.reason = \"detected_not_quantified\"\n is_faecal = entry.parameter.strip().lower() == \"e. coli\"\n stated = \"detected, count not quantified\" if bound == 0 else f\"more than {bound:g}\"\n\n def maximum(limit):\n return limit.maximum if limit is not None else None\n\n health = maximum(entry.who_health)\n national = maximum(entry.sl_standard)\n if national is None:\n national = maximum(entry.who_aesthetic)\n # The bound settles it whenever the bound is already over the limit; a\n # zero limit is over as soon as anything is detected.\n over_health = health is not None and bound >= health\n over_national = national is not None and bound >= national\n\n if over_health:\n row.status = \"exceeds_health\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"{stated}, which is above the WHO health based guideline \"\n f\"({entry.who_health}); the laboratory did not quantify it\"\n )\n elif over_national and is_faecal:\n row.status = \"exceeds_health\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"faecal indicator {stated}, above the limit \"\n f\"({entry.sl_standard or entry.who_aesthetic}); a health concern, \"\n \"not aesthetic\"\n )\n elif over_national:\n row.status = \"exceeds_national\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"{stated}, above the national limit \"\n f\"({entry.sl_standard or entry.who_aesthetic}); an indicator of \"\n \"ingress or inadequate wellhead protection, not of faecal \"\n \"contamination in itself, and WHO sets no health based guideline \"\n \"for it\"\n )\n else:\n # The bound is inside every limit, so the result is an open question\n # rather than a pass: the true value is somewhere above it.\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.remark = (\n f\"{stated}; the laboratory did not quantify it, so it cannot be \"\n \"shown to meet the limit\"\n )\n return row\n\n\ndef _assess_below_detection(\n row: ParameterAssessment, result, entry: StandardEntry, limits: list[float]\n) -> ParameterAssessment:\n \"\"\"A \"< X\" result proves compliance only when X is under the limit.\"\"\"\n if not limits:\n row.status = \"below_detection\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"below detection limit ({result.detection_limit:g})\"\n if result.detection_limit is not None\n else \"below detection limit\"\n )\n return row\n\n strictest = min(limits)\n microbiological = entry.category == \"microbiological\"\n if microbiological and result.detection_limit is None:\n # \"Absent\", \"ND\", \"not detected\": the count found nothing in the\n # sample, which for a guideline of \"not detectable in any 100 mL\n # sample\" is the guideline being met, not an unknown\n row.status = \"below_detection\"\n row.remark = (\n \"reported not detected; the guideline is met provided the \"\n \"laboratory examined a 100 mL sample\"\n )\n return row\n if result.detection_limit is None:\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.reason = \"detection_limit_unknown\"\n row.remark = (\n \"reported below the detection limit, but the limit itself was not \"\n f\"reported, so compliance with {strictest:g} {entry.unit} cannot \"\n \"be shown. Ask the laboratory for the detection limit.\"\n )\n return row\n\n dl, reason = _convert_to_guideline_unit(\n float(result.detection_limit), result.unit, entry\n )\n if dl is None:\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.reason = reason\n row.remark = (\n f\"reported below a detection limit of {result.detection_limit:g} \"\n f\"'{result.unit}', which cannot be compared with the guideline in \"\n f\"'{entry.unit}': {INDETERMINATE_REASONS[reason]}.\"\n )\n return row\n\n row.value_in_guideline_unit = None\n if microbiological and dl <= 1.0:\n # A membrane-filtration count cannot resolve below one colony per\n # volume filtered, so \"<1 CFU/100 mL\" is exactly what \"not\n # detectable in any 100 mL sample\" looks like on a certificate.\n # Refusing it as a detection limit above zero made the documented\n # way of transcribing a clean E. coli result \"not proven safe\".\n row.status = \"below_detection\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"not detected in a 100 mL sample (reported as <{dl:g} {entry.unit})\"\n )\n return row\n if dl > strictest:\n row.status = \"indeterminate\"\n row.evaluable = False\n row.reason = \"detection_limit_above_guideline\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"below a detection limit of {dl:g} {entry.unit}, which is above \"\n f\"the limit of {strictest:g} {entry.unit}. The method cannot see \"\n \"the guideline value, so the result does not show compliance; \"\n \"re-test with a more sensitive method.\"\n )\n return row\n\n row.status = \"below_detection\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"below detection limit ({dl:g} {entry.unit}), which is at or under \"\n f\"the limit of {strictest:g} {entry.unit}\"\n )\n return row\n\n\ndef _grade(\n row: ParameterAssessment, entry: StandardEntry, value: float, unit_note: str\n) -> None:\n \"\"\"Apply the limit hierarchy to a converted value.\"\"\"\n is_micro = (entry.category or \"\").strip().lower() == \"microbiological\"\n is_faecal = entry.parameter.strip().lower() == \"e. coli\"\n if entry.who_health and entry.who_health.exceeded_by(value):\n row.status = \"exceeds_health\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"exceeds the WHO health based guideline ({entry.who_health})\"\n f\"{unit_note}\"\n )\n elif is_micro and (\n (entry.sl_standard and entry.sl_standard.exceeded_by(value))\n or (entry.who_aesthetic and entry.who_aesthetic.exceeded_by(value))\n ):\n # A microbiological indicator is never an aesthetic matter, even when\n # its limit is carried in the national column. E. coli is the faecal\n # indicator and any detection is a health exceedance. Total coliforms\n # are not: WHO sets no health-based guideline for them and they\n # indicate ingress or an unprotected wellhead, not faecal\n # contamination, so they are a national-limit failure that calls for\n # disinfection and a sanitary inspection. Three reports used to call a\n # sample with E. coli 0 \"faecal contamination\" on total coliforms.\n limit = entry.sl_standard or entry.who_aesthetic\n if is_faecal:\n row.status = \"exceeds_health\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"faecal indicator detected above the limit ({limit}); a health \"\n f\"concern, not aesthetic{unit_note}\"\n )\n else:\n row.status = \"exceeds_national\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"detected above the national limit ({limit}); an indicator of \"\n \"ingress or inadequate wellhead protection, not of faecal \"\n \"contamination in itself, and WHO sets no health based guideline \"\n f\"for it{unit_note}\"\n )\n elif entry.sl_standard and entry.sl_standard.exceeded_by(value):\n if entry.who_health:\n # WHO sets a health value and the national limit is stricter:\n # failing it is a compliance failure, not a matter of taste, and\n # must not be reported as aesthetic.\n row.status = \"exceeds_national\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"exceeds the national standard limit ({entry.sl_standard}), \"\n f\"which is stricter than the WHO health based guideline \"\n f\"({entry.who_health}){unit_note}\"\n )\n else:\n # No WHO health value exists for this parameter, so the national\n # limit is an acceptability one (iron staining, chloride taste,\n # turbidity). Every national value in the bundled table is\n # provisional - a WHO or regional figure carried across, not a\n # confirmed Standards Bureau one - so the remark says so rather\n # than reporting a legal failure the toolkit cannot establish.\n row.status = \"exceeds_aesthetic\"\n # The WHO figure is what the national one was carried across\n # from, and naming it is the only way a reader can tell a limit\n # somebody set from a limit this toolkit assumed.\n who_note = (\n f\"; the WHO acceptability value is {entry.who_aesthetic}\"\n if entry.who_aesthetic\n else \"; WHO sets no value for this determinand\"\n )\n row.remark = (\n f\"exceeds the national acceptability limit \"\n f\"({entry.sl_standard}), which is provisional{who_note}{unit_note}\"\n )\n elif entry.who_aesthetic and entry.who_aesthetic.exceeded_by(value):\n row.status = \"exceeds_aesthetic\"\n row.remark = (\n f\"exceeds the WHO acceptability value ({entry.who_aesthetic})\"\n f\"{unit_note}\"\n )\n elif not (entry.who_health or entry.who_aesthetic or entry.sl_standard):\n row.status = \"no_guideline\"\n row.remark = entry.note or \"no guideline value\"\n else:\n row.status = \"within_limits\"\n row.remark = unit_note.strip() if unit_note else \"\"\n\n\ndef _missing_essential(rows: list[ParameterAssessment], table: dict) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"Essential health parameters with no evaluable result in the sample.\"\"\"\n graded = {\n normalise_parameter(r.parameter)\n for r in rows\n if r.evaluable\n and r.status\n in (\n \"exceeds_health\",\n \"exceeds_national\",\n \"exceeds_aesthetic\",\n \"within_limits\",\n \"below_detection\",\n )\n }\n missing = []\n for key in ESSENTIAL_HEALTH_PARAMETERS:\n if key in graded or any(alt in graded for alt in ESSENTIAL_EQUIVALENTS.get(key, ())):\n continue\n entry = table.get(key)\n missing.append(entry.parameter if entry is not None else key)\n return missing\n\n\ndef assess_sample(\n sample: table.get(normalise_parameter(result.parameter))\n row = _assess_result(result, entry)\n rows.append(row)\n\n if row.reason == \"unknown_parameter\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"unknown_parameter\",\n f\"No guideline entry for '{result.parameter}'; it was not \"\n \"checked against any limit and keeps the sample out of a \"\n \"'suitable for drinking' verdict. Add it to the standards \"\n \"CSV if a limit applies.\",\n )\n )\n elif row.reason == \"unit_assumed\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"info\",\n \"unit_not_reported\",\n f\"'{result.parameter}' carries no usable unit\"\n + (f\" ('{result.unit}')\" if result.unit else \"\")\n + f\"; it was read as {row.guideline_unit}. Confirm against \"\n \"the laboratory certificate.\",\n )\n )\n elif row.reason == \"unit_basis_assumed\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"unit_basis_assumed\",\n f\"'{result.parameter}' is reported in '{result.unit}' but \"\n f\"the guideline is written in '{row.guideline_unit}'. The \"\n \"values were taken as the same basis; confirm with the \"\n \"laboratory, since an 'as CaCO3' figure is about 2.5 times \"\n \"the same concentration expressed as the element.\",\n )\n )\n elif row.status == \"indeterminate\":\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n f\"indeterminate_{row.reason}\",\n f\"'{result.parameter}' could not be assessed: {row.remark}\",\n )\n )\n\n # WHO combined nitrate + nitrite rule: the sum of the ratio of each to\n # its own guideline value must not exceed 1. A sample can pass both\n # single-parameter checks yet fail this combined limit, so it is applied\n # only when neither ion is individually in exceedance (the individual\n # exceedance is already reported on its own row).\n combined = _nitrate_nitrite_index(rows, table)\n if combined is not None:\n ratio, no3, no2, gv3, gv2, bounded = combined\n if ratio > 1.0 and no3 <= gv3 and no2 <= gv2:\n # A bounded index is an upper bound, not a measurement: it says\n # the rule *may* be breached, which is a question rather than a\n # finding, so it is reported as indeterminate rather than as a\n # health exceedance the laboratory never demonstrated.\n rows.append(\n ParameterAssessment(\n parameter=\"Nitrate + nitrite (combined)\",\n value=round(ratio, 2),\n unit=\"ratio\",\n below_detection=False,\n who_health=\"<= 1\",\n who_aesthetic=\"\",\n sl_standard=\"\",\n status=\"indeterminate\" if bounded else \"exceeds_health\",\n remark=(\n f\"An upper bound on the combined index \"\n f\"({no3:g}/{gv3:g} + {no2:g}/{gv2:g} = {ratio:.2f}) \"\n \"exceeds 1, taking the below-detection component at \"\n \"its detection limit. The WHO combined nitrate and \"\n \"nitrite limit cannot be shown to be met; ask the \"\n \"laboratory for a lower detection limit.\"\n if bounded else\n f\"The combined index ({no3:g}/{gv3:g} + {no2:g}/{gv2:g} \"\n f\"= {ratio:.2f}) exceeds 1; the WHO combined nitrate and \"\n \"nitrite limit is not met even though each is within its \"\n \"own guideline value.\"\n ),\n guideline_unit=\"ratio\",\n value_in_guideline_unit=None if bounded else round(ratio, 2),\n evaluable=not bounded,\n reason=\"detection_limit_above_guideline\" if bounded else \"\",\n )\n )\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\" if bounded else \"warning\",\n \"nitrate_nitrite_combined_unproven\" if bounded\n else \"nitrate_nitrite_combined\",\n \"The combined nitrate + nitrite index cannot be shown to \"\n \"meet the WHO limit: one component is below detection and \"\n \"its detection limit is high enough that the sum may \"\n \"exceed 1.\"\n if bounded else\n \"Combined nitrate + nitrite index exceeds 1 (WHO); treat as \"\n \"a health exceedance.\",\n )\n )\n\n missing_essential = _missing_essential(rows, table)\n if missing_essential:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"incomplete_health_panel\",\n \"No evaluable result for \" + \", \".join(missing_essential) + \". \"\n \"The sample cannot show the water is safe to drink until the \"\n \"health panel is complete.\",\n )\n )\n if not [r for r in rows if r.evaluable and r.status != \"not_measured\"]:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"nothing_evaluable\",\n \"No result in this sample could be graded against a guideline \"\n \"value, so no suitability verdict can be given.\",\n )\n )\n\n ionic = ionic_balance(sample)\n if ionic is not None and ionic.flag is not None:\n flags.append(ionic.flag)\n elif ionic is None:\n # The balance is the one check that says whether a certificate's own\n # numbers hang together, and it was skipped in silence: a report with\n # no charge-balance line reads as an analysis that balanced, rather\n # than as one nobody could check.\n gap = ionic_balance_gap(sample)\n if gap:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"ionic_balance_not_checked\",\n \"The charge balance could not be computed: the analysis \"\n f\"carries no {plural_noun(len(gap), 'value')} for \"\n + \", \".join(gap)\n + \". Ask the laboratory for the major ions if the \"\n \"analysis is to be relied on.\",\n )\n )\n\n corrosivity = assess_corrosivity(sample)\n flags.extend(corrosivity.flags)\n\n wqi = compute_wqi(sample, standards_path)\n health_risk = assess_health_risk(sample)\n if health_risk is not None:\n flags.extend(health_risk.flags)\n\n return WaterQualityAssessment(\n sample=sample,\n rows=rows,\n ionic=ionic,\n corrosivity=corrosivity,\n wqi=wqi,\n health_risk=health_risk,\n flags=flags,\n missing_essential=missing_essential,\n )\n\n\ndef _nitrate_nitrite_index(rows: list[ParameterAssessment], table):\n \"\"\"The WHO combined nitrate + nitrite index.\n\n Returns ``(ratio, no3, no2, gv3, gv2, bounded)`` where ``ratio`` is\n ``no3/gv3 + no2/gv2``, or ``None`` when a value or guideline is missing\n altogether. Both concentrations are the unit-converted ones, so a result\n reported in ug/L is not silently added as though it were mg/L.\n\n A component reported below detection is taken at its detection limit,\n and ``bounded`` says so. That reading is deliberately the pessimistic\n one: \"< 3 mg/L nitrite\" beside 49 mg/L nitrate cannot rule out a\n combined index of 1.98, and treating the unknown as zero turned a\n sample that might fail the rule into one that passed it silently.\n \"\"\"\n\n def _value_and_gv(key):\n entry = table.get(key)\n gv = entry.who_health.maximum if entry and entry.who_health else None\n for row in rows:\n if normalise_parameter(row.parameter) != key:\n continue\n if row.value_in_guideline_unit is not None:\n return float(row.value_in_guideline_unit), gv, False\n if row.below_detection and entry is not None:\n dl, reason = to_standard_unit(\n float(row.detection_limit), row.unit, entry\n ) if row.detection_limit is not None else (None, \"\")\n if dl is not None:\n return float(dl), gv, True\n return None, gv, False\n return None, gv, False\n\n no3, gv3, b3 = _value_and_gv(\"nitrate (as no3)\")\n no2, gv2, b2 = _value_and_gv(\"nitrite (as no2)\")\n if no3 is None or no2 is None or not gv3 or not gv2:\n return None\n return no3 / gv3 + no2 / gv2, no3, no2, gv3, gv2, (b3 or b2)\n"}, "groundwater/quality/corrosivity.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Corrosivity and scaling indices, and a materials recommendation.\n\nSoft, low-alkalinity, low-pH water from crystalline basement aquifers is\nchemically aggressive and corrodes galvanised iron and mild-steel rising\nmains and pump parts, which is a leading cause of premature handpump\nfailure across West Africa. The water can be aggressive even when the pH\nis inside the 6.5 to 8.5 acceptability range, so a pH check alone is not\nenough.\n\nThis module computes the classical indices from parameters the toolkit\nalready parses (pH, calcium, alkalinity, TDS or EC, temperature) and\nturns them into a plain-language verdict and a rising-main / pump material\nrecommendation:\n\n* Langelier Saturation Index (LSI) - CaCO3 saturation; < 0 is corrosive.\n* Ryznar Stability Index (RSI) - practical corrosion/scaling scale.\n* Aggressive Index (AI) - AWWA index for asbestos-cement, a\n useful aggressiveness check.\n* Larson-Skold Index - chloride/sulfate attack on steel.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualitySample\nfrom .standards import canonical_values, normalise_parameter\n\n# milli-equivalents per mg for the Larson-Skold ratio\n_MEQ = {\n \"chloride\": 1 / 35.453,\n \"sulfate\": 2 / 96.06,\n \"bicarbonate\": 1 / 61.017,\n \"carbonate\": 2 / 60.009,\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass CorrosivityAssessment:\n lsi: Optional[float] = None\n rsi: Optional[float] = None\n aggressive_index: Optional[float] = None\n larson_skold: Optional[float] = None\n classification: str = \"Insufficient data\"\n is_aggressive: bool = False\n verdict: str = \"\"\n materials_note: str = \"\"\n assumptions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\ndef _value(sample: WaterQualitySample, key: str) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"One parameter on the standards table's scale.\n\n The Langelier and Ryznar indices take log10 of concentrations in mg/L, so\n a value on another scale does not shift the index - it invalidates it. A\n conductivity given in mS/cm produced a TDS estimate of 0 mg/L and an\n index pair computed from it.\n \"\"\"\n canonical = canonical_values(sample)\n if key in canonical:\n return canonical[key]\n for result in sample.results:\n if normalise_parameter(result.parameter) == key:\n if result.value is not None:\n # present but not convertible: refuse it rather than use the\n # raw number on an unknown scale\n return None\n if result.value is not None:\n return float(result.value)\n return 0.0 if result.below_detection else None\n return None\n\n\ndef _classify_rsi(rsi: float) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n \"\"\"Map a Ryznar index to a class and an is-aggressive flag.\"\"\"\n if rsi < 6.0:\n return \"Scale-forming\", False\n if rsi <= 7.0:\n return \"Balanced (near CaCO3 equilibrium)\", False\n if rsi <= 8.0:\n return \"Corrosive\", True\n return \"Strongly corrosive\", True\n\n\ndef assess_corrosivity(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> CorrosivityAssessment:\n \"\"\"Assess corrosivity/scaling from a water quality sample.\n\n Returns an assessment with whichever indices the available data\n supports. When pH, calcium and alkalinity are all present the\n saturation indices are computed; the Larson-Skold ratio additionally\n needs chloride and sulfate.\n \"\"\"\n assessment = CorrosivityAssessment()\n assumptions = assessment.assumptions\n\n ph = _value(sample, \"ph\")\n calcium = _value(sample, \"calcium\")\n alkalinity = _value(sample, \"alkalinity\")\n tds = _value(sample, \"tds\")\n ec = _value(sample, \"electrical conductivity\")\n temp = _value(sample, \"temperature\")\n\n # TDS: measured, else estimated from EC, else a soft-water default\n if tds is None or tds <= 0:\n if ec and ec > 0:\n tds = 0.64 * ec\n assumptions.append(\n f\"TDS estimated as 0.64 x EC = {tds:.0f} mg/L (TDS not reported).\"\n )\n else:\n tds = 250.0\n assumptions.append(\"TDS assumed 250 mg/L (neither TDS nor EC reported).\")\n if temp is None or temp <= 0:\n temp = 25.0\n assumptions.append(\"Temperature assumed 25 C (not reported).\")\n\n if ph is None or calcium is None or alkalinity is None or calcium <= 0 or alkalinity <= 0:\n assessment.verdict = (\n \"Corrosivity could not be assessed: pH, calcium and alkalinity are \"\n \"all required. Supply them to obtain a materials recommendation.\"\n )\n return assessment\n\n # calcium hardness as CaCO3 (Ca mg/L x 100.09/40.08)\n ca_hardness = calcium * 2.497\n\n # Langelier: pHs = (9.3 + A + B) - (C + D)\n a = (math.log10(tds) - 1.0) / 10.0\n b = -13.12 * math.log10(temp + 273.15) + 34.55\n c = math.log10(ca_hardness) - 0.4\n d = math.log10(alkalinity)\n ph_s = (9.3 + a + b) - (c + d)\n lsi = ph - ph_s\n rsi = 2 * ph_s - ph\n ai = ph + math.log10(alkalinity * ca_hardness)\n\n assessment.lsi = round(lsi, 2)\n assessment.rsi = round(rsi, 2)\n assessment.aggressive_index = round(ai, 2)\n\n # Larson-Skold (optional): (Cl + SO4) / (HCO3 + CO3) in meq/L\n chloride = _value(sample, \"chloride\")\n sulfate = _value(sample, \"sulfate\")\n bicarbonate = _value(sample, \"bicarbonate\")\n carbonate = _value(sample, \"carbonate\")\n if bicarbonate is None:\n # alkalinity (as CaCO3) -> bicarbonate equivalent meq/L\n hco3_meq = alkalinity / 50.04\n else:\n hco3_meq = bicarbonate * _MEQ[\"bicarbonate\"]\n co3_meq = (carbonate or 0.0) * _MEQ[\"carbonate\"]\n if chloride is not None and sulfate is not None and (hco3_meq + co3_meq) > 0:\n ls = (chloride * _MEQ[\"chloride\"] + sulfate * _MEQ[\"sulfate\"]) / (\n hco3_meq + co3_meq\n )\n assessment.larson_skold = round(ls, 2)\n\n classification, aggressive = _classify_rsi(rsi)\n # corroborate with LSI and AI\n if lsi < -0.5:\n aggressive = True\n if assessment.aggressive_index is not None and assessment.aggressive_index < 10:\n aggressive = True\n # Keep the class label consistent with the flag and verdict: when the\n # LSI/AI corroboration promotes borderline water to aggressive, the RSI\n # class (\"Balanced\", \"Scale-forming\") must not still say otherwise, else\n # a report shows a \"Balanced\" label beside an \"aggressive\" verdict.\n if aggressive and classification not in (\"Corrosive\", \"Strongly corrosive\"):\n classification = \"Corrosive\"\n assessment.classification = classification\n assessment.is_aggressive = aggressive\n\n if aggressive:\n # The pH sentence used to say \"within the acceptability range\" for\n # a sample the same report flagged at 5.9. It now says what the pH is.\n if ph < 6.5:\n ph_note = (\n f\"The pH of {ph:.1f} is below the 6.5 to 8.5 acceptability range, \"\n \"which adds to the attack on metal; soft, low-alkalinity basement \"\n \"groundwater is aggressive even at a pH inside that range.\"\n )\n elif ph > 8.5:\n ph_note = (\n f\"The pH of {ph:.1f} is above the 6.5 to 8.5 acceptability range; \"\n \"the aggressiveness comes from the low calcium and alkalinity.\"\n )\n else:\n ph_note = (\n f\"The pH of {ph:.1f} is within the 6.5 to 8.5 acceptability range, \"\n \"and the water is aggressive all the same, which is typical of \"\n \"soft basement groundwater.\"\n )\n assessment.verdict = (\n f\"The water is chemically aggressive (Ryznar index {rsi:.1f}, \"\n f\"Langelier index {lsi:+.1f}). It will corrode metal fittings. \"\n + ph_note\n )\n assessment.materials_note = (\n \"Specify uPVC or stainless steel (grade 304 or 316) for the rising \"\n \"main and pump components, and avoid galvanised iron and mild steel, \"\n \"which corrode rapidly in this water and are a leading cause of \"\n \"premature pump failure. Inspect the rising main and the wetted \"\n \"metal parts of the pump for corrosion at each service.\"\n )\n if assessment.larson_skold is not None and assessment.larson_skold > 0.8:\n assessment.materials_note += (\n f\" The Larson-Skold ratio ({assessment.larson_skold:.1f}) is \"\n \"elevated, so chloride and sulfate add to the attack on steel.\"\n )\n assessment.flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"aggressive_water\",\n \"Water is chemically aggressive; specify uPVC or stainless rising \"\n \"main and pump components.\",\n )\n )\n elif classification == \"Scale-forming\":\n assessment.verdict = (\n f\"The water tends to deposit calcium carbonate scale (Ryznar index \"\n f\"{rsi:.1f}, Langelier index {lsi:+.1f}).\"\n )\n assessment.materials_note = (\n \"Monitor the screen and pump for encrustation and de-scale as needed; \"\n \"corrosion of metal parts is a lesser concern.\"\n )\n else:\n assessment.verdict = (\n f\"The water is close to calcium carbonate equilibrium (Ryznar index \"\n f\"{rsi:.1f}, Langelier index {lsi:+.1f}); neither strong corrosion nor \"\n \"scaling is expected.\"\n )\n assessment.materials_note = (\n \"Standard materials are acceptable; inspect fittings for corrosion \"\n \"during routine maintenance.\"\n )\n return assessment\n"}, "groundwater/quality/diagrams.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Hydrochemical facies diagrams: Piper and Stiff.\n\nBoth work from the meq/L values produced by the ionic balance module,\nso they need the major ions to be present in the sample. Multiple\nsamples can be plotted on one Piper diagram for comparison.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..config import HouseStyle\nfrom ..models import WaterQualitySample\nfrom ..plotting import figure_context, save_figure\nfrom .ionic import ionic_balance\n\n_SQ3 = np.sqrt(3.0)\n\n\ndef _ternary_xy(a: float, b: float, c: float, origin=(0.0, 0.0), size=1.0):\n \"\"\"Barycentric (a bottom-left, b bottom-right, c top) to xy.\"\"\"\n total = a + b + c\n if total <= 0:\n return None\n a, b, c = a / total, b / total, c / total\n x = origin[0] + (b + 0.5 * c) * size\n y = origin[1] + (_SQ3 / 2.0) * c * size\n return x, y\n\n\ndef _triangle(ax, origin, size, labels, ticks=True):\n x0, y0 = origin\n verts = np.array(\n [[x0, y0], [x0 + size, y0], [x0 + 0.5 * size, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size], [x0, y0]]\n )\n ax.plot(verts[:, 0], verts[:, 1], color=\"#444444\", lw=1.2)\n for frac in (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8):\n # grid lines parallel to each side\n ax.plot(\n [x0 + frac * size, x0 + 0.5 * size + 0.5 * frac * size],\n [y0, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size * (1 - frac)],\n color=\"#DDDDDD\", lw=0.6, zorder=0,\n )\n ax.plot(\n [x0 + (1 - frac) * size, x0 + 0.5 * size - 0.5 * frac * size],\n [y0, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size * (1 - frac)],\n color=\"#DDDDDD\", lw=0.6, zorder=0,\n )\n ax.plot(\n [x0 + 0.5 * frac * size, x0 + size - 0.5 * frac * size],\n [y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size * frac, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size * frac],\n color=\"#DDDDDD\", lw=0.6, zorder=0,\n )\n la, lb, lc = labels\n # The two base labels sit under their own vertex, centred, so the\n # cation triangle's \"Na+K\" and the anion triangle's \"HCO3\" no longer\n # meet in the gap between the triangles and print as \"HNO3+K\".\n ax.text(x0, y0 - 0.05, la, ha=\"center\", va=\"top\", fontsize=9)\n ax.text(x0 + size, y0 - 0.05, lb, ha=\"center\", va=\"top\", fontsize=9)\n ax.text(x0 + 0.5 * size, y0 + _SQ3 / 2 * size + 0.04, lc, ha=\"center\", fontsize=9)\n\n\ndef plot_piper(\n samples: list[WaterQualitySample],\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str = \"Piper diagram\",\n):\n \"\"\"Piper trilinear diagram for one or more samples.\n\n The diamond point is the classical construction: the intersection\n of the +60 degree line through the cation point and the -60 degree\n line through the anion point. Samples without a complete major ion\n analysis are skipped.\n \"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n size = 1.0\n gap = 0.34\n cat_origin = (0.0, 0.0)\n an_origin = (size + gap, 0.0)\n\n # diamond vertices from the projection geometry\n x_mid = size + gap / 2.0\n y_bot = _SQ3 / 2.0 * gap\n diamond = np.array(\n [\n [x_mid, y_bot], # bottom: Ca+Mg with HCO3\n [x_mid + size / 2.0, y_bot + _SQ3 / 2.0 * size], # right: Na+K with SO4+Cl\n [x_mid, y_bot + _SQ3 * size], # top: Ca+Mg with SO4+Cl\n [x_mid - size / 2.0, y_bot + _SQ3 / 2.0 * size], # left\n [x_mid, y_bot],\n ]\n )\n\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.9, 5.6))\n ax.set_aspect(\"equal\")\n ax.axis(\"off\")\n _triangle(ax, cat_origin, size, (\"Ca\", \"Na+K\", \"Mg\"))\n _triangle(ax, an_origin, size, (\"HCO3\", \"Cl\", \"SO4\"))\n ax.plot(diamond[:, 0], diamond[:, 1], color=\"#444444\", lw=1.2)\n ax.annotate(\n \"SO4 + Cl increases upward; Na + K increases to the right\",\n xy=(x_mid, y_bot + _SQ3 * size + 0.06),\n ha=\"center\", fontsize=7.5, color=\"#555555\",\n )\n\n markers = [\"o\", \"s\", \"^\", \"D\", \"v\", \"P\", \"X\"]\n plotted = []\n for i, sample in enumerate(samples):\n ionic = ionic_balance(sample)\n if ionic is None:\n continue\n cat = ionic.cations_meq\n an = ionic.anions_meq\n ca, mg = cat.get(\"calcium\", 0), cat.get(\"magnesium\", 0)\n nak = cat.get(\"sodium\", 0) + cat.get(\"potassium\", 0)\n cl = an.get(\"chloride\", 0)\n so4 = an.get(\"sulfate\", 0)\n hco3 = an.get(\"bicarbonate\", 0) + an.get(\"carbonate\", 0)\n\n p_cat = _ternary_xy(ca, nak, mg, cat_origin, size)\n p_an = _ternary_xy(hco3, cl, so4, an_origin, size)\n if p_cat is None or p_an is None:\n continue\n # intersection of +60 deg line through the cation point and\n # -60 deg line through the anion point\n xc, yc = p_cat\n xa, ya = p_an\n xd = 0.5 * (xc + xa) + (ya - yc) / (2.0 * _SQ3)\n yd = yc + _SQ3 * (xd - xc)\n marker = markers[i % len(markers)]\n label = sample.sample_id or sample.site.community or f\"sample {i + 1}\"\n color = style.accent_color if i % 2 == 0 else style.secondary_color\n first = True\n for px, py in ((xc, yc), (xa, ya), (xd, yd)):\n ax.plot(px, py, marker, ms=6, mfc=color, mec=\"white\", mew=0.8,\n label=label if first else None)\n first = False\n plotted.append(label)\n if plotted:\n ax.legend(loc=\"upper left\", fontsize=8, frameon=True)\n ax.set_title(title)\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef plot_stiff(\n sample: WaterQualitySample,\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n style: HouseStyle | None = None,\n title: str | None = None,\n):\n \"\"\"Stiff diagram: Na+K / Ca / Mg on the left, Cl / HCO3 / SO4 right.\"\"\"\n style = style or HouseStyle()\n ionic = ionic_balance(sample)\n if ionic is None:\n raise ValueError(\"Stiff diagram needs the major ions (Ca, Mg, Na, Cl, HCO3)\")\n cat = ionic.cations_meq\n an = ionic.anions_meq\n rows = [\n (cat.get(\"sodium\", 0) + cat.get(\"potassium\", 0), an.get(\"chloride\", 0), \"Na+K\", \"Cl\"),\n (cat.get(\"calcium\", 0), an.get(\"bicarbonate\", 0) + an.get(\"carbonate\", 0), \"Ca\", \"HCO3\"),\n (cat.get(\"magnesium\", 0), an.get(\"sulfate\", 0), \"Mg\", \"SO4\"),\n ]\n with figure_context(style):\n fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(style.figure_width_in * 0.7, 2.8))\n ys = [2, 1, 0]\n xs_left = [-r[0] for r in rows]\n xs_right = [r[1] for r in rows]\n poly_x = xs_left + xs_right[::-1]\n poly_y = ys + ys[::-1]\n ax.fill(poly_x, poly_y, color=style.accent_color, alpha=0.25, lw=0)\n ax.plot(poly_x + [poly_x[0]], poly_y + [poly_y[0]], color=style.accent_color, lw=1.6)\n ax.axvline(0, color=\"#555555\", lw=1.0)\n for y, (c_meq, a_meq, _c_label, _a_label) in zip(ys, rows, strict=True):\n ax.plot([-c_meq], [y], \"o\", ms=4, color=style.accent_color)\n ax.plot([a_meq], [y], \"o\", ms=4, color=style.accent_color)\n ax.text(ax.get_xlim()[0], y, \"\", fontsize=8)\n span = max(max(map(abs, xs_left)), max(xs_right), 0.5) * 1.3\n ax.set_xlim(-span, span)\n ax.set_ylim(-0.6, 2.6)\n for y, (_c, _a, c_label, a_label) in zip(ys, rows, strict=True):\n ax.text(-span * 0.98, y, c_label, ha=\"left\", va=\"center\", fontsize=9)\n ax.text(span * 0.98, y, a_label, ha=\"right\", va=\"center\", fontsize=9)\n ax.set_yticks([])\n ax.set_xlabel(\"meq/L (cations left, anions right)\")\n ax.set_title(title or f\"Stiff diagram - {sample.sample_id or sample.site.community}\")\n fig.tight_layout()\n if path is not None:\n return save_figure(fig, path, style)\n return fig\n\n\ndef facies_of(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> dict | None:\n \"\"\"The hydrochemical facies of a sample, from its major ions.\n\n Returns ``None`` without a complete major-ion analysis. Otherwise the\n dominant cation and anion (above half of the meq/L total, else\n \"mixed\"), the milliequivalent percentages, and a sentence for the\n report: the Piper diagram used to be the whole of a section headed\n \"Hydrochemical Facies\", with nothing said about what it showed.\n \"\"\"\n ionic = ionic_balance(sample)\n if ionic is None:\n return None\n cat = ionic.cations_meq\n an = ionic.anions_meq\n ca, mg = cat.get(\"calcium\", 0.0), cat.get(\"magnesium\", 0.0)\n nak = cat.get(\"sodium\", 0.0) + cat.get(\"potassium\", 0.0)\n hco3 = an.get(\"bicarbonate\", 0.0) + an.get(\"carbonate\", 0.0)\n cl, so4 = an.get(\"chloride\", 0.0), an.get(\"sulfate\", 0.0)\n cat_total, an_total = ca + mg + nak, hco3 + cl + so4\n if cat_total <= 0 or an_total <= 0:\n return None\n cations = {\"Ca\": ca / cat_total, \"Mg\": mg / cat_total, \"Na+K\": nak / cat_total}\n anions = {\"HCO3\": hco3 / an_total, \"Cl\": cl / an_total, \"SO4\": so4 / an_total}\n lead_cat = max(cations, key=cations.get)\n lead_an = max(anions, key=anions.get)\n cat_name = lead_cat if cations[lead_cat] >= 0.5 else \"mixed-cation\"\n an_name = lead_an if anions[lead_an] >= 0.5 else \"mixed-anion\"\n facies = f\"{cat_name}-{an_name}\"\n pct = lambda d: \", \".join(f\"{k} {v * 100:.0f}%\" for k, v in d.items()) # noqa: E731\n if an_name == \"HCO3\" and cat_name in (\"Ca\", \"Mg\"):\n meaning = (\n \"a fresh, recently recharged water of the kind weathering of \"\n \"silicate rock gives; typical of shallow basement groundwater\"\n )\n elif an_name == \"HCO3\":\n meaning = (\n \"a bicarbonate water in which sodium and potassium have replaced \"\n \"calcium, which points to longer contact with the rock or to ion \"\n \"exchange in a clayey weathered zone\"\n )\n elif an_name == \"Cl\" and cat_name == \"Na+K\":\n meaning = (\n \"a sodium chloride water, which in this setting points to \"\n \"salinity from the coast, an estuary or evaporation rather than \"\n \"to rock weathering\"\n )\n elif an_name == \"SO4\":\n meaning = (\n \"a sulfate water, which is unusual in basement ground and worth \"\n \"checking against the sample's provenance\"\n )\n else:\n meaning = \"a mixed water with no single dominant ion pair\"\n sentence = (\n f\"The water is a {facies} type ({pct(cations)}; {pct(anions)}, in \"\n f\"milliequivalent percent): {meaning}.\"\n )\n return {\n \"facies\": facies, \"cations\": cations, \"anions\": anions,\n \"sentence\": sentence,\n }\n"}, "groundwater/quality/indices.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Aggregate water quality index and health-risk scoring.\n\nTwo summary numbers a district water office can use to rank many\nboreholes and prioritise treatment or rehabilitation:\n\n* Water Quality Index (WQI) - a weighted-arithmetic 0-based index over the\n physico-chemical parameters, with the usual rating classes (Excellent to\n Unsuitable). One number per borehole for comparison.\n\n* Health Hazard Index (HI) - the sum of hazard quotients (chronic daily\n intake over the oral reference dose) for the toxicants that matter for\n long-term ingestion (arsenic, fluoride, nitrate, manganese, lead,\n uranium and others), plus a lifetime carcinogenic risk for arsenic. HI\n below 1 is generally acceptable; at or above 1 there is a potential\n non-carcinogenic health concern.\n\nBoth are computed from the values and guideline limits the toolkit already\ncarries, and both degrade gracefully when parameters are missing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualitySample\nfrom .standards import (\n Limit,\n StandardEntry,\n canonical_values,\n load_standards,\n)\n\n# adult chronic exposure (WHO/EPA default)\n_INTAKE_L_PER_DAY = 2.0\n_BODY_WEIGHT_KG = 70.0\n\n# oral reference doses, mg/kg/day (EPA IRIS / WHO), for the toxicants that\n# drive long-term ingestion risk in this setting\n_RFD = {\n \"arsenic\": 3.0e-4,\n \"fluoride\": 0.06,\n \"nitrate (as no3)\": 1.6,\n \"nitrite (as no2)\": 0.1,\n \"manganese\": 0.14,\n \"lead\": 3.5e-3,\n \"cadmium\": 5.0e-4,\n \"chromium (total)\": 3.0e-3,\n \"uranium\": 3.0e-3,\n \"nickel\": 0.02,\n \"copper\": 0.04,\n \"zinc\": 0.3,\n \"barium\": 0.2,\n \"selenium\": 5.0e-3,\n \"antimony\": 4.0e-4,\n}\n# oral cancer slope factors, (mg/kg/day)^-1\n_CANCER_SLOPE = {\"arsenic\": 1.5}\n\n# The EPA IRIS reference doses for nitrate (1.6) and nitrite (0.1) are\n# expressed as nitrogen (NO3-N / NO2-N), but the toolkit records nitrate and\n# nitrite as the whole ion (as NO3 / as NO2). Convert the measured \"as ion\"\n# concentration to a nitrogen basis before dividing by the RfD, else the\n# hazard quotient is overstated by the mass ratio (NO3/N = 62/14 = 4.43,\n# NO2/N = 46/14 = 3.29).\n_AS_NITROGEN_FACTOR = {\n \"nitrate (as no3)\": 62.004 / 14.007,\n \"nitrite (as no2)\": 46.005 / 14.007,\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass WaterQualityIndex:\n value: float\n rating: str\n n_parameters: int\n top_contributors: list[tuple[str, float]] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass HealthRiskAssessment:\n hazard_index: float\n hazard_quotients: dict # parameter -> HQ\n cancer_risk: Optional[float] # lifetime, arsenic\n rating: str\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\ndef _measured(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> dict[str, float]:\n \"\"\"Every measured value, converted onto the standards table's scale.\n\n The reference doses and the index weights below are all mg/L figures, so\n a laboratory reporting in ug/L used to produce a hazard index a thousand\n times too high - \"High\" risk and a 0.4 lifetime cancer risk for water\n that is well inside every guideline. A value whose unit cannot be\n reconciled is left out rather than used raw.\n \"\"\"\n return canonical_values(sample)\n\n\ndef _wqi_limit(entry: StandardEntry) -> Optional[Limit]:\n for limit in (entry.who_health, entry.who_aesthetic, entry.sl_standard):\n if limit is not None:\n return limit\n return None\n\n\ndef _wqi_rating(value: float) -> str:\n if value <= 50:\n return \"Excellent\"\n if value <= 100:\n return \"Good\"\n if value <= 200:\n return \"Poor\"\n if value <= 300:\n return \"Very poor\"\n return \"Unsuitable for drinking\"\n\n\ndef compute_wqi(sample: WaterQualitySample, standards_path=None) -> Optional[WaterQualityIndex]:\n \"\"\"Weighted-arithmetic Water Quality Index over physico-chemical data.\n\n Returns None when fewer than three usable parameters are available.\n \"\"\"\n table = load_standards(standards_path)\n values = _measured(sample)\n weight_sum = 0.0\n weighted_q = 0.0\n contributors: list[tuple[str, float]] = []\n n = 0\n for key, value in values.items():\n entry = table.get(key)\n if entry is None or entry.category == \"microbiological\":\n continue\n if key in _RFD:\n # Health-based trace toxicants (arsenic, lead, fluoride, nitrate,\n # ...) have tiny standards, so 1/s weighting and the value/s\n # sub-index let a single one dominate and drown out the general\n # chemistry this index is meant to summarise. They are reported\n # through the separate Hazard Index instead; excluding them keeps\n # the WQI a physico-chemical/acceptability measure as documented.\n continue\n limit = _wqi_limit(entry)\n if limit is None or not limit.maximum or limit.maximum <= 0:\n continue\n s_i = limit.maximum\n if key == \"ph\":\n ideal = 7.0\n denom = s_i - ideal\n q_i = 100.0 * abs(value - ideal) / denom if denom else 0.0\n else:\n q_i = 100.0 * value / s_i\n w_i = 1.0 / s_i\n weight_sum += w_i\n weighted_q += w_i * q_i\n contributors.append((entry.parameter, w_i * q_i))\n n += 1\n if n < 3 or weight_sum <= 0:\n return None\n wqi = weighted_q / weight_sum\n contributors.sort(key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)\n return WaterQualityIndex(\n value=round(wqi, 1),\n rating=_wqi_rating(wqi),\n n_parameters=n,\n top_contributors=[(name, round(c / weight_sum, 1)) for name, c in contributors[:3]],\n )\n\n\ndef assess_health_risk(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> Optional[HealthRiskAssessment]:\n \"\"\"Non-carcinogenic Hazard Index and arsenic carcinogenic risk.\n\n Returns None when none of the scored toxicants were measured.\n \"\"\"\n values = _measured(sample)\n hq: dict[str, float] = {}\n intake_factor = _INTAKE_L_PER_DAY / _BODY_WEIGHT_KG\n for key, rfd in _RFD.items():\n if key in values and rfd > 0:\n conc = values[key]\n factor = _AS_NITROGEN_FACTOR.get(key)\n if factor:\n conc = conc / factor # the RfD is expressed as nitrogen\n cdi = conc * intake_factor # mg/kg/day\n hq[key] = cdi / rfd\n if not hq:\n return None\n hazard_index = sum(hq.values())\n cancer_risk = None\n if \"arsenic\" in values:\n cdi_as = values[\"arsenic\"] * intake_factor\n cancer_risk = cdi_as * _CANCER_SLOPE[\"arsenic\"]\n\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n if hazard_index >= 1.0:\n worst = max(hq, key=hq.get)\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"hazard_index\",\n f\"Non-carcinogenic Hazard Index {hazard_index:.1f} is at or above \"\n f\"1 (dominated by {worst}); chronic ingestion poses a potential \"\n \"health concern.\",\n )\n )\n if cancer_risk is not None and cancer_risk > 1e-4:\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"cancer_risk\",\n f\"Estimated lifetime arsenic cancer risk {cancer_risk:.1e} exceeds \"\n \"the 1e-4 screening level.\",\n )\n )\n\n if hazard_index < 1.0:\n rating = \"Acceptable (Hazard Index below 1)\"\n elif hazard_index < 4.0:\n rating = \"Elevated (Hazard Index at or above 1)\"\n else:\n rating = \"High (Hazard Index at or above 4)\"\n\n return HealthRiskAssessment(\n hazard_index=round(hazard_index, 2),\n hazard_quotients={k: round(v, 2) for k, v in sorted(hq.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)},\n cancer_risk=cancer_risk,\n rating=rating,\n flags=flags,\n )\n"}, "groundwater/quality/ionic.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Ionic balance check for major ion analyses.\n\nThe charge balance error is ``100 x (sum cations - sum anions) /\n(sum cations + sum anions)`` in meq/L. Errors within 5 percent are\nnormal laboratory practice; 5 to 10 percent is flagged for review and\nmore than 10 percent indicates an unreliable analysis or a missing\nmajor ion.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, WaterQualitySample\nfrom .standards import canonical_values, normalise_parameter\n\n# meq per mg: charge / molar mass\n_CATIONS = {\n \"calcium\": 2 / 40.078,\n \"magnesium\": 2 / 24.305,\n \"sodium\": 1 / 22.990,\n \"potassium\": 1 / 39.098,\n \"iron\": 2 / 55.845, # ferrous, minor\n \"manganese\": 2 / 54.938, # minor\n}\n_ANIONS = {\n \"chloride\": 1 / 35.453,\n \"sulfate\": 2 / 96.06,\n \"bicarbonate\": 1 / 61.017,\n \"carbonate\": 2 / 60.009,\n \"nitrate (as no3)\": 1 / 62.004,\n \"fluoride\": 1 / 18.998,\n}\n\n# the majors on each side that make a balance meaningful. Sulfate is one of\n# the three major anions: without it the balance came out 15% short and was\n# reported as an unreliable analysis, when the analysis was merely incomplete\n_REQUIRED_CATIONS = (\"calcium\", \"magnesium\", \"sodium\")\n_REQUIRED_ANIONS = (\"chloride\", \"bicarbonate\", \"sulfate\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass IonicBalanceResult:\n sum_cations_meq: float\n sum_anions_meq: float\n error_percent: float\n cations_meq: dict\n anions_meq: dict\n used_alkalinity_for_bicarbonate: bool\n flag: Optional[DataFlag]\n\n\ndef _value(sample: WaterQualitySample, key: str) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"One ion in milliequivalents-ready mg/L.\n\n The meq factors above are per mg/L, so the value has to be on that scale\n before it is multiplied: the same chemistry reported in ug/L gave a\n charge balance error of 8.7% and was flagged as a laboratory problem.\n \"\"\"\n canonical = canonical_values(sample)\n if key in canonical:\n return canonical[key]\n for result in sample.results:\n if normalise_parameter(result.parameter) == key:\n if result.value is not None:\n # present but not convertible: refuse it rather than use the\n # raw number on an unknown scale\n return None\n return 0.0 if result.below_detection else None\n return None\n\n\ndef ionic_balance(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> Optional[IonicBalanceResult]:\n \"\"\"Compute the charge balance; returns None when the major ions are\n not sufficiently covered by the analysis.\"\"\"\n cations: dict[str, float] = {}\n anions: dict[str, float] = {}\n\n for key, factor in _CATIONS.items():\n value = _value(sample, key)\n if value is not None:\n cations[key] = value * factor\n\n used_alk = False\n for key, factor in _ANIONS.items():\n value = _value(sample, key)\n if value is not None:\n anions[key] = value * factor\n if \"bicarbonate\" not in anions:\n alk = _value(sample, \"alkalinity\")\n if alk is not None:\n # alkalinity as CaCO3 -> bicarbonate equivalent: meq = mg/L / 50.04\n anions[\"bicarbonate\"] = alk / 50.04\n used_alk = True\n\n if not all(k in cations for k in _REQUIRED_CATIONS) or not all(\n k in anions for k in _REQUIRED_ANIONS\n ):\n return None\n\n total_cat = sum(cations.values())\n total_an = sum(anions.values())\n if total_cat + total_an <= 0:\n return None\n error = 100.0 * (total_cat - total_an) / (total_cat + total_an)\n\n flag = None\n if abs(error) > 10:\n flag = DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"ionic_balance\",\n f\"Charge balance error {error:+.1f}% exceeds 10%; the analysis is \"\n \"unreliable or a major ion is missing.\",\n )\n elif abs(error) > 5:\n flag = DataFlag(\n \"warning\",\n \"ionic_balance\",\n f\"Charge balance error {error:+.1f}% is between 5% and 10%; review \"\n \"the laboratory analysis.\",\n )\n return IonicBalanceResult(\n sum_cations_meq=total_cat,\n sum_anions_meq=total_an,\n error_percent=error,\n cations_meq=cations,\n anions_meq=anions,\n used_alkalinity_for_bicarbonate=used_alk,\n flag=flag,\n )\n\n\n#: What the balance needs, in the order a certificate lists them.\n_ION_LABELS = {\n \"calcium\": \"calcium\", \"magnesium\": \"magnesium\", \"sodium\": \"sodium\",\n \"potassium\": \"potassium\", \"chloride\": \"chloride\", \"sulfate\": \"sulfate\",\n \"bicarbonate\": \"bicarbonate (or alkalinity)\",\n}\n\n\ndef ionic_balance_gap(sample: WaterQualitySample) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"The major ions the balance needs and the analysis does not carry.\n\n The balance is the one check that says whether a certificate's own\n numbers hang together, and it was skipped in silence whenever a major\n ion was missing: the report simply had no charge-balance line, which\n reads as \"the analysis balanced\" rather than \"nobody could tell\".\n \"\"\"\n missing = []\n for key in _REQUIRED_CATIONS:\n if _value(sample, key) is None:\n missing.append(_ION_LABELS.get(key, key))\n for key in _REQUIRED_ANIONS:\n if _value(sample, key) is not None:\n continue\n if key == \"bicarbonate\" and _value(sample, \"alkalinity\") is not None:\n continue\n missing.append(_ION_LABELS.get(key, key))\n return missing\n"}, "groundwater/quality/standards.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Guideline and standard values for drinking water parameters.\n\nThe bundled table (``data/who_guidelines.csv``) carries WHO Guidelines\nfor Drinking-water Quality values (4th edition with addenda) split\ninto health based and acceptability values, plus a Sierra Leone\nstandard column. Where a confirmed national value is not to hand the\nnational column mirrors the WHO/regional figure; confirm the values\nagainst the current Sierra Leone Standards Bureau specification and\nedit the CSV (or pass a custom file) - no code change is needed.\n\nRange values such as pH are written ``6.5-8.5`` and evaluated as an\nallowed interval.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport functools\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom importlib import resources\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom ..units import _normalise as normalise_unit_text\nfrom ..units import comparable, convert, parse_unit\n\n_RANGE_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*-\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*$\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Limit:\n \"\"\"A guideline limit: either a maximum or an allowed range.\"\"\"\n\n maximum: Optional[float] = None\n minimum: Optional[float] = None\n\n @classmethod\n def parse(cls, text: str) -> Optional[\"Limit\"]:\n text = (text or \"\").strip()\n if not text:\n return None\n match = _RANGE_RE.match(text)\n if match:\n return cls(minimum=float(match.group(1)), maximum=float(match.group(2)))\n try:\n return cls(maximum=float(text))\n except ValueError:\n return None\n\n def exceeded_by(self, value: float) -> bool:\n if self.minimum is not None and value < self.minimum:\n return True\n if self.maximum is not None and value > self.maximum:\n return True\n return False\n\n def __str__(self) -> str:\n if self.minimum is not None:\n return f\"{self.minimum:g}-{self.maximum:g}\"\n if self.maximum is not None:\n return f\"{self.maximum:g}\"\n return \"\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StandardEntry:\n parameter: str\n unit: str\n who_health: Optional[Limit]\n who_aesthetic: Optional[Limit]\n sl_standard: Optional[Limit]\n category: str\n note: str\n #: Where the national value came from. ``\"provisional\"`` means it has not\n #: been checked against the Sierra Leone Standards Bureau specification -\n #: it is a WHO figure carried across, or one adopted from regional\n #: practice. Set it to the issuing specification once confirmed.\n sl_source: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def sl_provisional(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether the national value is unconfirmed against the SLSB spec.\"\"\"\n return self.sl_standard is not None and self.sl_source == \"provisional\"\n\n\n#: Said wherever a national verdict is shown, while any national value is\n#: still provisional. A compliance failure against an unconfirmed limit is a\n#: prompt to check the specification, not a finding to put in front of a\n#: regulator.\nPROVISIONAL_NATIONAL_NOTE = (\n \"The national column in the standards table is provisional: its values \"\n \"are WHO guideline figures carried across, or limits adopted from \"\n \"regional practice, and have not been confirmed against the Sierra Leone \"\n \"Standards Bureau drinking water specification. Confirm the figures \"\n \"before treating a national exceedance as a compliance finding.\"\n)\n\n\ndef provisional_national_parameters(\n table: dict[str, \"StandardEntry\"] | None = None,\n) -> list[str]:\n \"\"\"Parameters whose national limit is still unconfirmed.\"\"\"\n entries = (table or load_standards()).values()\n return sorted(e.parameter for e in entries if e.sl_provisional)\n\n\n_ALIASES = {\n \"ec\": \"electrical conductivity\",\n \"conductivity\": \"electrical conductivity\",\n \"total dissolved solids\": \"tds\",\n \"hardness\": \"total hardness\",\n \"nitrate\": \"nitrate (as no3)\",\n \"no3\": \"nitrate (as no3)\",\n \"nitrite\": \"nitrite (as no2)\",\n \"no2\": \"nitrite (as no2)\",\n \"ammonia\": \"ammonia (as n)\",\n \"ammonium\": \"ammonia (as n)\",\n \"nh3\": \"ammonia (as n)\",\n \"nh4\": \"ammonia (as n)\",\n \"chromium\": \"chromium (total)\",\n \"cr\": \"chromium (total)\",\n \"faecal coliforms\": \"e. coli\",\n \"fecal coliforms\": \"e. coli\",\n \"e.coli\": \"e. coli\",\n \"escherichia coli\": \"e. coli\",\n \"coliforms\": \"total coliforms\",\n \"sulphate\": \"sulfate\",\n \"so4\": \"sulfate\",\n \"aluminum\": \"aluminium\",\n # the spellings a Sierra Leone certificate actually carries\n \"total alkalinity\": \"alkalinity\",\n \"alkalinity (as caco3)\": \"alkalinity\",\n \"alkalinity as caco3\": \"alkalinity\",\n \"total alkalinity as caco3\": \"alkalinity\",\n \"total iron\": \"iron\",\n \"iron (total)\": \"iron\",\n \"total dissolved solid\": \"tds\",\n \"dissolved solids\": \"tds\",\n \"specific conductance\": \"electrical conductivity\",\n \"ph value\": \"ph\",\n \"color\": \"colour\",\n \"true colour\": \"colour\",\n \"apparent colour\": \"colour\",\n \"thermotolerant coliforms\": \"e. coli\",\n \"thermotolerant coliform\": \"e. coli\",\n \"faecal coliform\": \"e. coli\",\n \"fecal coliform\": \"e. coli\",\n \"total coliform\": \"total coliforms\",\n \"residual chlorine\": \"free chlorine\",\n \"chlorine residual\": \"free chlorine\",\n \"free residual chlorine\": \"free chlorine\",\n \"nitrate-n\": \"nitrate (as n)\",\n \"nitrate n\": \"nitrate (as n)\",\n \"nitrate as n\": \"nitrate (as n)\",\n \"nitrate nitrogen\": \"nitrate (as n)\",\n \"no3-n\": \"nitrate (as n)\",\n \"nitrite-n\": \"nitrite (as n)\",\n \"nitrite n\": \"nitrite (as n)\",\n \"nitrite as n\": \"nitrite (as n)\",\n \"nitrite nitrogen\": \"nitrite (as n)\",\n \"no2-n\": \"nitrite (as n)\",\n \"orthophosphate\": \"phosphate\",\n \"phosphate (as po4)\": \"phosphate\",\n \"po4\": \"phosphate\",\n \"silica (as sio2)\": \"silica\",\n \"sio2\": \"silica\",\n \"tss\": \"total suspended solids\",\n \"suspended solids\": \"total suspended solids\",\n \"co3\": \"carbonate\",\n \"hco3\": \"bicarbonate\",\n}\n\n# \"Iron (Fe)\", \"Turbidity (NTU)\", \"Conductivity (EC)\", \"Temperature (\u00b0C)\":\n# a trailing bracket that is a symbol or a unit, not a basis (\"(as NO3)\")\n# and not the table's own qualifier (\"(total)\")\n_TRAILING_QUALIFIER_RE = re.compile(r\"\\s*\\((?!\\s*as\\s)[^)]*\\)\\s*$\")\n\n\ndef normalise_parameter(name: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"The standards-table key a certificate's parameter name refers to.\n\n Every laboratory writes the same determinand differently (\"Iron (Fe)\",\n \"Total iron\", \"Nitrate (NO3)\", \"pH value\").
