The assessment is\n fail-closed - an unknown name makes the whole sample \"not proven safe\" -\n so name resolution is load-bearing, and it used to know only the\n template's own spellings.\n \"\"\"\n key = re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", str(name or \"\").strip().lower())\n if key in _ALIASES:\n return _ALIASES[key]\n stripped = _TRAILING_QUALIFIER_RE.sub(\"\", key)\n if stripped != key:\n # \"chromium (total)\" strips to \"chromium\", which the aliases map\n # straight back; \"iron (fe)\" strips to \"iron\", a table key\n return _ALIASES.get(stripped, stripped)\n return key\n\n\n_PARAMETER_BASIS_RE = re.compile(r\"\\(\\s*as\\s+([^)]+?)\\s*\\)\")\n\n\ndef _parameter_basis(parameter: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"The chemical basis a parameter name states: \"Nitrate (as NO3)\" -> \"no3\".\"\"\"\n match = _PARAMETER_BASIS_RE.search(str(parameter or \"\"))\n return match.group(1).lower().replace(\" \", \"\") if match else \"\"\n\n\ndef to_standard_unit(\n value: float, reported_unit: str, entry: StandardEntry\n) -> tuple[Optional[float], str]:\n \"\"\"Put a reported value on the scale the standards table uses.\n\n Returns ``(converted, reason)``. ``converted`` is ``None`` when the value\n must not be used against this parameter's limits - an unreadable unit, or\n one that measures something else. That is never the same as zero, and a\n caller must drop the value rather than fall back to the raw number.\n\n ``reason`` is ``\"\"`` on a clean conversion, ``\"unit_assumed\"`` when the\n laboratory reported no usable unit and the guideline's own was assumed,\n ``\"unit_basis_assumed\"`` when one side names a chemical basis the other\n does not, or an ``INDETERMINATE_REASONS`` code on refusal.\n \"\"\"\n reported = str(reported_unit or \"\").strip()\n guideline = str(entry.unit or \"\").strip()\n\n # \"-\", \"n/a\" and friends normalise away to nothing: they are how a sheet\n # writes \"no unit here\", so they take the no-unit path rather than the\n # unreadable one.\n if reported and not normalise_unit_text(reported):\n reported = \"\"\n\n if not reported:\n # No unit on the sheet. The guideline's own unit is the only reading\n # under which the number means anything; the assumption is recorded\n # rather than hidden.\n return float(value), \"unit_assumed\"\n if not guideline:\n # The standards table itself names no unit, so there is no scale to\n # convert onto and nothing to disagree about.\n return float(value), \"\"\n if normalise_unit_text(reported) == normalise_unit_text(guideline):\n # Written the same way: same scale, whether or not the unit module has\n # ever heard of the unit. Keeps a newly added guideline unit from\n # making every sample indeterminate.\n return float(value), \"\"\n\n source = parse_unit(reported)\n target = parse_unit(guideline)\n\n if target is not None and target.dimension == \"ph\":\n # pH is the one absolute scale here with no rival: there is no such\n # thing as pH in another unit, so a sheet carrying \"mg/L\" beside a pH\n # of 7.2 is a template artefact, not a different measurement.\n if source is None or source.dimension != \"ph\":\n return float(value), \"unit_assumed\"\n return float(value), \"\"\n\n if source is None or target is None:\n return None, \"unit_unreadable\"\n if not comparable(source, target):\n return None, \"unit_mismatch\"\n converted = convert(value, reported, guideline)\n if converted is None: # pragma: no cover - comparable() already checked\n return None, \"unit_mismatch\"\n if source.basis and not target.basis:\n # The unit names a chemical reference the guideline's unit does not.\n # The parameter name often carries it instead, so look there before\n # deciding: \"Nitrate (as NO3)\" reported in \"mg/L as N\" is a different\n # number by a factor of 4.4, and grading it at face value passed a\n # sample at 44 mg/L as NO3 that the guideline puts over its limit.\n named = _parameter_basis(entry.parameter)\n if named and named != source.basis:\n return None, \"unit_basis_conflict\"\n if not named:\n # Nothing states the guideline's basis, so the reading is taken\n # but it is worth an analyst's eye: calcium as Ca and calcium as\n # CaCO3 differ by a factor of 2.5.\n return converted, \"unit_basis_assumed\"\n elif target.basis and not source.basis:\n return converted, \"unit_basis_assumed\"\n return converted, \"\"\n\n\ndef canonical_values(\n sample, table: dict[str, StandardEntry] | None = None\n) -> dict[str, float]:\n \"\"\"Every measured result in the sample, on the standards table's scale.\n\n Keyed by normalised parameter name. A result whose unit cannot be\n reconciled with its guideline is *left out* rather than passed through\n raw: the aggregate indices built on these numbers - the water quality\n index, the hazard index, the ionic balance, the corrosivity indices -\n all assume mg/L, and a sample reported in ug/L quietly produced a hazard\n index a thousand times too high and an \"unsuitable for drinking\" rating\n for clean water.\n \"\"\"\n table = table if table is not None else load_standards()\n values: dict[str, float] = {}\n for result in getattr(sample, \"results\", []):\n if result.value is None:\n continue\n key = normalise_parameter(result.parameter)\n entry = table.get(key)\n if entry is None:\n # No guideline entry, so no declared scale to convert onto. The\n # value is carried as written; nothing downstream has a limit for\n # it either.\n values[key] = float(result.value)\n continue\n converted, _ = to_standard_unit(float(result.value), result.unit, entry)\n if converted is not None:\n values[key] = converted\n return values\n\n\n@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)\ndef _bundled_rows() -> tuple[dict, ...]:\n \"\"\"The bundled CSV, parsed once per process.\n\n assess_sample used to open and parse the file about twenty-six times\n per sample (once per ion the ionic balance and the corrosivity indices\n asked for); the portfolio and the Streamlit pages assess every borehole\n on each rerun, and the Pyodide build pays for file IO dearly. Callers\n still get fresh StandardEntry objects, so a table they edit stays theirs.\n \"\"\"\n source = resources.files(\"groundwater.data\").joinpath(\"who_guidelines.csv\")\n with source.open(\"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n return tuple(csv.DictReader(fh))\n\n\ndef load_standards(path: str | Path | None = None) -> dict[str, StandardEntry]:\n \"\"\"Load the standards table keyed by normalised parameter name.\"\"\"\n if path is None:\n rows = _bundled_rows()\n else:\n with open(path, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))\n table: dict[str, StandardEntry] = {}\n for row in rows:\n entry = StandardEntry(\n parameter=row[\"parameter\"],\n unit=row[\"unit\"],\n who_health=Limit.parse(row.get(\"who_health_gv\", \"\")),\n who_aesthetic=Limit.parse(row.get(\"who_aesthetic\", \"\")),\n sl_standard=Limit.parse(row.get(\"sl_standard\", \"\")),\n category=row.get(\"category\", \"\"),\n note=row.get(\"note\", \"\"),\n sl_source=(row.get(\"sl_source\") or \"\").strip(),\n )\n table[normalise_parameter(entry.parameter)] = entry\n return table\n"}, "groundwater/readiness.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Whether a project's results are complete enough to certify.\n\nA completion report is the document a borehole is handed over on. It gets\nfiled, invoiced against, and read years later by someone deciding whether\nthe village still has water. The toolkit will write one from whatever it\nhas - and it should, because an interim report is a real need - but it must\nnot let a document that rests on missing evidence look like one that does\nnot.\n\nSo every report carries its own provenance. This module answers one\nquestion, over the results the project already holds: which of the things a\ncertifiable report needs are actually established? The answer is a list of\n:class:`Requirement` records, each either met, unmet, not applicable, or\noverridden by a named person with a stated reason. A report built from a\nproject that is not ready is stamped PROVISIONAL on its cover and carries\nthe list; a report built from one that is ready is not stamped at all.\nNothing is blocked, and nothing is quietly passed off as final.\n\n**Completeness, not outcome.** A borehole whose water fails the arsenic\nguideline is a perfectly certifiable borehole: the finding is the point of\nthe report. What is not certifiable is a borehole whose arsenic result\ncould not be read. The requirements here ask \"do we know?\", never \"is the\nanswer the one we wanted?\" - a gate that failed bad news would teach people\nto leave the bad news out.\n\nThe signals are not re-derived. Every module in the toolkit already raises\n:class:`~groundwater.models.DataFlag` for what it could not do, and the\nwater quality assessment already exposes its own uncertainties; this module\nreads those. A requirement that invented its own check would drift from the\nanalysis it is supposed to describe.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom .utils import plural, plural_noun\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport os\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom functools import lru_cache\nfrom importlib import resources\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Iterable, Optional\n\n__all__ = [\n \"Requirement\",\n \"Readiness\",\n \"REPORTS\",\n \"REQUIREMENTS\",\n \"SampleProvenance\",\n \"assess_readiness\",\n \"load_sample_provenance\",\n \"source_provenance\",\n]\n\n#: Flag codes that mean a reading was refused, converted from an unreadable\n#: unit, or otherwise could not be used. Raised by ingestion/pumping.py and\n#: quality/assess.py; listed here so the gate and the parsers cannot drift.\n_UNIT_BLOCKERS = (\n \"time_unit_unknown\",\n \"discharge_unit_unknown\",\n \"discharge_ambiguous\",\n \"time_reading_unreadable\",\n)\n\n#: Codes that say a value was assumed rather than read. Not blocking - the\n#: assumption is stated in the report - but worth surfacing beside the gate.\n_UNIT_ASSUMPTIONS = (\n \"discharge_unit_assumed\",\n \"unit_not_reported\",\n \"unit_basis_assumed\",\n \"utm_zone_assumed\",\n \"test_type_inferred\",\n)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass SampleProvenance:\n \"\"\"What one bundled example file actually contains.\n\n ``kind`` is one of:\n\n ``transcribed``\n Copied verbatim off a real survey or completion document. Numbers\n read out of it are somebody's real measurements.\n ``reconstructed``\n Real measurements, but a column the original left blank has been\n filled in illustratively. Worth stating on the report; not a reason\n to withhold certification, because the measurements are real.\n ``synthetic``\n The readings were invented. Nothing was measured, and a report that\n quotes them is describing a sample that was never taken.\n \"\"\"\n\n file: str\n kind: str\n note: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def measured(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether the readings in this file were taken from something real.\"\"\"\n return self.kind != \"synthetic\"\n\n\n@lru_cache(maxsize=4)\ndef load_sample_provenance(path: str | Path | None = None) -> dict[str, SampleProvenance]:\n \"\"\"The bundled example files, keyed by basename.\n\n Keyed by basename rather than by the path each engine happens to use:\n the browser bundles ``dr_timbo/dr_timbo_water_quality.xlsx``, the\n Streamlit picker offers the same relative path, and\n ``examples/run_dr_timbo_completion.py`` opens it straight off disk. It\n is one file, and what it contains does not depend on which of those\n opened it.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n if path is not None:\n text = Path(path).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n else:\n text = (resources.files(\"groundwater\") / \"data\" /\n \"sample_provenance.csv\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n except (OSError, ModuleNotFoundError):\n # The record is packaged with the library, so this should not\n # happen - but losing it must not take the gate down with it. An\n # empty record means no file is *known* to be synthetic, and the\n # bundled-sample marker below still does its half of the job.\n return {}\n out: dict[str, SampleProvenance] = {}\n for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text)):\n name = os.path.basename((row.get(\"file\") or \"\").strip())\n if not name:\n continue\n out[name.lower()] = SampleProvenance(\n file=(row.get(\"file\") or \"\").strip(),\n kind=(row.get(\"provenance\") or \"\").strip().lower(),\n note=(row.get(\"note\") or \"\").strip(),\n )\n return out\n\n\ndef source_provenance(source: Any) -> SampleProvenance | None:\n \"\"\"The provenance record for one loaded source, if it is a bundled file.\n\n ``source`` is a source dict as both apps hold them: ``{\"name\": ...}``\n for an upload, ``{\"sample\": }`` for a bundled pick, and\n in the browser both at once. Either key is matched against the record\n by basename, so a file is recognised however it was loaded.\n\n Matching on the name means a user file that happens to share a bundled\n file's name is taken for the bundled one. That is deliberate: the cost\n is a report stamped provisional that need not have been, which an\n analyst can see and override, and the alternative error is a report\n that quotes invented water quality results without saying so.\n \"\"\"\n if not isinstance(source, dict):\n return None\n known = load_sample_provenance()\n for key in (\"sample\", \"name\"):\n value = source.get(key)\n if not value:\n continue\n found = known.get(os.path.basename(str(value)).lower())\n if found is not None:\n return found\n return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Requirement:\n \"\"\"One thing a certifiable report needs, and whether it is established.\"\"\"\n\n key: str\n title: str\n #: \"met\" | \"unmet\" | \"not_applicable\" | \"overridden\"\n state: str\n #: What was found, in a sentence an analyst can act on.\n detail: str\n #: Who overrode it and why, when ``state`` is \"overridden\".\n override_reason: str = \"\"\n override_by: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def satisfied(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether this requirement stops holding the report back.\n\n An override satisfies it for the purpose of issuing the document and\n is recorded in the document; it does not make the evidence exist.\n \"\"\"\n return self.state in (\"met\", \"not_applicable\", \"overridden\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Readiness:\n \"\"\"The readiness of one project for one kind of report.\"\"\"\n\n report: str\n requirements: list[Requirement] = field(default_factory=list)\n #: Assumptions the analysis made that the reader should see. Never\n #: blocking; a stated assumption is not a missing result.\n assumptions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n @property\n def unmet(self) -> list[Requirement]:\n return [r for r in self.requirements if r.state == \"unmet\"]\n\n @property\n def overridden(self) -> list[Requirement]:\n return [r for r in self.requirements if r.state == \"overridden\"]\n\n @property\n def state(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"``\"ready\"``, ``\"ready_with_overrides\"`` or ``\"not_ready\"``.\"\"\"\n if self.unmet:\n return \"not_ready\"\n return \"ready_with_overrides\" if self.overridden else \"ready\"\n\n @property\n def is_certifiable(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether the document may be issued without a PROVISIONAL stamp.\n\n An override is deliberately *not* certifiable. Overriding says \"issue\n it anyway, on my authority\", which is a legitimate thing to need and\n a different thing from the evidence being there.\n \"\"\"\n return self.state == \"ready\"\n\n @property\n def summary(self) -> str:\n \"\"\"One line for a cover stamp or a status chip.\"\"\"\n if self.state == \"ready\":\n return \"All certification requirements are met.\"\n if self.state == \"ready_with_overrides\":\n names = \", \".join(r.title for r in self.overridden)\n return f\"Issued on override: {names}.\"\n names = \", \".join(r.title for r in self.unmet)\n return f\"Not ready to certify - outstanding: {names}.\"\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n \"\"\"JSON- and YAML-safe, so it round-trips in a saved project.\"\"\"\n return {\n \"report\": self.report,\n \"state\": self.state,\n \"requirements\": [\n {\n \"key\": r.key, \"title\": r.title, \"state\": r.state,\n \"detail\": r.detail, \"override_reason\": r.override_reason,\n \"override_by\": r.override_by,\n }\n for r in self.requirements\n ],\n \"assumptions\": list(self.assumptions),\n }\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The requirements themselves\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _flags(*objects) -> list:\n \"\"\"Every DataFlag carried by the objects given, skipping the absent.\"\"\"\n out = []\n for obj in objects:\n if obj is None:\n continue\n out.extend(getattr(obj, \"flags\", None) or [])\n return out\n\n\ndef _has(flags: Iterable, codes: Iterable[str]) -> list:\n wanted = set(codes)\n return [f for f in flags if getattr(f, \"code\", \"\") in wanted]\n\n\ndef _project_site(state: dict):\n \"\"\"The site, merged across whatever the project holds.\n\n Field crews write the position on one sheet and not the others, so a\n project can be perfectly well located while the drilling log's own header\n block is blank. ``SiteMetadata.merged_with`` fills blanks without\n overwriting anything, which is the same rule the app's header uses.\n \"\"\"\n site = state.get(\"site\")\n for obj in (state.get(\"drilling_log\"), state.get(\"wq_assessment\"),\n state.get(\"borehole_design\")):\n other = getattr(obj, \"site\", None) or getattr(\n getattr(obj, \"sample\", None), \"site\", None)\n if other is not None:\n site = other if site is None else site.merged_with(other)\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is not None:\n site = analysis.test.site if site is None else site.merged_with(\n analysis.test.site)\n return site\n\n\ndef _site_located(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n site = _project_site(state)\n if site is None or site.easting is None or site.northing is None:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"No GPS position is recorded on any sheet in this project. A \"\n \"borehole that cannot be found again on the ground cannot be \"\n \"certified, revisited or maintained.\"\n )\n from .ingestion.checks import check_site_consistency\n\n errors = [f for f in check_site_consistency(site) if f.level == \"error\"]\n if errors:\n return \"unmet\", errors[0].message\n return \"met\", f\"Position recorded: {site.utm}.\"\n\n\ndef _borehole_logged(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n log = state.get(\"drilling_log\")\n if log is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No drilling log has been loaded.\"\n if not log.total_depth_m:\n return \"unmet\", \"The drilling log records no total depth.\"\n if not log.intervals:\n return \"unmet\", \"The drilling log records no lithology.\"\n return \"met\", (\n f\"Logged to {log.total_depth_m:.0f} m with \"\n f\"{plural(len(log.intervals), 'lithological interval')}.\"\n )\n\n\ndef _pumping_measured(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No pumping test has been analysed.\"\n test = analysis.test\n if test.static_water_level_m is None:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"The static water level is missing, so no drawdown can be \"\n \"computed from the test.\"\n )\n if not test.has_discharge:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"No discharge is recorded for the test, so transmissivity and \"\n \"yield stay pending.\"\n )\n missing = [s.step_number for s in test.steps if s.discharge_m3_per_h is None]\n if missing:\n return \"unmet\", (\n f\"Discharge is missing for {plural_noun(len(missing), 'step')} \"\n + \", \".join(str(n) for n in missing) + \".\"\n )\n return \"met\", (\n f\"{plural(len(test.steps), 'step')} with discharge, static water level \"\n f\"{test.static_water_level_m:.2f} m.\"\n )\n\n\ndef _readings_usable(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"No reading was refused for a unit the toolkit could not read.\"\"\"\n flags = _flags(state.get(\"pump_analysis\"), state.get(\"drilling_log\"))\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is not None:\n flags += analysis.test.flags or []\n refused = _has(flags, _UNIT_BLOCKERS)\n if refused:\n return \"unmet\", \"; \".join(f.message for f in refused)\n return \"met\", \"Every reading carried a unit the toolkit could read.\"\n\n\ndef _yield_established(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is None or analysis.yield_recommendation is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No yield recommendation has been derived.\"\n rec = analysis.yield_recommendation\n if rec.pending_reason:\n return \"unmet\", rec.pending_reason\n if rec.safe_yield_m3_per_h is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"The safe yield could not be derived from this test.\"\n # A yield the analysis itself calls indicative is not established. The\n # gate used to certify a 30-minute test inside its casing storage on\n # the strength of the number alone.\n if getattr(rec, \"is_indicative\", False):\n return \"unmet\", (\n f\"The safe yield of {rec.yield_range_text} is indicative, not \"\n \"established: \" + \"; \".join(rec.confidence_reasons) + \".\"\n )\n return \"met\", f\"Safe yield {rec.yield_range_text}.\"\n\n\ndef _water_quality_evaluable(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"Every determinand in the sample was graded against a limit.\n\n Deliberately not \"the verdict state is not indeterminate\". A health\n exceedance outranks uncertainty in the *verdict* - and rightly, since a\n demonstrated failure is a finding - but it does not make an unreadable\n arsenic result readable. Certifying is about the evidence, so the rows\n are checked, not the headline.\n \"\"\"\n assessment = state.get(\"wq_assessment\")\n if assessment is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No water quality results have been assessed.\"\n ungraded = assessment.indeterminate_rows + assessment.unknown_parameters\n if ungraded:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"Not graded against any limit: \"\n + \", \".join(dict.fromkeys(r.parameter for r in ungraded))\n + \".\"\n )\n if not assessment.evaluated_rows:\n return \"unmet\", \"No result in the sample could be graded.\"\n return \"met\", (\n f\"{plural(len(assessment.evaluated_rows), 'determinand')} graded; verdict \"\n f\"{assessment.verdict_state}.\"\n )\n\n\ndef _water_quality_panel(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n assessment = state.get(\"wq_assessment\")\n if assessment is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No water quality results have been assessed.\"\n if assessment.missing_essential:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"No evaluable result for \"\n + \", \".join(assessment.missing_essential) + \".\"\n )\n return \"met\", \"The health panel was run and every result was evaluable.\"\n\n\ndef _design_derived(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n design = state.get(\"borehole_design\")\n if design is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No borehole design has been derived.\"\n errors = [f for f in (design.flags or []) if f.level == \"error\"]\n if errors:\n return \"unmet\", errors[0].message\n if not design.screens:\n return \"unmet\", \"The design places no screen.\"\n return \"met\", (\n f\"{design.total_screen_length_m:.1f} m of screen in \"\n f\"{plural(len(design.screens), 'run')}.\"\n )\n\n\ndef _no_errors(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"Nothing anywhere raised an error-level flag.\n\n A catch-all, deliberately last: a module that learns to report a new\n fatal condition is covered by the gate the day it does, without this\n file having to be edited.\n \"\"\"\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n sources = [\n state.get(\"drilling_log\"), analysis, state.get(\"wq_assessment\"),\n state.get(\"borehole_design\"), state.get(\"cost_estimate\"),\n ]\n if analysis is not None:\n sources.append(analysis.test)\n errors = [f for f in _flags(*sources) if f.level == \"error\"]\n if errors:\n return \"unmet\", \"; \".join(dict.fromkeys(f.message for f in errors))\n return \"met\", \"No module reported a fatal problem with the data.\"\n\n\ndef _cost_basis(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"A cost estimate exists and is built on a stated depth.\n\n An estimate is a pre-construction document by its own words, so it is\n not held to a drilling log and an as-built design: demanding those\n stamped every budget PROVISIONAL at exactly the time a budget is needed.\n \"\"\"\n estimate = state.get(\"cost_estimate\")\n if estimate is None:\n return \"unmet\", \"No cost estimate has been computed.\"\n depth = getattr(getattr(estimate, \"inputs\", None), \"total_depth_m\", None)\n if not depth:\n return \"unmet\", \"The cost estimate has no total depth to price against.\"\n return \"met\", f\"Estimate priced for a {depth:.0f} m borehole.\"\n\n\ndef _field_data(state: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"The report describes this borehole, not a worked example.\n\n The toolkit ships example datasets and offers them from a picker, which\n is the right thing to do: nobody should have to have drilled a borehole\n to find out what the software does. But the documents it writes from\n them are indistinguishable from the ones it writes from real work - the\n same letterhead, the same tables, the same signature block - and they\n leave the machine that made them as .docx files that get forwarded,\n filed and read years later by somebody who was not there when they were\n generated.\n\n So the fact travels with the document. Two different things make a\n project fail this, and they are not equally serious:\n\n * a source whose readings were **invented**. The Dr Timbo water quality\n workbook is the one in the bundle: no sample was ever taken, and the\n determinand values exist to exercise the assessment. A quality report\n drawn from it states arsenic and coliform results for a sample that\n does not exist.\n * a source **picked from the sample list**, whoever it was transcribed\n from. The Rokel soundings are a real 2015 survey, faithfully copied,\n and the numbers in them are sound - but a report an evaluator\n produces by clicking \"load a sample\" is a survey of Rokel, not of the\n site they are evaluating, and it should not be issuable as one.\n\n This one turns on the ``sample`` marker rather than on the file,\n because it is a fact about the session and not about the data. A\n script that opens the same workbook to publish the worked example\n itself is reporting Rokel as Rokel, and is not caught.\n\n Both are stated rather than blocked, like every other requirement here.\n An override is available and is recorded on the cover, which is the\n right escape hatch for the one case that needs it: someone\n deliberately publishing the worked example itself.\n \"\"\"\n sources = state.get(\"sources\") or {}\n if not isinstance(sources, dict):\n return \"met\", \"No input is a bundled example file.\"\n\n invented, bundled = [], []\n for source in sources.values():\n record = source_provenance(source)\n if record is None:\n continue\n name = os.path.basename(record.file)\n if not record.measured:\n # True of the file however it was opened: nothing was sampled.\n invented.append(name)\n elif isinstance(source, dict) and source.get(\"sample\"):\n # Only when it was *picked from the sample list*. The marker is\n # set by the two apps' pickers and by nothing else, which is the\n # distinction that matters: the Rokel soundings are a real survey,\n # so examples/run_rokel_geophysics.py publishing them under the\n # Rokel name is reporting exactly what it says it is. The same\n # file pulled into somebody else's project is not.\n bundled.append(name)\n\n if invented:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"Readings that were never measured are in this project: \"\n + \", \".join(sorted(dict.fromkeys(invented)))\n + \". The values in \"\n + (\"that file were\" if len(set(invented)) == 1 else \"those files were\")\n + \" invented to demonstrate the toolkit, so no result derived \"\n \"from them describes anything that was sampled.\"\n )\n if bundled:\n return \"unmet\", (\n \"This project is built on the bundled example data (\"\n + \", \".join(sorted(dict.fromkeys(bundled)))\n + \"), which was recorded at another site. The analysis is of \"\n \"that example, not of the borehole named on this report.\"\n )\n return \"met\", \"No input is a bundled example file.\"\n\n\n#: Every requirement, in the order a reader should see them: the borehole\n#: first, then what was measured in it, then what it produced.\nREQUIREMENTS: dict[str, tuple[str, Any]] = {\n # First, because it qualifies every other answer below it: a met\n # requirement established from invented readings is still invented.\n \"field_data\": (\"Field data\", _field_data),\n \"site_located\": (\"Site position\", _site_located),\n \"borehole_logged\": (\"Drilling log\", _borehole_logged),\n # Negative checks: vacuously met when there is nothing to have gone wrong\n # with, which is harmless because the positive requirements beside them\n # (a log, a test, a sample) already catch absence.\n \"readings_usable\": (\"Readable units\", _readings_usable),\n \"pumping_measured\": (\"Pumping test measured\", _pumping_measured),\n \"yield_established\": (\"Yield established\", _yield_established),\n \"water_quality_panel\": (\"Water quality panel\", _water_quality_panel),\n \"water_quality_evaluable\": (\"Water quality evaluable\", _water_quality_evaluable),\n \"design_derived\": (\"Borehole design\", _design_derived),\n \"cost_basis\": (\"Cost estimate\", _cost_basis),\n \"no_errors\": (\"No fatal data problems\", _no_errors),\n}\n\n#: What each report has to be able to stand behind. A pumping report makes\n#: no claim about water quality, so an unassessed sample does not hold it\n#: back; a handover report tells a village the water is safe to drink, so it\n#: needs everything.\nREPORTS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n \"completion\": (\n \"field_data\",\n \"site_located\", \"borehole_logged\", \"readings_usable\",\n \"pumping_measured\", \"yield_established\", \"water_quality_panel\",\n \"water_quality_evaluable\", \"design_derived\", \"no_errors\",\n ),\n \"handover\": (\n \"field_data\",\n \"site_located\", \"borehole_logged\", \"pumping_measured\",\n \"yield_established\", \"water_quality_panel\", \"water_quality_evaluable\",\n \"no_errors\",\n ),\n \"quality\": (\n \"field_data\",\n \"site_located\", \"water_quality_panel\", \"water_quality_evaluable\",\n \"no_errors\",\n ),\n \"pumping\": (\n \"field_data\",\n \"site_located\", \"readings_usable\", \"pumping_measured\",\n \"yield_established\", \"no_errors\",\n ),\n \"geophysical\": (\"field_data\", \"site_located\"),\n # An estimate is priced before anything is drilled, so it is judged on\n # its own inputs, not on a log and an as-built design it cannot have.\n \"costing\": (\"field_data\", \"site_located\", \"cost_basis\", \"no_errors\"),\n \"supervision\": (\"field_data\", \"site_located\"),\n # The asset documents and the payment certificate. Without an entry each\n # of these fell back to the completion set, so a plate for the headworks\n # was stamped PROVISIONAL for want of a water quality panel - which a\n # plate makes no claim about. What a plate does claim is that the\n # identifier on it leads back to this borehole, and that identifier is\n # minted from the position, so the position is the requirement.\n \"placard\": (\"field_data\", \"site_located\"),\n \"asset\": (\"field_data\", \"site_located\"),\n # A certificate is a claim that work was done at a place and is worth\n # paying for. It makes no claim about the water.\n \"procurement\": (\"field_data\", \"site_located\", \"no_errors\"),\n}\n\n\ndef assess_readiness(\n state: dict,\n report: str = \"completion\",\n overrides: Optional[dict] = None,\n) -> Readiness:\n \"\"\"Judge one project against what one kind of report has to stand behind.\n\n ``state`` is keyed as the app's session is - ``site``, ``drilling_log``,\n ``pump_analysis``, ``wq_assessment``, ``borehole_design``,\n ``cost_estimate`` - so the app can pass its session straight in and a\n test can pass a dict.\n\n ``overrides`` maps a requirement key to ``{\"reason\": ..., \"by\": ...}``\n (a bare string is taken as the reason). An override is recorded on the\n requirement and reproduced on the report, and never makes the project\n certifiable - only issuable.\n \"\"\"\n overrides = overrides or {}\n keys = REPORTS.get(report, REPORTS[\"completion\"])\n requirements: list[Requirement] = []\n\n for key in keys:\n title, check = REQUIREMENTS[key]\n try:\n found, detail = check(state)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - a broken check is not a pass\n found, detail = \"unmet\", (\n f\"The {title.lower()} check could not run: \"\n f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\"\n )\n override = overrides.get(key)\n if found == \"unmet\" and override:\n reason = override.get(\"reason\", \"\") if isinstance(override, dict) else str(override)\n by = override.get(\"by\", \"\") if isinstance(override, dict) else \"\"\n requirements.append(Requirement(\n key=key, title=title, state=\"overridden\", detail=detail,\n override_reason=reason, override_by=by,\n ))\n continue\n requirements.append(\n Requirement(key=key, title=title, state=found, detail=detail)\n )\n\n try:\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n sources = [\n state.get(\"drilling_log\"), analysis, state.get(\"wq_assessment\"),\n state.get(\"borehole_design\"),\n ]\n if analysis is not None:\n sources.append(analysis.test)\n assumptions = list(dict.fromkeys(\n f.message for f in _has(_flags(*sources), _UNIT_ASSUMPTIONS)\n ))\n except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a malformed object costs the list, not the gate\n assumptions = []\n\n # A bundled file whose measurements are real but whose blank columns were\n # filled in illustratively. Not blocking - the readings are somebody's\n # real readings - but the reader should know which column is which.\n try:\n for source in (state.get(\"sources\") or {}).values():\n record = source_provenance(source)\n if record is not None and record.kind == \"reconstructed\":\n assumptions.append(\n f\"{os.path.basename(record.file)}: {record.note}\")\n assumptions = list(dict.fromkeys(assumptions))\n except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - as above\n pass\n\n return Readiness(report=report, requirements=requirements,\n assumptions=assumptions)\n"}, "groundwater/recompute.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Recompute analysis objects from the data sources saved in a project.\n\nThe web app stores the raw uploaded data files (or a reference to a bundled\nsample) in the project file, plus the few extra inputs an analysis needs\nthat are not in the file itself (pumping-test step discharges and the\nborehole-design static water level). On load, this module rebuilds the\nresult objects so the reports can be regenerated without re-uploading.\n\nA rebuild that fails is *reported*, not swallowed. It used to be: four bare\n``except Exception: pass`` blocks turned a failed rebuild into an absent\ndictionary key, and every consumer reads an absent key as \"the user never\nsupplied that data\". So a project whose water-quality workbook no longer\nparsed came back looking like a borehole nobody had ever sampled - the\noverview showed the stage as not started, the portfolio summary carried no\nverdict, and the handover report was written without a water-quality\nsection. Nothing anywhere said a file had failed to load.\n\nFailures are still contained - one bad source must not cost the other three\n- but each one now produces a :class:`RecomputeIssue` naming what failed,\nwhich file it was, and what to do about it.\n\nPure and Streamlit-free, so the round trip is unit-testable.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport os\nfrom dataclasses import asdict, dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .config import Config\nfrom .design import design_borehole\nfrom .hydraulics import analyse_pumping_test\nfrom .ingestion import (\n read_drilling_workbook,\n read_pumping_docx,\n read_pumping_workbook,\n read_quality_workbook,\n read_ves_workbook,\n)\nfrom .quality import assess_sample\nfrom .ves import interpret_model, invert_sounding\nfrom .ves.interpret import rank_interpretations\n\n_log = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n#: The session key each upload key produces. An issue names it even when the\n#: file could not be opened at all: the key really is absent, and a banner\n#: that cannot say which result is missing can never be cleared when the\n#: analyst supplies it by hand.\nSOURCE_RESULTS = {\n \"ves\": \"ves_results\",\n \"wiz_ves\": \"ves_results\",\n \"pump\": \"pump_analysis\",\n \"wq\": \"wq_assessment\",\n \"log\": \"drilling_log\",\n}\n\n#: What each upload key is called in front of a user.\nSOURCE_LABELS = {\n \"ves\": \"Geophysics (VES)\",\n \"wiz_ves\": \"Geophysics (VES)\",\n \"pump\": \"Pumping test\",\n \"wq\": \"Water quality\",\n \"log\": \"Drilling log\",\n}\n\n#: Why a source did not produce its result.\nISSUE_CODES = {\n \"bad_payload\": \"the saved file content could not be read\",\n \"unreadable_file\": \"the saved file could not be written to disk\",\n \"missing_sample\": \"the bundled sample it refers to is no longer present\",\n \"outside_sample_root\": \"it refers to a file outside the sample directory\",\n \"parse_error\": \"the workbook could not be parsed\",\n \"analysis_error\": \"the data parsed but the analysis failed\",\n \"sounding_failed\": \"one sounding could not be inverted\",\n \"recompute_crashed\": \"the rebuild itself failed\",\n}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass RecomputeIssue:\n \"\"\"One saved source that did not produce its result.\"\"\"\n\n source: str # upload key: \"ves\" | \"wiz_ves\" | \"pump\" | \"wq\" | \"log\"\n result: str # the session key now absent, \"\" for a partial failure\n label: str # what the user calls it: \"Water quality\"\n level: str # \"error\" (no result at all) | \"warning\" (partial result)\n code: str # a key of ISSUE_CODES\n message: str # one plain, actionable sentence\n context: str = \"\" # the file name or sample path the user recognises\n detail: str = \"\" # \"ValueError: ...\", truncated\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:\n return asdict(self)\n\n\ndef _issue(source, result, code, message, context=\"\", exc=None, level=\"error\"):\n detail = \"\"\n if exc is not None:\n detail = f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\"[:300]\n return RecomputeIssue(\n source=source,\n result=result,\n label=SOURCE_LABELS.get(source, source),\n level=level,\n code=code,\n message=message,\n context=context,\n detail=detail,\n )\n\n\ndef _source_name(source) -> str:\n if not isinstance(source, dict):\n return \"\"\n return str(source.get(\"name\") or source.get(\"sample\") or \"\")\n\n\ndef _materialize(source, sample_root, tmp_dir) -> tuple[Path | None, str]:\n \"\"\"Turn a saved source into a readable file path.\n\n Never raises. Returns ``(path, \"\")`` on success or ``(None, code)`` with\n a code from :data:`ISSUE_CODES`, so the caller can say which of several\n quite different failures happened rather than reporting them all as an\n absent file.\n \"\"\"\n if not isinstance(source, dict):\n return None, \"bad_payload\"\n if source.get(\"bytes\") is not None:\n try:\n # basename only, so a hand-edited project cannot write outside tmp_dir\n name = os.path.basename(str(source.get(\"name\") or \"data\")) or \"data\"\n path = Path(tmp_dir) / name\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n path.write_bytes(bytes(source[\"bytes\"]))\n return path, \"\"\n except OSError:\n return None, \"unreadable_file\"\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n # a str or out-of-range payload from a hand-edited project file;\n # this used to escape the function entirely and abort the whole load\n return None, \"bad_payload\"\n if source.get(\"sample\") and sample_root is not None:\n try:\n root = Path(sample_root).resolve()\n candidate = (root / str(source[\"sample\"])).resolve()\n except OSError:\n return None, \"unreadable_file\"\n if not candidate.is_relative_to(root):\n return None, \"outside_sample_root\"\n if not candidate.exists():\n return None, \"missing_sample\"\n return candidate, \"\"\n return None, \"bad_payload\"\n\n\ndef recompute_results(\n sources: dict,\n discharges: dict | None = None,\n design_swl: float | None = None,\n config: Config | None = None,\n sample_root=None,\n tmp_dir=\".\",\n) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Rebuild the analysis objects a saved project needs.\n\n ``sources`` maps an upload key (``ves``/``wiz_ves``/``pump``/``wq``/``log``)\n to a source dict. Returns session updates keyed like the app's session\n state (``ves_results``, ``pump_analysis``, ``wq_assessment``,\n ``borehole_design``, ``drilling_log``), plus ``recompute_diagnostics``\n - always present - carrying ``{\"ok\": [...], \"issues\": [...]}``. A source\n that fails is skipped and recorded; it never aborts the others.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or Config()\n discharges = discharges or {}\n out: dict = {}\n issues: list[RecomputeIssue] = []\n ok: list[str] = []\n\n def _path(key) -> Path | None:\n \"\"\"Resolve one source, recording why if it cannot be resolved.\"\"\"\n source = sources.get(key)\n if not source:\n return None\n path, code = _materialize(source, sample_root, tmp_dir)\n if path is None:\n issues.append(_issue(\n key, SOURCE_RESULTS.get(key, \"\"), code,\n f\"{SOURCE_LABELS.get(key, key)}: the saved file could not be \"\n f\"opened because {ISSUE_CODES[code]}. Upload it again.\",\n context=_source_name(source),\n ))\n return path\n\n # VES: the main tab wins over the guided-wizard upload\n ves_key = \"ves\" if sources.get(\"ves\") else \"wiz_ves\"\n ves_path = _path(\"ves\") or _path(\"wiz_ves\")\n if ves_path is not None:\n try:\n soundings = read_ves_workbook(ves_path)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - reported, not swallowed\n _log.exception(\"VES workbook could not be parsed\")\n soundings = None\n issues.append(_issue(\n ves_key, \"ves_results\", \"parse_error\",\n \"The geophysics workbook could not be read, so the soundings \"\n \"were not restored. Open it and check the layout, or upload it \"\n \"again.\",\n context=ves_path.name, exc=exc,\n ))\n if soundings:\n kept, results, interps = [], [], []\n # Per sounding, so one bad curve costs one curve rather than the\n # whole survey.\n for sounding in soundings:\n try:\n result = invert_sounding(sounding, config.ves)\n interps.append(interpret_model(sounding, result.model, config.ves))\n results.append(result)\n kept.append(sounding)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001\n _log.exception(\"sounding %s could not be inverted\", sounding.label)\n issues.append(_issue(\n ves_key, \"\", \"sounding_failed\",\n f\"Sounding {sounding.label} could not be inverted and \"\n \"was left out; the other soundings were restored.\",\n context=sounding.label, exc=exc, level=\"warning\",\n ))\n if kept:\n # rank now: the dashboard reads interp.rank, and an unranked\n # set leaves every rank None so \"best\" silently becomes\n # \"first parsed\"\n rank_interpretations(interps)\n out[\"ves_results\"] = (kept, results, interps)\n ok.append(ves_key)\n else:\n issues.append(_issue(\n ves_key, \"ves_results\", \"analysis_error\",\n \"No sounding in the geophysics workbook could be inverted, \"\n \"so there are no VES results to show.\",\n context=ves_path.name,\n ))\n\n pump_path = _path(\"pump\")\n if pump_path is not None:\n try:\n reader = (\n read_pumping_docx\n if pump_path.suffix.lower() == \".docx\"\n else read_pumping_workbook\n )\n test = reader(pump_path)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001\n _log.exception(\"pumping test could not be parsed\")\n test = None\n issues.append(_issue(\n \"pump\", \"pump_analysis\", \"parse_error\",\n \"The pumping test sheet could not be read, so the drawdown and \"\n \"yield results were not restored.\",\n context=pump_path.name, exc=exc,\n ))\n if test is not None:\n try:\n for step in test.steps:\n q = discharges.get(str(step.step_number))\n if q:\n step.discharge_m3_per_h = float(q)\n out[\"pump_analysis\"] = analyse_pumping_test(test, config.pumping)\n ok.append(\"pump\")\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001\n _log.exception(\"pumping test could not be analysed\")\n issues.append(_issue(\n \"pump\", \"pump_analysis\", \"analysis_error\",\n \"The pumping test sheet was read but the analysis failed, \"\n \"so there is no transmissivity or yield recommendation.\",\n context=pump_path.name, exc=exc,\n ))\n\n wq_path = _path(\"wq\")\n if wq_path is not None:\n try:\n sample = read_quality_workbook(wq_path)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001\n _log.exception(\"water quality workbook could not be parsed\")\n sample = None\n issues.append(_issue(\n \"wq\", \"wq_assessment\", \"parse_error\",\n \"The water quality workbook could not be read, so no \"\n \"suitability verdict was restored. Do not treat the absence of \"\n \"a verdict as a pass.\",\n context=wq_path.name, exc=exc,\n ))\n if sample is not None:\n try:\n out[\"wq_assessment\"] = assess_sample(sample)\n ok.append(\"wq\")\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001\n _log.exception(\"water quality sample could not be assessed\")\n issues.append(_issue(\n \"wq\", \"wq_assessment\", \"analysis_error\",\n \"The laboratory results were read but could not be assessed \"\n \"against the standards, so there is no verdict. Do not \"\n \"treat the absence of a verdict as a pass.\",\n context=wq_path.name, exc=exc,\n ))\n\n log_path = _path(\"log\")\n if log_path is not None:\n try:\n log = read_drilling_workbook(log_path)\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001\n _log.exception(\"drilling log could not be parsed\")\n log = None\n issues.append(_issue(\n \"log\", \"drilling_log\", \"parse_error\",\n \"The drilling log could not be read, so the lithology and the \"\n \"borehole design were not restored.\",\n context=log_path.name, exc=exc,\n ))\n if log is not None:\n out[\"drilling_log\"] = log\n ok.append(\"log\")\n try:\n out[\"borehole_design\"] = design_borehole(\n log=log,\n static_water_level_m=design_swl or None,\n rules=config.design,\n )\n except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001\n _log.exception(\"borehole design could not be derived\")\n issues.append(_issue(\n \"log\", \"borehole_design\", \"analysis_error\",\n \"The drilling log was read but the borehole design could \"\n \"not be derived from it, so the screen layout and the bill \"\n \"of quantities are missing.\",\n context=log_path.name, exc=exc, level=\"warning\",\n ))\n\n # Always present, so loading a second project clears the first one's\n # banner rather than leaving a stale one on screen.\n out[\"recompute_diagnostics\"] = {\n \"ok\": ok,\n \"issues\": [issue.as_dict() for issue in issues],\n }\n return out\n"}, "groundwater/registry.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"The borehole as an asset, not as a project.\n\nA drilling project ends. The borehole does not: it is pumped every day for\ntwenty years by people who were not there when it was drilled, and the\nquestion that matters after handover is not \"what did the pumping test say\"\nbut \"is it working, when was it last looked at, and when was the water last\ntested\". The completion report cannot answer that, because it was written\nonce and never touched again.\n\nSo this module holds the other half. An asset has a stable identifier that\nsurvives the project file, a position, and an append-only stream of events -\ncommissioned, inspected, sampled, broken down, repaired, abandoned. From\nthat stream it derives what is true today: whether the point is working,\nhow long it has been out, and what is now overdue.\n\nThree things shape the design.\n\n**Offline first.** Field updates are recorded on a phone at the wellhead\nwith no signal, often by two people who each write the visit down. Events\nare therefore identified by their content rather than by a counter, so the\nsame visit recorded twice merges into one, and a merge is a set union that\nneeds no server to arbitrate it.\n\n**Append-only.** A maintenance record that can be edited is a maintenance\nrecord nobody can rely on. A mistake is corrected by recording the\ncorrection, which leaves both in the history where an auditor can see them.\n\n**Nothing is assumed working.** An asset with no events is ``unknown``, not\n``functional``. A failure with no recorded repair stays a failure. The\ncommon way an asset register becomes useless is that absence of bad news\ngets read as good news, and after two years everything is green.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom datetime import date, timedelta\n\nfrom .geo import infer_zone_for_sierra_leone, utm_to_geographic\n\n__all__ = [\n \"Asset\",\n \"AssetEvent\",\n \"AssetState\",\n \"DISTRICT_CODES\",\n \"EVENT_KINDS\",\n \"FUNCTION_LABELS\",\n \"Schedule\",\n \"asset_from_project\",\n \"asset_state\",\n \"check_character\",\n \"event_id\",\n \"format_asset_id\",\n \"merge_events\",\n \"mint_asset_id\",\n \"parse_asset_id\",\n \"placard_lines\",\n \"qr_payload\",\n \"registry_rows\",\n \"registry_stats\",\n \"validate_asset_id\",\n]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The identifier\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Crockford's base 32: no I, L, O or U, so nothing in a code can be confused\n#: with 1, 0 or V when it is read off a plate or repeated over a radio.\n_ALPHABET = \"0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ\"\n\n#: What a reader who writes I, L, O or U anyway almost certainly meant.\n_FOLD = {\"I\": \"1\", \"L\": \"1\", \"O\": \"0\", \"U\": \"V\"}\n\n#: The check character is ISO 7064 MOD 37,36, whose alphabet is the full 36.\n_CHECK_ALPHABET = \"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ\"\n\n#: District codes. Written out rather than derived, for the same reason the\n#: site statuses are: a rule that produces \"BO\" for Bo and \"BOM\" for Bombali\n#: today produces a collision the first time a district is renamed, and a\n#: collision here means two boreholes with one identifier.\nDISTRICT_CODES = {\n \"western area urban\": \"WAU\",\n \"western area rural\": \"WAR\",\n \"port loko\": \"PL\",\n \"kambia\": \"KAM\",\n \"karene\": \"KAR\",\n \"bombali\": \"BOM\",\n \"falaba\": \"FAL\",\n \"koinadugu\": \"KOI\",\n \"tonkolili\": \"TON\",\n \"kono\": \"KON\",\n \"kenema\": \"KEN\",\n \"kailahun\": \"KAI\",\n \"bo\": \"BO\",\n \"bonthe\": \"BON\",\n \"moyamba\": \"MOY\",\n \"pujehun\": \"PUJ\",\n}\n\n#: A district nobody could match. Deliberately not a guess: an identifier\n#: that says XX is one somebody can fix, and it still locates the borehole.\nUNKNOWN_DISTRICT = \"XX\"\n\n#: Positions are quantised to this before they go into the identifier.\nPOSITION_STEP_M = 10\n\n_ID_RE = re.compile(r\"^SL-([A-Z]{2,4})-([0-9A-Z]{7})-([0-9A-Z])$\")\n\n\ndef check_character(body: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"ISO 7064 MOD 37,36 over ``body``, ignoring separators.\n\n Chosen over a simpler weighted sum because it detects every single\n wrong character and every transposition of two adjacent ones - which\n between them are almost all the mistakes people make copying a code off\n a headworks plate into a phone.\n \"\"\"\n product = 36\n for char in body.upper():\n value = _CHECK_ALPHABET.find(char)\n if value < 0:\n continue # separators and spaces carry no value\n total = (product % 37) + value\n product = 2 * (total % 37 or 37)\n return _CHECK_ALPHABET[(37 - product % 37) % 36]\n\n\ndef _position_code(easting: float, northing: float, zone: int) -> str:\n \"\"\"Seven characters holding the position to the nearest ten metres.\n\n Derived rather than allocated, because there is no server to allocate\n from: two teams standing at the same wellhead with no connection between\n them have to arrive at the same identifier.\n \"\"\"\n east = int(round(float(easting) / POSITION_STEP_M))\n north = int(round(float(northing) / POSITION_STEP_M))\n if not 0 <= east < 1 << 17 or not 0 <= north < 1 << 17:\n raise ValueError(\n f\"({easting}, {northing}) is not a position inside Sierra Leone; \"\n \"an identifier minted from it would not be findable\"\n )\n value = ((1 if int(zone) == 29 else 0) << 34) | (east << 17) | north\n return \"\".join(_ALPHABET[(value >> shift) & 31]\n for shift in range(30, -1, -5))\n\n\ndef _district_code(district: str) -> str:\n return DISTRICT_CODES.get(str(district or \"\").strip().lower(),\n UNKNOWN_DISTRICT)\n\n\ndef format_asset_id(district_code: str, position_code: str) -> str:\n body = f\"SL-{district_code}-{position_code}\"\n return f\"{body}-{check_character(body)}\"\n\n\ndef mint_asset_id(site) -> str:\n \"\"\"The identifier for a borehole at ``site``.\n\n Minted once, at commissioning, and carried from then on. A later GPS fix\n a few metres off the first one produces a different code, which is why\n the registry matches on the recorded identifier first and on proximity\n only as a fallback - the derivation is how the first identifier is made\n and how a lost one is reconstructed, not something to re-run each visit.\n \"\"\"\n easting = getattr(site, \"easting\", None)\n northing = getattr(site, \"northing\", None)\n if easting is None or northing is None:\n raise ValueError(\n \"a borehole with no recorded position cannot be given an \"\n \"identifier: there would be nothing to find it by\"\n )\n zone = getattr(site, \"utm_zone\", None) or infer_zone_for_sierra_leone(\n float(easting))\n return format_asset_id(_district_code(getattr(site, \"district\", \"\")),\n _position_code(easting, northing, zone))\n\n\ndef parse_asset_id(text: str) -> str | None:\n \"\"\"Normalise a hand-entered identifier, or ``None`` if it is not one.\n\n Case, spacing and the four Crockford confusions (I and L for 1, O for 0,\n U for V) are forgiven in the position code, because they are reading\n mistakes rather than different codes. A failing check character is not\n forgiven: that is a wrong identifier, and a wrong identifier attaches a\n maintenance history to somebody else's borehole.\n \"\"\"\n raw = re.sub(r\"[\\s_]+\", \"\", str(text or \"\")).upper().replace(\"\u2013\", \"-\")\n if not raw:\n return None\n if not raw.startswith(\"SL-\"):\n raw = \"SL-\" + raw\n parts = raw.split(\"-\")\n if len(parts) != 4:\n return None\n _, district, code, given = parts\n # The position code is written in the 32-character Crockford alphabet,\n # which has no I, L, O or U, so folding them there is unambiguous. The\n # check character is drawn from the full 36, where those four mean\n # themselves - folding it rejected one identifier in nine that mint()\n # had just produced.\n code = \"\".join(_FOLD.get(c, c) for c in code)\n candidate = f\"SL-{district}-{code}-{given}\"\n if not _ID_RE.match(candidate):\n return None\n if check_character(f\"SL-{district}-{code}\") != given:\n return None\n return candidate\n\n\ndef validate_asset_id(text: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n \"\"\"``(ok, reason)`` - the reason is written to be shown to the person typing.\"\"\"\n raw = str(text or \"\").strip()\n if not raw:\n return False, \"No identifier was entered.\"\n parsed = parse_asset_id(raw)\n if parsed:\n return True, \"\"\n tidy = re.sub(r\"[\\s_]+\", \"\", raw.upper())\n if not tidy.startswith(\"SL-\"):\n tidy = \"SL-\" + tidy\n parts = tidy.split(\"-\")\n if len(parts) != 4:\n return False, (\"An identifier looks like SL-WAR-8T4KQ2A-7: country, \"\n \"district, position, check character.\")\n _, district, code, given = parts\n code = \"\".join(_FOLD.get(c, c) for c in code)\n if not re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9A-Z]{7}\", code):\n return False, \"The position part should be seven letters or digits.\"\n expected = check_character(f\"SL-{district}-{code}\")\n return False, (\n f\"The check character does not match: this identifier should end in \"\n f\"{expected}, not {given}. Something in it has been mistyped.\")\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Events\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: kind -> (label, what it establishes about function, is it a service visit)\nEVENT_KINDS = {\n \"commissioned\": (\"Commissioned\", \"functional\", False),\n \"inspection\": (\"Sanitary inspection\", None, True),\n \"water_sample\": (\"Water sampled\", None, False),\n \"repair\": (\"Repair\", \"functional\", True),\n \"failure\": (\"Failure\", \"non_functional\", True),\n \"restored\": (\"Returned to service\", \"functional\", True),\n \"decommissioned\": (\"Decommissioned\", \"decommissioned\", False),\n \"note\": (\"Note\", None, False),\n}\n\nFUNCTION_LABELS = {\n \"functional\": \"Working\",\n \"non_functional\": \"Not working\",\n \"decommissioned\": \"Decommissioned\",\n \"unknown\": \"Not known\",\n}\n\n\ndef _hash32(text: str) -> int:\n \"\"\"FNV-1a. Small, deterministic, and the same four lines in any language.\n\n The bytes hashed are the low byte of each UTF-16 code unit, because that\n is what the browser app's ``charCodeAt(i) & 0xFF`` sees. Iterating code\n points instead agrees for everything on the Basic Multilingual Plane and\n diverges on an emoji, and a note with a thumbs-up then carried a\n different identifier on the phone and in the office copy, so the same\n visit no longer merged into one.\n \"\"\"\n value = 0x811C9DC5\n for low in text.encode(\"utf-16-le\")[::2]:\n value = ((value ^ low) * 0x01000193) & 0xFFFFFFFF\n return value\n\n\ndef event_id(asset_id: str, when: str, kind: str, note: str = \"\",\n by: str = \"\") -> str:\n \"\"\"A content-derived identifier, so recording a visit twice merges to one.\n\n Two people at the same wellhead writing down the same repair on the same\n day produce the same event, and a union of their phones has one entry\n rather than two. The cost is that two genuinely separate events with\n identical wording on the same day also collapse - which is the right way\n round: a duplicated record is a lie about how much maintenance happened.\n \"\"\"\n digest = _hash32(f\"{asset_id}|{when}|{kind}|{note.strip()}|{by.strip()}\")\n tail = \"\".join(_ALPHABET[(digest >> shift) & 31] for shift in (15, 10, 5, 0))\n return f\"{when}/{kind}/{tail}\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass AssetEvent:\n \"\"\"One thing that happened to a borehole.\"\"\"\n\n when: str # ISO date; kept as written so a bad one is visible\n kind: str\n note: str = \"\"\n by: str = \"\"\n photo: str = \"\" # a data URL or a path; opaque here\n event_id: str = \"\"\n\n def identified_for(self, asset_id: str) -> \"AssetEvent\":\n \"\"\"A copy carrying its content-derived id.\"\"\"\n return AssetEvent(\n when=self.when, kind=self.kind, note=self.note, by=self.by,\n photo=self.photo,\n event_id=self.event_id or event_id(asset_id, self.when, self.kind,\n self.note, self.by),\n )\n\n @property\n def label(self) -> str:\n return EVENT_KINDS.get(self.kind, (\"Other\", None, False))[0]\n\n @property\n def date(self) -> date | None:\n \"\"\"The date, or ``None`` when it cannot be read.\n\n An event whose date is unreadable is kept - throwing away a\n maintenance record because of a typo is worse - but it can never\n establish when anything last happened.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n return date.fromisoformat(str(self.when).strip())\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n return None\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n return {\"when\": self.when, \"kind\": self.kind, \"note\": self.note,\n \"by\": self.by, \"photo\": self.photo, \"event_id\": self.event_id}\n\n\ndef _coerce_event(raw) -> AssetEvent | None:\n if isinstance(raw, AssetEvent):\n return raw\n if not isinstance(raw, dict):\n return None\n kind = str(raw.get(\"kind\") or \"\").strip()\n if kind not in EVENT_KINDS:\n kind = \"note\"\n return AssetEvent(\n when=str(raw.get(\"when\") or \"\").strip(), kind=kind,\n note=str(raw.get(\"note\") or \"\"), by=str(raw.get(\"by\") or \"\"),\n photo=str(raw.get(\"photo\") or \"\"),\n event_id=str(raw.get(\"event_id\") or \"\"),\n )\n\n\ndef merge_events(asset_id: str, *streams) -> list[AssetEvent]:\n \"\"\"Union of several event streams, in date order.\n\n This is the whole offline story. Two phones that have been out of touch\n for a fortnight each hold part of the history; merging them is a set\n union over content-derived identifiers, so it needs no clock agreement,\n no server and no conflict resolution. Merging is commutative and\n idempotent: order does not matter and doing it twice changes nothing.\n \"\"\"\n merged: dict[str, AssetEvent] = {}\n for stream in streams:\n for raw in stream or []:\n event = _coerce_event(raw)\n if event is None:\n continue\n event = event.identified_for(asset_id)\n existing = merged.get(event.event_id)\n if existing is None:\n merged[event.event_id] = event\n elif not existing.photo and event.photo:\n # the only asymmetry: a phone that has the photograph wins,\n # because the alternative is losing it\n merged[event.event_id] = event\n return sorted(merged.values(),\n key=lambda e: (e.when or \"9999\", e.kind, e.event_id))\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The asset\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass Asset:\n \"\"\"A borehole, as the people who maintain it see it.\"\"\"\n\n asset_id: str\n community: str = \"\"\n district: str = \"\"\n chiefdom: str = \"\"\n easting: float | None = None\n northing: float | None = None\n utm_zone: int | None = None\n total_depth_m: float | None = None\n safe_yield_m3_per_h: float | None = None\n pump_type: str = \"\"\n installed_by: str = \"\"\n events: list[AssetEvent] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n @property\n def latlon(self) -> tuple[float, float] | None:\n if self.easting is None or self.northing is None:\n return None\n zone = self.utm_zone or infer_zone_for_sierra_leone(float(self.easting))\n try:\n return utm_to_geographic(float(self.easting), float(self.northing),\n int(zone))\n except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a bad coordinate simply has no fix\n return None\n\n @property\n def label(self) -> str:\n place = self.community or \"(unnamed site)\"\n return f\"{place} ({self.district})\" if self.district else place\n\n def with_events(self, *streams) -> \"Asset\":\n \"\"\"A copy carrying the merged union of this asset's events and more.\"\"\"\n return Asset(**{**self.__dict__,\n \"events\": merge_events(self.asset_id, self.events,\n *streams)})\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n payload = {k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() if k != \"events\"}\n payload[\"events\"] = [e.identified_for(self.asset_id).as_dict()\n for e in self.events]\n return payload\n\n\ndef asset_from_dict(payload: dict) -> Asset | None:\n \"\"\"Rebuild an asset from a saved project file, or ``None`` if it is not one.\"\"\"\n if not isinstance(payload, dict):\n return None\n asset_id = parse_asset_id(payload.get(\"asset_id\"))\n if not asset_id:\n return None\n known = {f for f in Asset.__dataclass_fields__ if f != \"events\"}\n fields = {k: v for k, v in payload.items() if k in known}\n fields[\"asset_id\"] = asset_id\n asset = Asset(**fields)\n asset.events = merge_events(asset_id, payload.get(\"events\") or [])\n return asset\n\n\ndef asset_from_project(state: dict) -> Asset | None:\n \"\"\"Draft an asset from an assembled project, or ``None`` without a position.\n\n Nothing is invented: the commissioning event is not written here, because\n a borehole is commissioned by somebody deciding it is, on a day, and that\n decision is a record with a name on it rather than a side effect of\n opening a page.\n \"\"\"\n site = _project_site(state)\n if site is None:\n return None\n try:\n asset_id = mint_asset_id(site)\n except ValueError:\n return None\n log = state.get(\"drilling_log\")\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n depth = getattr(log, \"total_depth_m\", None) if log is not None else None\n recommendation = getattr(analysis, \"yield_recommendation\", None)\n return Asset(\n asset_id=asset_id,\n community=getattr(site, \"community\", \"\") or \"\",\n district=getattr(site, \"district\", \"\") or \"\",\n chiefdom=getattr(site, \"chiefdom\", \"\") or \"\",\n easting=getattr(site, \"easting\", None),\n northing=getattr(site, \"northing\", None),\n utm_zone=getattr(site, \"utm_zone\", None),\n total_depth_m=depth,\n safe_yield_m3_per_h=getattr(recommendation, \"safe_yield_m3_per_h\", None),\n installed_by=getattr(site, \"contractor\", \"\") or \"\",\n )\n\n\ndef _project_site(state: dict):\n \"\"\"The site metadata, merged across the sheets that carry any of it.\"\"\"\n candidates = [state.get(\"site\")]\n log = state.get(\"drilling_log\")\n if log is not None:\n candidates.append(getattr(log, \"site\", None))\n analysis = state.get(\"pump_analysis\")\n if analysis is not None:\n candidates.append(getattr(getattr(analysis, \"test\", None), \"site\", None))\n assessment = state.get(\"wq_assessment\")\n if assessment is not None:\n candidates.append(getattr(getattr(assessment, \"sample\", None), \"site\",\n None))\n merged = None\n for site in candidates:\n if site is None:\n continue\n if merged is None:\n merged = site\n continue\n try:\n merged = merged.merged_with(site)\n except AttributeError: # noqa: PERF203 - a plain object is fine as-is\n continue\n if merged is None:\n return None\n return merged if getattr(merged, \"easting\", None) is not None else None\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# What is true today\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schedule:\n \"\"\"How often a working point should be visited.\n\n These are defaults, not a standard. Surveillance intervals for rural\n point sources are set by the programme and by the district, and vary\n with how many people drink from the point and what the last result said;\n a six-monthly sanitary inspection and an annual water sample is a common\n baseline to start from and to argue with. Change them here and every\n due-date in the registry moves with them.\n \"\"\"\n\n inspection_months: int = 6\n water_sample_months: int = 12\n #: How long past due before an item stops being \"due\" and starts being\n #: \"overdue\". A visit is a journey, not a diary entry.\n grace_days: int = 30\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass DueItem:\n key: str\n title: str\n due_on: date | None\n state: str # \"due\" | \"overdue\" | \"unknown\"\n detail: str\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n return {\"key\": self.key, \"title\": self.title, \"state\": self.state,\n \"due_on\": self.due_on.isoformat() if self.due_on else None,\n \"detail\": self.detail}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass AssetState:\n \"\"\"What the event stream says about the borehole now.\"\"\"\n\n function: str\n since: date | None\n detail: str\n last_inspection: date | None\n last_sample: date | None\n commissioned: date | None\n days_out_of_service: int | None\n due: tuple[DueItem, ...]\n undated_events: int\n\n @property\n def label(self) -> str:\n return FUNCTION_LABELS.get(self.function, \"Not known\")\n\n @property\n def is_working(self) -> bool:\n \"\"\"True only when something says so. ``unknown`` is not a yes.\"\"\"\n return self.function == \"functional\"\n\n @property\n def overdue(self) -> tuple[DueItem, ...]:\n return tuple(item for item in self.due if item.state == \"overdue\")\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n return {\n \"function\": self.function, \"label\": self.label,\n \"since\": self.since.isoformat() if self.since else None,\n \"detail\": self.detail,\n \"last_inspection\": self.last_inspection.isoformat()\n if self.last_inspection else None,\n \"last_sample\": self.last_sample.isoformat()\n if self.last_sample else None,\n \"commissioned\": self.commissioned.isoformat()\n if self.commissioned else None,\n \"days_out_of_service\": self.days_out_of_service,\n \"due\": [item.as_dict() for item in self.due],\n \"undated_events\": self.undated_events,\n }\n\n\ndef _add_months(start: date, months: int) -> date:\n month = start.month - 1 + months\n year = start.year + month // 12\n month = month % 12 + 1\n # clamp rather than roll over: six months from 31 August is 28 February,\n # not 3 March, and a due date that drifts forward is one that gets missed\n day = min(start.day, [31, 29 if year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 or not\n year % 400) else 28,\n 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31][month - 1])\n return date(year, month, day)\n\n\ndef asset_state(asset: Asset, today: date | None = None,\n schedule: Schedule | None = None) -> AssetState:\n \"\"\"Reduce the event stream to the borehole's condition on ``today``.\"\"\"\n today = today or date.today()\n schedule = schedule or Schedule()\n events = merge_events(asset.asset_id, asset.events)\n dated = [(e.date, e) for e in events if e.date is not None]\n dated.sort(key=lambda pair: (pair[0], pair[1].kind, pair[1].event_id))\n undated = sum(1 for e in events if e.date is None)\n\n function, since, detail = \"unknown\", None, (\n \"Nothing has been recorded against this borehole, so whether it is \"\n \"working is not known.\")\n commissioned = last_inspection = last_sample = None\n for when, event in dated:\n if when > today:\n continue # a record dated in the future settles nothing yet\n establishes = EVENT_KINDS.get(event.kind, (\"\", None, False))[1]\n if establishes:\n function, since = establishes, when\n detail = f\"{event.label} recorded on {when.isoformat()}\"\n if event.by:\n detail += f\" by {event.by}\"\n if event.kind == \"commissioned\" and commissioned is None:\n commissioned = when\n if event.kind == \"inspection\":\n last_inspection = when\n if event.kind == \"water_sample\":\n last_sample = when\n\n out_for = ((today - since).days\n if function == \"non_functional\" and since else None)\n if undated and function == \"unknown\":\n detail = (f\"{undated} record(s) carry a date nobody can read, so \"\n \"nothing can be established from them.\")\n\n due: list[DueItem] = []\n if function != \"decommissioned\":\n due.append(_due_item(\n \"inspection\", \"Sanitary inspection\", last_inspection, commissioned,\n schedule.inspection_months, schedule.grace_days, today,\n \"A sanitary inspection is what catches a cracked apron or a \"\n \"latrine dug uphill before the water shows it.\"))\n due.append(_due_item(\n \"water_sample\", \"Water quality sample\", last_sample, commissioned,\n schedule.water_sample_months, schedule.grace_days, today,\n \"Water that was safe at handover is not evidence that it is safe \"\n \"now: the aquifer, the headworks and the catchment all change.\"))\n return AssetState(\n function=function, since=since, detail=detail,\n last_inspection=last_inspection, last_sample=last_sample,\n commissioned=commissioned, days_out_of_service=out_for,\n due=tuple(item for item in due if item is not None),\n undated_events=undated,\n )\n\n\ndef _due_item(key: str, title: str, last: date | None, commissioned: date | None,\n months: int, grace_days: int, today: date, why: str) -> DueItem:\n anchor = last or commissioned\n if anchor is None:\n return DueItem(key, title, None, \"unknown\",\n f\"No {title.lower()} has been recorded, and there is no \"\n f\"commissioning date to count from. {why}\")\n due_on = _add_months(anchor, months)\n if today > due_on + timedelta(days=grace_days):\n overdue_by = (today - due_on).days\n never = \"\" if last else \"has never been done; it \"\n return DueItem(key, title, due_on, \"overdue\",\n f\"{title} {never}has been due since \"\n f\"{due_on.isoformat()}, {overdue_by} days ago. {why}\")\n if today > due_on:\n return DueItem(key, title, due_on, \"due\",\n f\"{title} fell due on {due_on.isoformat()}.\")\n return DueItem(key, title, due_on, \"scheduled\",\n f\"Next {title.lower()} due {due_on.isoformat()}.\")\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# What goes on the borehole itself\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef qr_payload(asset: Asset) -> str:\n \"\"\"The text the QR code carries.\n\n Plain text rather than a link. A link is only useful where there is a\n network, and the whole reason this symbol is on the headworks is that\n there is not one - a technician who scans it should see the identifier,\n the place and the position on the screen immediately, with nothing to\n load and nothing to install.\n \"\"\"\n lines = [f\"BOREHOLE {asset.asset_id}\", asset.label]\n latlon = asset.latlon\n if latlon is not None:\n lat, lon = latlon\n lines.append(f\"{abs(lat):.5f} {'N' if lat >= 0 else 'S'}, \"\n f\"{abs(lon):.5f} {'E' if lon >= 0 else 'W'}\")\n facts = []\n if asset.total_depth_m:\n facts.append(f\"{float(asset.total_depth_m):.1f} m deep\")\n if asset.safe_yield_m3_per_h:\n facts.append(f\"{float(asset.safe_yield_m3_per_h):.2f} m3/h\")\n if asset.pump_type:\n facts.append(asset.pump_type)\n if facts:\n lines.append(\", \".join(facts))\n return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef placard_lines(asset: Asset, state: AssetState | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n \"\"\"Field-value rows for the plate that gets fixed to the headworks.\"\"\"\n rows = [(\"Identifier\", asset.asset_id), (\"Community\", asset.community or \"-\")]\n if asset.district:\n rows.append((\"District\", asset.district))\n latlon = asset.latlon\n if latlon is not None:\n rows.append((\"Position\", f\"{latlon[0]:.5f} N, {abs(latlon[1]):.5f} W\"))\n if asset.total_depth_m:\n rows.append((\"Depth\", f\"{float(asset.total_depth_m):.1f} m\"))\n if asset.safe_yield_m3_per_h:\n rows.append((\"Safe yield\", f\"{float(asset.safe_yield_m3_per_h):.2f} m3/h\"))\n if asset.pump_type:\n rows.append((\"Pump\", asset.pump_type))\n if asset.installed_by:\n rows.append((\"Installed by\", asset.installed_by))\n if state is not None:\n if state.commissioned:\n rows.append((\"Commissioned\", state.commissioned.isoformat()))\n rows.append((\"Status\", state.label))\n return rows\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Many of them\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef registry_rows(assets, today: date | None = None,\n schedule: Schedule | None = None) -> list[dict]:\n \"\"\"One formatted row per asset, for the registry table.\"\"\"\n today = today or date.today()\n rows = []\n for asset in assets:\n state = asset_state(asset, today, schedule)\n overdue = state.overdue\n rows.append({\n \"Identifier\": asset.asset_id,\n \"Community\": asset.community or \"(unnamed)\",\n \"District\": asset.district or \"\",\n \"Status\": state.label,\n \"Since\": state.since.isoformat() if state.since else \"\",\n \"Last inspected\": state.last_inspection.isoformat()\n if state.last_inspection else \"\",\n \"Last sampled\": state.last_sample.isoformat()\n if state.last_sample else \"\",\n \"Overdue\": \", \".join(item.title for item in overdue),\n \"Events\": len(asset.events),\n })\n return rows\n\n\ndef registry_stats(assets, today: date | None = None,\n schedule: Schedule | None = None) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Headline counts.\n\n ``n_unknown`` is reported beside the working and broken counts and never\n folded into either. A register where most points are unknown looks very\n like one where most points are working, unless the number is on the\n page next to them.\n \"\"\"\n today = today or date.today()\n assets = list(assets)\n counts = {key: 0 for key in FUNCTION_LABELS}\n overdue_by_key: dict[str, int] = {}\n out_days = []\n for asset in assets:\n state = asset_state(asset, today, schedule)\n counts[state.function] = counts.get(state.function, 0) + 1\n if state.days_out_of_service is not None:\n out_days.append(state.days_out_of_service)\n for item in state.overdue:\n overdue_by_key[item.key] = overdue_by_key.get(item.key, 0) + 1\n known = counts[\"functional\"] + counts[\"non_functional\"]\n return {\n \"n_assets\": len(assets),\n \"n_functional\": counts[\"functional\"],\n \"n_non_functional\": counts[\"non_functional\"],\n \"n_decommissioned\": counts[\"decommissioned\"],\n \"n_unknown\": counts[\"unknown\"],\n # over the points whose condition is actually known, and None when\n # none of them are - a functionality rate computed over silence is\n # the number that makes these registers untrustworthy\n \"functionality_rate\": (counts[\"functional\"] / known * 100.0)\n if known else None,\n \"n_overdue_inspection\": overdue_by_key.get(\"inspection\", 0),\n \"n_overdue_sample\": overdue_by_key.get(\"water_sample\", 0),\n \"mean_days_out_of_service\": (sum(out_days) / len(out_days))\n if out_days else None,\n }\n"}, "groundwater/reporting/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Templated .docx report generation.\n\nEvery builder the toolkit has is named here. The Phase 2 builders are still\nimported lazily - some of them pull in matplotlib and python-docx machinery\nthat a caller who only wants ``ReportBuilder`` should not pay for - but the\nlist is now complete, so ``from groundwater.reporting import X`` works for\nall of them rather than for four out of ten.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom .docx_utils import ReportBuilder\nfrom .geophysical import build_geophysical_report\n\n__all__ = [\n \"ReportBuilder\",\n \"build_asset_placard\",\n \"build_asset_record\",\n \"build_completion_report\",\n \"build_cost_report\",\n \"build_geophysical_report\",\n \"build_handover_report\",\n \"build_payment_certificate\",\n \"build_pumping_report\",\n \"build_quality_report\",\n \"build_supervision_report\",\n]\n\n_LAZY = {\n \"build_asset_placard\": \".registry\",\n \"build_asset_record\": \".registry\",\n \"build_completion_report\": \".completion\",\n \"build_cost_report\": \".costing\",\n \"build_handover_report\": \".handover\",\n \"build_payment_certificate\": \".procurement\",\n \"build_pumping_report\": \".pumping\",\n \"build_quality_report\": \".quality\",\n \"build_supervision_report\": \".supervision\",\n}\n\n\ndef __getattr__(name):\n module = _LAZY.get(name)\n if module is None:\n raise AttributeError(name)\n from importlib import import_module\n\n return getattr(import_module(module, __name__), name)\n\n\ndef __dir__():\n return sorted(__all__)\n"}, "groundwater/reporting/citations.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Reference citations and a glossary shared by the report builders.\n\nThe reports name methods, standards and datasets throughout (WHO\nguidelines, RWSN cost guidance, Theis, Cooper-Jacob, the bundled map\nsources). This module holds the full citations so a References section can\nclose each report, and a glossary of the abbreviations the reports use, so\nthey read as consultant-grade documents rather than naming sources that are\nnever fully cited.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\n# full bibliography entries, keyed by a short id\nCITATIONS: dict[str, str] = {\n \"who\": (\n \"World Health Organization (2022). Guidelines for Drinking-water \"\n \"Quality, 4th edition incorporating the first and second addenda. \"\n \"Geneva: World Health Organization.\"\n ),\n \"slsb\": (\n \"Sierra Leone Standards Bureau. Sierra Leone Standard for drinking \"\n \"water quality (SLS). Freetown: SLSB. Edition and date not verified \"\n \"against the issued specification: the national limits this toolkit \"\n \"applies are provisional (WHO or regional figures carried across) \"\n \"until confirmed against it.\"\n ),\n \"rwsn_cost\": (\n \"Rural Water Supply Network (2010). Code of Practice for Cost \"\n \"Effective Boreholes. St Gallen: RWSN.\"\n ),\n \"rwsn_drilling\": (\n \"Rural Water Supply Network (2015). Professional Water Well Drilling: \"\n \"A UNICEF Guidance Note. St Gallen: RWSN / UNICEF.\"\n ),\n \"theis\": (\n \"Theis, C.V. (1935). The relation between the lowering of the \"\n \"piezometric surface and the rate and duration of discharge of a well \"\n \"using groundwater storage. Transactions of the American Geophysical \"\n \"Union, 16, 519-524.\"\n ),\n \"cooper_jacob\": (\n \"Cooper, H.H. and Jacob, C.E. (1946). A generalized graphical method \"\n \"for evaluating formation constants and summarizing well-field \"\n \"history. Transactions of the American Geophysical Union, 27, 526-534.\"\n ),\n \"hantush\": (\n \"Hantush, M.S. (1964). Hydraulics of wells. In V.T.
