organisation=config.style.organisation,\n )\n return rb.save(out_path)\n"}, "groundwater/reporting/quality.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Water quality report generator.\n\nPresents the laboratory results against WHO guideline values and the\nnational standard, flags every exceedance clearly (bold red status),\nreports the ionic balance check and, where the major ions are\navailable, the Piper and Stiff diagrams, and closes with treatment\nrecommendations matched to the exceedances found.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom docx.shared import RGBColor\n\nfrom ..config import Config\nfrom ..quality.assess import STATUS_LABELS, WaterQualityAssessment\nfrom ..quality.diagrams import facies_of, plot_piper, plot_stiff\nfrom ..quality.standards import (\n PROVISIONAL_NATIONAL_NOTE,\n provisional_national_parameters,\n)\nfrom ..utils import fmt_num, safe_slug, plural_noun\nfrom .citations import GLOSSARY, references_for\nfrom .docx_utils import ReportBuilder\nfrom .context import add_area_section\n\n#: The wording lives with the assessment so every surface prints the same\n#: label and a new status can never leak out as a raw code.\n_STATUS_LABEL = STATUS_LABELS\n\ndef _sentence(text: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Upper-case the first letter only.\n\n str.capitalize() lower-cases everything after it, which turns \"E. coli\"\n into \"e. coli\" and \"Total petroleum hydrocarbons\" into a lower-case\n determinand halfway through a client-facing sentence.\n \"\"\"\n return text[:1].upper() + text[1:] if text else text\n\n\n_TREATMENT_ADVICE = {\n \"iron\": \"Iron above the acceptability value causes staining and metallic \"\n \"taste; aeration followed by sand filtration or a simple oxidation \"\n \"filter normally resolves it.\",\n \"manganese\": \"Manganese requires oxidation and filtration (aeration or \"\n \"chlorination followed by filtration); monitor infant exposure in the \"\n \"meantime.\",\n \"e. coli\": \"Any E. coli detection calls for shock chlorination of the \"\n \"borehole, verification of the sanitary seal and apron, and re-sampling \"\n \"before use.\",\n \"total coliforms\": \"Coliform detection calls for disinfection of the \"\n \"borehole and pump, a sanitary inspection of the wellhead, and re-sampling.\",\n \"nitrate (as no3)\": \"Elevated nitrate usually indicates pollution from \"\n \"sanitation or agriculture; investigate the sanitary protection zone. Do \"\n \"not give the water to bottle fed infants until resolved.\",\n \"fluoride\": \"Fluoride above 1.5 mg/L requires an alternative source or \"\n \"defluoridation (bone char or activated alumina).\",\n \"arsenic\": \"Arsenic above 0.01 mg/L requires an alternative source or \"\n \"specialised removal; re-test to confirm before any use for drinking.\",\n \"ph\": \"Low pH water is corrosive to metal fittings; a limestone contactor \"\n \"or careful choice of corrosion resistant materials is advised.\",\n \"turbidity\": \"High turbidity interferes with disinfection; extend \"\n \"development of the borehole and re-sample.\",\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass QualityReportInputs:\n assessment: WaterQualityAssessment\n figures_dir: Path\n analyst_name: str = \"\"\n analyst_role: str = \"Water Quality Analyst\"\n analyst_phone: str = \"\"\n include_diagrams: bool = True\n #: The certification gate for this report, from\n #: :func:`groundwater.readiness.assess_readiness`. When it is not\n #: certifiable the cover says so; when it is absent nothing is\n #: stamped, so an existing caller is unaffected.\n readiness: Any = None\n\n\ndef _executive_summary(assessment: WaterQualityAssessment) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:\n \"\"\"Compose the water-quality executive summary from the assessment.\"\"\"\n community = assessment.sample.site.community or \"the site\"\n health = assessment.health_exceedances\n national = assessment.national_exceedances\n aesthetic = assessment.aesthetic_exceedances\n state = assessment.verdict_state\n if state == \"national_fail\":\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in national)\n para = (\n f\"Laboratory results for the borehole water at {community} meet the \"\n \"WHO health based guideline values but do not comply with the \"\n f\"national standard {plural_noun(len(national), 'limit')} for {names}. \"\n \"A national limit is a \"\n \"legal requirement, not a matter of taste: treatment is required \"\n \"before the supply can be accepted.\"\n )\n key = [\n \"All WHO health based guideline values are met.\",\n f\"National standard {plural_noun(len(national), 'exceedance')}: {names}.\",\n \"Treatment is required before the supply is accepted.\",\n ]\n elif state == \"indeterminate\":\n para = (\n f\"Laboratory results for the borehole water at {community} do not \"\n \"establish that the water is suitable for drinking. \"\n + _sentence(\"; \".join(assessment.uncertainties))\n + \". No suitability verdict can be given until these are resolved.\"\n )\n key = [\n \"The water has NOT been shown to be safe to drink.\",\n ] + [_sentence(u) + \".\" for u in assessment.uncertainties]\n elif health:\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in health)\n para = (\n f\"Laboratory results for the borehole water at {community} were \"\n \"assessed against the WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality and \"\n \"the national/adopted limits. The water does not meet the health \"\n f\"based guideline {plural_noun(len(health), 'value')} for {names}, so treatment or an \"\n \"alternative source is required before it is used for drinking.\"\n )\n key = [\n f\"Health based {plural_noun(len(health), 'exceedance')}: {names}.\",\n \"Treatment or an alternative source is required before drinking.\",\n ]\n if national:\n # a national-limit failure beside a health one used to vanish\n # from the summary; the indicator that put it there is named\n also = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in national)\n para += (\n f\" The water also fails the national standard \"\n f\"{plural_noun(len(national), 'limit')} for {also}.\"\n )\n key.insert(1, f\"National standard {plural_noun(len(national), 'exceedance')}: {also}.\")\n elif aesthetic:\n names = \", \".join(r.parameter for r in aesthetic)\n para = (\n f\"Laboratory results for the borehole water at {community} meet all \"\n \"health based guideline values. Acceptability (aesthetic) limits are \"\n f\"exceeded for {names}; the water is usable for drinking, although \"\n \"taste, odour or staining complaints may arise.\"\n )\n key = [\n \"All health based guideline values are met.\",\n f\"Aesthetic {plural_noun(len(aesthetic), 'exceedance')}: {names}.\",\n ]\n else:\n para = (\n f\"Laboratory results for the borehole water at {community} comply \"\n \"with the WHO guideline values and the national/adopted limits \"\n \"applied. The water is suitable for drinking on the basis of the \"\n \"parameters tested.\"\n )\n key = [\n \"All measured parameters comply with the limits applied.\",\n \"The water is suitable for drinking on the parameters tested.\",\n ]\n return [para], key\n\n\ndef build_quality_report(\n inputs: QualityReportInputs,\n out_path: str | Path,\n config: Config | None = None,\n) -> Path:\n config = config or Config()\n assessment = inputs.assessment\n sample = assessment.sample\n site = sample.site\n figures = Path(inputs.figures_dir)\n figures.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n # Qualify figure filenames with the site: several reports share one\n # figures directory in an app session and generation is guarded by an\n # existence check, so fixed names made the second report silently reuse\n # the first site's figures.\n slug = safe_slug(sample.borehole_ref or site.community, \"site\")\n\n rb = ReportBuilder(config.style, title=f\"Water Quality Report - {site.community}\")\n rb.cover(\n title_lines=[\"WATER QUALITY REPORT\"],\n subtitle_lines=[\n f\"Borehole water assessment at {site.community}\"\n + (f\", {site.district} District\" if site.district else \"\"),\n ],\n details=[\n (\"Client\", site.client),\n (\"Sample ID\", sample.sample_id),\n (\"Borehole\", sample.borehole_ref),\n (\"Sample date\", sample.sample_date),\n (\"Laboratory\", sample.laboratory),\n ],\n )\n rb.provisional_stamp(inputs.readiness)\n\n # ---- executive summary ------------------------------------------------\n exec_paras, exec_key = _executive_summary(assessment)\n rb.executive_summary(exec_paras, exec_key)\n\n # ---- 1 sample details -------------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"1. Sample Details\", 1)\n rb.header_block_table(\n [\n (\"Community\", site.community), (\"Client\", site.client),\n (\"Sample ID\", sample.sample_id), (\"Borehole Ref. No.\", sample.borehole_ref),\n (\"Sample date\", sample.sample_date), (\"Laboratory\", sample.laboratory),\n (\"District\", site.district), (\"Project\", site.project),\n ]\n )\n rb.paragraph(\n \"Results are compared against the WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water \"\n \"Quality (fourth edition with addenda) and the national standard \"\n \"limits configured for this project. Where a confirmed national \"\n \"value is not available, the WHO or regional figure is adopted for \"\n \"that parameter and the status column reads national/adopted limit. \"\n \"Values reported by the laboratory as below the detection limit are \"\n \"shown as such.\",\n align=\"justify\",\n )\n # A national exceedance reads as a compliance failure, so the report must\n # say plainly when the limit it was judged against is not yet confirmed.\n if provisional_national_parameters():\n rb.paragraph(PROVISIONAL_NATIONAL_NOTE, align=\"justify\")\n\n add_area_section(rb, site, figures, config.style,\n heading=\"1.1 Location and setting\")\n\n # ---- 2 results table ------------------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"2. Results Against Guideline Values\", 1)\n table_no = rb.next_table_number\n rb.paragraph(\n f\"Table {table_no} lists every parameter tested. Exceedances are \"\n \"highlighted in the status column.\"\n )\n header = [\"Parameter\", \"Value\", \"Unit\", \"WHO health\", \"WHO acceptability\",\n \"National\", \"Status\"]\n rows = []\n highlight = []\n for r in assessment.rows:\n value = \"< DL\" if (r.below_detection and r.value is None) else fmt_num(r.value)\n rows.append([\n r.parameter, value, r.unit, r.who_health, r.who_aesthetic,\n r.sl_standard, _STATUS_LABEL.get(r.status, r.status),\n ])\n highlight.append(r.status in (\"exceeds_health\", \"exceeds_national\", \"exceeds_aesthetic\"))\n rb.table(rows, header=header, caption=\"Laboratory results against guideline values.\",\n font_size_pt=8.5)\n # bold red status text on exceedance rows\n table = rb.doc.tables[-1]\n for i, is_exceed in enumerate(highlight):\n if not is_exceed:\n continue\n cell = table.rows[i + 1].cells[len(header) - 1]\n for para in cell.paragraphs:\n for run in para.runs:\n run.font.bold = True\n run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xB0, 0x00, 0x00)\n\n rb.paragraph(assessment.verdict, bold=True, align=\"justify\")\n\n # headline aggregate scores for quick ranking of the source\n wqi = assessment.wqi\n if wqi is not None:\n rb.paragraph(\n f\"Water Quality Index: {wqi.value:.0f} ({wqi.rating}), over \"\n f\"{wqi.n_parameters} physico-chemical parameters.\",\n bold=True,\n )\n hr = assessment.health_risk\n if hr is not None:\n line = f\"Health Hazard Index: {hr.hazard_index:.2f} ({hr.rating}).\"\n if hr.cancer_risk is not None:\n line += (\n f\" Estimated lifetime arsenic cancer risk {hr.cancer_risk:.1e}.\"\n )\n rb.paragraph(line, bold=True)\n\n # ---- 3 ionic balance ---------------------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"3. Ionic Balance Check\", 1)\n ionic = assessment.ionic\n if ionic is None:\n rb.paragraph(\n \"The major ion analysis is incomplete, so no ionic balance check \"\n \"is possible for this sample.\"\n )\n else:\n note = (\n \" Bicarbonate was estimated from total alkalinity.\"\n if ionic.used_alkalinity_for_bicarbonate\n else \"\"\n )\n rb.paragraph(\n f\"Sum of cations {fmt_num(ionic.sum_cations_meq, 3)} meq/L, sum of \"\n f\"anions {fmt_num(ionic.sum_anions_meq, 3)} meq/L, charge balance \"\n f\"error {ionic.error_percent:+.1f} percent.{note} \"\n + (\n \"The analysis balances within the normal 5 percent tolerance.\"\n if abs(ionic.error_percent) <= 5\n else \"The balance error exceeds 5 percent; the laboratory \"\n \"analysis should be reviewed.\"\n ),\n align=\"justify\",\n )\n\n # ---- 4 corrosivity and materials ---------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"4. Corrosivity and Materials\", 1)\n corr = assessment.corrosivity\n if corr is None or corr.classification == \"Insufficient data\":\n rb.paragraph(\n corr.verdict if corr is not None else\n \"Corrosivity was not assessed; pH, calcium and alkalinity are \"\n \"required to compute the saturation indices.\"\n )\n else:\n rb.paragraph(corr.verdict, align=\"justify\")\n idx_rows: list[list[str]] = []\n if corr.lsi is not None:\n idx_rows.append([\"Langelier Saturation Index (LSI)\", f\"{corr.lsi:+.2f}\"])\n if corr.rsi is not None:\n idx_rows.append([\"Ryznar Stability Index (RSI)\", f\"{corr.rsi:.2f}\"])\n if corr.aggressive_index is not None:\n idx_rows.append([\"Aggressive Index (AI)\", f\"{corr.aggressive_index:.2f}\"])\n if corr.larson_skold is not None:\n idx_rows.append([\"Larson-Skold ratio\", f\"{corr.larson_skold:.2f}\"])\n idx_rows.append([\"Classification\", corr.classification])\n rb.table(idx_rows, header=[\"Index\", \"Value\"],\n caption=\"Corrosivity and scaling indices.\")\n rb.paragraph(corr.materials_note, align=\"justify\", bold=corr.is_aggressive)\n if corr.assumptions:\n rb.paragraph(\"Assumptions: \" + \" \".join(corr.assumptions))\n\n # ---- 5 diagrams ----------------------------------------------------------------\n if inputs.include_diagrams and ionic is not None:\n rb.heading(\"5. Hydrochemical Facies\", 1)\n piper_path = figures / f\"piper_{slug}.png\"\n stiff_path = figures / f\"stiff_{slug}.png\"\n plot_piper([sample], path=piper_path, style=config.style)\n plot_stiff(sample, path=stiff_path, style=config.style)\n # the section used to be two figures and no words\n facies = facies_of(sample)\n if facies is not None:\n rb.paragraph(facies[\"sentence\"], align=\"justify\")\n rb.figure(\n piper_path,\n \"Piper diagram: the sample's major-ion composition, with the \"\n \"cations on the left triangle, the anions on the right and the \"\n \"combined point in the diamond.\",\n width_cm=13.0,\n )\n rb.figure(\n stiff_path,\n \"Stiff diagram: the same composition as a shape, cations to the \"\n \"left and anions to the right of the axis.\",\n width_cm=11.0,\n )\n\n # ---- 6 recommendations -----------------------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"6. Recommendations\", 1)\n advice = []\n if corr is not None and corr.is_aggressive:\n advice.append(corr.materials_note)\n for r in assessment.all_exceedances:\n key = r.parameter.strip().lower()\n for match, text in _TREATMENT_ADVICE.items():\n if match in key:\n advice.append(text)\n break\n if assessment.verdict_state == \"indeterminate\":\n # \"No treatment is required\" is a clearance, and this report has not\n # established one. Say what is outstanding instead.\n advice.append(\n \"Do not treat this supply as safe to drink on these results. \"\n + _sentence(\"; \".join(assessment.uncertainties))\n + \". Resolve these and re-issue the assessment before any \"\n \"treatment decision is taken.\"\n )\n elif not advice:\n advice.append(\n \"No treatment is required on the basis of the parameters tested. \"\n \"Maintain the sanitary seal and apron in good condition.\"\n )\n advice.append(\n \"Repeat physico-chemical and bacteriological testing at least once a \"\n \"year, and after any flooding or repair work on the wellhead.\"\n )\n rb.bullets(advice)\n\n # ---- 7 limitations ---------------------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"7. Limitations and Uncertainty\", 1)\n rb.bullets(\n [\n (\"The results describe a single sample at one point in time. Water \"\n \"quality varies with the season, rainfall and the condition of the \"\n \"wellhead, so periodic re-testing is needed to confirm the \"\n \"verdict.\"),\n (\"Parameters reported below the laboratory detection limit are shown \"\n \"as such; a non-detection does not prove complete absence.\"),\n (\"The corrosivity and index calculations use the parameters \"\n \"supplied. Missing pH, calcium or alkalinity limit what can be \"\n \"assessed, and any assumptions made are stated where they are \"\n \"used.\"),\n ]\n )\n\n # ---- references and glossary -----------------------------------------------\n rb.references(references_for(\"quality\"))\n rb.glossary(GLOSSARY)\n\n rb.signature_block(\n name=inputs.analyst_name,\n role=inputs.analyst_role,\n phone=inputs.analyst_phone,\n organisation=config.style.organisation,\n )\n return rb.save(out_path)\n"}, "groundwater/reporting/registry.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"The asset record: what stays with the borehole after the project ends.\n\nTwo documents in one file, because they are two halves of the same job.\n\nThe **placard** is a single page meant to be printed, laminated and fixed\nto the headworks. It carries the identifier in large type, the QR symbol\nthat encodes it, and the handful of facts a technician needs before opening\nanything: where it is, how deep, what pump. Nothing on it goes out of date,\nwhich is why the maintenance history is deliberately not on it.\n\nThe **asset record** is the history: what has happened, what condition that\nleaves the borehole in, and what is now overdue. It is the document a\ndistrict water office reads when deciding where to send a repair team, and\nit says plainly when the answer is that nobody knows.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom ..utils import plural\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\n\nfrom .. import qr\nfrom ..config import Config\nfrom ..registry import (\n Asset,\n AssetState,\n Schedule,\n asset_state,\n placard_lines,\n qr_payload,\n)\nfrom ..models import SiteMetadata\nfrom .context import add_area_section\nfrom .docx_utils import ReportBuilder\n\n__all__ = [\n \"AssetReportInputs\",\n \"build_asset_placard\",\n \"build_asset_record\",\n \"write_qr_png\",\n]\n\n#: Level H, so the symbol still reads after a season of mud and sunlight.\nPLACARD_ECC = \"H\"\n\n\ndef write_qr_png(text: str, out_path: str | Path, *, scale: int = 10,\n ecc: str = PLACARD_ECC) -> Path:\n \"\"\"Render ``text`` as a QR symbol on disk, and return where it went.\"\"\"\n path = Path(out_path)\n path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n path.write_bytes(qr.to_png(qr.encode(text, ecc=ecc), scale=scale))\n return path\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass AssetReportInputs:\n asset: Asset\n figures_dir: str | Path\n today: date | None = None\n schedule: Schedule | None = None\n prepared_by: str = \"\"\n readiness: Any = None\n\n\ndef _state(inputs: AssetReportInputs) -> AssetState:\n return asset_state(inputs.asset, inputs.today or date.today(),\n inputs.schedule)\n\n\ndef build_asset_placard(inputs: AssetReportInputs, out_path: str | Path,\n config: Config | None = None) -> Path:\n \"\"\"The page that gets fixed to the borehole.\"\"\"\n asset = inputs.asset\n rb = ReportBuilder(config.style if config else None,\n title=f\"Borehole {asset.asset_id}\")\n\n rb.paragraph(\"BOREHOLE IDENTIFICATION PLATE\", bold=True, align=\"center\")\n rb.paragraph(asset.asset_id, bold=True, size_pt=26, align=\"center\")\n rb.paragraph(asset.label, size_pt=13, align=\"center\")\n\n image = write_qr_png(qr_payload(asset),\n Path(inputs.figures_dir) / f\"qr_{asset.asset_id}.png\")\n rb.figure(image, \"Scan for this borehole's identifier and position. The \"\n \"symbol carries the details themselves, so it reads with \"\n \"no network and no application installed.\", width_cm=7.0)\n\n rb.table([[label, value] for label, value in placard_lines(asset,\n _state(inputs))],\n header=[\"\", \"\"], caption=\"Borehole details\",\n col_widths_cm=[5.0, 10.0])\n rb.paragraph(\n \"Report a breakdown or a change to this borehole against the \"\n \"identifier above. Quote it in full, including the last character - \"\n \"it is a check character, and it is what stops a repair being \"\n \"recorded against a different village's borehole.\",\n italic=True)\n return rb.save(out_path)\n\n\ndef build_asset_record(inputs: AssetReportInputs, out_path: str | Path,\n config: Config | None = None) -> Path:\n \"\"\"The maintenance history and what it means today.\"\"\"\n asset = inputs.asset\n state = _state(inputs)\n today = inputs.today or date.today()\n rb = ReportBuilder(config.style if config else None,\n title=f\"Asset record - {asset.label}\")\n\n rb.cover(\n [\"Borehole Asset Record\"],\n [asset.label, asset.asset_id],\n [(\"Status\", state.label), (\"As at\", today.isoformat())]\n + ([(\"Prepared by\", inputs.prepared_by)] if inputs.prepared_by else []),\n )\n rb.provisional_stamp(inputs.readiness)\n\n rb.heading(\"Condition\")\n rb.paragraph(f\"{state.label}. {state.detail}\")\n if state.days_out_of_service is not None:\n rb.paragraph(\n f\"This borehole has been out of service for \"\n f\"{state.days_out_of_service} days. Every day counted here is a \"\n \"day the community went back to whatever they used before.\",\n bold=True)\n if state.undated_events:\n rb.paragraph(\n f\"{plural(state.undated_events, 'record')} \"\n f\"{'carries' if state.undated_events == 1 else 'carry'} a date that could not be \"\n \"read. They are listed below with the date as written, but they \"\n \"establish nothing about when anything last happened.\")\n\n add_area_section(\n rb,\n SiteMetadata(community=asset.community, chiefdom=asset.chiefdom,\n district=asset.district, easting=asset.easting,\n northing=asset.northing, utm_zone=asset.utm_zone),\n inputs.figures_dir, config.style if config else None,\n heading=\"Where it is\",\n )\n\n rb.heading(\"Details\")\n rb.table([[label, value] for label, value in placard_lines(asset, state)],\n header=[\"\", \"\"], col_widths_cm=[5.0, 10.0])\n\n rb.heading(\"Outstanding\")\n overdue = state.overdue\n unknown = [item for item in state.due if item.state == \"unknown\"]\n if overdue or unknown:\n rb.bullets([item.detail for item in overdue]\n + [item.detail for item in unknown])\n else:\n scheduled = [item for item in state.due\n if item.state in (\"scheduled\", \"due\")]\n if scheduled:\n rb.bullets([item.detail for item in scheduled])\n else:\n rb.paragraph(\"Nothing is outstanding.\")\n\n rb.heading(\"History\")\n if asset.events:\n rows = []\n for event in sorted(asset.events, key=lambda e: (e.when or \"9999\",\n e.kind)):\n rows.append([event.when or \"(no date)\", event.label,\n event.note or \"\", event.by or \"\",\n \"yes\" if event.photo else \"\"])\n rb.table(rows, header=[\"Date\", \"Event\", \"Note\", \"Recorded by\", \"Photo\"],\n caption=\"Everything recorded against this borehole\",\n col_widths_cm=[2.4, 3.2, 6.0, 2.4, 1.5])\n rb.paragraph(\n \"This history is append-only: a mistake is corrected by recording \"\n \"the correction, so both entries stay visible. Nothing here has \"\n \"been edited or removed.\", italic=True)\n else:\n rb.paragraph(\n \"Nothing has ever been recorded against this borehole. That is \"\n \"not the same as nothing having happened to it.\", bold=True)\n return rb.save(out_path)\n"}, "groundwater/reporting/supervision.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Drilling supervision checklist report generator.\n\nTurns the supervisor's checklist responses into a signed record: stage\nby stage tables with each item's status and remark, the critical\nfailures up front, and the three party sign off block (supervisor,\ndriller, community representative) that RWSN supervision practice\nexpects.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom ..config import Config\nfrom ..models import SiteMetadata\nfrom ..supervision.checklists import (\n ChecklistAssessment,\n ChecklistItem,\n ChecklistResponse,\n stage_title,\n)\nfrom ..supervision.field_checks import FieldCheck\nfrom .citations import GLOSSARY, references_for\nfrom .context import _figures_dir\nfrom .docx_utils import ReportBuilder\nfrom .context import add_area_section\n\n_STATUS_LABEL = {\n \"yes\": \"Yes\",\n \"no\": \"NO\",\n \"na\": \"N/A\",\n \"pending\": \"-\",\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SupervisionReportInputs:\n site: SiteMetadata\n items: list[ChecklistItem]\n responses: dict[str, ChecklistResponse]\n assessment: ChecklistAssessment\n supervisor: str = \"\"\n driller: str = \"\"\n community_rep: str = \"\"\n notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n #: Sand content, verticality, screen open area, specific capacity and the\n #: rest of :mod:`groundwater.supervision.field_checks`. A checklist says\n #: what was inspected; these say what was measured, and they are what the\n #: works are accepted or rejected against.\n field_checks: list[FieldCheck] = field(default_factory=list)\n #: Where the location map is written. A supervision record is a record\n #: of a place as much as of a checklist, so it carries one. Left unset,\n #: the figures go beside the document rather than into whatever\n #: directory the process happens to be running in.\n figures_dir: Path | None = None\n #: :class:`~groundwater.readiness.Readiness` for this report, from\n #: :func:`groundwater.readiness.assess_readiness`. When it is not\n #: certifiable the cover carries a PROVISIONAL stamp listing why.\n readiness: Any = None\n\n\ndef build_supervision_report(\n inputs: SupervisionReportInputs,\n out_path: str | Path,\n config: Config | None = None,\n) -> Path:\n config = config or Config()\n site = inputs.site\n assessment = inputs.assessment\n\n rb = ReportBuilder(\n config.style,\n title=f\"Supervision Checklist - {site.community or 'Borehole'}\",\n )\n rb.cover(\n title_lines=[\"DRILLING SUPERVISION\", \"CHECKLIST RECORD\"],\n subtitle_lines=[\n f\"at {site.community}\" + (f\", {site.district} District\" if site.district else \"\")\n if site.community\n else \"Borehole Construction Supervision\",\n ],\n details=[\n (\"Client\", site.client),\n (\"Project\", site.project),\n (\"Contractor\", site.contractor),\n (\"Supervisor\", inputs.supervisor or site.supervisor),\n (\"Date\", site.date),\n ],\n )\n rb.provisional_stamp(inputs.readiness)\n rb.table_of_contents()\n\n # ---- 1 summary -------------------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"1. Summary\", 1)\n rb.paragraph(assessment.verdict, bold=True)\n rb.table(\n [\n [\n progress.title,\n f\"{progress.answered}/{progress.total}\",\n str(progress.failed),\n str(progress.critical_failed),\n ]\n for progress in assessment.stages\n ],\n header=[\"Stage\", \"Answered\", \"Failed\", \"Critical failed\"],\n caption=\"Checklist progress by supervision stage.\",\n )\n critical = [f for f in assessment.flags if f.code == \"critical_item_failed\"]\n if critical:\n rb.paragraph(\"Critical items that failed:\", bold=True)\n rb.bullets([f\"{f.context}: {f.message}\" for f in critical])\n\n add_area_section(rb, site, _figures_dir(inputs.figures_dir, out_path),\n config.style, heading=\"1.1 Location and setting\")\n\n # ---- 2 checklists -----------------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"2. Checklist Record\", 1)\n rb.paragraph(\n \"The checklists follow the RWSN/UNICEF guidance for supervising \"\n \"water well drilling. Critical items are marked with an asterisk; \"\n \"a failed critical item stops acceptance of the works.\"\n )\n stage_keys: list[str] = []\n for item in inputs.items:\n if item.checklist not in stage_keys:\n stage_keys.append(item.checklist)\n for number, key in enumerate(stage_keys, start=1):\n stage_items = [i for i in inputs.items if i.checklist == key]\n rb.heading(f\"2.{number} {stage_title(key)}\", 2)\n rows = []\n for item in stage_items:\n response = inputs.responses.get(item.item_id)\n status = _STATUS_LABEL.get(\n response.status if response else \"pending\", \"-\"\n )\n remark = response.remark if response else \"\"\n marker = \"*\" if item.critical else \"\"\n rows.append([f\"{item.text}{marker}\", status, remark])\n rb.table(\n rows,\n header=[\"Item\", \"Status\", \"Remark\"],\n caption=f\"{stage_title(key)} checklist.\",\n )\n\n # ---- 3 notes ----------------------------------------------------------\n if inputs.notes or inputs.field_checks:\n rb.heading(\"3. Site Record\", 1)\n if inputs.notes:\n rb.heading(\"3.1 Site Notes and Instructions\", 2)\n rb.paragraph(\n \"Site instructions are issued in writing and signed in \"\n \"duplicate by the supervisor and the driller.\"\n )\n rb.bullets(inputs.notes)\n\n # ---- field acceptance checks -------------------------------------------\n if inputs.field_checks:\n rb.heading(\"3.2 Field Acceptance Checks\", 2)\n rb.paragraph(\n \"Measured against the acceptance limits in the RWSN and UNICEF \"\n \"supervision guidance. A failed check is a defect the contractor \"\n \"is required to make good before the works are accepted.\",\n align=\"justify\",\n )\n rb.table(\n [[c.name, c.measured, c.limit, c.status.upper(), c.message]\n for c in inputs.field_checks],\n header=[\"Check\", \"Measured\", \"Acceptance limit\", \"Result\", \"Note\"],\n caption=\"Field acceptance checks.\",\n )\n\n # ---- signatures --------------------------------------------------------\n rb.heading(\"4. Sign Off\", 1)\n rb.paragraph(\n \"The undersigned confirm that the checklist record above reflects \"\n \"the works as inspected.\"\n )\n for role, name in (\n (\"Supervisor\", inputs.supervisor or site.supervisor),\n (\"For the driller\", inputs.driller or site.contractor),\n (\"For the community\", inputs.community_rep),\n ):\n rb.paragraph(\"\")\n rb.paragraph(\".\" * 30)\n rb.paragraph(f\"{role}: {name}\", bold=True)\n rb.paragraph(\"Date: ........................\")\n\n rb.references(references_for(\"supervision\"))\n rb.glossary(GLOSSARY)\n\n return rb.save(out_path)\n"}, "groundwater/seasonal.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"When in the year the test was run, and what the borehole will do later.\n\nA pumping test measures one day. The borehole has to supply a village on\nthe worst day, and in Sierra Leone those are months apart: a single wet\nseason from about June to October recharges the aquifer, the water table\npeaks around the end of it, and it falls through the dry season to an\nannual low in April or May. A test run in August sits on a static level the\nborehole will not see again until the following August.\n\nThe toolkit already reserved a fixed allowance for that decline before\ncomputing the usable drawdown. A fixed allowance is right for exactly one\nmonth of the year. Applied to a test run in April it takes two metres of\ndrawdown that has already been spent, and understates a yield the borehole\nhas demonstrably got; applied to a test run in September it is the whole\nstory and may not be enough. So this module puts the test in the year and\ncomputes the decline still to come, then reports the yield under named\nscenarios instead of one number resting on a hidden assumption.\n\n**What is assumed, and what is measured.** The shape of the year - which\nmonths are high and which are low - is well established for a single-wet-\nseason climate and is stated here as a table anyone can read and argue\nwith. The *size* of the annual range is not: it varies with the aquifer,\nthe catchment and the year, and a single test cannot measure it. It is\ntherefore a parameter, defaulting to the configured allowance, and every\nscenario says which range it used and where that came from.\n\n**The month has to be known.** A date written 10/05/2018 is 10 May under\none convention and 5 October under the other - opposite ends of the year,\nand opposite answers. An ambiguous date is treated as no date at all: the\nseason is unknown, the full range is reserved because that is the\nconservative reading, and the report says why rather than quietly picking\none.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, replace\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom .config import PumpingConfig\n\n__all__ = [\n \"MONTH_NAMES\",\n \"SCENARIOS\",\n \"SEASONAL_POSITION\",\n \"SeasonalScenario\",\n \"SeasonalYield\",\n \"month_of\",\n \"season_of\",\n \"seasonal_yield\",\n]\n\nMONTH_NAMES = [\"January\", \"February\", \"March\", \"April\", \"May\", \"June\", \"July\",\n \"August\", \"September\", \"October\", \"November\", \"December\"]\n\n#: Where the water table sits in the annual cycle, by month: 0.0 at the\n#: annual high, 1.0 at the annual low. A single wet season from June to\n#: October fills the aquifer; levels peak at the end of it and recede\n#: through the dry season to a low in April and May, just before the rains\n#: return. The shape is the standard one for this climate; the size of the\n#: swing is not stated here, because that is a property of the aquifer and\n#: is carried separately.\nSEASONAL_POSITION = {\n 1: 0.35, # January - two months into the recession\n 2: 0.55,\n 3: 0.75,\n 4: 0.95, # April - the low, or within a few weeks of it\n 5: 1.00, # May - the driest the borehole will be\n 6: 0.80, # the rains have started but the table lags them\n 7: 0.45,\n 8: 0.15,\n 9: 0.00, # September - fully recovered\n 10: 0.05, # October - the rains end, the recession has barely begun\n 11: 0.15,\n 12: 0.25,\n}\n\n#: Which part of the year a month belongs to, for plain-language reporting.\n_SEASON_OF_MONTH = {\n 1: \"dry season\", 2: \"dry season\", 3: \"late dry season\",\n 4: \"late dry season\", 5: \"late dry season\", 6: \"early wet season\",\n 7: \"wet season\", 8: \"wet season\", 9: \"wet season\",\n 10: \"late wet season\", 11: \"early dry season\", 12: \"dry season\",\n}\n\n#: The scenarios a design is judged against. ``factor`` multiplies the\n#: annual range: 0 is the level on the day of the test, 1 is the normal\n#: annual low, and the drought case allows for the low being deeper in a\n#: run of poor years than in an average one.\nSCENARIOS = {\n \"as_tested\": (\n \"As tested\", 0.0,\n (\"The level on the day of the test. Not a design figure: unless the \"\n \"test was run at the end of the dry season the borehole will be \"\n \"lower than this for part of every year.\"),\n ),\n \"dry_season\": (\n \"End of dry season\", 1.0,\n (\"The normal annual low, which the borehole reaches every year. This \"\n \"is the figure a design should be sized on.\"),\n ),\n \"drought\": (\n \"Drought year\", 1.5,\n (\"A low deeper than a normal year's, for a run of poor rains. The \"\n \"pump has to still be under water here, or the village loses the \"\n \"borehole in exactly the year it is needed most.\"),\n ),\n}\n\n\ndef month_of(text) -> tuple[int | None, str]:\n \"\"\"``(month, why)`` for a date as written on a field sheet.\n\n ``month`` is ``None`` whenever the answer would be a guess, and ``why``\n says what stopped it - the wording goes into the report, because the\n fix is somebody writing the date less ambiguously next time.\n \"\"\"\n raw = str(text or \"\").strip()\n if not raw:\n return None, \"No date is recorded for the test.\"\n\n # A month written by name settles it wherever it sits in the text. Only\n # the first word used to be looked at, so \"Wed 25/04/2018\" and\n # \"Date: 14/09/2018\" - both perfectly clear - were reported as naming\n # no month at all.\n words = re.findall(r\"[A-Za-z]{3,}\", raw)\n for word in words:\n head = word.lower()[:3]\n for index, month in enumerate(MONTH_NAMES, start=1):\n if month.lower().startswith(head):\n return index, \"\"\n\n parts = [int(p) for p in re.findall(r\"\\d+\", raw)]\n if len(parts) < 3:\n if words:\n return None, f\"The date {raw!r} does not name a month.\"\n return None, f\"The date {raw!r} is not a full date.\"\n\n # An ISO date is unambiguous: a four-digit year can only be the year.\n if parts[0] > 31:\n month = parts[1]\n return (month, \"\") if 1 <= month <= 12 else (\n None, f\"The date {raw!r} has no month in it.\")\n\n first, second = parts[0], parts[1]\n if first > 12 and 1 <= second <= 12:\n return second, \"\" # 25/04/2018 - only one reading\n if second > 12 and 1 <= first <= 12:\n return first, \"\" # 04/25/2018 - likewise\n if 1 <= first <= 12 and 1 <= second <= 12:\n return None, (\n f\"The date {raw!r} could be read either way round: \"\n f\"{MONTH_NAMES[second - 1]} or {MONTH_NAMES[first - 1]}. Those are \"\n \"different ends of the year and give different answers, so the \"\n \"season is treated as unknown. Record the month by name, or pick \"\n \"it below.\")\n return None, f\"The date {raw!r} has no month in it.\"\n\n\ndef season_of(month: int | None) -> str:\n \"\"\"Plain language for a month, or \"unknown\" when there is no month.\"\"\"\n if not month or month not in _SEASON_OF_MONTH:\n return \"unknown\"\n return _SEASON_OF_MONTH[month]\n\n\ndef _decline_to_come(month: int | None, annual_range_m: float,\n factor: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"Metres the water table still has to fall from the tested level.\n\n With no month the whole range is reserved. That is the conservative\n reading and it is what the toolkit did before this module existed - the\n difference is that now it is a stated fallback rather than the only\n behaviour.\n \"\"\"\n if month is None:\n position = 0.0\n else:\n position = SEASONAL_POSITION.get(month, 0.0)\n # never negative: a test at the annual low needs no further allowance,\n # and a scenario shallower than the tested level is not a scenario\n return max(annual_range_m * (factor - position), 0.0)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass SeasonalScenario:\n key: str\n title: str\n decline_m: float\n static_water_level_m: Optional[float]\n available_drawdown_m: Optional[float]\n safe_yield_m3_per_h: Optional[float]\n pump_installation_depth_m: Optional[float]\n note: str\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n return {\n \"key\": self.key, \"title\": self.title,\n \"decline_m\": self.decline_m,\n \"static_water_level_m\": self.static_water_level_m,\n \"available_drawdown_m\": self.available_drawdown_m,\n \"safe_yield_m3_per_h\": self.safe_yield_m3_per_h,\n \"pump_installation_depth_m\": self.pump_installation_depth_m,\n \"note\": self.note,\n }\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SeasonalYield:\n \"\"\"The yield under each scenario, and what a design should be sized on.\"\"\"\n\n month: Optional[int]\n season: str\n month_note: str\n annual_range_m: float\n range_source: str\n scenarios: list[SeasonalScenario]\n pending_reason: str = \"\"\n\n def scenario(self, key: str) -> Optional[SeasonalScenario]:\n for item in self.scenarios:\n if item.key == key:\n return item\n return None\n\n @property\n def is_established(self) -> bool:\n design = self.scenario(\"dry_season\")\n return design is not None and design.safe_yield_m3_per_h is not None\n\n @property\n def design_yield_m3_per_h(self) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"What to size on: the normal annual low, not the day of the test.\"\"\"\n design = self.scenario(\"dry_season\")\n return design.safe_yield_m3_per_h if design else None\n\n @property\n def pump_installation_depth_m(self) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"Deep enough for the worst scenario, because the pump is fitted once.\"\"\"\n depths = [s.pump_installation_depth_m for s in self.scenarios\n if s.pump_installation_depth_m is not None]\n return max(depths) if depths else None\n\n @property\n def dry_season_loss_percent(self) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"How much of the tested yield the dry season takes away.\"\"\"\n tested = self.scenario(\"as_tested\")\n design = self.scenario(\"dry_season\")\n if not tested or not design:\n return None\n if not tested.safe_yield_m3_per_h:\n return None\n if design.safe_yield_m3_per_h is None:\n # the dry season takes all of it: the pump is dry at the annual low\n return 100.0\n return (1.0 - design.safe_yield_m3_per_h\n / tested.safe_yield_m3_per_h) * 100.0\n\n @property\n def summary(self) -> str:\n if self.pending_reason:\n return self.pending_reason\n tested = self.scenario(\"as_tested\")\n design = self.scenario(\"dry_season\")\n drought = self.scenario(\"drought\")\n if design is None:\n return \"The seasonal yield could not be established.\"\n if design.safe_yield_m3_per_h is None:\n # Not \"could not be established\": it was, and the answer is that\n # the pump runs dry before the annual low is reached.\n text = (\"No yield at the end of the dry season: the pump would be \"\n \"dry at the dry-season low\")\n if tested and tested.safe_yield_m3_per_h is not None:\n text += (f\" (the test itself gave \"\n f\"{tested.safe_yield_m3_per_h:.2g} m3/h)\")\n else:\n text = (f\"Sized on the end of the dry season: \"\n f\"{design.safe_yield_m3_per_h:.2g} m3/h\")\n if drought and drought.safe_yield_m3_per_h is not None:\n text += (f\", falling to {drought.safe_yield_m3_per_h:.2g} m3/h \"\n \"in a drought year\")\n elif drought is not None:\n # a clause that used to be dropped, which read as if a\n # drought year cost nothing\n text += \", and the pump would be dry in a drought year\"\n if self.month:\n text += (f\". The test was run in {MONTH_NAMES[self.month - 1]}, \"\n f\"the {self.season}\")\n return text + \".\"\n\n def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n return {\n \"month\": self.month, \"season\": self.season,\n \"month_note\": self.month_note,\n \"annual_range_m\": self.annual_range_m,\n \"range_source\": self.range_source,\n \"pending_reason\": self.pending_reason,\n \"design_yield_m3_per_h\": self.design_yield_m3_per_h,\n \"pump_installation_depth_m\": self.pump_installation_depth_m,\n \"dry_season_loss_percent\": self.dry_season_loss_percent,\n \"summary\": self.summary,\n \"scenarios\": [s.as_dict() for s in self.scenarios],\n }\n\n\ndef seasonal_yield(analysis, config: PumpingConfig | None = None, *,\n month: int | None = None,\n annual_range_m: float | None = None) -> SeasonalYield:\n \"\"\"Re-run the yield recommendation at each scenario's water level.\n\n ``month`` overrides whatever the field sheet says - a supervisor who\n knows when the test was run should be able to say so. ``annual_range_m``\n overrides the configured allowance, for a programme that has measured\n the swing in its own boreholes rather than assuming one.\n \"\"\"\n from .hydraulics.analysis import recommend_yield\n\n config = config or PumpingConfig()\n test = getattr(analysis, \"test\", None)\n recommendation = getattr(analysis, \"yield_recommendation\", None)\n\n if month is not None:\n found_month, note = (month if 1 <= int(month) <= 12 else None), \"\"\n if found_month is None:\n note = f\"{month!r} is not a month.\"\n else:\n found_month, note = month_of(\n getattr(getattr(test, \"site\", None), \"date\", \"\") if test else \"\")\n\n if annual_range_m is not None and annual_range_m >= 0:\n band, source = float(annual_range_m), \"measured for this programme\"\n else:\n band, source = float(config.seasonal_allowance_m), (\n \"the configured dry-season allowance, not a measurement\")\n\n blank = SeasonalYield(month=found_month, season=season_of(found_month),\n month_note=note, annual_range_m=band,\n range_source=source, scenarios=[])\n if test is None or recommendation is None:\n blank.pending_reason = (\n \"No pumping test has been analysed, so there is nothing to project \"\n \"through the year.\")\n return blank\n if recommendation.safe_yield_m3_per_h is None:\n blank.pending_reason = (\n recommendation.pending_reason\n or \"The yield recommendation is pending, so it cannot be projected \"\n \"through the year.\")\n return blank\n\n transmissivity = getattr(analysis, \"transmissivity_m2_per_day\", None)\n if transmissivity is None:\n blank.pending_reason = (\n \"No transmissivity was fitted, so the seasonal projection has \"\n \"nothing to run on.\")\n return blank\n\n scenarios = []\n for key, (title, factor, why) in SCENARIOS.items():\n decline = _decline_to_come(found_month, band, factor)\n # The scenario is the same borehole with its static level lowered:\n # everything downstream - available drawdown, usable fraction, the\n # projection and the pump depth - follows from that one change, so\n # the recommendation is re-run rather than scaled.\n lowered = replace(test, static_water_level_m=test.static_water_level_m\n + decline)\n trial = recommend_yield(\n lowered, transmissivity, getattr(analysis, \"step_test\", None),\n replace(config, seasonal_allowance_m=0.0),\n )\n note_text = why\n if key == \"as_tested\" and found_month:\n note_text += (\n f\" The test was run in {MONTH_NAMES[found_month - 1]}, \"\n f\"the {season_of(found_month)}.\")\n if key != \"as_tested\" and decline == 0.0 and found_month:\n note_text += (\n f\" No further decline is reserved: a test run in \"\n f\"{MONTH_NAMES[found_month - 1]} is already at or below this \"\n \"level.\")\n if trial.safe_yield_m3_per_h is None:\n # the pump would be dry at this level; the table cell is blank,\n # so the note has to carry the reason\n note_text += (\n \" No yield at this level: \"\n + (trial.pending_reason\n or \"the projection leaves no usable drawdown\") + \".\")\n scenarios.append(SeasonalScenario(\n key=key, title=title, decline_m=decline,\n static_water_level_m=lowered.static_water_level_m,\n available_drawdown_m=trial.available_drawdown_m,\n safe_yield_m3_per_h=trial.safe_yield_m3_per_h,\n pump_installation_depth_m=trial.pump_installation_depth_m,\n note=note_text,\n ))\n\n return SeasonalYield(\n month=found_month, season=season_of(found_month), month_note=note,\n annual_range_m=band, range_source=source, scenarios=scenarios,\n )\n"}, "groundwater/site_status.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"What a borehole's recorded status actually means.\n\nField sheets carry the status as free text - \"Successful\", \"Completed -\nDry\", \"Incomplete, rig broke down\", \"Unproductive\" - and the portfolio has\nto turn that into one of a few classes to colour a map and compute a\nsuccess rate. Substring matching cannot do it: \"complete\" is inside\n\"incomplete\", \"productive\" is inside \"unproductive\", and \"sit\" is inside\n\"visited\". Every one of those read as a producing borehole, so a programme\nthat had drilled a run of dry holes reported them as successes and painted\nthem green on the national map.\n\nSo the mapping is explicit. Known phrasings are listed; the rest are\nmatched by word-boundary rules ordered so that a negation is always seen\nbefore the word it negates; and anything still unrecognised lands in\n:attr:`SiteStatus.OTHER` rather than being guessed at. Failing to classify\nis visible and harmless. Classifying a dry hole as a success is neither.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom enum import Enum\n\n\nclass SiteStatus(str, Enum):\n \"\"\"The portfolio classes. ``str`` mixin, so ``== \"successful\"`` works.\"\"\"\n\n SUCCESSFUL = \"successful\"\n DRY = \"dry\"\n SITED = \"sited\"\n IN_PROGRESS = \"in_progress\"\n OTHER = \"other\"\n\n\n# The lookup tables are keyed by the wire strings rather than by members.\n# Enum hashes by member name, not by value, so a member-keyed dict cannot\n# also be indexed with the plain string that a saved project file carries -\n# and the callers that do exactly that (mapping/regional.py, the Streamlit\n# chip) would raise a KeyError at render time.\n\n#: Map colours: red for a problem, green for a producing hole, grey for a\n#: status nobody could read - grey so it reads as missing data rather than\n#: as an outcome.\nSTATUS_COLORS = {\n \"successful\": \"#2E7D5B\",\n \"dry\": \"#B23A2E\",\n \"sited\": \"#17527E\",\n \"in_progress\": \"#C1772A\",\n \"other\": \"#6B7785\",\n}\n\nSTATUS_LABELS = {\n \"successful\": \"Successful\",\n \"dry\": \"Dry / failed\",\n \"sited\": \"Sited (not drilled)\",\n \"in_progress\": \"In progress\",\n \"other\": \"Status not recognised\",\n}\n\n#: Exact phrasings seen on real sheets and in saved projects, normalised.\n#: An entry here beats every rule below, so a known wording can never be\n#: caught by a rule meant for something else.\nLEGACY_STATUS_MAP = {\n \"successful\": SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n \"success\": SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n \"completed\": SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n \"complete\": SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n \"productive\": SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n \"equipped\": SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n \"commissioned\": SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n \"handed over\": SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n \"dry\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"dry hole\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"failed\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"failure\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"unsuccessful\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"not successful\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"unproductive\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"non productive\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"abandoned\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"no water\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"completed dry\": SiteStatus.DRY,\n \"sited\": SiteStatus.SITED,\n \"siting\": SiteStatus.SITED,\n \"surveyed\": SiteStatus.SITED,\n \"not drilled\": SiteStatus.SITED,\n \"incomplete\": SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n \"not completed\": SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n \"uncompleted\": SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n \"in progress\": SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n \"ongoing\": SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n \"drilling\": SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n \"pending\": SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n \"on hold\": SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n}\n\n# Ordered rules, first match wins. The order is load-bearing: every rule\n# that recognises a negation (\"unproductive\", \"not completed\") must be\n# tried before the rule that would match the word being negated.\n_RULES: list[tuple[re.Pattern, SiteStatus]] = [\n # 1. Outright failure.\n (\n re.compile(\n r\"\\b(dry|no\\s+water|water\\s+not\\s+struck|failed|failure|\"\n r\"unsuccessful|not\\s+successful|abandon\\w*|collapsed|backfilled|\"\n r\"plugged|caved)\\b\"\n ),\n SiteStatus.DRY,\n ),\n # 2. Failure written as a negated success. THIS is the bug: \"unproductive\"\n # contains \"productive\" and used to be read as a producing borehole.\n (\n re.compile(\n r\"\\b(un|non|not)[\\s-]*(productive|producing)\\b\"\n r\"|\\b(low|poor|insufficient|inadequate|marginal|nil)\\s+\"\n r\"(yield|productivity|production)\\b\"\n r\"|\\bproductivity\\s+(low|poor)\\b\"\n ),\n SiteStatus.DRY,\n ),\n # 3. Unfinished written as a negated completion. \"incomplete\" contains\n # \"complete\" and used to be read as a finished, producing hole.\n (\n re.compile(\n r\"\\b(in|un)complet\\w*\\b|\\bnot\\s+complet\\w*\\b\"\n r\"|\\b(partially|part|partly)\\s+complet\\w*\\b\"\n ),\n SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n ),\n # 4. Unfinished, said plainly.\n (\n re.compile(\n r\"\\b(in\\s+progress|ongoing|under\\s+(construction|way|test\\w*)|\"\n r\"drilling|pending|awaiting|suspended|on\\s+hold|deferred|\"\n r\"standing\\s+by|rework)\\b\"\n ),\n SiteStatus.IN_PROGRESS,\n ),\n # 5. Sited but not drilled. Word-anchored, so \"visited\" and \"deposit\" no\n # longer count as a siting. (\"not sited\" is refused before the rules\n # run - written as a plain check rather than a lookbehind so the same\n # expression compiles in both this engine and the browser one.)\n (\n re.compile(\n r\"\\bsit(e|ed|ing)\\b\"\n r\"|\\b(surveyed|survey\\s+complete|geophysics\\s+complete|\"\n r\"recommended\\s+for\\s+drilling|to\\s+be\\s+drilled|not\\s+drilled)\\b\"\n ),\n SiteStatus.SITED,\n ),\n # 6. Success, last, so every negation above has already had its turn.\n (\n re.compile(\n r\"\\bsuccess(ful)?\\b|\\bcomplet(e|ed)\\b|\\bproductive\\b\"\n r\"|\\b(equipped|commissioned|handed\\s+over|operational|functional)\\b\"\n ),\n SiteStatus.SUCCESSFUL,\n ),\n]\n\n_SEPARATORS = re.compile(r\"[_/\\\\|,;()\\[\\].\u2013\u2014-]+\")\n\n\ndef normalise_status(raw: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Fold punctuation and spacing so \"Completed - Dry\" == \"completed dry\".\"\"\"\n text = _SEPARATORS.sub(\" \", str(raw or \"\").lower())\n return re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", text).strip()\n\n\ndef coerce_status(value) -> SiteStatus:\n \"\"\"Turn a stored wire value back into a member, unrecognised -> OTHER.\"\"\"\n if isinstance(value, SiteStatus):\n return value\n try:\n return SiteStatus(str(value or \"\").strip().lower())\n except ValueError:\n return SiteStatus.OTHER\n\n\ndef status_label(value) -> str:\n \"\"\"Display label for a member or its wire value.\"\"\"\n return STATUS_LABELS[coerce_status(value).value]\n\n\ndef status_color(value) -> str:\n \"\"\"Map colour for a member or its wire value.\"\"\"\n return STATUS_COLORS[coerce_status(value).value]\n\n\ndef classify_text(raw: str) -> SiteStatus | None:\n \"\"\"Classify a free-text status, or ``None`` when it is not recognised.\n\n ``None`` rather than a guess: an unreadable status is data to fix, and\n the caller decides what to show for it.\n \"\"\"\n key = normalise_status(raw)\n if not key:\n return None\n exact = LEGACY_STATUS_MAP.get(key)\n if exact is not None:\n return exact\n if re.search(r\"\\bnot\\s+sited\\b\", key):\n return None # a negation, not a siting\n for pattern, status in _RULES:\n if pattern.search(key):\n return status\n return None\n"}, "groundwater/siting/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Drill-target siting decision support (prototype).\n\nTurns the hydrogeological interpretation the toolkit already computes into\na single, ranked \"where should I drill?\" answer: a transparent 0-100\nsuitability score per candidate VES point, a grade, a plain-language\nrationale, and a drill-target map.\n\nThe score is a transparent weighted scorecard over features that a siting\nhydrogeologist already weighs in crystalline basement terrain, so a water\nmanager can see *why* a point is preferred, not just that it is. It is a\nstarting point: as a programme accumulates its own (VES features ->\ndrilling outcome) pairs, the weights can be replaced by a fitted model.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom .suitability import (\n SitingSuitability,\n SuitabilityComponents,\n assess_siting,\n ranking_tie,\n suitability_map_points,\n)\n\n__all__ = [\n \"SitingSuitability\",\n \"SuitabilityComponents\",\n \"assess_siting\",\n \"ranking_tie\",\n \"suitability_map_points\",\n]\n"}, "groundwater/siting/suitability.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Transparent drill-target suitability scorecard.\n\nEach candidate VES point is scored 0-100 from four components a siting\nhydrogeologist weighs in crystalline basement terrain:\n\n* aquifer thickness - total interpreted water-bearing thickness,\n* resistivity fit - how central the water-zone resistivity sits in the\n productive fractured/weathered window (too high is\n dry/fresh rock, too low is clay or, on the coast,\n saline),\n* overburden - a favourable weathered profile (not too thin to\n store water, not so deep that basement is out of\n reach),\n* basal fracture - a water zone at or just above the weathered/fresh\n basement contact, the prime basement target.\n\nThe weights are explicit and configurable. They are a defensible default,\nnot a calibrated model; the intended upgrade path is to fit them against\nreal drilling outcomes as a programme accumulates them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom ..config import VESConfig\nfrom ..ves.interpret import SiteInterpretation\n\n# component weights (must sum to 1.0)\n_WEIGHTS = {\n \"aquifer_thickness\": 0.35,\n \"resistivity_fit\": 0.25,\n \"overburden\": 0.20,\n \"basal_fracture\": 0.20,\n}\n_THICKNESS_TARGET_M = 25.0 # aquifer thickness scoring saturates here\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SuitabilityComponents:\n \"\"\"The four normalised (0-1) component scores behind a suitability.\"\"\"\n\n aquifer_thickness: float\n resistivity_fit: float\n overburden: float\n basal_fracture: float\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SitingSuitability:\n sounding_id: str\n suitability: float # 0-100, the geological score\n grade: str # Poor / Moderate / Good / Very good\n components: SuitabilityComponents\n rationale: str\n easting: float | None = None\n northing: float | None = None\n rank: int | None = None\n #: 0-1: how far the model fit and an unresolved basement discount the\n #: score. The points are ranked on suitability x confidence, so a point\n #: whose curve was fitted to 27 percent does not outrank one fitted to\n #: 13 percent on a few ohm-m of half-space resistivity.\n confidence: float = 1.0\n\n @property\n def weighted(self) -> float:\n \"\"\"The number the ranking is decided on.\"\"\"\n return self.suitability * self.confidence\n\n\ndef _grade(score: float) -> str:\n if score >= 75:\n return \"Very good\"\n if score >= 55:\n return \"Good\"\n if score >= 35:\n return \"Moderate\"\n return \"Poor\"\n\n\ndef _thickness_score(interp: SiteInterpretation) -> float:\n return min(interp.aquifer_thickness_m / _THICKNESS_TARGET_M, 1.0)\n\n\ndef _zone_geomean_rho(interp: SiteInterpretation) -> float | None:\n \"\"\"Thickness-weighted geometric mean resistivity across the water zones.\"\"\"\n acc = 0.0\n total = 0.0\n for top, bottom in interp.water_zones:\n for layer in interp.layers:\n lo = max(layer.top_m, top)\n hi = min(\n layer.bottom_m if math.isfinite(layer.bottom_m) else bottom, bottom\n )\n if hi > lo:\n acc += math.log(layer.rho) * (hi - lo)\n total += hi - lo\n return math.exp(acc / total) if total > 0 else None\n\n\ndef _resistivity_fit_score(interp: SiteInterpretation, config: VESConfig) -> float:\n mid = _zone_geomean_rho(interp)\n if mid is None:\n return 0.0\n lo, hi = config.fractured_zone_rho\n centre = math.sqrt(lo * hi)\n return 1.0 / (1.0 + abs(math.log(max(mid, 1e-3) / centre)))\n\n\ndef _overburden_score(interp: SiteInterpretation) -> float:\n dtb = interp.depth_to_basement_m\n if dtb is None:\n return 0.5 # unknown: neutral\n if dtb < 5:\n return 0.15 # too thin to store much water\n if dtb <= 35:\n return 1.0 # favourable weathered profile\n # deep overburden is still drillable but basement/target sits deeper\n return max(0.4, 1.0 - (dtb - 35) / 60.0)\n\n\ndef _basal_fracture_score(interp: SiteInterpretation) -> float:\n zones = interp.water_zones\n if not zones:\n return 0.0\n dtb = interp.depth_to_basement_m\n if dtb is not None:\n for top, bottom in zones:\n # a zone straddling or just above the fresh-basement contact is\n # the highest-yield basement target\n if top <= dtb <= bottom or abs(bottom - dtb) <= 5.0:\n return 1.0\n return 0.5\n\n\ndef _rationale(interp: SiteInterpretation, comp: SuitabilityComponents) -> str:\n if not interp.water_zones:\n return (\n \"No water-bearing zone was resolved within the investigated depth, \"\n \"so the drilling prospect here is weak.\"\n )\n parts = []\n thick = interp.aquifer_thickness_m\n open_ended = getattr(interp, \"basement_not_resolved\", False)\n parts.append(\n (f\"at least {thick:.0f} m of interpreted water-bearing thickness, the \"\n \"base of the zone being below the depth the sounding resolves\"\n if open_ended else\n f\"about {thick:.0f} m of interpreted water-bearing thickness\")\n + (\" (thick)\" if comp.aquifer_thickness >= 0.7 else\n \" (modest)\" if comp.aquifer_thickness >= 0.4 else \" (thin)\")\n )\n if comp.resistivity_fit >= 0.6:\n parts.append(\"resistivities well within the productive fracture window\")\n elif comp.resistivity_fit >= 0.35:\n parts.append(\"resistivities near the edge of the productive window\")\n else:\n parts.append(\"resistivities outside the ideal productive window\")\n if comp.basal_fracture >= 1.0:\n parts.append(\"a fractured zone at the basement contact\")\n if interp.depth_to_basement_m is not None and comp.overburden < 0.4:\n parts.append(\n f\"overburden of about {interp.depth_to_basement_m:.0f} m that limits the target\"\n )\n text = \"Driven by \" + \"; \".join(parts) + \".\"\n confidence = getattr(interp, \"confidence\", 1.0)\n if confidence < 1.0:\n reasons = []\n err = getattr(interp, \"fit_error_percent\", None)\n if getattr(interp, \"fit_quality\", \"ok\") != \"ok\":\n reasons.append(f\"a model fit of {err:.1f} percent (ERR)\")\n if open_ended:\n reasons.append(\"a basement the sounding did not reach\")\n text += (\n f\" Confidence {confidence:.2f}: \"\n + \" and \".join(reasons)\n + \" discount the score before ranking.\"\n )\n return text\n\n\ndef ranking_tie(results: list[\"SitingSuitability\"], within_points: float = 3.0) -> str:\n \"\"\"One sentence when the top two points cannot be told apart.\n\n Two weighted scores within a few points of each other are the same\n number for siting purposes: a table that ranks them 1st and 2nd on a\n difference hidden by rounding gives the client a preference with no\n visible basis. Returns \"\" when the ranking is clear or there is one point.\n \"\"\"\n ranked = sorted(results, key=lambda r: r.rank if r.rank is not None else 99)\n if len(ranked) < 2:\n return \"\"\n first, second = ranked[0], ranked[1]\n if abs(first.weighted - second.weighted) >= within_points:\n return \"\"\n return (\n f\"Points {first.sounding_id} and {second.sounding_id} are indistinguishable \"\n f\"on geophysical grounds (confidence-weighted suitability \"\n f\"{first.weighted:.1f} and {second.weighted:.1f}); {first.sounding_id} is \"\n \"listed first by name only, and the choice between them should be made \"\n \"on access, sanitary distances and the community's preference.\"\n )\n\n\ndef assess_siting(\n interpretations: list[SiteInterpretation],\n config: VESConfig | None = None,\n) -> list[SitingSuitability]:\n \"\"\"Score and rank candidate VES points by drilling suitability.\n\n Returns the results ranked most suitable first (rank 1 = best), so the\n first entry is the recommended drilling target.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or VESConfig()\n results: list[SitingSuitability] = []\n for interp in interpretations:\n comp = SuitabilityComponents(\n aquifer_thickness=_thickness_score(interp),\n resistivity_fit=_resistivity_fit_score(interp, config),\n overburden=_overburden_score(interp),\n basal_fracture=_basal_fracture_score(interp),\n )\n score = 100.0 * (\n _WEIGHTS[\"aquifer_thickness\"] * comp.aquifer_thickness\n + _WEIGHTS[\"resistivity_fit\"] * comp.resistivity_fit\n + _WEIGHTS[\"overburden\"] * comp.overburden\n + _WEIGHTS[\"basal_fracture\"] * comp.basal_fracture\n )\n results.append(\n SitingSuitability(\n sounding_id=interp.sounding_id,\n suitability=round(score, 1),\n grade=_grade(score),\n components=comp,\n rationale=_rationale(interp, comp),\n easting=interp.site_easting,\n northing=interp.site_northing,\n confidence=round(float(getattr(interp, \"confidence\", 1.0)), 3),\n )\n )\n # rank on the confidence-weighted score, highest first; ties broken by\n # sounding id for stability, and said in words by ranking_tie()\n ranked = sorted(results, key=lambda r: (-r.weighted, r.sounding_id))\n for rank, result in enumerate(ranked, start=1):\n result.rank = rank\n return ranked\n\n\ndef suitability_map_points(results: list[SitingSuitability]):\n \"\"\"Build MapPoints (value = suitability) for the drill-target map.\n\n Only points that carry coordinates are returned.\n \"\"\"\n from ..mapping.maps import MapPoint\n\n points = []\n for r in results:\n if r.easting is None or r.northing is None:\n continue\n points.append(\n MapPoint(\n label=f\"{r.sounding_id}\",\n easting=float(r.easting),\n northing=float(r.northing),\n # the confidence-weighted score: the number the ranking is\n # decided on, so the map colours agree with the table's order\n value=round(r.weighted, 1),\n kind=r.grade,\n rank=r.rank,\n )\n )\n return points\n"}, "groundwater/supervision/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Drilling supervision: stage checklists and field acceptance checks.\n\nEncodes RWSN/UNICEF supervision guidance: the nine step supervision\nworkflow as editable checklists, the minimum site separation\ndistances, and the numeric acceptance criteria (sand content,\nverticality, screen open area, specific capacity, disinfection dose).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom .checklists import (\n RESPONSE_STATES,\n STAGE_ORDER,\n STAGE_TITLES,\n ChecklistAssessment,\n ChecklistItem,\n ChecklistResponse,\n SeparationDistance,\n StageProgress,\n evaluate_checklist,\n load_checklists,\n load_separation_distances,\n stage_title,\n)\nfrom .field_checks import (\n DisinfectionDose,\n FieldCheck,\n annular_space_check,\n disinfection_dose,\n handpump_corrosion_check,\n metres_reconciliation_check,\n pack_aquifer_ratio_check,\n sand_content_check,\n screen_open_area_check,\n specific_capacity_check,\n verticality_check,\n)\n\n__all__ = [\n \"RESPONSE_STATES\",\n \"STAGE_ORDER\",\n \"STAGE_TITLES\",\n \"ChecklistAssessment\",\n \"ChecklistItem\",\n \"ChecklistResponse\",\n \"SeparationDistance\",\n \"StageProgress\",\n \"evaluate_checklist\",\n \"load_checklists\",\n \"load_separation_distances\",\n \"stage_title\",\n \"DisinfectionDose\",\n \"FieldCheck\",\n \"annular_space_check\",\n \"disinfection_dose\",\n \"handpump_corrosion_check\",\n \"metres_reconciliation_check\",\n \"pack_aquifer_ratio_check\",\n \"sand_content_check\",\n \"screen_open_area_check\",\n \"specific_capacity_check\",\n \"verticality_check\",\n]\n"}, "groundwater/supervision/checklists.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Drilling supervision checklists as data.\n\nThe checklist content follows RWSN/UNICEF \"Supervising Water Well\nDrilling: a Guide for Supervisors\" (Adekile), whose Annex B checklists\ncover the nine step borehole construction workflow, and the WASH\nfunders infrastructure checklists for boreholes and handpumps. Items\nlive in an editable CSV (``data/supervision_checklists.csv``) so a\nproject can adapt them without code changes.\n\nCritical items are the ones whose failure should stop acceptance of\nthe works (safety, records, acceptance criteria and sign offs).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom importlib import resources\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom ..models import DataFlag\n\n# Ordered stages of the supervision workflow, keyed as in the CSV.\nSTAGE_TITLES: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (\n (\"procurement\", \"Procurement and contract\"),\n (\"pre_contract\", \"Pre-contract inspection\"),\n (\"siting\", \"Siting\"),\n (\"mobilisation\", \"Mobilisation\"),\n (\"drilling\", \"Drilling\"),\n (\"design\", \"Design and installation\"),\n (\"development\", \"Development and completion\"),\n (\"demobilisation\", \"Demobilisation\"),\n (\"handover\", \"Documentation and handover\"),\n (\"post_construction\", \"Post-construction monitoring\"),\n)\n\nSTAGE_ORDER = tuple(key for key, _ in STAGE_TITLES)\n\nRESPONSE_STATES = (\"pending\", \"yes\", \"no\", \"na\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ChecklistItem:\n \"\"\"One supervision checklist requirement.\"\"\"\n\n item_id: str # stable id from the CSV, e.g. \"drl-depth-measured-marked\"\n checklist: str # stage key, e.g. \"drilling\"\n section: str # grouping within the stage, e.g. \"Safety\"\n text: str\n critical: bool = False\n guidance: str = \"\"\n #: The id this row had before ids were written into the CSV: its position\n #: within its stage (\"drilling-03\"). Saved answers were keyed by it, and\n #: inserting one row re-mapped every later answer to a different\n #: question; the loader keeps it so those answers can be carried across.\n legacy_id: str = \"\"\n\n\ndef stage_title(key: str) -> str:\n for stage_key, title in STAGE_TITLES:\n if stage_key == key:\n return title\n return key.replace(\"_\", \" \").capitalize()\n\n\ndef load_checklists(path: str | Path | None = None) -> list[ChecklistItem]:\n \"\"\"Load the checklist items (bundled CSV unless a path is given).\"\"\"\n if path is not None:\n text = Path(path).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n else:\n text = (\n resources.files(\"groundwater\") / \"data\" / \"supervision_checklists.csv\"\n ).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n items: list[ChecklistItem] = []\n counters: dict[str, int] = {}\n seen: set[str] = set()\n for row in csv.DictReader(text.splitlines()):\n checklist = row[\"checklist\"].strip()\n counters[checklist] = counters.get(checklist, 0) + 1\n positional = f\"{checklist}-{counters[checklist]:02d}\"\n # the CSV's own id when it has one, so a row inserted or reworded\n # never moves anybody's saved answer; a project CSV without the\n # column keeps the positional ids it always had\n item_id = (row.get(\"id\") or \"\").strip() or positional\n if item_id in seen:\n raise ValueError(f\"checklist id {item_id!r} appears twice in the CSV\")\n seen.add(item_id)\n items.append(\n ChecklistItem(\n item_id=item_id,\n checklist=checklist,\n section=row[\"section\"].strip(),\n text=row[\"item\"].strip(),\n critical=(row.get(\"critical\") or \"\").strip().lower() == \"yes\",\n guidance=(row.get(\"guidance\") or \"\").strip(),\n legacy_id=positional,\n )\n )\n return items\n\n\ndef legacy_item_ids(items: list[ChecklistItem]) -> dict[str, str]:\n \"\"\"Positional id -> stable id, for every item whose id changed.\"\"\"\n return {\n item.legacy_id: item.item_id\n for item in items\n if item.legacy_id and item.legacy_id != item.item_id\n }\n\n\ndef migrate_response_keys(keys: dict, items: list[ChecklistItem] | None = None,\n prefixes: tuple[str, ...] = (\"chk_\", \"rmk_\")) -> dict:\n \"\"\"``keys`` with positional checklist ids replaced by the stable ones.\n\n A project file saved before the CSV carried ids keys its answers by\n position; this carries them onto the questions they were given to. A\n key that already uses a stable id, or one the current CSV does not\n know, is left as it is - nothing is guessed.\n \"\"\"\n legacy = legacy_item_ids(items if items is not None else load_checklists())\n if not legacy:\n return dict(keys)\n out: dict = {}\n for key, value in keys.items():\n for prefix in prefixes:\n if isinstance(key, str) and key.startswith(prefix) and key[len(prefix):] in legacy:\n key = prefix + legacy[key[len(prefix):]]\n break\n out.setdefault(key, value)\n return out\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ChecklistResponse:\n \"\"\"The supervisor's answer to one checklist item.\"\"\"\n\n item_id: str\n status: str = \"pending\" # pending | yes | no | na\n remark: str = \"\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StageProgress:\n stage: str\n title: str\n total: int\n answered: int\n passed: int\n failed: int\n critical_failed: int\n critical_open: int\n\n @property\n def complete(self) -> bool:\n return self.answered == self.total\n\n @property\n def percent(self) -> float:\n return 100.0 * self.answered / self.total if self.total else 0.0\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ChecklistAssessment:\n \"\"\"Roll-up of the responses across all stages.\"\"\"\n\n stages: list[StageProgress]\n flags: list[DataFlag] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n @property\n def total(self) -> int:\n return sum(s.total for s in self.stages)\n\n @property\n def answered(self) -> int:\n return sum(s.answered for s in self.stages)\n\n @property\n def percent(self) -> float:\n return 100.0 * self.answered / self.total if self.total else 0.0\n\n @property\n def critical_failures(self) -> int:\n return sum(s.critical_failed for s in self.stages)\n\n @property\n def verdict(self) -> str:\n if self.critical_failures:\n return (\n f\"{self.critical_failures} critical item(s) failed; the works \"\n \"should not be accepted until they are resolved.\"\n )\n open_critical = sum(s.critical_open for s in self.stages)\n if open_critical:\n return (\n f\"{open_critical} critical item(s) still open; complete them \"\n \"before sign off.\"\n )\n if self.answered < self.total:\n return \"No critical failures; routine items remain open.\"\n return \"All checklist items answered with no critical failures.\"\n\n\ndef evaluate_checklist(\n items: list[ChecklistItem],\n responses: dict[str, ChecklistResponse] | list[ChecklistResponse],\n) -> ChecklistAssessment:\n \"\"\"Score responses against the checklist and flag critical failures.\"\"\"\n if not isinstance(responses, dict):\n responses = {r.item_id: r for r in responses}\n stages: list[StageProgress] = []\n flags: list[DataFlag] = []\n stage_keys = [k for k in STAGE_ORDER if any(i.checklist == k for i in items)]\n stage_keys += sorted({i.checklist for i in items} - set(stage_keys))\n for key in stage_keys:\n stage_items = [i for i in items if i.checklist == key]\n answered = passed = failed = critical_failed = critical_open = 0\n for item in stage_items:\n response = responses.get(item.item_id)\n status = response.status if response else \"pending\"\n if status not in RESPONSE_STATES:\n status = \"pending\"\n if status != \"pending\":\n answered += 1\n if status in (\"yes\", \"na\"):\n passed += 1\n elif status == \"no\":\n failed += 1\n if item.critical:\n critical_failed += 1\n flags.append(\n DataFlag(\n \"error\",\n \"critical_item_failed\",\n item.text,\n context=stage_title(key),\n )\n )\n elif item.critical:\n critical_open += 1\n stages.append(\n StageProgress(\n stage=key,\n title=stage_title(key),\n total=len(stage_items),\n answered=answered,\n passed=passed,\n failed=failed,\n critical_failed=critical_failed,\n critical_open=critical_open,\n )\n )\n return ChecklistAssessment(stages=stages, flags=flags)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SeparationDistance:\n structure: str\n min_distance_m: float\n note: str = \"\"\n\n\ndef load_separation_distances(\n path: str | Path | None = None,\n) -> list[SeparationDistance]:\n \"\"\"Minimum borehole separation distances (FGN/NWRI 2010, via RWSN).\"\"\"\n if path is not None:\n text = Path(path).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n else:\n text = (\n resources.files(\"groundwater\") / \"data\" / \"site_separation_distances.csv\"\n ).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n return [\n SeparationDistance(\n structure=row[\"structure\"].strip(),\n min_distance_m=float(row[\"min_distance_m\"]),\n note=(row.get(\"note\") or \"\").strip(),\n )\n for row in csv.DictReader(text.splitlines())\n ]\n"}, "groundwater/supervision/field_checks.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Field acceptance checks and calculators for drilling supervision.\n\nEach function encodes a numeric standard from RWSN/UNICEF \"Supervising\nWater Well Drilling\" so the supervisor can check acceptance criteria\non site: sand content, verticality, screen open area, the handpump\nspecific capacity rule and the WHO chlorine disinfection dose.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Optional\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"The outcome of one field acceptance check.\"\"\"\n\n name: str\n passed: Optional[bool] # None when the check is informational\n measured: str\n limit: str\n message: str\n\n @property\n def status(self) -> str:\n if self.passed is None:\n return \"info\"\n return \"pass\" if self.passed else \"fail\"\n\n\ndef sand_content_check(samples_cm3: list[float], sample_volume_l: float = 20.0) -> FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"Sand content at the end of the pumping test.\n\n Three 20 litre samples are collected; the settled sand in each must\n not exceed 0.2 cubic centimetres (10 parts per million by volume).\n \"\"\"\n limit_cm3 = sample_volume_l * 1000.0 * 10e-6 # 10 ppm by volume, in cm3\n worst = max(samples_cm3) if samples_cm3 else 0.0\n passed = bool(samples_cm3) and worst <= limit_cm3\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Sand content\",\n passed=passed if samples_cm3 else None,\n measured=f\"{worst:g} cm3 worst of {len(samples_cm3)} sample(s)\",\n limit=f\"{limit_cm3:g} cm3 per {sample_volume_l:g} L sample (10 ppm by volume)\",\n message=(\n \"Sand content acceptable.\"\n if passed\n else \"Excessive sand: check drilling technique, gravel pack and \"\n \"development; a replacement borehole may be at the driller's cost.\"\n ),\n )\n\n\ndef verticality_check(\n deviation_mm: float, depth_m: float, casing_inner_diameter_mm: float\n) -> FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"Plumb test: deviation must not exceed two thirds of the casing\n inner diameter per 30 m of depth.\"\"\"\n allowed_mm = (2.0 / 3.0) * casing_inner_diameter_mm * (depth_m / 30.0)\n passed = deviation_mm <= allowed_mm\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Verticality (plumb test)\",\n passed=passed,\n measured=f\"{deviation_mm:g} mm over {depth_m:g} m\",\n limit=f\"{allowed_mm:.0f} mm (two thirds of {casing_inner_diameter_mm:g} mm ID per 30 m)\",\n message=(\n \"Borehole is acceptably straight and vertical.\"\n if passed\n else \"Deviation exceeds the limit; the driller re-drills at own cost.\"\n ),\n )\n\n\ndef screen_open_area_check(\n design_yield_l_per_s: float, screen_open_area_m2: float\n) -> FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"Screen entrance velocity rule: open area A >= Q/30 (A in m2, Q in\n L/s) keeps the entrance velocity below 0.03 m/s.\"\"\"\n required = design_yield_l_per_s / 30.0\n passed = screen_open_area_m2 >= required\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Screen open area\",\n passed=passed,\n measured=f\"{screen_open_area_m2:g} m2\",\n limit=f\">= {required:.3f} m2 for Q = {design_yield_l_per_s:g} L/s\",\n message=(\n \"Entrance velocity within 0.03 m/s.\"\n if passed\n else \"Open area too small: turbulent inflow, encrustation and a \"\n \"shortened screen life are likely; use more or larger screen.\"\n ),\n )\n\n\ndef specific_capacity_check(\n discharge_m3_per_h: float, drawdown_m: float\n) -> FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"Handpump adequacy rule of thumb: a specific capacity around\n 1 m3/h per metre of drawdown suggests the borehole suits a handpump.\"\"\"\n if drawdown_m <= 0:\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Specific capacity\",\n passed=None,\n measured=\"n/a\",\n limit=\">= 1 m3/h per m for a handpump\",\n message=\"Drawdown must be positive to compute specific capacity.\",\n )\n sc = discharge_m3_per_h / drawdown_m\n passed = sc >= 1.0\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Specific capacity\",\n passed=passed,\n measured=f\"{sc:.2f} m3/h per m\",\n limit=\">= 1 m3/h per m for a handpump\",\n message=(\n \"Adequate for a handpump (about 1 m drawdown at 1 m3/h).\"\n if passed\n else \"Below the handpump rule of thumb; review the test data and \"\n \"the pump setting before acceptance.\"\n ),\n )\n\n\ndef pack_aquifer_ratio_check(d50_pack_mm: float, d50_aquifer_mm: float) -> FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"Filter pack sizing: pack D50 / aquifer D50 should be 4 to 6.\"\"\"\n if d50_aquifer_mm <= 0:\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Pack aquifer ratio\",\n passed=None,\n measured=\"n/a\",\n limit=\"4 to 6\",\n message=\"Aquifer D50 must be positive.\",\n )\n ratio = d50_pack_mm / d50_aquifer_mm\n passed = 4.0 <= ratio <= 6.0\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Pack aquifer ratio\",\n passed=passed,\n measured=f\"{ratio:.1f}\",\n limit=\"4 to 6 (D50 pack / D50 aquifer)\",\n message=(\n \"Filter pack correctly sized for the formation.\"\n if passed\n else \"Pack aquifer ratio outside 4 to 6: risk of sand pumping \"\n \"(too coarse) or a choked screen (too fine).\"\n ),\n )\n\n\ndef annular_space_check(\n borehole_diameter_in: float, casing_od_mm: float\n) -> FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"Annular space rule: at least 50 mm all round for placement, and a\n gravel pack needs at least 70 mm to work as a filter (thinner is\n only a formation stabiliser).\"\"\"\n borehole_mm = borehole_diameter_in * 25.4\n annulus_mm = (borehole_mm - casing_od_mm) / 2.0\n passed = annulus_mm >= 50.0\n if annulus_mm >= 70.0:\n note = \"Full gravel pack possible.\"\n elif passed:\n note = (\n \"Meets the 50 mm placement minimum, but under 70 mm the annular \"\n \"fill acts as a formation stabiliser rather than a filter pack.\"\n )\n else:\n note = (\n \"Annulus below the 50 mm minimum: gravel is likely to bridge \"\n \"during placement; use a larger bit or smaller casing.\"\n )\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Annular space\",\n passed=passed,\n measured=f\"{annulus_mm:.0f} mm\",\n limit=\">= 50 mm (70 mm for a true gravel pack)\",\n message=note,\n )\n\n\ndef metres_reconciliation_check(\n logged_m: float, claimed_m: float, tolerance_m: float = 3.0\n) -> FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"Compare invoiced metres against the signed daily drilling logs.\n\n Paying per metre invites overstated depths; the daily logs (signed\n by the rig operator and the supervisor) are the audit trail.
