The\n 3 m tolerance mirrors the casing reconciliation rule in the\n supervision guidance.\n \"\"\"\n difference = claimed_m - logged_m\n passed = difference <= tolerance_m\n if difference > tolerance_m:\n message = (\n f\"Invoice claims {difference:g} m more than the signed daily \"\n \"logs; withhold payment for the unsupported metres and \"\n \"reconcile with the driller.\"\n )\n elif difference < -tolerance_m:\n message = (\n \"Logs record more metres than invoiced; check that the invoice \"\n \"covers all completed work.\"\n )\n else:\n message = \"Invoiced metres are supported by the daily logs.\"\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Drilled metres reconciliation\",\n passed=passed,\n measured=f\"logged {logged_m:g} m, invoiced {claimed_m:g} m\",\n limit=f\"difference within {tolerance_m:g} m\",\n message=message,\n )\n\n\ndef handpump_corrosion_check(ph: float) -> FieldCheck:\n \"\"\"Handpump corrosion risk rule (RWSN Stop the Rot).\n\n Below pH 6.5 galvanised iron riser pipes and rods corrode rapidly\n (failures within 3 months to 2 years), shedding iron and possibly\n heavy metals into the supply; corrosion resistant components\n (stainless steel 304/316 or uPVC risers) must be used instead.\n \"\"\"\n at_risk = ph < 6.5\n return FieldCheck(\n name=\"Handpump corrosion risk\",\n passed=not at_risk,\n measured=f\"pH {ph:g}\",\n limit=\">= 6.5 for galvanised iron components\",\n message=(\n \"Corrosion risk low; standard components acceptable.\"\n if not at_risk\n else \"Corrosive water: specify stainless steel (grade 304/316) \"\n \"or uPVC riser pipes and rods; galvanised iron can fail within \"\n \"months and taint the water with iron.\"\n ),\n )\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass DisinfectionDose:\n \"\"\"Chlorine quantities for shock disinfection at 20 mg/L (WHO).\"\"\"\n\n well_volume_l: float\n solution_02pct_l: float # litres of 0.2 percent chlorine solution\n hth_grams: float # grams of 65 percent HTH powder for that solution\n contact_hours: float = 4.0\n\n def summary(self) -> str:\n return (\n f\"Well volume about {self.well_volume_l:,.0f} L: add \"\n f\"{self.solution_02pct_l:,.1f} L of 0.2% chlorine solution \"\n f\"(about {self.hth_grams:,.0f} g of 65% HTH in that much water) \"\n f\"and wait at least {self.contact_hours:g} hours before pumping.\"\n )\n\n\ndef disinfection_dose(\n water_column_m: float, casing_inner_diameter_mm: float\n) -> DisinfectionDose:\n \"\"\"WHO shock dose: 1 L of 0.2 percent solution per 100 L of well\n volume gives 20 mg/L; do not pump for at least 4 hours.\"\"\"\n radius_m = casing_inner_diameter_mm / 2000.0\n volume_l = math.pi * radius_m**2 * max(0.0, water_column_m) * 1000.0\n solution_l = volume_l / 100.0\n # 0.2 percent solution = 2 g chlorine per litre; 65 percent HTH\n # carries 0.65 g available chlorine per gram of powder.\n hth_grams = solution_l * 2.0 / 0.65\n return DisinfectionDose(\n well_volume_l=volume_l,\n solution_02pct_l=solution_l,\n hth_grams=hth_grams,\n )\n"}, "groundwater/units.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Unit strings as field sheets and laboratories actually write them.\n\nEvery number this toolkit reads arrives beside a unit written by hand, and\nuntil now those units were decoration: a laboratory result was compared\nagainst a guideline value whatever unit each carried, and a pumping test's\ndischarge was taken as cubic metres per hour whatever the sheet said. Both\nare silent, order-of-magnitude errors. An arsenic result of 5 reported in\nug/L is a quarter of the WHO guideline; read as mg/L it is five hundred\ntimes over it, and the same arithmetic run the other way certifies unsafe\nwater as safe. A discharge of 2 L/s read as 2 m3/h understates the yield by\na factor of 1.8.\n\nSo units are parsed, not assumed. Each recognised spelling maps onto a\n:class:`Unit` carrying a dimension and a factor to that dimension's base,\nand two quantities are comparable only when their dimensions agree. A\nspelling this module does not recognise is *not* guessed at: the caller is\ntold it could not be read, and the toolkit reports the value as\nindeterminate rather than grading it against a limit it may not share a\nscale with.\n\nBases: concentration mg/L, conductivity uS/cm, turbidity NTU, microbial\nCFU/100 mL, flow m3/h, time min, length m.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom .utils import parse_number\n\n__all__ = [\n \"Unit\",\n \"Quantity\",\n \"parse_unit\",\n \"convert\",\n \"comparable\",\n \"canonical_unit\",\n \"unit_from_label\",\n \"read_quantity\",\n \"AMBIGUOUS_UNITS\",\n \"CANONICAL_UNITS\",\n]\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Unit:\n \"\"\"A recognised unit and how to reach its dimension's base unit.\n\n ``value_in_base = value * factor + offset``. ``basis`` records a\n chemical reference the unit itself names (\"as CaCO3\", \"as N\"); two\n units that both name a basis are comparable only when it is the same\n one, because 10 mg/L as N and 10 mg/L as NO3 are different waters.\n \"\"\"\n\n canonical: str\n dimension: str\n factor: float\n offset: float = 0.0\n basis: str = \"\"\n\n\n#: Spellings that name a real quantity but do not pin it down. Guessing at\n#: one of these is exactly the failure this module exists to prevent, so\n#: they are refused by name and the message says why.\nAMBIGUOUS_UNITS = {\n \"gpm\": \"gallons per minute is ambiguous (US gallon 3.785 L, imperial 4.546 L)\",\n \"gph\": \"gallons per hour is ambiguous (US gallon 3.785 L, imperial 4.546 L)\",\n \"gal/min\": \"gallons per minute is ambiguous (US gallon 3.785 L, imperial 4.546 L)\",\n \"gal/h\": \"gallons per hour is ambiguous (US gallon 3.785 L, imperial 4.546 L)\",\n \"ppt\": \"ppt means parts per thousand to some laboratories and parts per \"\n \"trillion to others\",\n \"jtu\": \"Jackson turbidity units are not numerically interchangeable with NTU\",\n}\n\n# Superscripts and micro signs as spreadsheets, PDFs and handwriting produce\n# them. Normalised away before anything is matched.\n_CHAR_FIXES = {\n \"\u00b5\": \"u\", # MICRO SIGN\n \"\u03bc\": \"u\", # GREEK SMALL LETTER MU\n \"\u00b3\": \"3\", # SUPERSCRIPT THREE\n \"\u00b2\": \"2\",\n \"\u00b0\": \"deg \",\n \"\u2044\": \"/\", # FRACTION SLASH\n \"\u2019\": \"\",\n}\n\n_BASIS_RE = re.compile(r\"\\bas\\s+([a-z0-9()\\.\\-]+)\\s*$\")\n\n\ndef _normalise(text: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Lowercase and regularise a written unit before matching it.\"\"\"\n s = str(text or \"\")\n for bad, good in _CHAR_FIXES.items():\n s = s.replace(bad, good)\n s = s.lower().strip()\n s = s.replace(\"\u2013\", \"-\").replace(\"\u2014\", \"-\")\n # \"per\" written out, and the odd \"l per s\"\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bper\\b\", \"/\", s)\n # spelled-out units, longest first so \"minutes\" does not become \"min utes\"\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bmilli\\s*litres?\\b|\\bmilli\\s*liters?\\b|\\bmillilitres?\\b\"\n r\"|\\bmilliliters?\\b\", \"ml\", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\blitres?\\b|\\bliters?\\b\", \"l\", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bmetres?\\b|\\bmeters?\\b\", \"m\", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bcubic\\s*m\\b\", \"m3\", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bminutes?\\b|\\bmins\\b\", \"min\", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bseconds?\\b|\\bsecs\\b\", \"s\", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bhours?\\b|\\bhrs\\b\", \"h\", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bdays?\\b\", \"d\", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bdegrees?\\b|\\bdeg\\b\", \"deg \", s)\n s = re.sub(r\"\\bcelsius\\b|\\bcentigrade\\b\", \"c\", s)\n s = s.replace(\".\", \"\")\n # \"-\", \"n/a\" and friends are how a sheet writes \"no unit here\", not a\n # unit. Reading \"-\" as pH units made every non-pH row carrying the\n # ordinary blank marker unevaluable.\n if s in (\"-\", \"--\", \"n/a\", \"na\", \"none\", \"nil\", \"?\"):\n return \"\"\n # collapse whitespace, and drop it around a solidus so \"mg / l\" == \"mg/l\"\n s = re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", s).strip()\n return re.sub(r\"\\s*/\\s*\", \"/\", s)\n\n\ndef _split_basis(text: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"Separate a trailing chemical basis: \"mg/l as caco3\" -> (\"mg/l\", \"caco3\").\"\"\"\n match = _BASIS_RE.search(text)\n if not match:\n return text, \"\"\n return text[: match.start()].strip(), match.group(1).replace(\" \", \"\")\n\n\n# (dimension, factor to base, offset), keyed by normalised spelling.\n_UNITS: dict[str, tuple[str, str, float, float]] = {}\n\n\ndef _register(canonical: str, dimension: str, factor: float,\n spellings: list[str], offset: float = 0.0) -> None:\n for spelling in spellings:\n _UNITS[_normalise(spelling)] = (canonical, dimension, factor, offset)\n\n\n# --- concentration, base mg/L ------------------------------------------------\n_register(\"mg/L\", \"concentration\", 1.0,\n [\"mg/l\", \"mg/L\", \"milligrams/l\", \"mg per l\", \"mg/dm3\", \"ppm\",\n \"parts per million\", \"g/m3\"])\n_register(\"ug/L\", \"concentration\", 1e-3,\n [\"ug/l\", \"\u00b5g/l\", \"\u03bcg/l\", \"mcg/l\", \"ppb\",\n \"parts per billion\", \"mg/m3\"])\n_register(\"ng/L\", \"concentration\", 1e-6, [\"ng/l\", \"ppt-mass-ng\"])\n_register(\"g/L\", \"concentration\", 1e3, [\"g/l\", \"g/dm3\", \"kg/m3\"])\n_register(\"mg/mL\", \"concentration\", 1e3, [\"mg/ml\"])\n\n# --- electrical conductivity, base uS/cm ------------------------------------\n_register(\"uS/cm\", \"conductivity\", 1.0,\n [\"us/cm\", \"\u00b5s/cm\", \"\u03bcs/cm\", \"umho/cm\", \"umhos/cm\",\n \"micro siemens/cm\"])\n_register(\"mS/cm\", \"conductivity\", 1e3, [\"ms/cm\", \"mmho/cm\", \"mmhos/cm\"])\n_register(\"mS/m\", \"conductivity\", 10.0, [\"ms/m\"])\n_register(\"S/m\", \"conductivity\", 1e4, [\"s/m\"])\n\n# --- turbidity, base NTU ----------------------------------------------------\n# NTU, FNU and FTU are numerically interchangeable by convention; JTU is not,\n# and is refused above rather than converted.\n_register(\"NTU\", \"turbidity\", 1.0, [\"ntu\", \"fnu\", \"ftu\", \"nephelometric\"])\n\n# --- microbiological, base CFU/100 mL ---------------------------------------\n_register(\"CFU/100 mL\", \"microbial\", 1.0,\n [\"cfu/100ml\", \"cfu/100 ml\", \"mpn/100ml\", \"mpn/100 ml\", \"/100ml\",\n \"count/100ml\", \"counts/100ml\", \"no/100ml\", \"cfu/100cm3\"])\n_register(\"CFU/mL\", \"microbial\", 100.0, [\"cfu/ml\", \"mpn/ml\", \"count/ml\"])\n_register(\"CFU/L\", \"microbial\", 0.1, [\"cfu/l\", \"mpn/l\", \"count/l\"])\n\n# --- pH ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n_register(\"pH units\", \"ph\", 1.0, [\"ph units\", \"ph unit\", \"ph\", \"su\",\n \"standard units\"])\n\n# --- temperature, base deg C ------------------------------------------------\n_register(\"deg C\", \"temperature\", 1.0, [\"deg c\", \"c\", \"\u00b0c\", \"degc\",\n \"celsius\"])\n_register(\"deg F\", \"temperature\", 5.0 / 9.0, [\"deg f\", \"f\", \"\u00b0f\", \"degf\"],\n offset=-32.0 * 5.0 / 9.0)\n\n# --- volumetric flow, base m3/h ---------------------------------------------\n_register(\"m3/h\", \"flow\", 1.0,\n [\"m3/h\", \"m3/hr\", \"m\u00b3/h\", \"cum/h\", \"cubic m/h\", \"m3 h-1\"])\n_register(\"m3/d\", \"flow\", 1.0 / 24.0, [\"m3/d\", \"m3/day\", \"cum/d\"])\n_register(\"m3/min\", \"flow\", 60.0, [\"m3/min\"])\n_register(\"m3/s\", \"flow\", 3600.0, [\"m3/s\"])\n_register(\"L/s\", \"flow\", 3.6, [\"l/s\", \"lps\", \"l s-1\"])\n_register(\"L/min\", \"flow\", 0.06, [\"l/min\", \"lpm\", \"l/m\"])\n_register(\"L/h\", \"flow\", 1e-3, [\"l/h\", \"lph\"])\n_register(\"L/d\", \"flow\", 1e-3 / 24.0, [\"l/d\", \"l/day\"])\n\n# --- time, base minutes -----------------------------------------------------\n_register(\"min\", \"time\", 1.0, [\"min\", \"mins\", \"minute\"])\n_register(\"s\", \"time\", 1.0 / 60.0, [\"s\", \"sec\"])\n_register(\"h\", \"time\", 60.0, [\"h\", \"hr\"])\n_register(\"d\", \"time\", 1440.0, [\"d\", \"day\"])\n\n# --- length, base metres ----------------------------------------------------\n_register(\"m\", \"length\", 1.0, [\"m\", \"metre\"])\n_register(\"cm\", \"length\", 0.01, [\"cm\"])\n_register(\"mm\", \"length\", 1e-3, [\"mm\"])\n_register(\"ft\", \"length\", 0.3048, [\"ft\", \"feet\", \"foot\"])\n_register(\"in\", \"length\", 0.0254, [\"in\", \"inch\", \"inches\", '\"'])\n\n#: Dimensions where a bare \"m\", \"s\" or \"d\" is meant as this dimension. A unit\n#: string alone cannot tell metres from minutes-of-arc; the caller says which\n#: family it is reading, so \"m\" in a depth column is length and \"min\" in a\n#: time column is time.\n_DIMENSION_HINT_OVERRIDES = {\n (\"time\", \"m\"): (\"min\", \"time\", 1.0, 0.0),\n (\"time\", \"min\"): (\"min\", \"time\", 1.0, 0.0),\n (\"length\", \"m\"): (\"m\", \"length\", 1.0, 0.0),\n (\"concentration\", \"-\"): None,\n}\n\n\ndef parse_unit(text: str, *, dimension: str | None = None) -> Optional[Unit]:\n \"\"\"Read a written unit, or ``None`` when it cannot be read with confidence.\n\n ``dimension`` disambiguates spellings that mean different things in\n different columns - a bare \"m\" is metres in a depth column and minutes\n in a time column - and, when given, also rejects a unit belonging to\n another family outright.\n \"\"\"\n normalised = _normalise(text)\n if not normalised:\n return None\n body, basis = _split_basis(normalised)\n if body in AMBIGUOUS_UNITS or normalised in AMBIGUOUS_UNITS:\n return None\n\n if dimension is not None:\n override = _DIMENSION_HINT_OVERRIDES.get((dimension, body))\n if override is not None:\n canonical, dim, factor, offset = override\n return Unit(canonical, dim, factor, offset, basis)\n\n entry = _UNITS.get(body)\n if entry is None:\n return None\n canonical, dim, factor, offset = entry\n if dimension is not None and dim != dimension:\n return None\n return Unit(canonical, dim, factor, offset, basis)\n\n\ndef canonical_unit(text: str, *, dimension: str | None = None) -> str:\n \"\"\"The canonical spelling of a unit, or the text as written if unknown.\"\"\"\n unit = parse_unit(text, dimension=dimension)\n return unit.canonical if unit is not None else str(text or \"\").strip()\n\n\ndef comparable(a: Unit | None, b: Unit | None) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether two parsed units measure the same thing on the same basis.\n\n A basis stated on one side only is accepted: a laboratory writing plain\n \"mg/L\" for hardness against a \"mg/L as CaCO3\" guideline means the same\n thing, and the parameter name already carries the reference. Two\n *different* stated bases are refused, because \"as N\" and \"as NO3\" are\n not the same number.\n \"\"\"\n if a is None or b is None:\n return False\n if a.dimension != b.dimension:\n return False\n if a.basis and b.basis and a.basis != b.basis:\n return False\n return True\n\n\n#: The unit each dimension is stored in once a sheet has been read. Field\n#: names elsewhere in the package encode these - ``discharge_m3_per_h``,\n#: ``time_min`` - so they are the contract, not a preference.\nCANONICAL_UNITS = {\n \"concentration\": \"mg/L\",\n \"conductivity\": \"uS/cm\",\n \"turbidity\": \"NTU\",\n \"microbial\": \"CFU/100 mL\",\n \"ph\": \"pH units\",\n \"temperature\": \"deg C\",\n \"flow\": \"m3/h\",\n \"time\": \"min\",\n \"length\": \"m\",\n}\n\n# A unit written on a field sheet appears in brackets: \"Time (min)\",\n# \"Discharge per step (m3/h)\", \"Q [L/s]\". Only bracketed text is treated as a\n# declared unit, so an ordinary word in a label (\"Discharge per step\") is\n# never mistaken for one and never reported as unreadable.\n_BRACKETED_RE = re.compile(r\"[(\\[]([^)\\]]{1,20})[)\\]]\")\n_RANGE_IN_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"\\d\\s*-\\s*\\d\")\n_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r\"[-+]?\\d*\\.?\\d+(?:[eE][-+]?\\d+)?\")\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Quantity:\n \"\"\"A number read off a sheet together with what its unit turned out to be.\n\n ``value`` is in the dimension's canonical unit and is ``None`` whenever\n the reading must not be used - an unrecognised unit is refused, never\n guessed at. ``status`` is one of:\n\n ``\"absent\"``\n no number in the cell at all.\n ``\"ok\"``\n a unit was declared and it is already the canonical one.\n ``\"converted\"``\n a unit was declared and the value has been scaled onto the canonical\n one; ``unit_text`` says which.\n ``\"assumed\"``\n no unit was declared anywhere, so the canonical one was assumed.\n ``\"unknown\"``\n a unit was declared and could not be read. ``value`` is ``None``.\n \"\"\"\n\n value: Optional[float]\n raw_value: Optional[float]\n unit_text: str\n status: str\n dimension: str = \"\"\n\n @property\n def ok(self) -> bool:\n return self.value is not None\n\n\ndef _is_unit_shaped(text: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Whether a bracketed group is shaped like a unit rather than a word.\n\n Every unit a field sheet writes is short, or carries a solidus, or\n carries a digit: \"min\", \"hrs\", \"L/s\", \"m3/h\", \"uS/cm\". A longer bare\n word is a description of the column - \"Time (elapsed)\", \"(cumulative)\",\n \"(recovery)\" - and treating one as an unreadable unit threw away every\n reading in the column, which is a far worse answer than reading the\n times in the minutes the sheet's own template uses.\n \"\"\"\n normalised = _normalise(text)\n if not normalised or not any(ch.isalpha() for ch in normalised):\n return False\n # \"0-60 min\" is a range of readings and \"mm:ss\" is a clock format; both\n # describe the column rather than scaling it.\n if _RANGE_IN_LABEL_RE.search(normalised) or \":\" in normalised:\n return False\n return (\"/\" in normalised or any(ch.isdigit() for ch in normalised)\n or len(normalised) <= 5)\n\n\ndef unit_from_label(text: str, *, dimension: str) -> tuple[str, Optional[Unit]]:\n \"\"\"The unit a column header or row label declares, if any.\n\n Returns ``(written, parsed)``. ``(\"\", None)`` means nothing was declared;\n ``(\"L/s\", Unit(...))`` means it was declared and read; ``(\"fur/s\",\n None)`` means a unit was declared and could not be read, which the\n caller must treat as a refusal rather than a default.\n \"\"\"\n raw = str(text or \"\")\n first_written = \"\"\n for match in _BRACKETED_RE.finditer(raw):\n candidate = match.group(1).strip()\n if not candidate:\n continue\n # \"(0-60 min)\" and \"(step or constant)\" are prose, not units\n if len(candidate.split()) > 2 or _NUMBER_RE.fullmatch(candidate):\n continue\n unit = parse_unit(candidate, dimension=dimension)\n if unit is not None:\n return candidate, unit\n if not first_written and _is_unit_shaped(candidate):\n first_written = candidate\n return first_written, None\n\n\n# A unit beside a number is a short token: \"L/s\", \"m3/h\", \"min\". Anything\n# longer, or with a space inside, or with no letter in it, is a field\n# annotation - \"5 (pump off)\", \"12 pump stopped\", \"5*\" - and reading one as a\n# unit refused the reading and, for a time column, dropped the whole series.\n_CELL_UNIT_RE = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9/\\u00b3\\u00b2^-]{1,12}$\")\n\n\ndef _unit_in_cell(cell) -> str:\n \"\"\"Any unit written next to the number inside a value cell itself.\n\n A crew that types \"0.81 L/s\" into a column headed m3/h means L/s, so the\n cell outranks its header. A note written beside the reading is not a\n unit and is ignored, so the header still speaks for the column.\n \"\"\"\n if cell is None or isinstance(cell, (int, float)):\n return \"\"\n text = str(cell).strip().replace(\",\", \"\")\n match = _NUMBER_RE.search(text)\n if match is None:\n return \"\"\n tail = (text[: match.start()] + \" \" + text[match.end():]).strip()\n tail = tail.strip(\"()[]:= \\t\")\n if not tail:\n return \"\"\n normalised = _normalise(tail)\n if not normalised or not _CELL_UNIT_RE.match(normalised):\n return \"\"\n if not any(ch.isalpha() for ch in normalised):\n return \"\"\n return tail\n\n\ndef read_quantity(cell, *hints: str, dimension: str) -> Quantity:\n \"\"\"Read a value off a sheet and put it in the canonical unit.\n\n The unit is taken from the cell's own text first, then from each hint in\n turn - typically the column header, then the row label. ``hints`` are\n scanned with :func:`unit_from_label`, so only bracketed text counts.\n \"\"\"\n canonical = CANONICAL_UNITS[dimension]\n raw = parse_number(cell)\n if raw is None:\n return Quantity(None, None, \"\", \"absent\", dimension)\n\n written = _unit_in_cell(cell)\n if written:\n unit = parse_unit(written, dimension=dimension)\n if unit is None:\n return Quantity(None, raw, written, \"unknown\", dimension)\n value = convert(raw, written, canonical, dimension=dimension)\n status = \"ok\" if unit.canonical == canonical else \"converted\"\n return Quantity(value, raw, written, status, dimension)\n\n for hint in hints:\n declared, unit = unit_from_label(hint, dimension=dimension)\n if not declared:\n continue\n if unit is None:\n return Quantity(None, raw, declared, \"unknown\", dimension)\n value = convert(raw, declared, canonical, dimension=dimension)\n status = \"ok\" if unit.canonical == canonical else \"converted\"\n return Quantity(value, raw, declared, status, dimension)\n\n return Quantity(float(raw), raw, \"\", \"assumed\", dimension)\n\n\ndef convert(value: float, from_unit: str, to_unit: str,\n *, dimension: str | None = None) -> Optional[float]:\n \"\"\"Convert ``value`` between two written units, or ``None`` if it cannot.\n\n ``None`` means \"do not use this number against that limit\" - either\n unit was unreadable, or they measure different things. It never means\n zero and must never be treated as a pass.\n \"\"\"\n source = parse_unit(from_unit, dimension=dimension)\n target = parse_unit(to_unit, dimension=dimension)\n if not comparable(source, target):\n return None\n base = float(value) * source.factor + source.offset\n return (base - target.offset) / target.factor\n"}, "groundwater/utils.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Shared utilities: robust number parsing, rounding and formatting.\n\nField sheets and transcribed reports carry values such as ``078.7``\n(leading zeros), ``80m`` (units appended), ``19.28M`` or ``6.5''``.\nThe helpers here turn those into clean floats and format numbers\nconsistently across figures, tables and reports.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport datetime\nimport math\nimport re\nfrom typing import Iterable\n\n_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r\"[-+]?\\d*\\.?\\d+(?:[eE][-+]?\\d+)?\")\n# a comma followed by exactly three digits that end the number is a thousands\n# separator; any other comma between digits is a decimal point\n_THOUSANDS_RE = re.compile(r\"(?<=\\d),(?=\\d{3}(?!\\d))\")\n_DECIMAL_COMMA_RE = re.compile(r\"(?<=\\d),(?=\\d)\")\n\n\ndef parse_number(value, default=None) -> float | None:\n \"\"\"Parse a numeric value from field data.\n\n Handles plain numbers, strings with leading zeros (``078.7``),\n appended units (``80m``, ``19.28M``, ``2,933lts/hr``), thousands\n separators and stray whitespace. Returns ``default`` (``None``\n unless given) when no number can be found.\n\n >>> parse_number(\"078.7\")\n 78.7\n >>> parse_number(\"0708958\")\n 708958.0\n >>> parse_number(\"19.28M\")\n 19.28\n >>> parse_number(\"2,933\")\n 2933.0\n >>> parse_number(\"\") is None\n True\n\n A comma is a thousands separator only when exactly three digits follow\n it and end the number; otherwise it is a decimal comma, which crews\n trained on French-language sheets type as a matter of course. ``1,5``\n used to parse as 15 and ``078,7`` as 787, a silent tenfold error in an\n electrode spacing or a resistivity.\n\n >>> parse_number(\"1,5\")\n 1.5\n >>> parse_number(\"078,7\")\n 78.7\n >>> parse_number(\"1.234,5\")\n 1234.5\n >>> parse_number(\"12,345,678\")\n 12345678.0\n \"\"\"\n if value is None:\n return default\n if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n if isinstance(value, float) and math.isnan(value):\n return default\n return float(value)\n text = str(value).strip()\n if not text:\n return default\n if \",\" in text:\n if \".\" in text and text.rfind(\",\") > text.rfind(\".\"):\n # 1.234,5 - point-grouped thousands with a decimal comma\n text = text.replace(\".\", \"\").replace(\",\", \".\")\n else:\n text = _THOUSANDS_RE.sub(\"\", text)\n text = _DECIMAL_COMMA_RE.sub(\".\", text)\n text = text.replace(\",\", \"\")\n match = _NUMBER_RE.search(text)\n if match is None:\n return default\n return float(match.group(0))\n\n\n_INTERVAL_RE = re.compile(\n r\"(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*(?:-|to)\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\", re.IGNORECASE\n)\n\n\ndef parse_depth_interval(value) -> tuple[float, float] | None:\n \"\"\"Parse a depth interval such as ``0-5``, ``5 - 10`` or ``12 to 18 m``.\n\n Depths are unsigned; the hyphen is the range separator, never a\n minus sign. Returns ``(top, bottom)`` in metres or ``None``.\n\n A date is never an interval. Excel silently turns ``5-10`` typed into a\n General cell into 10 May, and openpyxl hands that back as a datetime;\n read as text it yielded a 5 to 2026 m interval, which then placed\n screens and priced casing against a two-kilometre hole.\n\n >>> import datetime\n >>> parse_depth_interval(datetime.datetime(2026, 5, 10)) is None\n True\n \"\"\"\n if value is None or isinstance(value, (datetime.date, datetime.datetime)):\n return None\n match = _INTERVAL_RE.search(str(value))\n if match is None:\n return None\n top, bottom = float(match.group(1)), float(match.group(2))\n if bottom < top:\n top, bottom = bottom, top\n return top, bottom\n\n\ndef round_sig(value: float, sig: int = 3) -> float:\n \"\"\"Round ``value`` to ``sig`` significant figures.\n\n >>> round_sig(2102.804, 4)\n 2103.0\n >>> round_sig(0.0123456, 3)\n 0.0123\n \"\"\"\n if value == 0 or not math.isfinite(value):\n return value\n ndigits = sig - 1 - int(math.floor(math.log10(abs(value))))\n return round(value, ndigits)\n\n\ndef fmt_num(value, sig: int = 3, unit: str = \"\") -> str:\n \"\"\"Format a number for reports with consistent significant figures.\n\n Integers within tolerance print without a decimal part. ``None``\n or NaN prints as an em-dash free placeholder ``n/a``.\n \"\"\"\n if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value)):\n return \"n/a\"\n v = round_sig(float(value), sig)\n if abs(v - round(v)) < 1e-9 and abs(v) < 1e15:\n text = f\"{int(round(v)):,}\"\n else:\n text = f\"{v:g}\"\n return f\"{text} {unit}\".strip() if unit else text\n\n\ndef fmt_range(a, b, unit: str = \"m\", sep: str = \"-\") -> str:\n \"\"\"Format a depth range such as ``20-30 m``.\"\"\"\n return f\"{fmt_num(a)}{sep}{fmt_num(b)} {unit}\".strip()\n\n\ndef ordinal(n: int) -> str:\n \"\"\"Return ``1st``, ``2nd``, ``3rd``, ``4th`` ... for ranking tables.\"\"\"\n if 10 <= n % 100 <= 20:\n suffix = \"th\"\n else:\n suffix = {1: \"st\", 2: \"nd\", 3: \"rd\"}.get(n % 10, \"th\")\n return f\"{n}{suffix}\"\n\n\ndef strictly_increasing(values: Iterable[float]) -> bool:\n vals = list(values)\n # vals[1:] is one shorter by design - each value pairs with its successor.\n return all(b > a for a, b in zip(vals, vals[1:], strict=False))\n\n\ndef clean_text(value) -> str:\n \"\"\"Normalise whitespace in a text cell; empty for None.\"\"\"\n if value is None:\n return \"\"\n return re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", str(value)).strip()\n\n\ndef safe_slug(value, default: str = \"item\") -> str:\n \"\"\"A filesystem-safe slug for building figure filenames.\n\n Keeps only ``[A-Za-z0-9_-]`` so an identifier such as a borehole ref or\n community name cannot introduce path separators or collide across sites\n when several reports share one figures directory.\n \"\"\"\n slug = re.sub(r\"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]+\", \"_\", str(value or \"\")).strip(\"_\")\n return slug or default\n\n\ndef utm_text(site, axis: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"``\"778000 m E (UTM zone 28N)\"``: a grid coordinate as a coordinate.\n\n Reports printed \"778,000\" with a thousands separator and no zone, which\n is a number, not a position anyone can type into a GPS.\n \"\"\"\n value = getattr(site, axis, None)\n if value is None:\n return \"\"\n utm = getattr(site, \"utm\", None)\n zone = f\" (UTM zone {utm.zone}N)\" if utm is not None and axis == \"easting\" else \"\"\n letter = \"E\" if axis == \"easting\" else \"N\"\n return f\"{float(value):.0f} m {letter}{zone}\"\n\n\ndef plural(count: int, singular: str, plural_form: str | None = None) -> str:\n \"\"\"``\"1 point\"``, ``\"2 points\"``: the noun agrees with the count.\n\n Reports used to print \"2 vertical electrical sounding point(s)\" and\n \"Health based exceedance(s): Manganese\", which is a form, not a\n sentence.\n \"\"\"\n word = singular if count == 1 else (plural_form or singular + \"s\")\n return f\"{count} {word}\"\n\n\ndef plural_noun(count: int, singular: str, plural_form: str | None = None) -> str:\n \"\"\"The noun alone, agreeing with a count the sentence already carries.\"\"\"\n return singular if count == 1 else (plural_form or singular + \"s\")\n"}, "groundwater/ves/__init__.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Vertical electrical sounding analysis.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .arrays import geometric_factor, apparent_resistivity\nfrom .forward import forward_schlumberger, forward_wenner, forward_for_sounding\nfrom .inversion import invert_sounding, InversionResult\nfrom .ipi2win import read_ipi2win_models\nfrom .classify import classify_curve\nfrom .interpret import interpret_model, drilling_preference_table, SiteInterpretation\nfrom .splice import splice_segments\n\n__all__ = [\n \"geometric_factor\",\n \"apparent_resistivity\",\n \"forward_schlumberger\",\n \"forward_wenner\",\n \"forward_for_sounding\",\n \"invert_sounding\",\n \"InversionResult\",\n \"read_ipi2win_models\",\n \"classify_curve\",\n \"interpret_model\",\n \"drilling_preference_table\",\n \"SiteInterpretation\",\n \"splice_segments\",\n]\n"}, "groundwater/ves/arrays.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Electrode array geometric factors.\n\nAll spacings are in metres and resistances in ohm; apparent\nresistivity is returned in ohm-m. ``mn`` is always the full potential\nelectrode spacing MN, matching the field sheets, not MN/2.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\ndef geometric_factor(\n array_type: str,\n ab2: float | np.ndarray | None = None,\n mn: float | np.ndarray | None = None,\n a: float | np.ndarray | None = None,\n n: float | np.ndarray | None = None,\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Geometric factor K such that rho_a = K * (delta V / I).\n\n Parameters\n ----------\n array_type:\n \"schlumberger\", \"wenner\", \"dipole-dipole\" or \"pole-pole\".\n ab2:\n Half current electrode spacing AB/2 (Schlumberger).\n mn:\n Full potential electrode spacing MN (Schlumberger).\n a:\n Electrode spacing (Wenner) or dipole length (dipole-dipole,\n pole-pole).\n n:\n Dipole separation multiplier (dipole-dipole).\n\n For the Schlumberger array with finite MN the exact factor is\n ``K = pi (L^2 - b^2) / (2 b)`` with L = AB/2 and b = MN/2.\n \"\"\"\n kind = array_type.strip().lower()\n if kind.startswith(\"schlum\"):\n if ab2 is None or mn is None:\n raise ValueError(\"Schlumberger needs ab2 and mn\")\n L = np.asarray(ab2, dtype=float)\n b = np.asarray(mn, dtype=float) / 2.0\n if np.any(b <= 0) or np.any(L <= b):\n raise ValueError(\"Require 0 < MN/2 < AB/2 for Schlumberger\")\n return np.pi * (L**2 - b**2) / (2.0 * b)\n if kind.startswith(\"wenner\"):\n if a is None:\n raise ValueError(\"Wenner needs the spacing a\")\n return 2.0 * np.pi * np.asarray(a, dtype=float)\n if kind.startswith(\"dipole\"):\n if a is None or n is None:\n raise ValueError(\"dipole-dipole needs a and n\")\n a_arr = np.asarray(a, dtype=float)\n n_arr = np.asarray(n, dtype=float)\n return np.pi * n_arr * (n_arr + 1) * (n_arr + 2) * a_arr\n if kind.startswith(\"pole-pole\") or kind.startswith(\"pole pole\"):\n if a is None:\n raise ValueError(\"pole-pole needs the spacing a\")\n return 2.0 * np.pi * np.asarray(a, dtype=float)\n raise ValueError(f\"Unknown array type: {array_type}\")\n\n\ndef apparent_resistivity(\n array_type: str,\n resistance_ohm: float | np.ndarray,\n **spacings,\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Apparent resistivity from measured resistance (delta V / I).\"\"\"\n K = geometric_factor(array_type, **spacings)\n return K * np.asarray(resistance_ohm, dtype=float)\n"}, "groundwater/ves/classify.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Sounding curve type classification (H, K, A, Q and combinations).\n\nFor three layers the classical types are\n\n* H: rho1 > rho2 < rho3 (conductive middle layer)\n* K: rho1 < rho2 > rho3 (resistive middle layer)\n* A: rho1 < rho2 < rho3 (ascending)\n* Q: rho1 > rho2 > rho3 (descending)\n\nModels with more layers are classified by the sequence of overlapping\nthree layer triplets, giving the usual combined names such as HK, KH,\nHKH or QQ.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..models import LayeredModel\n\n__all__ = [\"classify_curve\", \"describe_curve_type\"]\n\n_TRIPLET = {\n (1, 0): \"K\", # up then down\n (0, 1): \"H\", # down then up\n (1, 1): \"A\", # up, up\n (0, 0): \"Q\", # down, down\n}\n\n\ndef classify_curve(model: LayeredModel) -> str:\n \"\"\"Curve type letters for a layered model.\n\n Two layer models return \"2-layer ascending\" or \"2-layer\n descending\"; models with three or more layers return letter codes.\n \"\"\"\n rho = np.asarray(model.resistivities, dtype=float)\n if len(rho) < 2:\n return \"uniform\"\n if len(rho) == 2:\n return \"2-layer ascending\" if rho[1] > rho[0] else \"2-layer descending\"\n letters = []\n for i in range(len(rho) - 2):\n up1 = 1 if rho[i + 1] > rho[i] else 0\n up2 = 1 if rho[i + 2] > rho[i + 1] else 0\n letters.append(_TRIPLET[(up1, up2)])\n return \"\".join(letters)\n\n\n_DESCRIPTIONS = {\n \"H\": \"a conductive layer between two more resistive layers, the classical \"\n \"signature of a saturated weathered zone above fresh basement\",\n \"K\": \"a resistive layer between two more conductive layers, often dry \"\n \"laterite or duricrust over a conductive saprolite\",\n \"A\": \"resistivity increasing with depth, typical of progressively less \"\n \"weathered rock towards fresh basement\",\n \"Q\": \"resistivity decreasing with depth, typical of deepening weathering \"\n \"or increasing saturation with depth\",\n}\n\n\ndef describe_curve_type(curve_type: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Short hydrogeological reading of a curve type for report text.\"\"\"\n if curve_type.startswith(\"2-layer\"):\n direction = \"ascending\" if \"ascending\" in curve_type else \"descending\"\n if direction == \"descending\":\n return (\n \"a two layer response with resistivity decreasing at depth, \"\n \"consistent with weathered or fractured, possibly water bearing \"\n \"rock beneath a resistive surface layer\"\n )\n return (\n \"a two layer response with resistivity increasing at depth, \"\n \"consistent with more competent rock beneath the surface layer\"\n )\n parts = [f\"type {curve_type}\"]\n seen = []\n for letter in curve_type:\n if letter in _DESCRIPTIONS and letter not in seen:\n seen.append(letter)\n parts.append(_DESCRIPTIONS[letter])\n return \"; \".join(parts)\n"}, "groundwater/ves/forward.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"1D layered earth forward modelling for resistivity soundings.\n\nThe apparent resistivity over a stack of horizontal layers is obtained\nfrom the resistivity transform ``T(lambda)`` (Koefoed recurrence) and\na Hankel transform:\n\n* ideal Schlumberger (gradient array, MN -> 0)::\n\n rho_a(L) = L^2 * Int_0^inf T(lam) J1(lam L) lam dlam\n\n* finite MN Schlumberger, from the surface potential\n ``F(r) = Int_0^inf T(lam) J0(lam r) dlam``::\n\n rho_a = (L^2 - b^2) / (2 b) * [F(L - b) - F(L + b)], b = MN/2\n\n* Wenner::\n\n rho_a(a) = 2 a * [F(a) - F(2a)]\n\nThe integrals are evaluated by direct quadrature on a hybrid\nlogarithmic + linear abscissa after subtracting the half space\nasymptote (``T -> rho_1`` for large lambda), which makes the integrand\ndecay exponentially. This avoids relying on tabulated digital filter\ncoefficients and is validated against the analytic two layer image\nseries in the test suite (agreement better than 0.2 percent).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom numpy.polynomial.legendre import leggauss\nfrom scipy.special import j0, j1, jn_zeros\n\nfrom ..models import LayeredModel, VESSounding\n\n__all__ = [\n \"resistivity_transform\",\n \"forward_schlumberger\",\n \"forward_schlumberger_finite_mn\",\n \"forward_wenner\",\n \"forward_for_sounding\",\n \"two_layer_schlumberger_series\",\n]\n\n\ndef resistivity_transform(\n lam: np.ndarray, resistivities: np.ndarray, thicknesses: np.ndarray\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Koefoed/Pekeris recurrence for the resistivity transform T(lambda).\n\n Stable downward recurrence starting from the half space:\n ``T_n = rho_n``;\n ``T_i = (T_{i+1} + rho_i tanh(lam h_i)) / (1 + T_{i+1} tanh(lam h_i) / rho_i)``.\n \"\"\"\n lam = np.asarray(lam, dtype=float)\n rho = np.asarray(resistivities, dtype=float)\n h = np.asarray(thicknesses, dtype=float)\n T = np.full_like(lam, rho[-1])\n for i in range(len(h) - 1, -1, -1):\n th = np.tanh(lam * h[i])\n T = (T + rho[i] * th) / (1.0 + T * th / rho[i])\n return T\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Hankel integration machinery\n#\n# Integrals of the form Int_0^inf g(x) Jn(x) dx with g smooth and\n# exponentially decaying are computed in two sections:\n#\n# * x in (0, z1), z1 the first zero of Jn: composite Gauss-Legendre on\n# log-subdivided panels. The resistivity transform varies over about\n# a decade of lambda, so sub-decade panels resolve it for any layer\n# thickness / spacing ratio.\n# * x > z1: 10 point Gauss-Legendre panels between consecutive zeros\n# of Jn. Within a half period the integrand is smooth, so each panel\n# is near exact. The number of panels follows the exponential decay\n# scale of (T - rho1).\n#\n# Nodes and (weight x Bessel) products are precomputed once per order,\n# so each integral is two vectorised evaluations of g.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n_N_ZEROS = 1200\n\n# The quadrature runs out to the largest tabulated Bessel zero. A sounding\n# needs panels out to 9 * (AB/2) / h_min, so 1200 zeros (largest abscissa\n# 3770.7) covers spacings up to about 419 times the thinnest layer. Beyond\n# that the table is grown on demand: truncating the integral part-way\n# through an oscillation of J1 leaves a large spurious residue - at AB/2 =\n# 1000 m over a 0.5 m layer the model returned 574 ohm-m instead of 30.\n# The inversion explores thin layers, so it can walk into that regime.\n# Growth ceiling. 60000 zeros reach x = 188495, covering spacings up to about\n# 20900 times the thinnest layer - far past anything a real sounding sees, and\n# bounded so the browser build cannot be made to allocate without limit.\n_MAX_ZEROS = 60_000\n\n# Floor on the layer thickness used to size the decay scale. The inversion\n# bounds thicknesses at 0.2 m; this only guards a hand-built degenerate model.\n_MIN_DECAY_H = 0.02\n\n\ndef _build_tables(order: int, n_zeros: int = _N_ZEROS):\n zeros = jn_zeros(order, n_zeros)\n bessel = j0 if order == 0 else j1\n\n # section 1: 14 log-spaced panels from 1e-6 to the first zero, GL-8\n nodes8, weights8 = leggauss(8)\n edges = np.geomspace(1e-6, zeros[0], 15)\n s1_nodes, s1_wb = [], []\n for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:], strict=True):\n mid, half = 0.5 * (lo + hi), 0.5 * (hi - lo)\n x = mid + half * nodes8\n s1_nodes.append(x)\n s1_wb.append(half * weights8 * bessel(x))\n\n # section 2: GL-10 between consecutive zeros\n nodes10, weights10 = leggauss(10)\n s2_nodes, s2_wb = [], []\n lo = zeros[0]\n for hi in zeros[1:]:\n mid, half = 0.5 * (lo + hi), 0.5 * (hi - lo)\n x = mid + half * nodes10\n s2_nodes.append(x)\n s2_wb.append(half * weights10 * bessel(x))\n lo = hi\n return {\n \"s1_nodes\": np.concatenate(s1_nodes),\n \"s1_wb\": np.concatenate(s1_wb),\n \"s2_nodes\": np.concatenate(s2_nodes),\n \"s2_wb\": np.concatenate(s2_wb),\n \"panel_ends\": zeros[1:],\n }\n\n\n_TABLES = {0: _build_tables(0), 1: _build_tables(1)}\n\n\ndef _table_for(order: int, x_stop: float) -> dict:\n \"\"\"Quadrature table for ``order`` reaching at least ``x_stop``.\n\n Grows (and caches) the table rather than truncating the integral, which\n silently returned resistivities an order of magnitude wrong.\n \"\"\"\n table = _TABLES[order]\n if table[\"panel_ends\"][-1] >= x_stop or len(table[\"panel_ends\"]) + 1 >= _MAX_ZEROS:\n return table\n # zeros of J are spaced about pi apart, so this is the count that reaches\n # x_stop, with headroom so a sweep of spacings does not rebuild each time\n needed = min(int(x_stop / math.pi) + 32, _MAX_ZEROS)\n needed = min(max(needed, 2 * (len(table[\"panel_ends\"]) + 1)), _MAX_ZEROS)\n table = _build_tables(order, needed)\n _TABLES[order] = table\n return table\n\n\ndef _hankel_integral(g, order: int, x_decay: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"Int_0^inf g(x) J_order(x) dx for smooth g decaying like\n exp(-x / x_decay) at large x.\"\"\"\n x_stop = 18.0 * max(x_decay, 1.0)\n t = _table_for(order, x_stop)\n acc = float(np.dot(g(t[\"s1_nodes\"]), t[\"s1_wb\"]))\n n_panels = int(np.searchsorted(t[\"panel_ends\"], x_stop)) + 1\n n_panels = min(max(n_panels, 8), len(t[\"panel_ends\"]))\n k = n_panels * 10\n acc += float(np.dot(g(t[\"s2_nodes\"][:k]), t[\"s2_wb\"][:k]))\n return acc\n\n\ndef forward_schlumberger(\n model: LayeredModel | tuple, ab2: np.ndarray\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Ideal (gradient) Schlumberger apparent resistivity at AB/2 values.\"\"\"\n rho, h = _model_arrays(model)\n ab2 = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ab2, dtype=float))\n h_min = float(np.min(h)) if len(h) else 1.0\n out = np.empty_like(ab2)\n for i, L in enumerate(ab2):\n # substitute x = lambda L: rho_a = rho1 + Int (T(x/L) - rho1) J1(x) x dx\n # (the L^2 prefactor cancels against the 1/L^2 from the substitution)\n def g(x, L=L):\n return (resistivity_transform(x / L, rho, h) - rho[0]) * x\n\n # (T - rho1) decays like exp(-2 lambda h_min) = exp(-x / (L / (2 h_min)))\n out[i] = rho[0] + _hankel_integral(g, 1, L / (2.0 * max(h_min, _MIN_DECAY_H)))\n return out\n\n\ndef _potential_integral(rho, h, r: float, h_min: float) -> float:\n \"\"\"F(r) = Int T(lam) J0(lam r) dlam = (rho1 + Int (T - rho1) J0(x) dx) / r.\"\"\"\n\n def g(x, r=r):\n return resistivity_transform(x / r, rho, h) - rho[0]\n\n return (rho[0] + _hankel_integral(g, 0, r / (2.0 * max(h_min, _MIN_DECAY_H)))) / r\n\n\ndef forward_schlumberger_finite_mn(\n model: LayeredModel | tuple, ab2: np.ndarray, mn: np.ndarray\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Schlumberger apparent resistivity with finite MN spacing.\n\n Reproduces what the instrument actually measures at each\n (AB/2, MN) pair, including the small jumps at segment changes.\n \"\"\"\n rho, h = _model_arrays(model)\n ab2 = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ab2, dtype=float))\n mn = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(mn, dtype=float))\n h_min = float(np.min(h)) if len(h) else 1.0\n out = np.empty_like(ab2)\n for i, (L, m) in enumerate(zip(ab2, mn, strict=True)):\n b = m / 2.0\n if not np.isfinite(b) or b <= 0 or b >= L:\n # fall back to the ideal gradient value\n out[i] = forward_schlumberger((rho, h), np.array([L]))[0]\n continue\n f_in = _potential_integral(rho, h, L - b, h_min)\n f_out = _potential_integral(rho, h, L + b, h_min)\n out[i] = (L**2 - b**2) / (2.0 * b) * (f_in - f_out)\n return out\n\n\ndef forward_wenner(model: LayeredModel | tuple, a: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Wenner apparent resistivity at spacings a.\"\"\"\n rho, h = _model_arrays(model)\n a = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(a, dtype=float))\n h_min = float(np.min(h)) if len(h) else 1.0\n out = np.empty_like(a)\n for i, s in enumerate(a):\n f1 = _potential_integral(rho, h, s, h_min)\n f2 = _potential_integral(rho, h, 2.0 * s, h_min)\n # rho_a = 2 pi a (V_M - V_N)/I; with A and B both contributing,\n # V_M - V_N = (I/pi) (F(a) - F(2a)), so rho_a = 2 a (F(a) - F(2a)).\n out[i] = 2.0 * s * (f1 - f2)\n return out\n\n\ndef forward_for_sounding(\n model: LayeredModel | tuple,\n sounding: VESSounding,\n finite_mn: bool = False,\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Model response at a sounding's abscissas.\"\"\"\n if sounding.array_type.startswith(\"wenner\"):\n return forward_wenner(model, sounding.ab2)\n if finite_mn and np.all(np.isfinite(sounding.mn)):\n return forward_schlumberger_finite_mn(model, sounding.ab2, sounding.mn)\n return forward_schlumberger(model, sounding.ab2)\n\n\ndef two_layer_schlumberger_series(\n rho1: float, rho2: float, h: float, ab2: np.ndarray, n_terms: int = 4000\n) -> np.ndarray:\n \"\"\"Analytic two layer ideal Schlumberger curve from image theory.\n\n ``rho_a(L) = rho1 [1 + 2 sum_n k^n L^3 / (L^2 + (2 n h)^2)^(3/2)]``\n with reflection coefficient k = (rho2 - rho1) / (rho2 + rho1).\n Used to validate the numerical Hankel evaluation.\n \"\"\"\n ab2 = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ab2, dtype=float))\n k = (rho2 - rho1) / (rho2 + rho1)\n n = np.arange(1, n_terms + 1)[:, None]\n L = ab2[None, :]\n terms = (k**n) * L**3 / (L**2 + (2.0 * n * h) ** 2) ** 1.5\n return rho1 * (1.0 + 2.0 * np.sum(terms, axis=0))\n\n\ndef _model_arrays(model: LayeredModel | tuple) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n if isinstance(model, LayeredModel):\n return model.resistivities, model.thicknesses\n rho, h = model\n return np.asarray(rho, dtype=float), np.asarray(h, dtype=float)\n"}, "groundwater/ves/interpret.py": {"t": "text", "d": "\"\"\"Hydrogeological interpretation of layered models.\n\nThe rules target crystalline basement terrain typical of Sierra Leone:\na lateritic or clayey cover, saprolite, a weathered/fractured zone\nthat forms the main aquifer, and fresh basement at depth. Thresholds\nlive in :class:`~groundwater.config.VESConfig` so they can be tuned\nper area (coastal sedimentary sites use different ranges).\n\nOutputs:\n\n* per layer lithological/hydrogeological labels,\n* possible water zones as depth ranges,\n* estimated depth to (fresh) basement and aquifer thickness,\n* a recommended maximum drilling depth,\n* the ranked drilling preference table used in survey reports.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom ..config import VESConfig\nfrom ..models import DataFlag, LayeredModel, VESSounding\nfrom ..utils import fmt_num, ordinal\nfrom .classify import classify_curve, describe_curve_type\n\n__all__ = [\n \"LayerInterpretation\",\n \"SiteInterpretation\",\n \"depth_of_investigation\",\n \"fit_confidence\",\n \"interpret_model\",\n \"drilling_preference_table\",\n \"rank_interpretations\",\n]\n\n\ndef depth_of_investigation(max_spacing_m: float, config: VESConfig | None = None) -> float:\n \"\"\"How deep a sounding with this largest AB/2 actually resolves.\n\n One rule for the whole toolkit: the interpretation, the model panel of\n the curve figure, the layer column, the section and the drilling-depth\n cap all read it, so a document no longer shows the same half-space\n ending at 40 m in one figure and 80 m in the next.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or VESConfig()\n return float(max_spacing_m) * config.depth_of_investigation_factor\n\n\ndef fit_confidence(fit_error_percent: float | None, config: VESConfig | None = None) -> float:\n \"\"\"How far a model's misfit should discount what is read from it.\n\n 1.0 at or under the target misfit, falling linearly to the floor at the\n unreliable level and staying there. A 26.8 percent two-layer fit is not\n a description of the curve, and a ranking that cannot see that prefers\n it over a 13 percent fit on 2.7 ohm-m of half-space resistivity.\n \"\"\"\n config = config or VESConfig()\n if fit_error_percent is None:\n return 1.0\n target = config.target_fit_percent\n unreliable = max(config.unreliable_fit_percent, target + 1e-9)\n if fit_error_percent <= target:\n return 1.0\n frac = min((fit_error_percent - target) / (unreliable - target), 1.0)\n return 1.0 - (1.0 - config.fit_confidence_floor) * frac\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass LayerInterpretation:\n number: int\n rho: float\n thickness_m: float | None # None for the half space\n top_m: float\n bottom_m: float # inf for the half space\n unit: str\n water_bearing: bool\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SiteInterpretation:\n sounding_id: str\n model: LayeredModel\n curve_type: str\n layers: list[LayerInterpretation]\n water_zones: list[tuple[float, float]]\n depth_to_basement_m: float | None\n aquifer_thickness_m: float\n max_drilling_depth_m: float\n investigation_depth_m: float\n score: float # used for ranking between sites\n # Dar-Zarrouk parameters over the resolved overburden\n longitudinal_conductance_s: float = 0.0 # siemens, Sum(h/rho), full section\n transverse_resistance_t: float = 0.0 # ohm m2, Sum(h*rho), full section\n # conductance of the cover overlying the aquifer, used for protection\n protective_conductance_s: float = 0.0\n protective_capacity: str = \"\" # from the protective (cover) conductance\n narrative: str = \"\"\n rank: int | None = None\n site_easting: float | None = None\n site_northing: float | None = None\n site_elevation_m: float | None = None\n flags: list = field(default_factory=list)\n #: True when the deepest water-bearing layer is the half-space: the\n #: sounding never reached its base, so the zone is open-ended, the\n #: aquifer thickness is a lower bound and the drilling depth a minimum\n basement_not_resolved: bool = False\n #: 0-1 discount from the fit quality and the unresolved basement,\n #: applied to the score and the suitability before ranking\n confidence: float = 1.0\n fit_error_percent: float | None = None\n #: \"ok\", \"poor\" (above the target) or \"unreliable\" (above the\n #: unreliable level), judged against the config the model was read with\n fit_quality: str = \"ok\"\n #: the largest AB/2 the sounding was expanded to; the depth of\n #: investigation is a fraction of it, not the spacing itself\n max_spacing_m: float | None = None\n\n\ndef _unit_label(\n rho: float, is_top: bool, is_bottom: bool, config: VESConfig\n) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n \"\"\"Label a layer and judge whether it is potentially water bearing.\"\"\"\n lo, hi = config.fractured_zone_rho\n if is_top:\n if rho >= config.laterite_min_rho:\n return \"dry lateritic topsoil / duricrust\", False\n if rho >= hi:\n return \"compact laterite / dry overburden\", False\n if rho <= config.clay_max_rho:\n return \"clayey topsoil\", False\n return \"topsoil / laterite\", False\n if rho >= config.fresh_basement_min_rho:\n return \"fresh basement\", False\n if rho >= hi:\n if is_bottom:\n return \"slightly weathered or fractured bedrock (limited water potential)\", False\n return \"compact or dry weathered rock (regolith)\", False\n if rho <= config.clay_max_rho:\n return \"clay rich saprolite (low permeability)\", float | None = None\n if sounding is not None:\n max_spacing = float(np.max(sounding.ab2))\n investigation = depth_of_investigation(max_spacing, config)\n elif n > 1:\n investigation = float(bottoms[-2] * 2 + 20)\n else:\n # A bare half-space with no sounding carries no depth scale at all -\n # bottoms is just [inf], and bottoms[-2] used to raise IndexError.\n # Zero is the honest answer: nothing was resolved, so nothing is\n # recommended.\n investigation = 0.0\n\n layers: list[LayerInterpretation] = []\n for i in range(n):\n unit, water = _unit_label(\n float(rho[i]), is_top=(i == 0), is_bottom=(i == n - 1), config=config\n )\n layers.append(\n LayerInterpretation(\n number=i + 1,\n rho=float(rho[i]),\n thickness_m=float(model.thicknesses[i]) if i < n - 1 else the top few metres are vadose\n if math.isfinite(layer.bottom_m):\n bottom = layer.bottom_m\n else:\n bottom = investigation\n basement_not_resolved = bottom - top >= 1.0\n if bottom - top >= 1.0:\n zones.append((round(top), round(bottom)))\n # merge touching zones\n merged: list[tuple[float, float]] = []\n for zone in sorted(zones):\n if merged and zone[0] <= merged[-1][1] + 1:\n merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(merged[-1][1], zone[1]))\n else:\n merged.append(zone)\n zones = merged\n\n # ---- depth to basement -------------------------------------------------\n depth_to_basement = None\n for layer in layers:\n if layer.rho >= config.fresh_basement_min_rho and layer.top_m > 0:\n depth_to_basement = layer.top_m\n break\n if depth_to_basement is None and layers[-1].rho >= config.fractured_zone_rho[1]:\n depth_to_basement = layers[-1].top_m\n\n aquifer_thickness = sum(b - t for t, b in zones)\n\n # ---- recommended maximum drilling depth ---------------------------------\n # deepest target zone plus a margin, but never past the depth the\n # sounding actually investigated (taken as the maximum AB/2)\n if zones:\n deepest = zones[-1][1] + config.max_drilling_margin_m\n else:\n deepest = investigation\n step = config.round_drilling_depth_to_m\n # Round up to the nearest step, then re-apply the investigated-depth cap:\n # rounding after the min() could push the recommendation past the depth the\n # sounding actually resolved, defeating the cap.\n max_depth = math.ceil(min(deepest, investigation) / step) * step\n max_depth = min(max_depth, investigation)\n\n # ---- suitability score for ranking --------------------------------------\n score = 0.0\n for top, bottom in zones:\n thickness = bottom - top\n mid_rho = _zone_rho(layers, top, bottom)\n # favour thick zones with resistivities in the productive window\n lo, hi = config.fractured_zone_rho\n centre = math.sqrt(lo * hi)\n rho_term = 1.0 / (1.0 + abs(math.log(max(mid_rho, 1e-3) / centre)))\n score += thickness * rho_term\n if depth_to_basement is not None and depth_to_basement < 5 and not zones:\n score *= 0.5 # {fmt_num(interp.investigation_depth_m)} m, and the \"\n \"conductive ground continues below that.\"\n )\n else:\n parts.append(\n \"No clearly water bearing low resistivity zone is resolved at this suitability section all rank on the same\n quantity. There used to be two scores - the interpretation's own and\n the scorecard's - and a report could recommend one point in the\n summary and another in the scorecard section.\n \"\"\"\n from ..siting.suitability import assess_siting # circular at module level\n\n result = assess_siting([interp], config)[0]\n return result.suitability * result.confidence\n\n\ndef rank_interpretations(\n interpretations: list[SiteInterpretation],\n preferred_order: list[str] | None = None,\n config: VESConfig | None = None,\n) -> list[SiteInterpretation]:\n \"\"\"Assign ``rank`` (1 = most preferred) in place; return them ranked.\n\n Kept separate from the preference table so callers that only need the\n ranking - the dashboard, a reloaded project - get it without building the\n table.
